### Milestone 118 — DONE (lock-step control in the hvx engine runner: stops at exact points of the instruction clock, input typed at an exact icount, console lines reported at every stop, snapshots that carry the input the guest has not read; the experiments of M116 as a permanent check; the cost of stopping at every event measured on the stack; 2026-10-31)

Branch `hvx-lockstep`. Step A4 of `docs/design/guest-control.md`. No change to `hvx.c`, `hvx_abi.h` or the loaded module (main module `0799F1B8EE2A35600D94EB4`, no reload); every VM went through `~/bin/hvx-run` from the own tree `~/hydo-ls` on the bare-metal machine, at most two at a time.
- **The protocol as implemented** (`hv/hvx/hvx_explore.c`, header section "Lock-step control", with two examples cut from real transcripts). It is opt-in per request. `CTL <tag> <schedule>` in serve mode is a RUN under control (restore S1, arm the host part, type the guest part; an empty guest part types nothing). `RESUME <tag> <snapshot>` continues a controlled run in a fresh VM from a snapshot that an earlier controlled run took. `hvx_explore --control one ... "<schedule>"` is the same from a fresh boot. Before every stop the engine prints `EVENT <tag> at=<icount> n=<k> <escaped line>` for each complete console line written since the last stop (bytes outside printable ASCII escaped as `\\`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\xHH`), `SENT <tag> id=<id> at=<icount>[ retype=1]` for each queued input typed at this stop, `DROP <tag> id=<id>` for queued input that a move to the recovery VM discards, and then `STOP <tag> at=<icount> n=<k> phase=workload|check|recovery why=start|resume|cadence|send|marker|exit`. It then reads host lines until `CONT` or `END [<verdict>]`. `SEND at=<icount> <escaped bytes>` (1 to 4,096 bytes) answers `OK send id=<id> sent=<icount>` when typed at once or `OK send id=<id> queued=<at>`; `ACK <id>` marks a send as read by the guest; `SNAP <name> [retype]` answers `OK snap <name> at=<icount> retype=<ids|->` or `ERR snap <name> unacked=<ids>`. `END` fingerprints at that stop and prints the RESULT with the host's verdict (without one, the last `HYDO-ORACLE` line). EOF ends the run with `ERROR control channel closed`. A controlled RESULT has three more facts before `verdict=`: `stops=` (the last stop's number), `typed=` and `inh=` (FNV-1a over every typed send's icount, length and bytes).
- **The rules.** Every return of a run call is a stop, except a return that was cut short only to land on a pending send and typed nothing; the schedule's `rb=<n>` is therefore the cadence (a stop after at most n events). While a send is pending, each run call gets at most max(1, (at − icount) / 2048) events, so no call runs past it; the send is typed at the first stop with icount ≥ at. A snapshot is refused while a typed send is unacknowledged; with `retype` it is taken, and RESUME types those sends again right after the restore (input still in the UART receive queue is in no snapshot, M116). A snapshot also carries the queued sends, the console offset up to which lines were reported, and the stop and event counters, so a continuation numbers its stops like its base (the resume stop repeats the number of the stop where SNAP was taken) and reports the base's `stops=`, `typed=` and `inh=`. SNAP is refused outside the workload phase and for schedules with `tj`, `xt`, `pp`, `q` or `cf` tokens; at most 8 names are kept (a SNAP with an existing name replaces it). The recovery VM after a power cut is its own clock (it starts from S0's icount); queued sends do not carry over into it.
- **The client** (`hydo/crates/hydo-engine/src/lockstep.rs`). Typed engine lines (`EngineLine`), host commands (`HostCmd`), the escaping, and a session `Lockstep` with `next_stop`, `send`, `ack`, `snap`, `cont`, `end` and an optional transcript log. `Worker::lockstep(&LockstepStart, log)` is a new trait method with a default answer of Unsupported; the hvx process worker implements it (hvm answers Unsupported; that is step A5). `Hvx::one_lockstep` starts `--control one`. No existing caller uses any of it, and it contains no controller logic.
- **Inert when unused.** On the bare-metal machine, `HVX_METAL_TREE=hydo-ls hv/hvx/deploy-metal.sh` gave ALL PASS (31 checks). Both pinned reproducers through this engine (`one`) gave `2403499c9a3f8419` (VIOLATION, `explore-disk.img`) and `f87130453609a5d6` (OK, `explore-fix-disk.img`); the same schedule as a CTL run whose host only answers CONT also gave `f87130453609a5d6`. A plain RUN and a CTL run that only answers CONT give the same fingerprint at every cadence measured: Redis plain `fd4b848eb8969419`, `rb=256` `c9aaf197fc1a6a4f`, `rb=16` `a6e72fcdff5f17ed`, `rb=1` `93d199cae9ab642d` (the plain, `rb=16` and `rb=1` values are M116's recorded ones); the stack image `explore-binlog-ret-xr-nq-disk.img`, `disk=none | run`, plain `2d2974fb9f5459f1`, `rb=256` `d6043688a17dd24c`, `rb=16` `64b74e5080fc55c3`, `rb=1` `1e53bac36a8f0f8e`; `explore-fix-disk.img` with the pinned schedule, `rb=16` `6eaa4f8b9090d6eb`, `rb=1` `b026a7772dcbbb0c`. The workspace's `cargo test --locked` (the explorer's identity corpora and golden tests included), clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- **The experiments of M116 as a permanent check** (`hv/hvx/lockstep-metal.sh check` from the Mac; `hydo/crates/hydo-engine/examples/lockstep_check.rs`; image `explore-ob-redis-nq-disk.img`, `disk=none | run K=redis@5+2`; result `/var/tmp/m118/c3` on the bare-metal machine: "lockstep_check: ALL PASS", 18 groups). Every group is identical in every run, and equal to its recorded value: typed at +20,000 `146dec7ffae541c1` (twice from S1 and once from a fresh boot), +20,001 `46a292f1a33788cc`, +60,000 `023bcafa7233eaf2`, two lines `2309a3b53b2db7d0`, a reaction 5,000 events after `KILLED redis` at `rb=16` `f6d7670d74596283`, typed at +60,000 with a snapshot at +11,569 (base, two continuations, the straight run without a snapshot and a fresh boot) `456001c6ec2263cb`, typed at +5,000 before that snapshot (acknowledged first) `8f87ca0fcdddf60a`: all of these are M116's values, now produced by the engine itself instead of the interposer. A reaction "at once" to the line `hydo-ob: KILLED redis before step 5` gives `24b5730593297b77` three times (twice from S1, once from a fresh boot); M116's `b83bf67d682b4609` differs because the interposer matched the substring `KILLED redis` 80 events before the line was complete (+11,841 against +11,921), and typing at once at the stop +11,841 gives `b83bf67d682b4609` again. The snapshot rule at the reaction's own stop: SNAP without `retype` is refused (`unacked=1`), with `retype` both continuations type the line again and give the base's `24b5730593297b77` with the base's 1,719 stops and input hash; a snapshot taken before the reaction's send gives continuations without the line, `a6e72fcdff5f17ed`, the no-input value (M116's "lost" case). END at the first stop at or after +30,000 (after a send at +20,000) gives `93e4960856f3a651` twice from S1 and once from a fresh boot, with the host's verdict. Seven of the transcripts are committed in `hydo/crates/hydo-engine/tests/lockstep/`; the test `tests/lockstep.rs` replays each one through the client (every engine line parses, the client writes exactly the recorded host lines, stop numbers count up by one, a resumed run starts with its snapshot's stop number).
- **Found: an hvx guest is not independent of where the host's run calls return.** The same bytes typed at the same icount (960,968) at `rb=16` give `b83bf67d682b4609` when they are typed at once at that stop and `8c738a6f79b1d1a7` when they were queued at the start, so that the run calls before them were capped. Ending runs without any input at the same icount with cadences 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 gives the same console, CPU snapshot and disk but four different guest RAM hashes. The difference is 32 bytes at offset 0x30880 of the guest's per-CPU area, which is `irq_randomness` (Linux's per-CPU interrupt entropy pool; its interrupt count, 42, and its jiffies are the same in both): some interrupt reaches the guest at another instruction or cycle value depending on where a run call returned, and leaves no other trace there. Runs stay reproducible (the same cadence and the same commands at the same stops give the same fingerprint every time), but a run is not defined by (icount, bytes) alone: it is defined by the cadence and by the host's commands at each numbered stop. At `rb=1` every event is already a stop, nothing is ever capped, and a queued send and a send typed at once give the same `a83d0d89f7c25811`. The module was not changed (outside this step); the cause inside `hvx.c` was not looked for.
- **The cost of stopping at every event** (`hv/hvx/lockstep-metal.sh cost`; the engine's own `secs`, one VM on an idle bare-metal machine; "stops" counts the workload, the check and the recovery boot):

  | schedule | plain RUN | RUN `rb=1` | CTL `rb=1` (stops) | CTL `rb=16` (stops) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | stack `explore-binlog-ret-xr-nq`, `disk=none \| run` | 4.8 s | 5.7 s | 9.2 s, 9.1 s (104,957) | 5.1 s (6,550) |
  | `explore-fix-disk`, `K=redis@11+1 C=24` (power cut, recovery boot) | 12.4 s | 15.3 s | 24.1 s (525,980) | 13.6 s (32,864) |
  | Redis `explore-ob-redis-nq`, `K=redis@5+2` | 2.5 s | 2.6 s | 3.2 s (27,343) | 2.5 s (1,704) |

  Stopping at every event adds 0.7 s, 4.4 s and 11.7 s to runs of 2.5 s, 4.8 s and 12.4 s (the stack's runs about double; most of a Redis run's 2.5 s is fingerprinting, M116). Per stop, the run calls themselves cost about 4–9 µs and the host round trip (the stop's lines, the CONT, the pipe) about 17–33 µs. At `rb=16` the cost is 0–10 %, at `rb=256` nothing measurable. The module's events are retired deterministic exits and PMU ticks, not every VM exit: the stack's workload has about 105,000 of them against its 3.9 million exits (docs/PERF-RUN-COST.md).
- **Size of the C change.** `hvx_explore.c` grew from 1,652 to 2,160 lines (544 added, 36 removed): 87 lines of protocol documentation in the header, `struct sched` moved up (19 lines), and about 430 lines of new code, most of it one block of helper functions (about 315 lines) plus RESUME (28 lines) and small hooks in `run_until_any`, `finish_sched`, `run_sched` and `main`; with `C.on` 0 the existing paths are unchanged. By the language policy this is a substantial change; the Rust in-process engine is the place for anything more.
- **Not done:** hvm (step A5); several vCPUs were not run under control (the code relies on `HVX_RUNC` reporting the shared clock and stopping at clean turn boundaries); the 64 KiB console copy at every return of a run call (`HVX_GET_CONSOLE`) was not measured apart from the run call itself; the cause of the run-call dependence in the module was not looked for.

### Milestone 119 — DONE (lock-step control in the Mac engine: `hvmx` speaks hvx_explore's lock-step protocol on the exit-count clock; M116's Mac experiment as a permanent test; mid-run branches with typed input proven on the Mac; 2026-10-31)

Branch `hvm-lockstep` (from `d2ec72e`), not merged. Step A5 of `docs/design/guest-control.md`. No change to `hvm.c`, the guest kernel, any image or manifest, the explorer or the CLI; `serve.c` grew by an opt-in mode and `virtio.c` by one free function.
- **One protocol for both engines.** The hvx side (step A4, M118, branch `hvx-lockstep`, work-in-progress commit `255d769`) had already fixed the wire format, so `hvmx` implements exactly that one, and the same typed client drives both engines. Requests: `CTL <tag> <schedule>` (like RUN: restore S1, arm the host part, type the guest part unless it is empty, then stop and wait), `RESUME <tag> <snapshot>` (a fresh VM from a SNAP of an earlier controlled run; it continues with the same schedule, console, queued input, stop and event numbers) and `hvmx --control one … "<schedule>"` (the same from a fresh boot). Engine lines before each stop: `EVENT <tag> at= n= <escaped line>` for every complete console line since the last stop, `SENT <tag> id= at=[ retype=1]`, `DROP <tag> id=` (queued input that a new VM discards), then `STOP <tag> at= n= phase=workload|check|recovery why=start|resume|send|marker|cadence|exit`. Host lines at a stop, each with one `OK`/`ERR` answer: `SEND at=<t> <escaped bytes>` (`OK send id= sent=` when typed at once, `queued=` otherwise), `ACK <id>`, `SNAP <name> [retype]` (`OK snap <name> at= retype=<ids|->`; refused with `unacked=<ids>` while a typed send is not acknowledged, unless `retype` is given, and RESUME then types those sends again), `CONT`, `END [<verdict>]`. RESULT gets `stops= typed= inh=` (FNV-1a over every typed send's time, length and bytes). EOF on stdin ends the run with `ERROR control channel closed`. Escapes are `\\ \n \r \t \xHH`. The error texts are hvx_explore's, except `ERR snap <name> not for tj/pct schedules` (hvm's timing tokens).
- **What is hvm's own.** The clock is the exit count `M.exits`; kicks and the spin observer's own exits are not exits, so every stop is a pure function of the run. A queued send is typed at the loop top of its exact exit, before the guest runs again (hvx caps its run calls to land on its icount). Markers are checked at every exit, as RUN does, so a CTL whose host only answers `CONT` gives RUN's fingerprint. The schedule's `rb=<n>` is the cadence (a stop every n exits from the phase's start; the default is 65,536, the interval at which hvx's run calls return without `rb=`); RUN still refuses `rb=` on hvm. The rewind mode is refused (it moves `M.exits` backwards), and a SPIN is reported, not re-run. `SNAP` is refused for `tj=`/`pct=` schedules, as hvx refuses it for its timing tokens.
- **The C change.** `hv/hvm/explore/serve.c` +435/−28 lines (about 370 lines of code and 62 of comments): the lock-step state and protocol (as in `hvx_explore.c`), a stop hook, `run_once` split at the workload's start into the setup and `run_rest` so that a RESUME can enter there, and the CTL/RESUME/`--control` dispatch. `hv/hvm/virtio.c`/`.h` +8 lines: `virtio_save_free`, used when a snapshot name is taken again. A first version of this milestone used its own variant of the protocol (`CTRL`, `WAKE`, `WATCH`, `FP`; commits `805d259` and `0b24f7a`); it was replaced once A4's format was known. It had reproduced the same M116 values.
- **hydo-engine.** `src/lockstep.rs`, `lib.rs` and `process.rs` are A4's (`255d769`) unchanged, except that `ProcessWorker::lockstep` no longer refuses hvm. `hvm.rs` adds `Hvm::one_lockstep` and `hvm::ControlledOne` (the counterparts of `Hvx::one_lockstep` and `hvx::ControlledOne`). No existing caller uses any of it. `cargo test --locked`, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass on the workspace.
- **Inert when unused** (this Mac, kernel `Image-explore` `f80c5655…`): the release's Redis example (`96f591d8…`/`9ddfc929…`), each schedule twice from serve and `disk=none | run` once from a fresh boot, gives `0f6aac764c64aac2`, `29fb0d55a5ab8101`, `f27a5cffb5d6fb47` and `19e3e8c9c2214a83` with the unchanged and with the new `hvmx` (the RESULT lines are identical except for `secs=`). M99's redis-bridge image (`e066eeee…`, `Image-explore-netns`) gives `307efc476cddb5c4` (also from a fresh boot), `K=replica@5+3` `310b32418083a8e7`, `disk=cut | run C=8` `d761c4b1ac47b64d`, `F=replica<primary@5#3:2000` `953bf35244e9367e` and `N=primary-replica@5-10:loss,100%` `a08d989df70a3e3b`, all as recorded. M96's images (shop, node-kv, python-kv) are not on this Mac with their recorded hashes, so they were not run. The explorer's golden tests pass unchanged (`cargo test`).
- **CTL equals RUN** (`hvm_lockstep_check run`, the same Redis image): for `disk=none | run`, `disk=cut | run C=12 R=everysec` (with its recovery phase), `O=redis@5-10:resp:loss,100%`, `tj=7 tjpm=500 tjmax=500` and `K=redis@5+2`, the plain RUN, a CTL whose host only answers CONT, and the same from `--control one` give one fingerprint each: `0f6aac764c64aac2`, `29fb0d55a5ab8101`, `f27a5cffb5d6fb47`, `19e3e8c9c2214a83` and `310186b549c81fd9`.
- **M116's Mac experiment as a permanent test** (`hv/hvm/explore/lockstep-check.sh`, which runs `hydo-engine/examples/hvm_lockstep_check.rs`). The image is `explore-ob-redis-oci-arm64` with `disk=none | run K=redis@5+2`; the workload starts at exit 19,899. Each configuration ran twice by CTL from S1 and once by `--control one`, and every group agreed on the fingerprint, the stop count, `typed=` and `inh=`. Nothing typed gives `6b9321d4b13e5d12`; `hydo-agent-ping 1\n` sent at +500 / +1,500 / +3,000 gives `dae633ebb392b3d8` / `7b01d5c261a5334a` / `ec004616904a49f0`; other text at +1,500 gives `5406af0d7002e705`; +1,501 gives `7b01d5c261a5334a` (the same as +1,500, as in M116); two lines at +500 and +3,000 give `d36401c377728af4`. These are every timed value that M116 recorded. The reactions ran with `rb=1` (a stop at every exit), and the host reacts at the first stop whose events contain `KILLED redis`, that is when the line is complete; M116's hook reacted as soon as the text appeared, so these are new values: at once `0fde36aac5dc2145`, 200 exits later `35a60b9b92709c8f`. `rb=1` with nothing typed gives `6b9321d4b13e5d12`, so the stops alone change nothing.
- **Mid-run branches with typed input on the Mac** (the design had left this unproven; hvx's BRANCH request is still answered `unsupported on hvm`). With a SNAP at the reaction's stop before the reaction is sent, the base run and a RESUME whose host sends the reaction again both give `35a60b9b92709c8f` (the straight run's value), and a RESUME that sends nothing gives `6b9321d4b13e5d12` (the line is lost, as M116 described). A SNAP with the reaction queued for 200 exits later carries it, and the base and two RESUMEs give `35a60b9b92709c8f`. With the reaction typed at once, SNAP is refused (`unacked=1`) and `SNAP … retype` is taken; the base and two RESUMEs (each prints `SENT … retype=1` at the resume stop) give `0fde36aac5dc2145`. Resumed runs continue the stop numbers (`stops=15342`, `15378`) and the `inh=` of their base runs.
- **Cost on this workload.** The default cadence gives 4–6 stops per run (engine `secs` 0.7–0.9, fingerprinting included); `rb=1` gives about 15,350 stops and 2.3 s, about 0.1 ms per stop with the Rust client writing a transcript.
- **Not done, and for the next steps.** The hvx-style `BRANCH` request (timing variants after a marker) on hvm is not done. SNAP for `tj=`/`pct=` schedules is refused: hvm could carry both exactly, but hvx refuses its timing tokens, so the protocol does too. The receive queue is not saved in a snapshot, although on hvm it could be; the protocol's `retype` stands in for it, as on hvx. A send that does not fit in the 4,096-byte receive queue at its time is truncated, with a message on stderr. No transcript files are committed (`tests/lockstep/` is the place A4 named). `hvm_lockstep_check` needs the images and the hypervisor, so it is a runnable check, not a cargo test. At the merge with `hvx-lockstep`, `src/lockstep.rs` is identical on both branches as of `255d769` (take A4's version if it changed since), and `process.rs` conflicts in one hunk (keep the lockstep method without the hvm refusal).

### Milestone 117 — DONE (the guest agent and its protocol: `hydo-agent-proto` version 1 with a generated schema, an additions-only check and permanent transcripts; `hydo-agent`, a static Rust PID 1 that only executes commands, byte-reproducible from a Mac and from Linux; the packet trigger proven in guests against hydo_fc; 2026-10-31)

Branch `guest-agent-2` (the start on `guest-agent`, `9cd6f64`, merged into it: its JSON codec, framing and field macros were kept). Steps A1–A3 of `docs/design/guest-control.md`. No change to `hvx.c`, `hvx_abi.h`, the module, `hvx_explore.c`, `serve.c`, `hvm.c`, any image, manifest or product command; the agent is not wired into `hydo-build` or the explorer.

- **The protocol (A1), `hydo/crates/hydo-agent-proto`** (workspace member, no dependencies, so the agent compiles the same code; README.md). Host lines: canonical JSON (keys sorted, integers only, `json.rs`) and `\n` on the serial input, envelope `v`, `id` (increasing), `op`. Agent lines: `HYDO-AG <len> <crc32> <json>` on the console (`frame.rs`), every one numbered by `seq` from 0 (the hello); a reply `re`, `op`, `ok: true` and the result's fields; a refusal `ok: false`, `err`, `msg` (and `re`/`op` when readable, `errno` for a system call); an event `ev`. Version 1 (`msg.rs`): commands `sync`, `spawn`, `signal`, `run`, `probe`, `write`, `read`, `mkdir`, `mount`, `syncfs`, `clock_set`, `clock_get`, `qlen`, `tail`, `untail`, `freeze`, `unfreeze`, each with its reply; events `hello` (proto, agent, ops, features, pid1), `exit`, `done`, `probe`, `line`, `froze`, `resumed`, `dropped`, `warn`; 14 error codes. Each record's encoder, decoder and schema come from one field list (`field.rs` macros), so they cannot drift. Decoding is strict for host lines (an unknown field, op or version is refused, never ignored) and lenient for agent lines (unknown fields ignored, an unknown event or code kept as such). The session (`session.rs`): `Session::from_hello` applies the version rule (the host reads every released version, `HOST_PROTOCOLS`, and refuses a newer agent: "this image's agent (hydo-agent 0.9.0) speaks agent protocol 2; this hydo (0.1.0) knows agent protocol 1..1; upgrade hydo"); `command` refuses an op or feature the hello did not list (a new optional command field comes with a feature name); `sync` is CAN + sync for the resynchronisation after a restore; `receive`/`console_line` check the numbering and pair every answer with its command; `position`/`resume_at` carry the numbers across a snapshot. Schema `hydo/schema/agent-v1.json` (draft 2020-12, 44 definitions: `command.*` closed, `reply.*`, `error`, `event.*` open; the root a choice of all) generated by `schema.rs`; `tests/schema.rs` fails on any difference (`HYDO_BLESS=1`), runs `hydo_results::compat::breaking` against `hydo/schema/released/agent-v1.json` (M117's; it caught the removal of an unused error code during the work, then both were re-blessed before the first commit of the final schema), shows a breaking and an additive change, and round-trips every kind with all fields and with required fields only, validated by the schema.
- **The agent (A2), `hydo/crates/hydo-agent`** (own workspace and lock file; std, libc 0.2.191 and the protocol crate). As PID 1 it mounts /dev (when /dev/null is missing), /proc, /sys, /tmp, runs /bin/hvx_seedrng (its pinned bytes unchanged), takes its console (`$HYDO_AGENT_TTY`, else `hydo.tty=`, else /dev/ttyS0) in raw mode without echo, says hello and serves; `hydo-agent serve [--root DIR]` serves on stdin/stdout for tests (paths it opens itself under DIR); installed as `hydo_fc` it is the freeze helper (below). One thread and one poll over the input, a SIGCHLD signalfd, inotify (tails), the netfilter queue and the output pipes of `run`; the only timeouts are deadlines from commands (`kill_after_ms`, a probe's schedule and deadline, a freeze's duration), so an idle agent sleeps with no timeout (a test checks it uses no CPU time). Fixed order in each round: queue, deadlines, pipes, exits, tails, input. Children get a new session, stdin /dev/null and exactly the given environment; process trees are found in /proc as hydo_fc does; orphans are reaped; no pid, wall time or host path appears in its output; errors name errno symbolically (`ENOENT`, not the C library's words).
- **Proofs of A2.** Native tests on the bare-metal machine (`~/hydo-ga2`, as the unprivileged user; `hydo/crates/hydo-agent/bare-metal.sh` from the Mac): six scenarios recorded as transcripts (`native-hello-sync-refusals`, `-files`, `-processes`, `-run-probe-qlen`, `-tail`, `-unprivileged`) and replayed twice each through a fresh agent, every agent line byte for byte equal to the recording — with the debug build and with the shipped static musl binary; `native-clock` (recorded once, its times differ per run); `pid1-namespace` (the agent as PID 1 of `sudo unshare --pid --fork --mount` on a pty: hello `pid1:true`, `/proc/1/comm` = hydo-agent, a tmpfs mount, an orphaned grandchild reaped so `zombies=0`, raw mode checked on the pty; replayed twice). The protocol crate's `tests/examples.rs` reads every transcript as the host would (session, numbering, pairing, canonical frames, every line valid by the committed schema, INDEX complete) and requires that together they show every op, reply, error code and event except the six listed (`froze`, `resumed`, `warn`, and the replies of `clock_set`, `freeze`, `unfreeze`: they need a netfilter queue or a guest; the bare-metal machine blocks unprivileged user namespaces). Static builds (`build.sh`, M113's recipe: `rustc-stable`, `hydo-elf-comment`): x86_64 665,632 bytes `ff7652a1…`, aarch64 564,768 bytes `6a3ea9f8…`, identical from this Mac, from the bare-metal machine and from a clean rebuild (docs/BUILD-PINS.md "hydo-agent").
- **The packet trigger (A3)**: `nfq.rs` (raw netlink netfilter queue, IPv4/TCP payload, the counter, hydo_fc's trace line), `tree.rs` (collect and all-stopped, hydo_fc's algorithm), used by the agent's `freeze`/`unfreeze` (SCHED_FIFO with SCHED_RESET_ON_FORK while armed, so services started later stay normal) and by `fc.rs`, hydo_fc.c's command line, output, trace file and markers. **Proof on the bare-metal machine** (main module, no reload; one VM at a time through `~/bin/hvx-run`; `hvx_explore` built from this tree; results and script `/var/tmp/m117-a3`): copies of `explore-ob-redis-fc-disk.img` with `/bin/hydo_fc` replaced by the agent (debugfs, mode and owner kept, `e2fsck -fn` clean), each schedule from a fresh boot on the original (C helper) and on the copy:

  | schedule | C hydo_fc | agent |
  |---|---|---|
  | redis `F=redis<workload@5#1:3000` | OK acked=19, `FROZE pid 95 (1 processes) at resp #1 (resp1, 48418>6379 len=30) …SET..k:5` | the same verdict and FROZE line |
  | redis `F=redis>workload@5#1:3000` | OK acked=19 | the same verdict and freeze lines |
  | redis `F=redis>workload@3#4:500` | OK acked=20, `FROZE … at req #4 (req4, 6379>48420 len=5) …+OK..` | the same, client port 48428 |
  | redis `F=redis<workload@2#0:100` (trace) | OK, 36 trace lines | the same lines apart from their times |

  Fingerprints differ (another `/bin/hydo_fc`, 665 KB against 68 KB, shifts guest timing by milliseconds), as the design expected; three agent schedules run twice gave the same fingerprint (`313a56f5a142bd92`, `efbfef3aba39a8e2`, `0c9eda6b5fd4a086`). **Found by the first guest run:** the netlink batch parser stepped past the end of a batch whose last message is not padded to 4 bytes (a panic, so the helper exited before the first packet); fixed with a pure, bounded `parse_batch` and a unit test.
- **Differences from the design.** The protocol crate has no serde: the agent is std + libc only, so the codec and the schema generator are written in the crate (the design said "no dependencies besides serde"). Replies carry `op` (self-describing lines and a discriminated schema). Transcripts live in `hydo/schema/examples/agent/v1/` (as the task asked) rather than the crate's `tests/transcripts/`. `run` and `probe` report their end as events (the agent keeps serving while they run). A repeated id is answered with a `duplicate-id` refusal rather than silence. The packet trigger arms by handle (the host's spawn), not by a pid file; hydo_fc's pid-file command line stays for today's images.
- **Not done / for wave 2** (`hydo/crates/hydo-agent-proto/HANDOFF.md`): the controller (B1, B2), `hydo-build --control agent` (B3), and booting an agent image at all — `hvx_explore` and `hvmx` wait for the shell init's S0/S1 markers before lock-step control starts; no transcript of the freeze events or of a successful `clock_set` yet. On the bare-metal machine, four root processes of the first PID-1 attempt (`sudo`/`timeout`/`unshare`/`hydo-agent`, pids 217992–217996) remain: `unshare --fork` ignores SIGTERM, so `timeout 20` never ended them; the test now uses `timeout -s KILL`. They sleep and use nothing; ending them needs `sudo kill -9 217995`, which this session was not allowed to run.

### Milestone 120 — DONE (the host controller for agent images, step B1: `hydo-control` with the `Controller` trait and a `ScheduleController` that drives today's schedules through hydo-agent's commands in the shell init's order; the control transcript with its hash and a replay; a scripted agent and engine and a shell model that check 1,986 runs of the explorer's identity corpus on 22 core manifests; 2026-10-31)

Branch `control-core` (from `main` = `1d2f4a7`, M117 merged). Step B1 of `docs/design/guest-control.md`. No VM ran. Nothing in the product calls the crate yet. No change to `hydo-build`, the engines, the module, any image, manifest, schedule or fingerprint. The crate's `HANDOFF.md` says what step C1 and wave 3 need.

- **The interface (`src/control.rs`).**
  - The trait: `trait Controller { fn name(&self) -> &str; fn step(&mut self, stop: &StopInfo, seen: &[Seen], out: &mut Out); }`.
  - The controller is called at every numbered stop. `StopInfo { n, at, why, seen }` gives the stop's number, its virtual time, why the engine stopped, and how many agent lines the session has read.
  - `Seen` is what the controller learns since the previous stop: the hello, a reply or refusal to command `id`, an agent event, an unknown event, other console text, or a broken line (an ERROR of the run).
  - The controller answers through `Out`: `send(by, cmd) -> id` (at this stop, or `send_at` a later virtual time), `report`, `note`, `snapshot`, `engine` (`EngineAction::DiskFaultsOff`, the shell's `go`), and `end`. An ending is `Ending::Verdict(line)`, `PowerCut { acked, failed }` or `AtSnapshot(name)`.
  - This is the design's `step(now, events) -> Vec<Action>` shape. The difference is that `Out` gives out the command ids, starting at the agent session's next id, so a controller never needs to know where the numbering stands. Every action carries `by`, the part of the controller that made it.
- **The core controller (`src/schedule.rs`, `src/plan.rs`).** `ScheduleController` does what `hydo/onboard/hydo-init.sh` does, in its order, with one Rust function per shell function under the same name:
  - It drives services (start order, setup, the log moved to `.log.old` on a restart, readiness through `probe` with `alive`, restarts of dead services), provisioning and `sync`, workload steps (busybox `timeout` kept inside the command), kills `K=`, timed kills `X=`, both pause forms `P=`, knobs, the periodic and final invariants with their HYDO-ASSERT records, the verdict, the power cut, and the heal path with its retry.
  - Its conversations follow today's serve protocol: `boot` (hello to S0 to S1), `run` (from S1), `recovery` (from S0, given the acked and failed ids) and `solo`.
  - The shell's background jobs (`periodic_loop`, `pause_timer`) are threads of `src/flow.rs`. That runtime runs each thread's straight-line code again over its recorded effects until it finishes (the replay technique of workflow engines), so every decision is a pure function of the schedule and the answers seen so far.
  - Report lines are the shell's console lines byte for byte. Notes are its `hydo-ob:` log lines, without the uptime.
  - `Plan::from_manifest` reads a validated manifest with manifest.sh's defaults. `Layout` holds the guest paths that agent images must keep.
  - The init extensions and fault kinds that are not driven yet are seams (`src/seams.rs`): liveness, clock (`T=`, clock_after_cut), history, freeze, buggify, fakes, error-logs, net-namespaces, composer, net-faults (`N=`/`O=`) and recovery-inputs. A manifest or schedule that needs one is refused with `Unsupported`, naming the seam, and `SEAM(<name>)` comments mark where its code goes.
- **The control transcript (`src/transcript.rs`, format 1).** It is one canonical JSON object per line:
  - a header with the controller, the conversation, the schedule, the cadence (`rb=<n>` or `default`) and where the conversation started (`boot`, `resume S1`);
  - a `stop` record (number, virtual time, why, agent lines seen) before the records of each stop at which the host acted;
  - `send` records (agent id, the requested time, the exact bytes, `by`), `ack` (the engine's send number), `report`, `note`, `snap`, `engine` and `end`.

  The hash (16 hex digits, the design's `ctl=`) covers everything except the notes. This answers M118's finding: the transcript records the cadence and the host's commands at each numbered stop, not only times and bytes. `ReplayController` types a transcript again. It checks each recorded stop's time and line count, ends with an ERROR verdict at the first difference, and leaves the runner's resynchronisation and acknowledgements to the runner. `src/runner.rs` drives one conversation over a `Link` (an engine in lock step):
  - it decodes the console through `hydo_agent_proto::Session`, with the version rule and the line numbering;
  - after a restore it sends the CAN byte and the `sync`;
  - it acknowledges a send at the stop where the agent's answer to it is seen (M118's snapshot rule);
  - it refuses ops the hello did not offer.

  `src/lockstep_link.rs` is the `Link` over `hydo_engine::lockstep::Lockstep`. **hydo-results:** `Run.control`, a list with one `Control` per conversation (conversation, controller, cadence, hash, sends, stops, transcript file), was added as an optional field. `hydo/schema/results-v1.json` was regenerated, and the additions-only check against the released schema passes.
- **Proofs.**
  - `tests/corpus.rs` reads every example manifest of the explorer's identity test. 22 are core; the other 20 name their seam (eventually invariants, `checks:`, `errors:`, `network: bridge`, fakes and proxies, freeze, composer plans).
  - Each core manifest boots on a scripted agent and engine (`tests/support/fake.rs`). The fake reads host lines strictly with `HostLine::decode`, as the real agent does. Its answers are pure functions of a salt and its state. Its world reaches the rare paths: crashes, readiness timeouts, failed setups, provisioning and knobs, an unmountable disk, invariants that hold, fail or cannot be evaluated, timed-out workload calls, failed and unknown outcomes. 23 boots were checked, one of them failing.
  - The schedules are those of the identity corpus (identity.rs's generators, option streams and per-seed flags, 40 seeds; `HYDO_CONTROL_FULL=1` uses 300), plus 11–14 per manifest written for the paths the explorer never draws for a manifest (X=, unknown services, a repeated letter, a knob at its default, unknown knobs, `C=0`, `C=<steps>`, `rb=1`). One schedule per guest part was kept; 3,903 others name their seam (clock 2,094, net-faults 1,431, buggify 378).
  - **1,986 runs** were made, 525 of them with a power cut and a recovery boot. Run verdicts: 777 OK, 592 VIOLATION, 92 ERROR. The tokens used: K= 1,068, P= 844, C= 525, X= 88, plus the knobs.
  - Every run and every recovery boot is checked against the **shell model** (`tests/support/model.rs`). The model is hydo-init.sh written again as blocking code, from the shell text and not from the controller. It parses the tokens with the shell's own `${x%@*}`-style cuts, and writes jesc, inv_detail, the failed ids and the clock text again, differently.
    - It checks the main sequence strictly in order, including that every answer the shell waits for came before the controller went on.
    - It checks each background job on its own, because its order against the main sequence depends on guest timing, in the shell too.
    - It reads shared state (alive, the first violated invariant, the records already printed) from the items before the point where the main sequence continues.
  - The model caught five deliberate mistakes in the controller: a wrong order at one point, a call not waited for, a wrong text escape, a cancelled checker that dropped answers already seen, and the last violated invariant instead of the first.
  - Every run's transcript is typed again by `ReplayController`, and the replay's transcript equals the policy run's.
  - Goldens: `tests/golden/corpus-quick.txt` (per manifest: the boots, the counts, and chunked SHA-256 of every command, report line and end) and six readable transcripts in `tests/golden/examples/`.
  - `tests/conversations.rs` covers solo mode against the model (88 runs), the determinism of two runs, the transcript file's round trip and hash, the results field, and the lock-step adapter over a scripted engine stream (the exact `SEND`, `CONT`, `ACK` and `END` lines).
  - `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. The corpus takes 22 s.
- **Decisions where the shell is ambiguous** (all 17 are in `hydo/crates/hydo-control/HANDOFF.md` and marked `AMBIGUOUS:` in the code):
  - The environment of every command is the kernel's HOME and TERM, the init's exports, and HYDO_SVC/HYDO_LOG of the last service started (the shell's export leaks). It is sorted, and the kernel's unknown command-line words are left out.
  - Standard input is /dev/null.
  - The readiness probe makes the same number of polls with another pacing.
  - A killed service counts as down once its exit is reported, and a restart waits for that exit; the shell's `kill -0` can still see a zombie.
  - The last lines of a failed setup's log are not printed.
  - A failed mount shows the agent's error text.
  - Invariant output is cut to its first 3,000 bytes.
  - A check still running when the checkers stop is ignored, while the answers seen up to that stop count.
  - Commands whose answer the shell ignores (mkdir, writes, signals) are not waited for.
  - X= gets the stack's kill_timer meaning: hydo-init.sh ignores it as an unknown knob, and the explorer never draws it for a manifest.
  - When a letter is repeated, the last token wins.
- **Not done / next.** C1 is the engine side:
  - the controlled boot phase (the other wave-2 agent builds it);
  - `DiskFaultsOff` and the power-cut hand-over in the engines (`LockstepLink` refuses both);
  - `control.jsonl`, `Run.control` and `ctl=` in runs, and `hydo repro --transcript`.

  Wave 3 is the eleven seams. Also open: a mid-run branch test (the controller is `Clone`, but nothing tests a branch), the full 300-seed corpus as a golden, and any agent image (B3) or real guest.

### Milestone 121 — DONE (agent images: `hydo build --control agent` stages hydo-agent as the guest's first process; a controlled boot phase in both engines, in which the host decides where S0 and S1 are; a Redis agent image booted, provisioned, snapshotted and driven from S1 and from a fresh boot to the same fingerprints on hvx and hvm; 2026-10-31)

Branch `agent-images` (from `1d2f4a7`, M117's merge), not merged. Step B3 of `docs/design/guest-control.md` plus the boot phase the engines needed for it (M117's HANDOFF item 7). No change to `hvx.c`, `hvx_abi.h` or the loaded module (`0799F1B8EE2A35600D94EB4`, no reload); every VM through `~/bin/hvx-run` from the own tree `~/hydo-ai` on the bare-metal machine, at most two at a time; image builds with `nice` and `flock ~/.hydo-imgbuild.lock`. B1 (`hydo-control`) was worked on in parallel by another agent and is not touched here.
- **The image (`hydo-build --control shell|agent`, `hydo/crates/hydo-build/src/agent.rs`; `hydo build` passes the flag through).** With `--control agent` the static agent is the first process: x86_64 `/sbin/init` (the switch_root initramfs execs it), arm64 `/init` (the kernel starts it; there is no shell shim before it, so the host waits for `/dev/vda2` itself). `/etc/hydo/control` = `agent 1` (`hydo_agent_proto::PROTO`). No `init.rs` splicing and no shell init; everything else (busybox, the project's files, the compiled manifest, the composer's files, the data disk) is staged as before, so the controller can read the manifest out of the image and services find their files. The binary comes from `HYDO_AGENT_BIN` / `HYDO_AGENT_BIN_ARM64` (default `<build dir>/hydo-agent`, `-arm64`; the CLI defaults to the release's `guest/hydo-agent`) and must have the pinned sha256 of docs/BUILD-PINS.md (constants `AGENT_SHA256_X86_64` `ff7652a1…`, `AGENT_SHA256_ARM64` `6a3ea9f8…`; `HYDO_AGENT_UNPINNED=1` stages another build with a warning). The default output name gets `-agent` (`explore-ob-redis-agent-disk.img`). `--print-init` refuses an agent image; `--check` is the same for both. The default stays `shell`, and a shell image is the same bytes.
- **Which images are agent images.** The engines do not read images: the host reads `/etc/hydo/control` (`hydo_engine::image::control` → `GuestControl::Shell` or `Agent { proto }`, through `debugfs` on x86_64 and the cpio on arm64, as the other embedded files) and asks for the controlled boot. A plain boot of an agent image now stops at the agent's first framed line (`HYDO-AG `, a third S0 marker that no shell image prints) with "the guest's first process is hydo-agent … boot it with --control boot" (1 s on hvx) instead of waiting for the S0 marker until the wall limit.
- **The boot-phase protocol, the same on both engines** (header comments of `hvx_explore.c` and `serve.c`, "Controlled boot"): `--control boot serve <kernel> <initramfs> [<disk>] <outdir> ["<boot schedule>"]` boots with ` quiet loglevel=1` added to the kernel command line (instead of hvm's `hydo_phase=serve`) and runs the M118/M119 lock-step protocol from the first instruction: `STOP boot at=0 n=1 phase=boot why=start`, then `cadence`/`send`/`exit` stops with `phase=boot` (the boot schedule's `rb=` is the cadence; its other tokens are not used). SNAP is allowed in the boot phase; the host names the points `S0` and `S1` (`SnapshotPoint::name`). END prints `RESULT boot fp= wfp= secs= stops= typed= inh= verdict=<the host's>` (the fingerprint at that stop), then `READY`. After it: `CTL <tag> <schedule>` restores the host's `S1`, arms the schedule's host part, types nothing (the guest part must be just `run`) and starts with `why=resume` at S1's stop number, as a RESUME does, continuing the boot's stop and event numbers, `typed=` and `inh=`; `RESUME <tag> <name>` works from any snapshot of the boot or of a CTL run (it continues as `phase=workload`); `RUN` and `BRANCH` are refused. `--control boot one … "<schedule>"` is the fresh-boot counterpart: the host's `SNAP S1` in the boot phase also arms the schedule's host part, and after the host's CONT the run goes on in `phase=workload` without another stop, so its stops, `typed=`, `inh=` and fingerprint are those of a CTL of the same schedule from that S1. hvx counts icount, hvm exits; markers are never looked for in an agent run.
- **hydo-engine.** `Engine::start_controlled(spec, boot, log) -> ControlledBoot` (`session()` is the boot's lock-step session, `ready()` reads READY and returns the `Worker`, whose `lockstep(Run{..})` is the CTL from the host's S1) and `Engine::one_controlled(spec, schedule, log) -> ControlledRun`, implemented by `Hvx` and `Hvm` (default: Unsupported); `lockstep::Phase::Boot`; `GuestControl`, `image::control`, `image::parse_control`. `hvx::ControlledOne` and `hvm::ControlledOne` are now one type, `ControlledRun` (process.rs). No existing caller changed.
- **The end-to-end check** (`hydo/crates/hydo-engine/examples/agent_boot_check.rs`, a scripted host over `hydo-agent-proto`'s `Session`; not the controller). On `examples/redis` built with `--control agent`: boot under control; at the stop where the hello is seen `SNAP S0` and `sync`; then a probe for `/dev/vda2`, `mount` it on `/data`, `run ip link set lo up`, `mkdir /data/redis`, `spawn` Redis, a probe of `redis-cli ping` (with `alive=redis`), `syncfs`, `SNAP S1`, END (serve). From S1 twice (CTL) and from a fresh boot twice (`one_controlled`): `sync`, `run redis-cli SET k:1 v1`, `run redis-cli GET k:1`, `read /etc/redis.conf`, `clock_set` (sec 1,800,000,000), `clock_get`, END with a verdict built from the answers. A RESUME from S0 provisions again and ENDs at the S1 point. Each reply is ACKed before the next snapshot. Rule used: a `sync` right after every SNAP of a snapshot point, in the straight run too, so a continuation and the straight run type the same bytes at the same stop. The host's state is cloned at S0 and S1 for the continuations.
  - **hvx** (the bare-metal machine, the PMU clock, `rb=16`): S0 at icount 820,484 (the hello's stop), S1 at 836,896; the boot `c24c475ea7a448ad` (22,619 stops, typed 8); the RESUME from S0 to the S1 point `c24c475ea7a448ad`; both runs from S1 and both fresh boots `8328c792aa149b20` (22,903 stops, typed 14, `inh=9eadf16b43963db9`), verdict `AGENT-E2E: OK … set=OK get=v1 conf=port_6379 clock_set=1800000000 clock_get=1800000000.002999544`. The same check ran twice with these values (`/var/tmp/m121/e2e-final`, `-final2`). At `rb=256`: S0 820,532, S1 837,771, boot and RESUME S0 `f0b91e48890448f4` (1,418 stops), workload from S1 and fresh `28b0e441681f3ee1` (1,438 stops). Before the clock steps were added, the same comparisons held with `b1fa129c6c94d8e5` (rb=16) and `dfd88c4238ecc413` (rb=256).
  - **hvm** (this Mac, `Image-explore`, `rb=64` exits): S0 at exit 2,368, S1 at 7,680; the boot and the RESUME from S0 `1a500744358512e2` (121 stops; also in a run before the clock steps were added); from S1 twice and fresh twice `f0d610541a5780ca` (164 stops, typed 14, `inh=2af602f9d184fe90`), `clock_get=1800000000.003914666`.
  - Six transcripts are committed in `hydo/crates/hydo-engine/tests/lockstep/` (`agent-boot-*`, `agent-s1-*`, `agent-one-*` for hvx at rb=256 and hvm); `tests/lockstep.rs` replays them through the client and checks that the boot starts at 0, that S0 is the hello's stop and that the CTL starts at S1's icount and stop number. They are also the first transcripts with a successful `clock_set` in a guest.
- **Cost.** hvx: the controlled boot to S1 with in-memory snapshots took 4.9 s at rb=16 (22,619 stops in about 1.3 s; shell images reach S1 in 4.1–4.7 s, M118's logs); with snapshot files on the bare-metal machine's disk the same boot took 20–26 s (two 1 GiB files). A workload run from S1 took 1.2 s. hvm: boot 1.0 s, workload 0.3 s.
- **Size of the C change.** `hvx_explore.c` 2,160 → 2,318 lines (+169/−11, 30 of them comments): the header section, `agent_boot`, `agent_boot_result`, `agent_guest_ok`, `ctl_find`, the S1 flag in `ctl_snap_cmd`/`run_until_any`, the serve and `one` dispatch, the guard. `serve.c` 978 → 1,115 (+158/−21, 28 comments): the same pieces, with `ctl_request`'s cadence parsing split out (`ctl_sched`) so a CTL can start from the host's S1. Both stay small because everything after the boot is M118/M119's code; by the language policy any further growth belongs to the Rust in-process engine.
- **Shell images and runs unchanged.** `cargo test --locked` on the workspace (the explorer's identity corpora and golden tests included), clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. On the bare-metal machine from `~/hydo-ai`: `deploy-metal.sh` ALL PASS (31 checks); both pinned reproducers through the new engine (`one`) `2403499c9a3f8419` (VIOLATION) and `f87130453609a5d6` (OK), the same schedule as a serve RUN `f87130453609a5d6` and as a CTL answered only with CONT `f87130453609a5d6` (18 stops); M118's `lockstep-metal.sh check` ALL PASS (18 groups). On this Mac with the new `hvmx`: the quickstart values `0f6aac764c64aac2`, `29fb0d55a5ab8101`, `f27a5cffb5d6fb47`, `19e3e8c9c2214a83` (each twice from serve; the first also from a fresh boot), and M119's `lockstep-check.sh` (every M116/M119 value, CTL = RUN). These ran with the final engines (the guard included), except deploy-metal, which does not use the engine runner.
- **Image bytes.** Shell images built by the new `hydo build` equal the recorded ones: x86_64 on the bare-metal machine with the Linux release's tools (M103's recipe), `redis` `c6a09428…`, `redis/hydo-hist` `2621d3ce…`, `redis-composed` `cfeb5cda…`, the release's Redis example `3529a0e0…` (M103's values); arm64 on this Mac from a release prefix, the quickstart Redis image `96f591d8…`/`9ddfc929…` (M119's) and the Redis history example `26e67eab…`/`ab08f785…`. Agent images, two builds each, byte-identical: x86_64 `explore-ob-redis-agent-disk.img` `53f09ccc7e643a1d…`; arm64 `explore-ob-redis-agent-arm64.cpio.gz` `dd6b64b86a56ae55…` with the data disk `9ddfc929…` (the shell image's: the same name-derived UUIDs).
- **For wave 3 (the controller, C1).** What a controller must do for an image is what the check's script does by hand: wait for the hello, SNAP S0, sync, provision with commands, SNAP S1, sync; and on a worker, CTL from S1 with the schedule's host part, sync first. Not done here: a power cut on an agent image (a guest `C=` cannot exist; the cut and the recovery VM from the host's S0 need a host command in both engines, for example a `CUT` at a stop that carries the flushed disk into a fresh VM restored from `S0`); host tokens in the boot phase other than `rb=`; `BRANCH` for agent images; several vCPUs under control from boot (not run); `hydo run`/`hydo explore` do not drive agent images (the engine now refuses them with the message above); the release build scripts do not ship `guest/hydo-agent` yet (both CLIs already default `HYDO_AGENT_BIN*` to it); the boot phase's cadence for a real controller (rb=16 gives the host a stop every 16 events, about 22,600 stops for this boot on hvx; at rb=256 1,418).

### Milestone 125 — DONE (the host controller for the fake outside world, step B2 for `fakes:`/`proxies:`: hydo-world started before the services, `H=` windows switched at step boundaries and healed once, the summary before the verdict, and the world carried across a power cut through the host instead of the acknowledged-ids line; 750 runs of the identity corpus, every `--sweep protocol` point and power-cut schedules on the two fakes manifests checked against a shell model of hydo-init-fakes.sh; 2026-10-31)

Branch `ctl-fakes` (from `main` = `883a866`, M120 merged). Step B2 of `docs/design/guest-control.md` for the fakes seam. No VM ran. Nothing in the product calls the controller yet. No change to `hydo-build`, `hydo-world`, the engines, any image, manifest, schedule or fingerprint. The crate's `HANDOFF.md` ("The fakes controller") has the details.

- **What the controller does (`hydo/crates/hydo-control/src/schedule/fakes.rs`).** It is `hydo/onboard/hydo-init-fakes.sh` driven through hydo-agent's commands, with one function per shell function. Each is called from the place in `schedule.rs` whose shell function the extension wraps, at the point where the wrapper runs. The edits in `schedule.rs` are one call per wrapped function, marked `SEAM(Fakes)`.
  - At the start of `start_all`, in every boot, it starts `hydo-world serve /etc/hydo/world.json` under the handle `fakes:world` with the shell's exact command text, and waits with one `probe` of `hydo-world ctl ping` (every 100 ms, 30 s, given up when the world exits). It then logs the number of endpoints, or prints the last 5 lines of `world.out` and ends with the shell's ERROR verdict.
  - `set_knob H` remembers each `H=` token whose target the world serves (the first one gets the `fault.protocol` declaration) and logs the others as ignored.
  - `step_range` cuts every range of steps at the windows' boundaries inside it, and before each piece switches the rules whose window ends or starts there (`ctl off <n>`, `ctl on <n> <token>`, the PROTOCOL FAULT log line and the `fault.protocol` record). A refused rule ends the run with the shell's ERROR verdict.
  - At the start of `restart_dead` (the end of fault injection without a cut) it heals every rule once (`ctl heal`).
  - Right after `failed_ids` at a power cut it freezes and dumps the world (`ctl dump` into `$H/world.dump`, then a `read`; a failed dump becomes `w:trunc`).
  - At the start of `final_verdict` it adds the world's summary to the report, one `hydo-world: ` line per line of `ctl summary`.
  - `Plan::world` (`PlanWorld`) holds manifest.sh's HYDO_WORLD and HYDO_WORLD_TARGETS. The plan no longer refuses `fakes:`/`proxies:`.
- **The carried world.** The `hydo-explore-acked:` report line still carries the dump, byte for byte as the shell printed it. The hand-over is a new field: `Ending::PowerCut { acked, failed, world }`, where `world` is the acked line's `w:` words and `acked` the other words. The transcript writes `world` only when it is not empty, so every earlier transcript reads back unchanged. The recovery conversation gets the world with `ScheduleController::recovery(..)?.with_world(&world)`, writes the shell's carry (the `w:` words of the acknowledged ids, then the world, then those of the failed ids) into `$H/world.carry` with `write` commands of at most 3,000 bytes each, keeps every `w:` word out of the id files, and starts the world with `--carry`.
  - The 3,584-byte limit of the recovery command line does not apply any more, because no command line carries the world.
  - The 3,000-byte limit of the carried records stays. It is hydo-world's own (`carryMax` in `world.go`; a longer world is dumped as `w:trunc` and every check then answers "cannot decide"), and hydo-world was not part of this task. The controller adds no limit of its own, so a hydo-world without `carryMax` (for example the Rust port on branch `port-world`) needs no controller change. Shell images keep the old behaviour, because nothing in them changed.
- **Proofs** (all on the Mac, no VM; `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass):
  - **The shell model** (`tests/support/model/fakes.rs`) is hydo-init-fakes.sh written again as blocking code from the shell text, with its files as fields. It is called from the core model's functions where the wrappers run, and in the recovery boot it reads the ids from the oracle line itself (`dst=$HYDO_ACKED; for id in ${CMD#oracle}`). The corpus now gives the recovery the oracle line the engine builds today from the run's report (`hvx_explore.c` `oracle_cmd`), and checks that the hand-over's acked ids and world are that line's words.
  - **The scripted world** (`tests/support/fake/world.rs`) answers `serve`, `--carry`, `ctl on|off|heal|dump|summary` as pure functions of the salt and its state. It reaches the rare paths: a world that cannot start, a refused rule, a world that dies after a rule (so a later dump fails and the heal fails), a dump that is too long (`w:trunc`), and a recovery whose world lists the carried records in its summary.
  - **The identity corpus** (`tests/corpus.rs`) now drives the two manifests M120 refused with the fakes seam, `examples/redis/hydo-proxy.yaml` and `examples/stack-grpc/hydo.yaml`. Each gets the identity corpus's schedules (with the explorer's protocol and gRPC fault streams), every point of the explorer's `--sweep protocol` with its per-point streams (60 and 300 points), the first 24 points again with a power cut while the rule is on, and 18 schedules written for the extension's other paths (unknown targets, empty and reversed windows, overlapping and repeated tokens, windows past the last step, faults together with kills, pauses, knobs and cuts, `C=0` and `C=<steps>`, `rb=1`). These were 750 runs (redis-proxy 273, stack-grpc 477) with 655 `H=` tokens; 135 had a power cut and a recovery boot. Every run and recovery was checked against the shell model, and every run's transcript typed again gave the same transcript. The core manifests' goldens are unchanged; `tests/golden/corpus-quick.txt` gained the two manifests (2,736 runs in all, 38 s).
  - **`tests/fakes.rs`** (9 tests):
    - `hydo-init-fakes.sh` is pinned by its sha256, so a change to the shell text fails the test until the model is looked at again. For every manifest with a fake world (also the shop and redis-bridge, which other seams still refuse), hydo-build's `--print-init` contains the extension and its `--print-shell` gives the plan's HYDO_WORLD and HYDO_WORLD_TARGETS.
    - The order of a window's switching and the single heal were checked, as were the carried world in the run, its hand-over, `world.carry`, the `--carry` start and the recovery's summary.
    - A carried world of 300 records (about 12 KB) was written into `world.carry` in pieces of at most 3,000 bytes.
    - The recovery transcripts replay to themselves, the same check as for the runs.
    - All nine rare paths were reached and checked against the model.
    - The shop's fakes (5 targets, with webhook rules) ran with its `eventually` invariants taken out, 20 runs. This says nothing about the shop manifest as a whole.
    - Three readable transcripts are in `tests/golden/fakes/`.
  - **Deliberate mistakes.** 14 conversations changed as a mistaken controller would produce them were each rejected by the model with the place it differs. The mistakes were a rule switched on after its step started, a changed token, a missing off, a missing heal, an uncut range, a missing summary, a summary not waited for, the world started after the services, the dump missing from the acked line, the hand-over without its world, the dump before the failed ids, a carried record written into the acked ids, a carried record lost, and the recovery's world started without its carry. Six mistakes were also made in the controller's code, one at a time, and reverted:
    - a heal at every `restart_dead`;
    - window boundaries counted at the range ends (caught on a window that ends at the last step, which the shell never switches off before the heal);
    - the world left among the acked ids in the hand-over;
    - the declaration printed for every token;
    - a wrong summary prefix;
    - carried records written into the id files.

    The corpus caught the first five. The sixth was caught only by `tests/fakes.rs`, because in the corpus the hand-over never puts records among the ids.
- **Decisions where the shell is ambiguous** (12, in HANDOFF.md and marked `AMBIGUOUS:` in the code):
  - The readiness is one probe instead of 300 pings.
  - `grep -c`, `tail`, `head` and `wc` run on the host over a `read`.
  - When ctl cannot reach the world, the ERROR verdict of a refused rule contains ctl's stderr.
  - The dump and the summary go through files, so no output limit applies.
  - At a cut the dump stays on the host and is not appended to the guest's acked file, because nothing reads that file after the cut.
  - The hand-over splits off the `w:` words.
  - The id files of the recovery never get a `w:` word.
  - The recovery's log line has the records after the ids.
  - The summary lines are report lines.
  - The processes are named `fakes:world`, `fakes:dump` and `fakes:summary`.
  - M120's environment decision also covers these commands.
  - `ctl off` and `ctl heal` are waited for.

  HANDOFF.md also gives the order of the fakes wrappers against the other extensions, for whoever merges another seam. For example, with `guest.clock_after_cut` the shell's acked line at a cut is the ids, then `clock=…`, then the `w:` records.
- **Not done / next.** The manifests with fakes and another feature (shop and redis-bridge, which use liveness; redis-bridge also uses network namespaces) stay refused until those seams are merged. Then the combined order above must be checked against the model. The controller has no architecture-specific part, and arm64 images stage hydo-world at the same paths (M96), but the only Mac manifest with fakes (`examples-mac/redis-bridge`) is refused by the liveness seam, so no arm64 run was made. C1 must pass `Ending::PowerCut::world` to `with_world`. No agent image or real guest has met this controller yet.

### Milestone 124 — DONE (the host controllers for network faults, the freeze at a packet and service networks, step B2 for the net-faults, freeze and net-namespaces seams: `N=`/`O=` on a port or a link with the M71 drain and heal, `F=` through the agent's packet trigger, `network: bridge` set up before S0; 4,042 runs of the identity corpus and 446 written, variant and freeze-sweep runs checked against a shell model of the four shell files; 2026-10-31)

Branch `ctl-net` (from `main` = `883a866`, M120; `main` = `221befe`, with M121 and M125, merged in before the end). Step B2 of `docs/design/guest-control.md` for three seams. No VM ran. Nothing in the product calls the controller yet. No change to `hydo-build`, the agent, the engines, any image, manifest, schedule or fingerprint. The crate's `HANDOFF.md` ("Network faults, the freeze and service networks") has the details.

- **What the controllers do.** Each is a module beside `src/schedule/fakes.rs`, called from its `SEAM` comment in `schedule.rs` at the place where the shell function it replaces runs:
  - `src/schedule/netfault.rs` (NET-FAULTS) is explore_run's `N=`/`O=` lines with hydo-init.sh's `net_on`/`net_heal`, hydo-init-links.sh's links (`a-b`, `a-*`) and hydo-init-netns.sh's netem on the veths and in a service's namespace. The `tc` invocations are the shell's, in its order, through `run`. The drain polls the netem queue with the agent's `qlen` (in a service's namespace, a `tc -s qdisc show` there and the shell's awk on the host), with `sleep 0.01` of guest time between polls, up to the largest delay + 500 ms and then up to 50 ms after the filters are gone. The heal lines and the `fault.oneway_*` records are the shell's.
  - `src/schedule/freeze.rs` (FREEZE) reads `F=` in token order among the knobs, prints the `fault.freeze_call` declaration at the first step range of a boot, and arms before the step: the netfilter modules, `XTABLES_LOCKFILE` exported, the agent's `freeze` with hydo_fc's arguments as its fields, then the pinned iptables rules through `run`. The heal (at the first `restart_dead`) waits for a running freeze to end, removes the rules, stops the trigger with `unfreeze`, continues a service it left stopped, and logs "freeze healed" or the "never fired" count with the `#0` trace. At a power cut and in die_oracle the trigger is stopped before the checkers. A thread reports hydo_fc's FROZE, RESUMED and warning lines from the agent's events.
  - `src/schedule/netns.rs` (NET-NAMESPACES) runs ns_setup (the bridge hydo0, one namespace and veth pair per service, IPv6 off, the log line) between the phase line and the declarations, before S0, and puts start_svc's setup, command and readiness check into the service's namespace.
  - `Plan` gained `freeze`, `bridge`, `net_extra` and each service's `addr`. `Layout` gained the pinned tools `tc`, `ip` and `iptables`, filled with hydo-build's `--print-shell` placeholders when the fault kinds need them. Step C1 must give the image's real paths. `Facts::events` keeps the agent's other events in order.
- **The order against the fakes controller (M125).** As hydo-build splices them, the fakes wrappers run outside freeze's: the fakes split of `step_range` calls freeze's wrapper for each piece, `set_knob` tries `H` before `F`, and `restart_dead` heals the fakes before the freeze. In the merge the freeze's heal moved into `restart_dead`, right after the fakes heal.
- **Proof** (on the Mac, `cargo test -p hydo-control --locked`, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean):
  - The shell model got a network part, `tests/support/model/net.rs`, written from hydo-init.sh, hydo-init-links.sh, hydo-init-freeze.sh and hydo-init-netns.sh with the shell's variables as strings and its expansions spelled out. ### Milestone 122 — DONE (guest control, step B2 for four seams: the host controller drives `eventually` invariants, the `T=` clock steps, `guest.clock_after_cut`, `B=` BUGGIFY and the power cut's recovery inputs; after the merges of main (M121, M124, M125, M126), 3,609 feature runs and 9,839 runs of the identity corpus checked against a shell model of the extensions; 2026-10-31)

Branch `ctl-liveness-clock` (from `main` = `883a866`, M120 merged). Part of step B2 of `docs/design/guest-control.md`; three other agents build the other feature controllers in parallel, and one builds the agent images and the controlled boot (M121). No VM ran. Nothing in the product calls the controller yet. No change to `hydo-build`, the engines, the module, any image, manifest, schedule or fingerprint.

- **Where the code is.** Each feature is a module in `hydo/crates/hydo-control/src/features/`, declared with `#[path]` as a child of `schedule`. A child module can use the private helpers of `schedule.rs`, so no visibility had to change. Each feature is called from its `SEAM(<name>)` place in `schedule.rs` with a one-line hook, so that the other wave-3 branches merge with few conflicts.
- **Liveness (`features/liveness.rs`, replaces `hydo/onboard/hydo-liveness.sh`).**
  - The shell extension wraps four init functions. The controller has one hook for each: the `start` anchor after start_periodic; the `heal` anchor after the step_range that ends at the last step (also for an empty range, as the shell's wrapper does); both anchors before start_all in the recovery boot; and live_resolve before finish.
  - An anchor reads the uptime once and starts one monitor per `eventually` invariant anchored there. A monitor is a thread of the flow runtime (`live:i<k>`). It runs the check under busybox `timeout <within+1>`, reads the uptime, and stops with `ok`, `late` (it held, but after the deadline) or `expired`; otherwise it sleeps `poll` seconds and tries again.
  - live_resolve waits for each monitor in manifest order, appends the shell's "satisfied …" or "not satisfied …" line to the check's output, prints one `HYDO-ASSERT` eventually record with `after`, `elapsed_s`, `out` and `within_s`, logs the result, and makes the first record that is not ok the violated invariant, unless another invariant was violated before.
  - The agent's `probe` op is not used for the monitor. A probe kills an attempt at the deadline and reports neither the elapsed time nor the output, so it cannot give the shell's `late` outcome or its details.
- **Clock (`features/clock.rs`).**
  - `T=<at>:<delta>` is part of hydo-init.sh itself. Before step `at` the controller reads the clock, sets it to that second plus delta, takes the new time from the `clock_set` reply (or from a `clock_get` when the set was refused), logs the jump, ends the run with `ERROR clock jump not applied` when the clock is more than 5 s off the request, and prints the `fault.clock_back` or `fault.clock_fwd` record.
  - `guest.clock_after_cut` (replaces `hydo-init-clock.sh`): at a power cut the controller reads the clock after failed_ids. The acked report line shows `clock=<epoch>` after the ids, byte for byte as the shell printed it. The recovery conversation sets its clock to that epoch plus clock_after_cut seconds before it mounts the data disk, and falls back to guest.clock_start when no epoch came, as the shell does for a missing token.
- **BUGGIFY (`features/buggify.rs`, replaces `hydo-init-buggify.sh`).** With `buggify: true`, `B=` is one `write` of its value and a newline to `/tmp/hydo-buggify` with mode 0644, at the knob's place in the token order. Without `buggify: true`, `B=` stays an unknown knob.
- **The recovery inputs (`features/recovery.rs`).** `RecoveryInputs { acked, failed, clock, world }` is what a power cut hands to the recovery conversation. `ScheduleController::recovery_inputs()` gives it after a run that ended with a power cut, and `ScheduleController::recovery_from(plan, &inputs, s0)` starts the recovery conversation with it. The values go from controller to controller as fields, so nothing has to fit into the engine's 3,584-byte oracle line. The ids lists hold ids only. `world` is the fake world's records of M125 (`Ending::PowerCut`'s `world`), which `recovery_from` passes on with `with_world`.
- **Manifests that the controller now accepts.** `Plan::from_manifest` no longer refuses `eventually` invariants, and `T=`, `B=` and `C=` with clock_after_cut are no longer refused. `redis/hydo-live.yaml` and `compose-voting/hydo-loopback.yaml` are now core manifests. The other manifests with `eventually` invariants are refused because of another seam (network namespaces for compose-voting and redis-bridge, fakes for shop). No example manifest sets `guest.clock_after_cut`, so the tests add it to copies of the plans.
- **The shell model (`tests/support/model_features.rs`).** The four features were written again as blocking code from the shell text, not from the controller: the monitor loop with awk's floating-point arithmetic, `/proc/uptime`'s text, the shell's `${T%%:*}` cuts, `date`, and the recovery's `sed -n 's/^clock=//p' | tail -1`. Each monitor is checked on its own, as the periodic checkers are, and live_resolve in the main sequence must come after the monitor's last answer. The recovery's oracle command for the model is built from the run's report lines, as hvx_explore's oracle_cmd builds it, so that the model checks what the controller carried.
- **The scripted agent (`tests/support/fake.rs`).** It now keeps a running realtime clock and an uptime (25 ms per unit of virtual time). It refuses a clock change to a time before 1970, and now and then a later clock change of a boot. It answers an `eventually` check the way a system that settles does: a few attempts fail first, one check in seven never holds, some attempts succeed only after the deadline, and some hang until the timeout ends them (status 143). For the M120 core runs these changes are inert.
- **Proofs.**
  - **The M120 runs are unchanged.** Each of the 1,986 M120 runs gives a byte-identical transcript (notes included) under the new controller and the new scripted agent. This was checked run by run against the M120 code.
  - Before the merge of main, `tests/corpus.rs` made 4,689 runs, because `T=` and `B=` schedules are no longer refused and two more manifests are core. Every run and recovery boot is checked against the shell model, and every run's transcript, typed again, gives the same transcript. The golden `corpus-quick.txt` was re-recorded. Each wave-3 branch changes this golden, so it has to be recorded once more after the merges.
  - Before the merge of main, `tests/features.rs` made 2,402 runs on ten plans: the liveness and BUGGIFY manifests, and copies with clock_after_cut, with a second eventually invariant anchored at `start` or at `heal`, and with zero steps. The schedules are the identity corpus streams (40 seeds) plus 16 written for these features. Every run and every recovery boot is checked against the shell model, and both transcripts are typed again by the ReplayController and must equal the policy's. Each of 27 feature paths must be reached; for example, a late result was reached 215 times in runs and 48 times in recovery boots, a refused clock change 85 times, and the recovery clock 145 times. The golden is `features-quick.txt`.
  - The model refused all 15 kinds of deliberate mistakes that the second test of `tests/features.rs` makes in recorded conversations. Examples are a wrong elapsed time, a late result counted as satisfied, a monitor with a later environment, a record printed before its monitor ended, `T=` stepped instead of set, a skipped 5 s check, the BUGGIFY file without its newline or in the wrong place, the acked line without the clock, and the clock written among the recovered ids.
  - Nine deliberate mistakes in the controller itself were run once and reverted, and the tests caught every one: the monitor's environment taken at each command, live_resolve not waiting, the heal anchor before the last step, `<` instead of `<=` for late, `T=` as a step, a 50 s bound instead of 5 s, the clock at the cut not carried, the recovery clock set after the mount, and `B=` written without `buggify: true`. The lost carried clock was caught by the model only after the oracle command was built from the report; before that, only an explicit assertion caught it.
  - `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- **Decisions where the shell is ambiguous** (18–24, in the crate's `HANDOFF.md`):
  - The monitor runs the shell's loop instead of a probe.
  - The uptime is the agent's CLOCK_MONOTONIC, shown in hundredths as /proc/uptime shows it.
  - A monitor keeps the environment of the moment its anchor was reached, as the shell's forked subshell does.
  - The monitors' files stay on the host, and a check's output is kept to 3,000 bytes.
  - `T=` takes the new time from the `clock_set` reply and sets an absolute second, as `date -s @` does.
  - The clock at a cut is not written into the guest's acked file, but the acked line shows it, and the ids lists never contain it.
  - `B=` is one write with mode 0644, not waited for.
- **Found, not changed (core).** M120's periodic checkers build their environment when each command is sent, while the shell's checker keeps the environment of the moment it was started. The two differ after a `K=` restart of a service other than the last one started. The core model does not check the periodic checker's environment. This is in the core's scope and was left for the merge of wave 3 (HANDOFF.md decision 20).
- **The order against the other extensions** (for the merge, in `HANDOFF.md`): history's `final:` read-backs come before live_resolve; history's declarations come after the `start` anchor; the fake world starts before the recovery boot's anchors; the `heal` anchor stays innermost in step_range; and the fake world's `w:` lines come after `clock=` in the acked line.
- **Merged with main (M121 agent images, M125 the fakes controller) before the end.** The hooks of both features sit in the shell's order: the world starts before the recovery boot's anchors; the fakes split a range of steps and call the liveness-wrapped step_range per piece, so only the piece that ends at the last step stamps `heal`; `H=` is checked before `B=` in set_knob; at a cut the controller reads the clock, then dumps the world, and the acked line is the ids, then `clock=`, then the `w:` records; the recovery's `command:` note has the same order. `RecoveryInputs` gained `world`. The model of the fakes oracle loop also leaves `clock=` out of the written ids. `shop/hydo.yaml` (fakes and `eventually` invariants) is now core, and its 279 written and 195 identity schedules pass the combined model. `tests/features.rs` gained a variant of the shop with clock_after_cut, and a path that requires the world's records after `clock=` on the acked line (reached 56 times). After the merge `tests/corpus.rs` makes 6,135 runs (1,270 recovery boots) and `tests/features.rs` 2,611 (588); both goldens were re-recorded, and the features golden only gained lines (the shop variant and the path counts).
- **Merged with main again (M124 network faults, freeze and service networks; M126 the C1 wiring) before the end.** In explore_run `T=` is read before `O=` and its step comes after the pause, as in the shell; in set_knob `H=` comes first, then `B=`, then `F=`; the `heal` anchor sits in hydo-init.sh's own step_range, inside freeze's wrapper and the fakes split. Every manifest that uses these features is now driven: redis-bridge (both copies: fakes, a bridge and an `eventually` check), the voting app's three bridge manifests and the shop; only 191 schedules with `F=` on a bridge are still refused (M124's own refusal). `tests/features.rs` gained redis-bridge and a redis-bridge copy with clock_after_cut. For C1, `RecoveryInputs::from_transcript` reads the hand-over from a run's transcript (the ending's ids and world, the `clock=` of the acked line), `drive::run` uses it with `recovery_from`, so a recovery after a run typed again from its transcript gets the same clock, and `tests/features.rs` checks that it equals the controller's own `recovery_inputs()` on every power cut. The explorer no longer leaves clock faults out of an agent image's space and no longer refuses `--buggify` on agent images (`hydo-explore/src/run.rs`, `agent_space`). After the last merge `tests/corpus.rs` makes 9,839 runs (2,390 recovery boots) and `tests/features.rs` 3,609 (896) on thirteen plans; the world's records came after `clock=` on 118 acked lines.
- **Not done.** No agent image or real guest has run these features (C2). The full 300-seed corpus was not recorded as a golden.
