Agent triggers (README "The triggers on the manifest images"), each twice identical: d9 `Q=3`, d10 `X=front@9~20`, d11 `cf=260`, the others unchanged; the control's known bug (order 26 twice) remains with v1.22.2. `P=kafka@14+16` passes on the agent control (`a41a29598b2738ea`).
- **The lost order after a long Kafka pause (M133, branch `lost-order`):** M129's agent-only difference is a real bug of the order service's Kafka client, not of the controller. franz-go v1.17.1 (`hydo/stack/go.mod`) fails a batch the broker had already appended (its records are older than `RecordDeliveryTimeout` when a retriable error arrives just after Kafka is continued), rewinds the partition's sequence under the same producer id and epoch, and the next single-record produce gets the old batch's sequence: the broker answers it as a duplicate, stores nothing, and the order service acknowledges an order Kafka does not have. franz-go fixed it in v1.22.2 (issue 1484: the epoch is bumped when a sent batch is failed). Evidence from diagnostic image copies (`hydo/bench/kafka-diag.sh`: Kafka's batches with producer id, epoch and sequence): on the agent control image sequence 14 is order 14 and sequence 15 is order 16, with no record of order 15; on the shell image every order has its own sequence. The control order service rebuilt with franz-go v1.17.1 fails the same way on the agent image, rebuilt with v1.22.2 it passes. Minimal schedule `disk=none dseed=0 | run P=kafka@14+16` on the agent control image (`c4a120cca428aa48`); shorter pauses pass; shell images pass it with tick jitter, a shorter tick period and inserted ticks (14 runs), and so does the original stack-explore control image. `docs/C2-BENCH.md` section 6 item 4, docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 133".
- **The bug benchmark on agent images (M129, step C2 for the benchmark; branch `c2-bench`):** the benchmark's own images (and every `explore-*` stack image, the pinned reproducers' included) cannot run under the agent: their init is `build-stack.sh`'s with `stack-explore.sh`, they carry no manifest, and the controller drives manifests (`hydo-explore` and hydo-bench now refuse such an agent image with the controller's message instead of failing every worker). `hydo/bench/manifest/hydo.yaml` is the benchmark guest as a manifest (the `-pin-kr` control image's files and configuration; `Q=` and `M=` as knobs, the oracle and the M59 crash oracle as invariants); `hydo/bench/build-bench-manifest.sh` builds a shell and an agent image of each defect on the bare-metal machine with the Linux release's tools (no Nix), `hydo/bench/agent-patch.sh` patches or swaps files of a copy and compares image trees (a patched shell image equals the built agent image; a swapped order service equals a full build), `hydo/bench/c2-cells.sh` runs hydo-bench plans on both kinds (`hydo/bench/c2-plans/`); hydo-bench drives agent images through `AgentEngine`. On M108's cells (same cells, seeds and budgets) the agent images find every defect at the same schedule as the original images (d1 2, d5 3, d8 5, d12 5, d10 7, d11 none); the manifest's shell images miss d10 because the generic shell init ignores `X=` (the controller gives it the stack's meaning). Three repetitions: d1, d5, d8, d12 found identically on both kinds; d10 0/3 shell, 2/3 agent; d11 1/3 shell, 0/3 agent (its cut window is a few flushes apart: 8 of 61 cut points fail on the shell kind, 9 on the agent kind). Every trigger of d0–d12 and the pinned reproducer's schedule (order 11) confirmed on both kinds except where a trigger moved (d9 crashes on 6 of 18 `Q=` runs shell, 15 of 18 agent; d10's `X=` trigger fails on the agent kind only; d11's `cf=238` passes on both). One agent-only difference, an acknowledged order missing from Kafka after a long Kafka pause, also on the control (`P=kafka@14+16`), is explained by M133 (next item). Tables and classifications: `docs/C2-BENCH.md`.
- **Agent images run end to end (M126, step C1; branch `control-wiring`):** both engines take two more host lines at a stop of an agent image's workload phase: `DISKOFF` (the workload's end: wfp, disk and timing faults off, then `phase=check`; a `cf=` schedule's answer is `cut=1` and the run goes into the recovery VM) and `CUT` (a power cut: the flushed data disk into a VM restored from the host's S0, `phase=recovery`); `hvx_explore.c` +40/−7, `serve.c` +33/−5. hydo-engine: `Driver`, `Worker::run_controlled`/`resume`, `Lockstep::diskoff`/`cut`. hydo-control: `Link::cut`/`engine_cut`, `Start::Here`, `drive` (boot, run, recovery with the carried world, a fresh boot's run; by policy or by transcript), `agent::AgentEngine`/`AgentWorker` (the engine interface for an image whose `/etc/hydo/control` says `agent`; tc/ip/iptables paths from its `manifest.sh`; cadence `rb=16` hvx, `rb=64` hvm, another `rb=` refused). A run leaves `<tag>.log` = its report lines (every console reader works unchanged), `<tag>.agent.log` = the agent's console, and the transcripts (`<tag>.control.jsonl`, `.control.recovery.jsonl`; a `hydo run` directory: `control.boot.jsonl`, `control.jsonl`, `control.recovery.jsonl`); the RESULT gets `ctl=`, the results `fingerprints.ctl` and `Run.control`. `hydo-explore`, `hydo run`, `hydo repro` and `hydo repro --transcript <control.jsonl>` drive agent images; the explorer leaves clock faults out of an agent image's space (the last fault seam). The release scripts build `guest/hydo-agent`. On the Redis example (hvx and hvm) clean, `K=`, `P=` and `C=12` with `R=everysec`/`R=always` give the shell image's verdicts, each agent run twice identical (hvx clean `f3fd12cdce944116`, `R=everysec` cut VIOLATION `d9d681b86845259e`; hvm `531838620cce7fb4`, `bf6afd74642bf703`); transcript replay and policy replay reproduce the fingerprints; swarm explorations find and shrink the shell image's failure classes (`lying-disk`, `unsafe-knob`). Shell images unchanged (deploy-metal ALL PASS, both pinned reproducers, M118/M119/M121 checks, the Mac quickstart values). docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 126".
- `docs/design/guest-control.md` is the proposed design (not yet reviewed by the user) for replacing `hydo-init.sh` and its spliced extensions: `hydo-agent` (Rust, PID 1, primitives only) in the guest, `hydo-control` on the host, commands on the serial input at exact virtual times (Phase 1, no module change), a host-call port later (Phase 2, side module first). The implementation plan (steps A1–D2) is at the end of that file. Experiment code: `hv/guest-control-exp/`. Measured: timed input is reproducible on both engines; host input not yet in the guest is in no snapshot, so the engine must re-type it after a restore; the stop cadence decides how late the host sees a guest line.
- **Lock-step control on hvx (M118, step A4):** `hvx_explore` answers `CTL <tag> <schedule>` (a RUN that stops at every return of a run call and waits for the host), `RESUME <tag> <snapshot>` and `--control one`; at a stop it reports `EVENT` (complete console lines), `SENT`, `DROP` and `STOP`, and takes `SEND at=<icount> <bytes>`, `ACK`, `SNAP <name> [retype]`, `CONT` and `END [<verdict>]` (the protocol and real examples are in `hvx_explore.c`'s header). A send is typed at the first stop with icount ≥ at, because run calls are capped so that none runs past it; the schedule's `rb=` is the cadence; SNAP is refused while a typed send is unacknowledged unless `retype` makes RESUME type it again. Typed client: `hydo-engine`'s `lockstep` module (`Worker::lockstep`, `Hvx::one_lockstep`; no controller logic). Check on the bare-metal machine: `hv/hvx/lockstep-metal.sh check` (18 groups, M116's values reproduced) and `… cost <image> "<schedule>" <rb>...`; transcripts in `hydo/crates/hydo-engine/tests/lockstep/`. Inert when unused (deploy-metal ALL PASS, both pinned reproducers). Stopping at every event (`rb=1`) about doubles a stack run (4.8 s → 9.2 s; with a power cut 12.4 s → 24.1 s); `rb=16` costs 0–10 %. **Found:** the guest depends on where run calls return (Linux's `irq_randomness` differs), so a run is defined by its cadence and the host's commands at each numbered stop, not by (icount, bytes) alone; at `rb=1` the two agree.
- **Lock-step control on the Mac (M119, step A5):** `hvmx` speaks the lock-step protocol of `hvx_explore` (M118): `CTL <tag> <schedule>`, `RESUME <tag> <snapshot>`, `hvmx --control one`; engine lines `EVENT`/`SENT`/`DROP`/`STOP … phase= why=`, host lines `SEND at=`/`ACK`/`SNAP [retype]`/`CONT`/`END`, RESULT extras `stops= typed= inh=`. The clock is the exit count; a queued send is typed at its exact exit; the schedule's `rb=<n>` is the cadence (default 65,536 exits). hydo-engine uses M118's client unchanged (`src/lockstep.rs`), plus `Hvm::one_lockstep`. Inert without the new requests (the quickstart and M99 values hold); a CTL whose host only answers CONT gives RUN's fingerprint. `hv/hvm/explore/lockstep-check.sh` (`hydo-engine/examples/hvm_lockstep_check.rs`) reproduces every timed value of M116's Mac table and proves mid-run branches with typed input (SNAP, RESUME) on the Mac.
- **Agent images and their controlled boot (M121, step B3; branch `agent-images`):** `hydo build --control agent` (`hydo-build --control shell|agent`, `hydo/crates/hydo-build/src/agent.rs`) stages the pinned agent (sha256 checked against docs/BUILD-PINS.md; `HYDO_AGENT_BIN`/`HYDO_AGENT_BIN_ARM64`) as the first process (x86_64 `/sbin/init`, arm64 `/init`), writes `/etc/hydo/control` = `agent 1`, splices nothing, and names the image `explore-ob-<name>-agent`; shell images stay the same bytes. The host reads the file (`hydo_engine::image::control`) and boots such an image with `--control boot serve|one` (`Engine::start_controlled` → `ControlledBoot`, `Engine::one_controlled` → `ControlledRun`): lock-step control from the first instruction (`STOP boot at=0 n=1 phase=boot why=start`, the boot schedule's `rb=` as cadence, ` quiet loglevel=1` on the kernel command line), the host takes `SNAP S0` and `SNAP S1` where it decides and ENDs the boot (`RESULT boot`, then READY); a worker's `CTL` restores that S1, arms the host part, types nothing (guest part `run`) and starts with `why=resume` at S1's stop number; in `one`, the host's `SNAP S1` arms the host part and starts the workload at that stop. RUN and BRANCH are refused for agent images; a plain boot of one stops at the agent's first line with a message. Check: `hydo/crates/hydo-engine/examples/agent_boot_check.rs` (a scripted host: hello → S0 → mount, `lo`, spawn Redis, probe, syncfs → S1 → SET, GET, read, clock_set, clock_get); on `examples/redis` hvx (rb=16) boot `c24c475ea7a448ad`, from S1 twice and from a fresh boot twice `8328c792aa149b20`, hvm (rb=64) boot `1a500744358512e2`, workload `f0d610541a5780ca`; a RESUME from S0 to the S1 point gives the boot's value. Transcripts `hydo-engine/tests/lockstep/agent-*.txt`. The C change: `hvx_explore.c` +169/−11, `serve.c` +158/−21 lines.
- **The agent and its protocol (M117, steps A1–A3):** `hydo/crates/hydo-agent-proto` (workspace member, no dependencies; README.md) defines protocol version 1: host lines are canonical JSON + `\n` on the serial input (`v`, `id`, `op`), agent lines are framed `HYDO-AG <len> <crc32> <json>` (`seq` from 0; replies `re`/`op`/`ok`, refusals `err`/`msg`, events `ev`). Ops: sync, spawn, signal, run, probe, write, read, mkdir, mount, syncfs, clock_set, clock_get, qlen, tail, untail, freeze, unfreeze; events: hello, exit, done, probe, line, froze, resumed, dropped, warn. `Session` is the host side (version rule: the host reads every released version and refuses a newer agent with a message naming both). Schema `hydo/schema/agent-v1.json` (generated; `tests/schema.rs` also checks it only grew from `hydo/schema/released/agent-v1.json`); transcripts `hydo/schema/examples/agent/v1/` (8, INDEX). `hydo/crates/hydo-agent` (own workspace; std + libc) is the PID 1 program: one thread, one poll, no timers except the deadlines commands give; as `/bin/hydo_fc` it is hydo_fc.c's helper. Native tests on Linux: `hydo/crates/hydo-agent/bare-metal.sh` (replays every native transcript twice byte for byte; `-- cargo test --locked -- --ignored` adds PID 1 in a private PID and mount namespace, needs `sudo -n`). Static builds `build.sh` (M113's recipe): x86_64 `ff7652a1…`, aarch64 `6a3ea9f8…`, the same from the Mac and from Linux (docs/BUILD-PINS.md). In copies of `explore-ob-redis-fc` with the agent as `/bin/hydo_fc`, four `F=` schedules give hydo_fc's verdicts and FROZE lines; results `/var/tmp/m117-a3` on the bare-metal machine.
- **The host controller (M120, step B1; branch `control-core`, not merged):** `hydo/crates/hydo-control` (workspace member).
  - **The interface:** `Controller::step(&mut self, stop: &StopInfo, seen: &[Seen], out: &mut Out)` runs at every numbered stop. `seen` holds the hello, replies and refusals by command id, agent events, console text and broken lines. Through `out` the controller sends commands (`out` gives out the ids), report and note lines, snapshots, `EngineAction::DiskFaultsOff` (the shell's `go`), and the end: a verdict, `PowerCut { acked, failed }` or `AtSnapshot`.
  - **What `ScheduleController` drives:** it does what `hydo-init.sh` does, in its order, with one function per shell function: services, readiness, restarts, provisioning, steps, `K=`, `X=` (the stack's timed kill), both `P=` forms, knobs, periodic and final invariants with their records, the verdict, the power cut and the heal. Its conversations are boot (to S0 and S1), run (from S1), recovery (from S0) and solo.
  - **The seams for wave 3:** liveness, clock, history, freeze, buggify, fakes, error-logs, net-namespaces, composer, net-faults and recovery-inputs. A manifest or schedule that needs one is refused, naming the seam. `HANDOFF.md` has one line per seam, the 17 decisions where the shell is ambiguous, and what step C1 needs.
  - **The control transcript:** one canonical JSON line per record. It holds the header with the cadence, then `stop`/`send`/`ack`/`report`/`note`/`snap`/`engine`/`end` records, each with its stop number. Its hash is `ctl=`. `ReplayController` types a transcript again. `Run.control` was added to hydo-results as an optional field.
  - **Proof, with no VM:** `tests/corpus.rs` makes 1,986 runs of the explorer's identity corpus on the 22 core example manifests (the other 20 name their seam). The runs use a scripted agent and engine, and 525 have a recovery boot. Every run is checked against a shell model of hydo-init.sh, written independently and thread by thread, and every transcript, typed again, gives the same transcript. The goldens are `tests/golden/corpus-quick.txt` and `examples/`.
  - **The fakes seam (M125, branch `ctl-fakes`, not merged):** `src/schedule/fakes.rs` is hydo-init-fakes.sh through the agent (hydo-world under `fakes:world`, `H=` windows by `ctl on/off`, one `ctl heal`, the summary as `hydo-world: ` report lines, the dump at a cut). The world is carried as `Ending::PowerCut::world` and given to the recovery with `ScheduleController::with_world`. The corpus now drives `redis/hydo-proxy.yaml` and `stack-grpc/hydo.yaml` (750 runs with every `--sweep protocol` point and cut variants) against a shell model of the extension; `tests/fakes.rs` has the semantic checks and the deliberate mistakes. The 12 decisions are in `HANDOFF.md`.
  - **Network faults, the freeze and service networks (M124, branch `ctl-net`, not merged):** `src/schedule/netfault.rs` is `N=`/`O=` with hydo-init.sh's net_on/net_heal, the links of hydo-init-links.sh and hydo-init-netns.sh's netem on the veths (the shell's tc lines through `run`, the M71 drain with `qlen` and `sleep 0.01` between polls, the heal lines); `src/schedule/freeze.rs` is hydo-init-freeze.sh through the agent's `freeze`/`unfreeze` and its `froze`/`resumed` events (hydo_fc's FROZE line names the handle); `src/schedule/netns.rs` sets the bridge and the namespaces up before S0 and runs start_svc in the service's namespace. `Layout` gained the pinned `tc`/`ip`/`iptables` (hydo-build's placeholders; C1 must give the image's paths). The corpus drives `redis/hydo-freeze.yaml`, `compose-voting/hydo.generated.yaml` and every N=/O= schedule (4,042 runs); `tests/corpus_net.rs` adds 446 runs (written schedules, plan variants, redis-bridge without its `eventually` check, M76's and M92's freeze-sweep point lists) against a shell model of the four shell files; 10 mistakes in conversations and 4 in the code were caught. The 13 decisions are in `HANDOFF.md`. F= with `network: bridge` was refused then; it is driven since M131 (the freeze's `netns` field).
- **Feature controllers, liveness, clock, BUGGIFY and the recovery inputs (M122, step B2 for four seams; branch `ctl-liveness-clock`, not merged):** each feature is a module in `hydo-control/src/features/` (a child of `schedule`, called from its `SEAM` with a one-line hook). `eventually` invariants run as monitor threads that do the shell's loop (not the agent's `probe`, which cannot report a late result); `T=` reads, sets and checks the realtime clock; `guest.clock_after_cut` reads the clock at a cut and the recovery boot continues from it; `B=` writes `/tmp/hydo-buggify`. A power cut hands `RecoveryInputs { acked, failed, clock }` from the run's controller to `ScheduleController::recovery_from`, so carried values never travel as tokens among the ids. Proof, with no VM: the 1,986 M120 runs give byte-identical transcripts; `tests/corpus.rs` makes 9,839 runs after the merges of M124–M126 (T= and B= run; redis-live, the voting app's manifests, redis-bridge and the shop are driven); `tests/features.rs` makes 3,609 runs on thirteen plans (with clock_after_cut, two eventually invariants, zero steps, the shop and redis-bridge with clock_after_cut), checked against a shell model of the extensions written from their text, with both transcripts replayed, 27 feature paths reached, and 15 kinds of deliberate mistakes refused by the model. 30. Guest control (M116 design; lock-step control in both engines: M118 hvx, M119 hvm): the guest agent and its protocol are done (M117: `hydo-agent-proto`, `hydo-agent`). The build machine was not used.

- **The module (`hv/hvx/hvx.c`, `hvx_abi.h`; additions only, every old binary keeps its ABI).** Two VM flags, inert when off: bit 8 `HVX_VM_HOSTCALL` and bit 9 `HVX_VM_DIRTY_LOG`; one exit reason `HVX_EXIT_HOSTCALL` (`0xfffffffa`); six ioctls, numbers 64–69: `HVX_RESET_VM`, `HVX_GET_DIRTY`, `HVX_HC_GET`, `HVX_HC_PUT`, `HVX_HC_GET_STATE`, `HVX_HC_SET_STATE`. What runs when the flags are off: one NULL test in `hvx_guest_rw` and in the two disk-write helpers, one flag test in `hvx_pio` and one in the run loop's retired-exit block. The main module ignores flags it does not know and answers the new ioctls with ENOTTY; the engine probes both after HVX_CREATE_VM, so the new engine keeps working with the loaded main module, and the main module's userspace is untouched.
  - **The host-call port** (ports 0x5f0 data, 0x5f4 control, 0x5f8 count, outside the virtio test doorbell range 0x500–0x52f): a 1/2/4-byte OUT to the data port appends to the record being written; a 4-byte OUT of the record's length to the control port commits it (the writer pads the last OUT, so the bytes may exceed the length by up to 3; anything else, or a record over the 64 KiB buffer, is dropped and counted) and ends the run call right after that instruction with `HVX_EXIT_HOSTCALL` (with the in-kernel scheduler the record waits for the next return); a 4-byte IN of the control port reads the magic `0x43485948`; an IN of the count port the staged bytes left; a 1/2/4-byte IN of the data port pops staged bytes (zero-filled past the end). No guest memory is touched and nothing loops on a guest value. Not a `rep outsb`, as the design proposed: the agent is a user-space program, and string I/O from user space would need the module to walk the guest's page tables. The two 64 KiB buffers are allocated at HVX_CREATE_VM only with the flag. The output buffer's partial record and the staged bytes the guest has not read are VM state; the host carries them with its own snapshots through `HVX_HC_GET_STATE`/`SET_STATE` (not inside struct hvx_snapshot, which would change the ABI of every binary).
  - **The dirty-page log**: with the flag, EPTP bit 6 turns on the EPT accessed/dirty flags (the bare-metal machine's CPU has them: `IA32_VMX_EPT_VPID_CAP` bit 21; HVX_CREATE_VM refuses the flag with ENODEV without them or without INVEPT), and two bitmaps record the pages the module itself writes: guest RAM written by `hvx_guest_rw` (every virtio DMA into the guest: disk reads, used rings, received packets), and disk pages written by the device (`vblk_disk_rw` towards the disk, `disk_write_bytes`, which commits the volatile cache at a flush). `HVX_GET_DIRTY` folds the EPT dirty flags into the RAM bitmap, copies both bitmaps out and, with `HVX_DIRTY_CLEAR`, clears them and the flags; every run call's entry already does INVEPT, so a cleared flag is set again by the guest's next write. The host's own writes through its mmap windows are not logged (the host knows them).
  - **`HVX_RESET_VM`**: the state HVX_CREATE_VM and the first HVX_SET_DISK left, except the contents of guest RAM and of the disk: every vCPU cleared and seeded as at creation (its VMXON, VMCS and FPU pages kept and cleared; registers, clocks, injection, the one-vCPU re-injection state and CR2, the LAPIC, all PMU, tick-jitter, inserted-tick and turn statistics), the IOAPIC, PIC and UART models, the console buffer, the UART receive queue, the fuzz input, the scheduler, the tick-jitter, inserted-tick and turn policies, the PMU period, the disk device (its pages, size, volatile-cache buffer and dirty bitmap kept; everything else, the flush-cut state and statistics included, back to the first-attach values; under the map lock, which the disk's mmap fault handler takes), the network device, the host-call port and its statistics, and the dirty log. A run call that returns with `HVX_EXIT_HOSTCALL` takes the committed records into the run's record stream (`pbuf`, kept beside the console as `ubuf` is) and makes a stop with `why=hostcall` (an addition to the lock-step protocol: `hydo-engine`'s `StopWhy::Hostcall`, `hydo-control`'s `Why::Hostcall`). At every stop the records' lines are reported as EVENT lines after the console's (the controller sees the same agent lines as over the serial line, in order, at the instruction that wrote them). The agent's first record makes the port its channel for the rest of the boot and for every run restored from it (`hc_active`, in the engine's snapshots): a SEND is then staged with `HVX_HC_PUT` and announced by one doorbell byte (0x07) on the serial input; a retype after a restore only rings again, because the snapshot kept the staged bytes. With the port in use, the fingerprint also takes the record stream and the port's buffers (`hvx-hostcall-v1`); a run whose agent never used the port has the fingerprint it always had.
  - **In-place reuse (`HYDO_HVX_REUSE=1`, off by default; `HYDO_HVX_CHECK_RESET=1` checks it).** VMs are made with `HVX_VM_DIRTY_LOG` (one vCPU, no tracing, a page-aligned data partition). A VM whose RAM and disk the engine restored itself goes into a pool of at most two when it is done (and only while the machine has room for one more VM of its size), with what it holds: the snapshot's number and its non-zero pages, and the data partition's. The next restore takes a pool VM holding the same snapshot (else any, once the pool is full; else a fresh VM): it reads and clears the dirty log, calls `HVX_RESET_VM`, sets the registers a fresh VM gets, loads the snapshot's vCPU state as before, and rewrites only the pages that may differ: the dirty ones, and when the VM held another snapshot, every page either snapshot has; each page as a fresh VM restored from the snapshot holds it (the snapshot's page, else the module's own default page tables a fresh VM starts with, else zeros; on the disk the base image outside the data partition, the partition's saved page or zeros inside). A power-cut run keeps two VMs, the workload's (from S1) and the recovery's (from S0), and each next run reuses its own. The prepared fresh VM (M132) is not made while reuse is on. `HYDO_HVX_CHECK_RESET=1` compares every page of RAM and of the disk after each in-place restore with what a fresh VM would hold and ends the run with an error on a difference.

### Milestone 139 — DONE (reactive exploration, design step D2: the schedule token `A=` — a fault or a heal the host controller decides during the run, at the first SDK assertion record of an event — with `hydo explore --reactive fault|heal|both` and `hydo-bench run --reactive`; every reactive run reproduced from its schedule string and from its control transcript; measured on the bug benchmark against the process strategy with `--more-faults`: NEGATIVE, no defect found more often, every reactive mode needs more runs to the first detection; 2026-11-02)

Branch `worktree-agent-ab7d04fb99da22824` (from `main` = `e36e7a9`, main `e367ea9` with M138 merged in before the end). No change to `hv/hvx/hvx.c`, `hvx_abi.h`, hydo-hvx or the loaded module; no reload. Every VM went through `~/bin/hvx-run` from the own tree `~/hydo-d2` on the bare-metal machine, one stack-sized VM at a time (`c2-cells.sh` waits for 6 GiB of free memory and honours `$HYDO_QUIET_FILE`, here M138's marker `~/m138-side-loading`), results in `/var/tmp/m139`; the build machine was not used.

**What only host control makes possible.** In an agent image the host controller sees the guest's console at every numbered stop, so it can decide *during* a run. Of the design's three examples (fault on an assertion, heal on no progress, branch at a reaction) the first two were built, as one schedule token, so that a reactive run stays a schedule string:

- **`A=<event>[@<step>][+<ms>]:<action>`** (`hydo_schedule::React`, letter `A` reserved; `hydo-manifest` refuses a knob `A`). From before workload step `step` (0 when not written) the controller watches the console for the first SDK assertion record (`HYDO-ASSERT`, which every SDK writes to the console) of `event` whose outcome is the event's (`ok:true` of a `sometimes`/`reachable`, `ok:false` of an `always`/`unreachable`), waits `ms` of guest time and acts: `cut` (a power cut at that instant: the workload's client and every service SIGSTOPped at once, the ids read, the recovery boot from S0 as for `C=`), `kill-<svc>` (down until the heal's restart pass, as after `X=`), `stop-<svc>-<ms>`, or `cont-<svc>` (resume a paused service: a `P=` pause healed at the first sign of no progress). Reactions live during the workload's steps only (cancelled, or joined when acting, after the last step; `C=` cancels them).
- **Controller** (`hydo-control/src/features/react.rs`, one flow thread per reaction): the console's assertion records become facts (`Facts::asserts`) only in a run with `A=`; a run without it keeps none and takes none of the new paths, so every recorded transcript and golden is unchanged (the identity corpora, `corpus-quick`, `features-quick`, `m123-quick`, the explorer's and hydo-bench's goldens all pass as they were). A reaction's cut is only marked by its thread; the main sequence's workload wait ends at the exit or at the mark and takes `C=`'s cut path (`POWER CUT at the reaction A=...`). HANDOFF.md "Reactions" has the six decisions.
- **Reproducible.** The controller's decision is a pure function of the schedule string and of the console lines at each numbered stop, so a reactive run is reproduced by `hydo repro "<schedule>"` and by `hydo repro --transcript <control.jsonl>` (the reaction's commands are in the transcript with their stops). Proven on the scripted agent and engine (`hydo-control/tests/react.rs`: 51 reactions acting at the first stop where their event is seen on the Redis example and the benchmark manifest, 21 of them power cuts with their recovery boot; never when the event does not come; two runs one transcript; the ReplayController and `drive::run` over one link replay both conversations; a reaction that never fires sends the same commands at the same stops as the schedule without it), and on the bare-metal machine: `hydo run` of `disk=cut dseed=0 | run P=kafka@5+2 A=client.place_failed:cut` on the d4 image (the reaction cut the power at order 5, recovery boot OK `acked=5/30`, `85ebed92d2f65c20`) and of `disk=none dseed=0 | run O=kafka@5-10:resp:loss,100% A=client.outcome_unknown+20:kill-front` on the d1–d7 control (`kafka order=5 present 2 times`, `c5278482e0d05640`): `hydo repro <run dir>` REPRODUCED both, `hydo repro --transcript` REPRODUCED both ("the same commands at the same stops", the cut's recovery transcript included); the fresh-boot fingerprints equal the serve worker's (`hydo-bench list`, each twice identical).
- **Shrinking** is defined on the anchored token: a candidate drops a reaction, makes it act at once (delay 0 or halved), arms it from the start, or halves a stop; because the reaction is anchored to its event, dropping another fault does not leave it at a meaningless time.
- **Strategies** (`hydo explore --reactive fault|heal|both`, `hydo-bench run --reactive`), drawn from their own stream (`REACT_SALT`) on top of any strategy, so a seed's schedule is the strategy's with `A=` added: **fault** gives 60% of the schedules `A=<event>[@<a fault's start>][+0..5000]:<cut|kill-|stop->` (the event from `--react-events`, by default the order service's nine workload-time events; a cut only without `cf=`, making the disk `cut`; never on the `K=`/`P=` service, with `cf=` only the order service); **heal** makes 70% of the counted pauses `P=svc@a+n` last to the workload's end with `A=<no-progress event>@a[+0..10000]:cont-svc` (`client.outcome_unknown` or `client.place_failed`). `tests/reactive.rs` checks on 36,000 schedules that only these fields change and the rules hold, and pins the stream (`tests/golden/reactive.txt`). `hydo-bench run --dry` prints a cell's schedules.

**Measured** (M136's agent benchmark images in `~/c3-work/bench/build`, hydo-bench with `--kind agent`, one worker; plans `hydo/bench/c2-plans/m139.txt` and `m139-modes.txt`, one `c2-cells.sh` step per defect and repetition; repetition r = seeds r·1000+1…+60, early stop at the first detection, a detection counts only if the control passes the same schedule and a re-run gives the same fingerprint). `px` = `--strategy process --more-faults --cf-range 1-309`, the current best; `pxr` = the same with `--reactive both`; `pxf`/`pxh` = `--reactive fault` / `heal` alone. Cells give the repetitions found, then the run of the first detection per repetition (an asterisk: the detecting verdict is not the defect's signature).

| defect | px | pxr (both) | pxf (fault) | pxh (heal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| d0-old-front-door | 3/3 (7\*, 1, 1) | 3/3 (7\*, 2, 1) | 3/3 (7\*, 1, 1) | 3/3 (7\*, 2, 1) |
| d1-kafka-first | 3/3 (2, 2, 4) | 3/3 (2, 2, 2) | 3/3 (2, 2, 2) | 3/3 (2, 2, 4) |
| d2-batched-publish-flag | 3/3 (6, 1, 3) | 3/3 (6, 5, 2) | 3/3 (6, 1, 2) | 3/3 (6, 5, 3) |
| d3-blind-retry | 3/3 (4, 4, 4) | 3/3 (4, 4, 4) | 3/3 (4, 4, 4) | 3/3 (4, 4, 4) |
| d4-produce-timeout-definite | 3/3 (7\*, 1, 1) | 3/3 (7\*, 18, 7\*) | 3/3 (7\*, 1, 30\*) | 3/3 (7\*, 18, 1) |
| d5-myisam | 3/3 (7\*, 1, 1) | 3/3 (7\*, 1, 1) | 3/3 (7\*, 1, 1) | 3/3 (7\*, 1, 1) |
| d6-client-deadline-definite | 3/3 (4, 1, 1) | 3/3 (4, 4, 4) | 3/3 (4, 1, 4) | 3/3 (4, 4, 1) |
| d7-skip-last-record | 3/3 (17, 9, 4) | 3/3 (17, 9, 6) | 3/3 (17, 9, 4) | 3/3 (17, 9, 6) |
| d10-outcome-in-memory | 3/3 (7, 44, 10) | 3/3 (7, 44, 10) | 3/3 (7, 44, 10) | 3/3 (7, 44, 10) |
| by signature, of 27 | 24 | 23 | 23 | 24 |
| runs to the first detection, sum | 154 | 187 | 183 | 181 |
| d11-ack-unflushed-flag (ten repetitions) | 2/10 (3, 8) | 2/10 (8, 25) | – | – |

- **Result: negative.** No defect was found more often by any reactive mode, and the sum of runs to the first detection grew from 154 (px) to 181–187. Per seed (the base schedule is the same in both columns), of the 178 seeds of d0–d7 and d10 that px and pxr both ran, 168 gave the same verdict class; the reactions turned 7 violations into passes and 3 passes into violations. d11 (AGENTS.md open item 6): px 2 of 10 repetitions (runs 3 and 8), pxr 2 of 10 (runs 8 and 25); of the 459 seeds both ran, 457 gave the same class, one each way. Three detections came from a reaction where the base schedule passed: d1 and d2 in repetition 3 (seed 3002, `A=server.redis_redialed@11:kill-mysql`) and pxr's d11 hit at seed 10025 (`A=server.outcome_unknown:kill-front` with `cf=33`).
- **Why.** A reaction that comes early pre-empts the later fault that made the base schedule fail (seed 3001: `A=client.place_failed+50:cut` cuts the power at order 4, before the base's `C=30`, where d4 and d6 fail). A heal resumes Kafka while d7 needs it down to the end (seed 3004), or its event never comes (the order service writes `client.outcome_unknown` only for some failures) and the pause the heal lengthened to the end hides the base's failure (seed 2001 on d0, d2, d4 and d6). Every extra command also moves guest timing, which moves d11's narrow window both ways (seeds 2003 and 10025). Reactions acted in 504 of the 792 drawn in pxr (heals 324 of 370; cuts, kills and stops 40–48 %). So the lesson of M41–M56 holds again: where faults land and in which combination matters more than how the next fault is chosen, and a fault anchored to an event the system writes lands in a narrower set of places than a seeded one.
- **Useful by hand.** Aimed at a moment already known to matter, the token reaches two-fault triggers with one guessed anchor (`/var/tmp/m139/demo`, each schedule twice with one fingerprint): `disk=cut dseed=0 | run O=kafka@5-30:resp:loss,100% A=client.place_failed+2000:cut` fails d4 with its signature (`dc71e9dd855afb04`) and passes on its control; `disk=none dseed=0 | run O=kafka@5-10:resp:loss,100% A=client.outcome_unknown+20:kill-front` fails d10 (`5dad4111935ccd9d`) and passes on its control. On real hardware a reaction that never acts is inert: `disk=none dseed=0 | run P=kafka@5+25` and the same with `A=client.outcome_unknown@5+500:cont-kafka` give one fingerprint on d4 (`55c8b28686400e7b`).
- **Not built: branching at a reaction.** The design's third example needs a mid-run SNAP/RESUME of an agent image driven by the explorer (the engines have it, M118/M119; the explorer's agent worker does not) and a cloned controller; M45 found branching around one moment worse than fresh schedules on this stack, and the measurement above gives no reason to expect a reaction point to be a better moment. Left as open work (AGENTS.md open item 30).
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` (102 test programs) on the Mac, before and after merging main with M138 (`e367ea9`). The explorer's, the controller's and hydo-bench's recorded goldens pass unchanged; the only re-recorded golden is hydo-cli's `guide manifest` answer (MANIFEST.md gained the `A=` row and the "Reactions" section). No pinned reproducer or recorded baseline is touched by this work (no engine or module change; schedules without `A=` run the same commands).
- **Files:** `hydo/crates/hydo-schedule/src/guest.rs` (`React`, `ReactAction`), `hydo/crates/hydo-control/src/features/react.rs` and its hooks in `schedule.rs`, `flow.rs` (`Facts::asserts`, `Fx::is_cancelled`), `hydo/crates/hydo-explore/src/{sched,gen,space,args,run}.rs`, `hydo/crates/hydo-bench/src/{cells,cli}.rs`, `hydo/crates/hydo-manifest/src/validate.rs`, tests `hydo-control/tests/react.rs`, `hydo-explore/tests/reactive.rs`, `hydo-schedule/tests/language.rs`; `hydo/bench/c2-plans/m139.txt`, `m139-modes.txt`, `c2-cells.sh` (`$HYDO_QUIET_FILE`); docs MANIFEST.md "Reactions", hydo/bench/README.md "Reactive exploration", hydo-control HANDOFF.md "Reactions", the design note's D2 line.

### Milestone 140, part A — DONE (the main module's Milestone 138 code under a debug kernel on the bare-metal machine itself, then loaded as the main module; 2026-11-02)

Branch `worktree-agent-a283674a8613c75d8` (from `main` = `e367ea9`). Approved by the user (2026-11-02): booting the bare-metal machine once into a debug kernel and back, and the main-module load afterwards. The build machine was not used. Tree on the bare-metal machine `~/hydo-dbg`, results `/var/tmp/m140a`, every VM through `~/bin/hvx-run`. Scripts: `hv/hvx/safety/onbox/` (`onbox.sh`, `debug.config`, `debug-chain.sh`, `hvx_m138_edge_test.c`); how to run them is in `hv/hvx/SAFETY.md`, "The debug kernel on the bare-metal machine itself".

- **The debug kernel.** kernel.org Linux 6.8.12 (M97's tarball, sha256 `19b31956…`), configured from the running `/boot/config-6.8.0-146-generic`, trimmed by `make localmodconfig` to the modules loaded at the time (95 built: ahci, md raid1 and the other md personalities, igb, ext4 and the rest of what the bare-metal machine uses; the md core built in), plus `onbox/debug.config`: KASAN generic inline with vmalloc, kmemleak (scan on demand), UBSAN (bounds, shift, bool, enum; no trap), PROVE_LOCKING and PROVE_RCU with larger lockdep tables, DEBUG_ATOMIC_SLEEP, full preemption with DEBUG_PREEMPT, DEBUG_LIST, DEBUG_VM, hardened usercopy, the lockup, hung-task and workqueue detectors, EFI pstore, no KVM, 64 possible CPUs, `LOCALVERSION=-hydodbg`. Module signing stayed on, because the lockdown LSM selects it (a first try with `MODULE_SIG=n` was refused by the script's check that every fragment option survived). Built on the bare-metal machine with Ubuntu's gcc 13.3 at nice 19 with 6 jobs in about 30 minutes, beside other sessions' work: `bzImage` `e52f702b89492a72…`. `onbox.sh install`: the modules into `/lib/modules/6.8.12-hydodbg` (7.2 MB, stripped), `bzImage`, config, System.map and an initramfs (`mkinitramfs`) into `~/hydo-dbg/boot`; the initramfs has raid1, mdadm with `mdadm.conf`, ahci, igb and ext4 (md-mod built in). Nothing was written to `/boot`, so `update-grub` never listed the debug kernel.
- **Why not `grub-reboot`, and what was done instead.** `/boot` is the RAID1 array md2, and the bare-metal machine's `/boot/grub/grub.cfg` says "GRUB lacks write support for diskfilter": GRUB cannot write `grubenv` there. `grub-reboot` relies on the `save_env next_entry` in `grub.cfg`'s header to clear its entry at boot; that write fails on this bare-metal machine, so a `grub-reboot` entry would have been booted again on every reboot and a hang would never have fallen back. The debug kernel was therefore started with kexec (kexec-tools 1:2.0.28-0ubuntu3 installed with apt, its question "handle reboots" preset to false; Ubuntu 24.04's package sets no `LOAD_KEXEC` and installs no init script, so plain reboots stay firmware reboots). Its command line was the running one plus `panic=30 softlockup_panic=1 kasan_multi_shot`, so a panic or a soft lockup would have rebooted to GRUB by itself.
- **GRUB's default.** Before M140 `GRUB_DEFAULT=0`, and entry 0 ("Ubuntu") boots `/boot/vmlinuz`, which pointed at 6.8.0-147-generic, an Ubuntu kernel installed on 2026-10-14 and never booted; a plain reboot would have left 6.8.0-146. `onbox.sh grub` ran: `sed -i 's/^GRUB_DEFAULT=.*/GRUB_DEFAULT=saved/' /etc/default/grub` (the original saved as `~/hydo-dbg/grub.default.orig`), `update-grub`, `grub-set-default 'gnulinux-advanced-d57150c5-7798-4a65-acc6-05ecb85e804e>gnulinux-6.8.0-146-generic-advanced-d57150c5-7798-4a65-acc6-05ecb85e804e'` (written from Linux, which can write the RAID). Checks: `grub-editenv list` printed only that `saved_entry`; the generated `grub.cfg` selects `set default="${saved_entry}"` when there is no `next_entry` (line 29) and has the named entry in the advanced submenu (line 216, "Ubuntu, with Linux 6.8.0-146-generic"); `grep -c 6.8.12-hydodbg /boot/grub/grub.cfg` printed 0. The bare-metal machine stays on this default: moving it to 6.8.0-147 is a separate decision (`grub-set-default` with that entry).
- **The reboot.** `~/m140-reboot-pending` was written at 06:07:29 (UTC) with the plan; M140 part B's nix gcc build (`~/hydo-nixb-work`) finished before the 15 minutes were up, and part B's image builds (no VMs) ended too. At 06:23:44 `GO=1 onbox.sh go` took the exclusive module lock (`flock -x -w 1800 ~/.hvx-module.lock`), found `/dev/hvx` closed and no hydo or hvx process of anyone, and ran `systemctl kexec`. The bare-metal machine answered remote logins at 06:25:16 on 6.8.12-hydodbg with both arrays `[UU]`, the network up, 26 GB visible (KASAN's shadow takes the rest), no report from the boot, and lockdep armed (`debug_locks: 1`).
- **The module under the debug kernel.** `onbox.sh module` built `~/hydo-dbg/hv/hvx/hvx.c` (main's, sha256 `b6d6b639…`, the code M138 proved on `hvxgc`) for 6.8.12-hydodbg and loaded it as `hvx` under the exclusive lock: srcversion `B5E97B37504F1A5F508BA30` (M138's side module had the same), "PMU branch clock available", "Intel PT guest tracing available". The compiler's only note was `hvx_ioctl`'s frame, now 2,768 bytes under KASAN (M97: 2,600; the kernel stack is 32 KiB under KASAN).
- **What ran, in order, and what it gave.** `dmesg`'s ring buffer rotates within minutes under hvx's exit histograms, so every scan read the whole boot's kernel journal (`journalctl -k -b`) and ran kmemleak's scan twice.
  - Before any VM: 0 kmemleak objects, 0 report lines.
  - `HVX_METAL_TREE=hydo-dbg hv/hvx/deploy-metal.sh` (no reload): **ALL PASS (33 checks)**, every recorded value: the 24 hand-written tests (iso `7e586473f6e494d7`, pci `3f95ef833747f3ec`, fault ×3, net, net-fault ×3, bug_f0 `1083e400458728ff`, pmu `86c4afcd0a799450`, avx `3bb428a134ce542a`, smp ×3), the 4 several-vCPU tests (sched_pmu, race `8cb7c61a2393f44e`, sipi ×2, sweep `39971eed9c2f35fe`), the 3 boots (`7a5559028ffbf52c`, `36583d533d7c989b`, 2 vCPUs `6584c954c2839491`) and both pinned reproducers (`2403499c9a3f8419` VIOLATION, `f87130453609a5d6` OK). So the PMU clock, the in-kernel scheduler and the 2-vCPU boot, which the nested debug VM of M97 could only refuse, ran under KASAN and lockdep here.
  - `hvx_m138_edge_test` (new, `onbox/`): PASS (90 checks): the port's magic, a 4+1-byte record, a commit that leaves 4 bytes over and a 70,000-byte record (both counted as errors and dropped), a 2-byte record, `HVX_HC_GET` in pieces, `HVX_HC_PUT` of exactly 64 KiB and one byte more (ENOSPC), the guest reading the count and 4+2+1 staged bytes, `HVX_HC_GET_STATE`/`SET_STATE` with short buffers, every invalid length, unmapped addresses (EFAULT) and a valid partial record read back, `HVX_GET_DIRTY` with short buffers, NULL and unmapped addresses, the two written pages and CLEAR, `HVX_RESET_VM` and the whole pass again with the same values, every new ioctl with no VM and on a VM without the flags (EINVAL), the port on a VM without it (IN reads all ones), and 50 lifecycles with both flags and a disk. It passed the same way on the normal kernel before (against a side module `hvxdbg` built from the same source and unloaded after) and after (against the new main module).

### Milestone 140, part B — DONE (hydo-agent 0.3.0 in every image and the host-call port on by default in the hvx engine; every x86_64 example image built for real on the bare-metal machine with Nix there; every example and the bug benchmark re-baselined; 2026-11-02)

Branch `worktree-agent-af7e40ec96f7a9e1c` (two agents) and then `worktree-agent-a4922cd909c013d6a`. The build machine was not used (off limits since 2026-10-30); the user approved Nix on the bare-metal machine (2026-11-02). Bare-metal machine tree `~/hydo-nixb`, work directory `~/hydo-nixb-work` (the scripts `img2.sh`, `cmp.sh`, `list.sh`, `bench.sh`, `xtable.py`, and the lists `recorded.txt`, `recorded-stack.txt`), results `/var/tmp/m140b`; every VM through `~/bin/hvx-run`, at most one stack-sized VM at a time; the main module was not reloaded (it is part A's `B5E97B37504F1A5F508BA30`).

- **The pin and the default (commit `f319586`).** `hydo-build` stages hydo-agent 0.3.0 (x86_64 `398f297e…`, aarch64 `099e5444…`, docs/BUILD-PINS.md), the agent that speaks the host-call port of M138 when the engine offers it; the hvx engine offers it by default (`HYDO_HVX_HOSTCALL=0` turns it off; `hydo-hvx/tests/options.rs`); in-place reuse stays off. Every agent image therefore has new bytes, and on hvx the agent's lines and the host's lines travel over the port, whose records are in the fingerprint. The hand-written images (stack-explore images, flagships, `deploy-metal.sh`, the pinned reproducers) are not agent images and keep their values.
- **Nix on the bare-metal machine (commit `26ec966`, docs/BUILD-PINS.md "Nix on the bare-metal machine").** Nix 2.18.9 single-user, the build machine's nixpkgs, the pinned static gcc built from its derivation, the other pinned store paths from cache.nixos.org; `iproute2-6.8.0` and `iptables-1.8.10` kept out of `/nix/store`. Images that need pinned store paths are built as uid 1000, gid 100 with `HYDO_KEEP_OWNERS=1`, as the build machine's plain `hydo-build` made them.
- **The Mac (docs/REBASELINE.md 9.1).** 67 schedules on 19 images, every one twice identical; 64 of 67 verdict lines word for word M136's, 3 differ in timing words only.
- **A hydo-build fix found by the real builds.** The first stack builds failed with `cp -a /nix/store/dbcw19ds…-glibc-2.39-52 failed`: on a machine with Nix and the Linux release's bundled closures, glibc 2.39-52 is reached twice, from `/nix/store` (MySQL's closure) and from the release's bundle (iproute2's closure, which must stay out of `/nix/store`), and the second `cp -a` wrote into the first copy's read-only directories (miniflux: `nghttp2-1.61.0-lib` the same way). `hydo-build` now stages each store path name once, preferring the `/nix/store` copy, in name order (the order of a closure taken from `/nix/store` alone, as on the build machine); no image built before changes (commit "hydo-build stages each store path once"). Also fixed in the bare-metal machine script `img2.sh`: rust-kv's fake checkout lacked `sdk/` (its `Cargo.toml` names `../../../../sdk/rust`); stack-grpc's `src()` was cut at the closing brace of its here-document (now taken up to `src cur;`); the generated-driver stack shared its staging folder with the tier-B stack cases, which re-staged it (now `ex/stackgen`).
