### Milestone 169 — DONE (`cargo install hydo` prepared, nothing published: the package `hydo` and the 19 workspace crates it depends on build from their packages alone, a check fails when one could not be published, a dry run packs all 20, installs `hydo` offline from a stand-in registry and runs it; a `hydo` installed by cargo uses `$HYDO_HOME/versions/<its version>` as its release root, which `hydo setup` fills from the release; the Mac quickstart with a cargo-installed `hydo` gives docs/REBASELINE.md 13.4's values; 2026-11-07)

**Goal (user, 2026-11-07):** a user types `cargo install hydo` and gets a working hydo, whose guest files hydo itself downloads on first use (M162). Prepare everything without publishing. docs/PUBLISHING.md "Publishing the hydo command" is the full description; this section records what was found and measured.

**What stopped `cargo publish` of the hydo command, and the fix of each:**

1. **The package name.** The binary crate was the package `hydo-cli`. It is now the package `hydo` (crates.io name free on 2026-11-07, as are the 19 others), in the same directory `hydo/crates/hydo-cli`; scripts and the two component lists say `-p hydo` and `hydo` (deploy-metal.sh, side-check.sh, kvm-check.sh, both build-release.sh, build-reproducers.sh, hv/hvm/explore/README.md, third-party.json). Cargo.lock changes only by the rename. The package has a crates.io README (`hydo/crates/hydo-cli/README.md`), keywords and categories.
2. **Path dependencies without versions.** Every `hydo-*` entry of `[workspace.dependencies]` has `version` next to `path`; `hydo-control`'s own path dependency on `hydo-agent-proto` uses the workspace entry.
3. **A dependency cycle through dev-dependencies.** `hydo-control`'s tests use `hydo-explore`, `hydo-errors`, `hydo-history` and `hydo-build`, and `hydo-explore` depends on `hydo-control`. Dev-dependencies on workspace crates are given by path only (`hydo-control`, `hydo-engine`'s `hydo-agent-proto`), so cargo leaves them out of the published manifests.
4. **`publish = false` on `hydo-agent-proto`.** Removed (its repository and homepage written out, because the guest agent's own workspace reads that file alone). It keeps its own version 0.1.0: the agent compiles it, so its version moves with the protocol (its `HYDO_VERSION`, used in the host's messages about agent versions, is its package version: those messages name 0.1.0 until it is bumped).
5. **Files compiled in from outside a crate.** `hydo-cli`'s setup.rs (the four pin lists of `hydo/dist/<platform>/`), `hydo-image`'s releases.rs (M162's `hydo/dist/releases.txt`) and `hydo-agents`' build script (the skill folder and MANIFEST.md) read through links inside each crate: `hydo-cli/pins/<platform>/{assets,guest-programs}.sha256`, `hydo-image/pins/releases.txt`, `hydo-agents/embed/hydo-onboard` and `embed/MANIFEST.md`; git tracks the links, the tree reads the same files through them, `cargo package` stores the linked contents (it follows a linked directory too). Every published crate has `LICENSE -> ../../../LICENSE`.
6. **The commit lookup.** `hydo-image`'s build script ran `git rev-parse HEAD` in its own directory, which for a crate unpacked from crates.io could be some other repository (a home directory in git). A packaged crate (recognised by the `Cargo.toml.orig` cargo writes into every package) never runs git and never reads `hydo/COMMIT`: its commit is `git.sha1` of `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, and none when the package was made from a dirty tree. The tree's behaviour is unchanged. `hydo --version` (and `-V`) is new: `hydo 0.1.0 (<commit>)`, or `hydo 0.1.0` without a known commit; it is not in the help text, so no golden changed.
7. **What a package holds.** Each published crate's `include` names its sources, build script, LICENSE and the linked files (and `hydo-hvx`'s `pt/` for the optional coverage decoder); tests, examples and their recorded answers stay in the repository (cargo prints "ignoring test …" while packing). The 20 `.crate` files are 14–140 KiB.
8. **The installed layout.** A `hydo` that `cargo install` put into `<prefix>/bin` took `<prefix>` (for example `~/.cargo`) as its release root. `hydo-cli/src/ctx.rs` `installed_root`: when `<prefix>` is not an unpacked release (no `SHA256SUMS`) and cargo's install record `<prefix>/.crates2.json` names the package `hydo`, the root is `$HYDO_HOME/versions/<its version>` (M162's directory; this closes open item 47 (b)). The test roots of the CLI's goldens have neither file, so nothing else changed. In that case plain `hydo setup` does what `hydo setup --get` does, the end line says the cargo-installed hydo uses the installed version, and `hydo doctor` names `hydo setup --get` as the fix for every missing release file (with one line for the missing version directory).
9. **Not needed at build time:** the guest programs (`hydo-agent`, `hydo-world`, `hydo-read`, `hydo-grpc`) are in no published crate's dependencies; the engine programs are not built by cargo either. Every workspace crate outside the closure has `publish = false` (`hydo-bench`, `hydo-tools`, `hydo-release`, `hydo-schema-compat`, `hydo-grpc-gen`, `hydo-grpc`, `hydo-world`).

**The crate layout decision:** publish the 20 crates as they are, each under its own name, in one documented order, rather than merging them first. Reasons: crates.io needs every path dependency published anyway; publishing as they are takes metadata only and changes no code, output or recorded value; merging would move every module of 19 crates and erase the boundaries the format crates' schema tests rely on, for a shorter publishing list only. Cost: 20 names, and crates.io's rate limit for new crates (a burst, then about one per ten minutes; publishing all 20 takes a few hours unless the limit is raised first).

**The engine programs come from the release, not from cargo:** `cargo install hydo` builds `hydo` only; `bin/hydo-hvm` (signed with the entitlement by `hydo setup`), `bin/hydo-hvx` and `bin/hydo-kvm` come with the version's archive, verified with it. Building them with cargo would put a Linux-only or a Mac-only program on every machine and a second, unverified engine next to the release's.

**The check:** `cargo test -p hydo-release --test crates` (`hydo-release/src/publish.rs`) computes the closure of `hydo` from `cargo metadata` and fails on: `publish` set, a missing description, a license other than Apache-2.0, a missing repository or homepage, a version other than `hydo/VERSION` (except `OWN_VERSION`: `hydo-agent-proto`), a dependency without its version, a dev-dependency with one, `cargo package --list` without LICENSE (and equal to the repository's) or the readme, tests/examples/benches in the package, more than 10 MiB of files, a file listed but unreadable, an `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`/`include!` of a literal outside the crate or not in the package (comments and strings parsed, not grepped), a build-script literal with `../` (one allowed: `hydo-image`'s tree-only `../../COMMIT`), a guest program in the closure, a workspace crate outside the closure without `publish = false`, and a `cargo publish --registry crates-io -p <crate>` order in docs/PUBLISHING.md that does not name the closure once each with every crate after its dependencies. Deliberate mistakes it named: a missing LICENSE link, an include of `../../../VERSION`, `hydo` listed before `hydo-build`, a versioned dev-dependency, `publish = false` on `hydo-errors`; M162's include of `releases.txt`, merged meanwhile, is one it names until it is linked. It runs in about 2 s.

**The dry run** (`hydo/dist/crates/rehearse.sh`): one `cargo package --locked` of all 20 crates (cargo builds each from its `.crate` against the other packed crates: all 20 verified on this Mac, 3 min 38 s); a stand-in for crates.io (the unpacked packages with their `.crate` sha256 as crates.io would serve them, plus `cargo vendor` of the workspace's third-party crates) as a directory source in a fresh Cargo home; `cargo install hydo --locked --offline` with Rust 1.90.0 in a directory outside the repository, so the lock file inside the packed `hydo` decided every version (its checksums of the hydo crates are the `.crate` files' sha256, as they will be on crates.io); then the installed program: `hydo --version`, `hydo guide`, `hydo init` (the `hydo/` skeleton and the AGENTS.md section) and `hydo doctor` (failing, as it must before `hydo setup`, and naming `hydo setup --get`). `HYDO_REHEARSAL_LINUX=1` adds `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` of the packed `hydo` (ring's C through clang when no musl gcc is installed).

**Results** (this Mac, Rust 1.90.0; the release fetched from a loopback mirror, `HYDO_RELEASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, of the v0.1.0 assets that are not published yet: the Mac tarball `5c02e7f3…` of `hydo/dist/releases.txt` and its `SHA256SUMS`, with `HYDO_HOME` in a scratch directory):

| install | `hydo --version` | `hydo setup` | `hydo doctor` after | Redis image | `disk=none \| run` | `disk=cut \| run C=12 R=everysec` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cargo install --locked --path hydo/crates/hydo-cli` (tree at `cda669cc`) | `hydo 0.1.0 (cda669cc…)` | fetched the 30.3 MB archive, unpacked, signed `bin/hydo-hvm`; a second `hydo setup`: nothing to do | all checks passed | `a3447614…`, disk `9ddfc929…` | OK acked=20, `67e5d6469f1a90a5` twice | VIOLATION k:0 lost, `a6870a92a1bbf0ae` twice |
| the dry run's `cargo install hydo --locked --offline` from the stand-in registry (packages of the clean commit `3bcc1462`) | `hydo 0.1.0 (3bcc146276abceb65164da66c6d8f65f845de08c)` | the same | all checks passed | the same bytes | `67e5d6469f1a90a5` twice | `a6870a92a1bbf0ae` twice |

These are docs/REBASELINE.md 13.4's Mac values (`67e5d6469f1a90a5`, `a6870a92a1bbf0ae`, image `a34476147cda279a…`). Before `hydo setup` the cargo-installed `hydo doctor` failed with 8 lines, each naming `hydo setup --get`; `hydo guide` and `hydo init` worked. The dry run from the clean commit packed and verified all 20 crates, installed `hydo` offline with the packed lock file, and `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` of the packed `hydo` passed. Found on the way: cargo unpacks the crates of `cargo package`'s temporary registry into the Cargo home (`registry/src/-<hash>/<crate>-<version>`) and reuses them on the next run although the package changed under the same version, which made a second dry run verify against the first run's crates; the script removes those leftovers first. A dirty-tree package records no commit (`hydo 0.1.0`), as designed.


**Byte identity:** the guest programs whose manifests changed, built again with their scripts: `hydo-agent` x86_64 `398f297e…` and aarch64 `099e5444…` (the pins), `hydo-world` x86_64 `082592ae…` and arm64 `fefcca66…` (the pins). The Redis example built by the cargo-installed `hydo` from the downloaded release: `a34476147cda279a…` and data disk `9ddfc929…`, docs/REBASELINE.md 13.4's.

**Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --release --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` (with `public_content`, the component lists and the new `crates` test) pass on this Mac.

**Left** (AGENTS.md open item 50): publishing itself (the user's decision; after the GitHub release v0.1.0 exists, since a `hydo` whose release is missing cannot set itself up); asking crates.io to raise the new-crate limit; the Linux side of a cargo-installed `hydo` ran only as a `cargo check` for the musl target on this Mac (no Linux install, no `hydo setup` of the Linux archive); `hydo-agent-proto`'s version in the host's messages; the published crates are an API nobody should depend on (their descriptions say what each is, nothing marks them internal).

### Milestone 166 — DONE (an experiment: a GUI application tested through a real browser in the guest. Headless Chromium 156 drives Docker's voting app; an acknowledgement is what the page SHOWS after a click; the screen is checked against the backend. Chromium is deterministic under hvx with nothing special: two fresh-boot runs give one fingerprint, and the screenshots are pixel-identical. A vote the screen showed as cast is lost at a power cut while the worker is down, and the results page stays down after a database restart; both twice with one fingerprint. On the Mac (arm64, hvm) the clean run and the power cut give the same verdicts, each twice with one fingerprint; 2026-11-07)

Branch `worktree-agent-acb2048b713e4492a` from `main` = `afa1186`. The existing `compose-voting` example and every recorded value are unchanged. The manifests are named `gui.yaml` and `gui-mac.yaml`, not `hydo*.yaml`, because hydo-control's and hydo-explore's identity corpora run every `examples/*/hydo*.yaml`, and their goldens would otherwise have to be re-recorded. The design and its results are in `docs/design/gui-testing.md`, and the example is `hydo/onboard/examples/compose-voting-browser/` (its `RESULTS.md` has every schedule). No workspace crate changed.

- **What was built:** the voting app's manifest plus two services.
  - `browser` is `chromedp/headless-shell:156.0.8078.48` by digest (docs/BUILD-PINS.md "Headless Chromium and the GUI driver"). It is an image service whose process is `sleep infinity`.
  - `cdn` is busybox `httpd` with jQuery 1.11.1 and jquery-cookie 1.4.1, under the public CDNs' names. The vote page draws its confirmation with jQuery from `code.jquery.com`, and without that no voter would ever see a vote confirmed.
  - `gui-driver/` is `hydo-gui`, a static Rust program of about 870 lines with no dependencies. It speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol as NUL-terminated JSON over `--remote-debugging-pipe` (file descriptors 3 and 4), clicks with `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` and reads the page with `Runtime.evaluate`.
  - The pipe was chosen because it needs nothing in the image beyond the browser: no WebSocket, no port, no language runtime and no automation library.
- **The workload:** voter i opens the vote page and clicks Cats or Dogs. The id `voter<i>-<option>` is acknowledged only when the page then shows that vote as cast: the button is disabled with the check icon and the other button is dimmed. Each voter's screenshot sha256 goes to the console.
- **The invariants:**
  - `screen.confirmed_counted_soon` (eventually, 60 s) and `screen.confirmed_counted` (final): every screen-confirmed vote is in PostgreSQL with the option the screen showed.
  - `results.screen_agrees_soon` (eventually, 60 s): the results page, rendered by Chromium, shows PostgreSQL's total and percentages.
  - `results.page_live` (`always_or_unreachable`, every 2 s while the workload runs): the results page shows a total whenever PostgreSQL answers.
- **x86_64** (the bare-metal machine; the Linux release `58aab3b1…` installed with `--no-module` into `~/hydo-gui/pfx`; the loaded main module `14D39A96F319623EC2AD8D1`; every run through `~/bin/hvx-run`, one VM at a time and only with at least 8 GiB available):
  - The image is `f84c3412…`, 3,356,491,776 bytes, built twice with the same bytes in 165 s. That is 537 MB more than the voting app.
  - Guest RAM is 3072 MiB. A run from a fresh boot takes 41–51 s of wall time.
  - Each schedule was run twice, and each pair gave one fingerprint:
    - `disk=none dseed=1 | run`: OK `f4c8cd57de61b337`.
    - `K=worker@5+10 C=12`: VIOLATION `screen.confirmed_counted_soon`, `0d240a50bec1aa87`. The screen confirmed 12 votes and PostgreSQL counts 5. After recovery, the results page shows 5 votes.
    - `K=db@5+5`: VIOLATION `results.page_live`, `b22f460ebda8308c`. The results page is refused while PostgreSQL answers, because the result app and the worker stop when the database restarts.
    - `C=12`: OK `e5a45f361ca3f0fa`.
    - `K=worker@5+5`: OK `61e4268bee3514ec`.
    - `N=vote-redis@5-12:loss,100%`: OK `d335d99370201477`. For voters 5 to 11 the screen showed `500 Internal Server Error`, not a confirmation.
  - Every engine counter (stops, typed, inh, ctl, wfp) was the same in both runs of each pair. An earlier version of the manifest gave `e923c6a7e6709266` twice from its first clean run on.
- **Determinism:** nothing was needed beyond quiet-browser flags:
  - `--headless --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --disable-dev-shm-usage`;
  - no background networking, component updates, extensions, sync or crash reporter;
  - a fixed window and scale (640×400), `--lang=en-US`, `TZ=UTC`, and the image's DejaVu fonts.

  `--single-process` was not needed. Which flags determinism needs was not tested. Every Cats confirmation in every run is the same PNG (`d390623351ec3f40…`), and so is every Dogs one (`b6f25aab…`) and every 500 page (`534a4542…`). A copy of the manifest that prints three PNGs as base64 (not committed, fingerprint `eb2d8d8d6510d4c7` twice) took them out of the guest; they are in the example's `screens/`.
- **What the browser changed about the known bug:** `C=12` alone loses votes with `../compose-voting`'s wget workload, but loses nothing at a browser's pace.
  - A vote takes about 0.3 s of guest time, and the .NET worker's 100 ms poll moves each vote into PostgreSQL before the next one.
  - So the loss needs the worker to fall behind, which this example makes happen with a kill.
- **What hydo's heal hides:** a service stopped by a fault is restarted at the heal. So an after-the-run check saw a working results page after `K=db@5+5` (an earlier image: OK `c3e107e35c19113f` twice). Only the check during the workload sees the outage.
- **Found natively** (the browser image unpacked in a private network namespace on the bare-metal machine): Chromium answers every load with `net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED` when the namespace has only `lo`. With `network: bridge` it has `eth0`, so it works.
- **The Mac (arm64),** with the Mac release installed into a scratch prefix and the second guest kernel:
  - `gui-mac.yaml` (4096 MiB, because the root is the initramfs in guest RAM) gives the initramfs `a3e7bb62…` (504,557,344 bytes, built in 11 minutes) and the data disk `8670640…`.

On the Mac's clock, the kill reached the worker before it had taken voter 4's vote.
  - Each run took 205–275 s of wall time on a Mac that other sessions were also using.
  - Every Cats confirmation is the PNG `23efcf607a2fdc8e…`. That is not the x86_64 PNG: the fonts, Skia and the CPU are the same kinds, but the builds differ.
  - The arm64 image was built only once, so its byte-for-byte reproducibility was not checked.

  - `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` pass for the driver (its own workspace).

## Milestone 170 — the onboarding skill's process apart from hydo's facts; a Claude Code plugin and `hydo skill update` (2026-11-07)

**Why (user decisions, 2026-11-07).** The onboarding skill mixed two things that change at different speeds: how to onboard a project (the process, which improves whenever someone learns something) and what a given hydo offers (the project format's keys, the commands and their options, the fault kinds, the limits, which change only with a hydo release). Shipped together inside `hydo`, a better process had to wait for a hydo release, and a skill copied into a repository could describe another hydo than the one installed. Decided: one skill folder in the Agent Skills format with the process only, its own version, and the oldest hydo it supports; every fact read from the installed hydo (`hydo guide <topic>`, `hydo guide schema`, every written file checked with `hydo build --check`); the skill checks first that hydo is installed and asks before installing it; no instructions downloaded while the skill runs; Claude Code gets the skill as a plugin from a marketplace in the repository, other tools through `hydo skill install` and a new `hydo skill update` that the user runs.

**The split.**
- **Process** (`skills/hydo-onboard/`, `metadata.version: "1.0.0"`, `metadata.hydo-min: "0.1.0"`, license Apache-2.0): SKILL.md (103 lines; it was 279) with step 0 (check hydo: `hydo --version`, or hydo 0.1.0's usage text; ask before installing; `hydo doctor`), "Facts: ask the installed hydo", then talk to the user, inventory, write the folder (each part pointing at its guide topic), `hydo build hydo/hydo.yaml --check` after every file, build and run, report, platforms; `references/install.md` (Homebrew on Apple Silicon, the release tarballs on Linux and the Mac, upgrading; `cargo install hydo` named as later), `inventory.md` (where to look in a repository), `choosing-checks.md` (which properties are worth checking: promises, not the code's present behaviour), `pitfalls.md` (what to look for in a project; the limits are left to `hydo guide hazards`). No `assets/`.
- **Facts** (`hydo/guide/`, compiled into `hydo` by hydo-agents' build.rs, so they always match the hydo that prints them): the ten former references, unchanged in substance, as topics (`capabilities`, `checks`, `composer`, `error-logs`, `faults`, `hazards`, `invariant-patterns`, `numbered-steps`, `outside-services`, `sdks`; links between them now written as `hydo guide <topic>`), two new topics with the facts that were in SKILL.md (`workflow`: the folder, the format rules, `hydo init`, the Compose import, where programs come from, the build and run commands; `services`: the service keys and guest settings), `examples/` (the redis-composed folder, still checked equal to `hydo/onboard/examples/redis-composed/hydo/`, and the miniflux manifest), `init/` (`hydo init`'s template and AGENTS.md section) and `overview.md`.
- **`hydo guide`** alone prints the hydo version, how to get the skill (the plugin commands, `hydo skill install`/`update`, `hydo guide skill` for any other tool) and the topic list; `hydo guide skill` prints the skill's SKILL.md; every earlier topic name answers, and so do the skill's old paths (`references/<topic>.md`, `assets/example-*`, `assets/hydo-init/*`). `hydo --version` (M169, merged into this branch: `hydo <version> (<commit>)`) is what the skill asks first; hydo 0.1.0 has none, and the skill recognises it by the usage text (its `hydo setup --check` names the version in its first line). With hydo 0.1.0 the skill's `hydo guide workflow` answers "no guide topic", and the skill then reads 0.1.0's `hydo guide`, which prints 0.1.0's whole old guide with the same topic names (checked with the published Mac 0.1.0 tarball).

**Claude Code plugin** (formats read from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces, `plugins-reference`, `plugins/marketplace-reference.md` and `plugins/loading.md` on 2026-11-07). `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repository root: marketplace `hydo`, one plugin entry `hydo-onboard` whose `source` is the skill folder itself, `./skills/hydo-onboard`, with `version` 1.0.0. With no `plugin.json` the entry is the plugin's manifest, and a plugin root with `SKILL.md` and no `skills/` loads as one skill, so the folder is shared by every tool without a copy or a symbolic link (the documentation says a relative-path plugin is copied into the cache with nothing outside its folder, and links that lead outside a plugin are refused). Users: `/plugin marketplace add kakoc/hydo`, then `/plugin install hydo-onboard@hydo` (README.md). `claude plugin validate .` (Claude Code 2.1.319): passed, also with `--strict`. Installed end to end in an isolated configuration (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in the scratch directory, so this Mac's own Claude Code configuration was never changed): `claude plugin marketplace add <worktree>` added `hydo`, `claude plugin install hydo-onboard@hydo` installed it (scope user, version 1.0.0, cached at `cache/hydo/hydo-onboard/1.0.0/` with exactly the skill's files), `claude plugin list` showed it enabled, `claude plugin details hydo-onboard` listed `Skills (1) hydo-onboard` (about 150 tokens always loaded, 1.4k on use). A `claude -p` session cannot run in an isolated configuration (it is not logged in), so the session test below used the project's `.claude/skills/` copy.

**`hydo skill update [--agent NAME ...] [--to DIR] [--user] [--force] [--version V] [--check] [--offline]`** (`hydo-cli` `src/skillupdate.rs`, with M162's `Fetcher`): the newest release is the highest `skill-v<version>` tag in the release list (`HYDO_RELEASE_API`, new, default `https://api.github.com/repos/kakoc/hydo/releases`; drafts, pre-releases and hydo's `v*` tags skipped); `SHA256SUMS` and `hydo-skill-<version>.tar.gz` come from `<HYDO_RELEASE_URL>/skill-v<version>/` over TLS (plain HTTP only to a loopback host), and the archive is accepted only with the sha256 the sums name. `hydo_agents::release::unpack` takes plain files and directories below `hydo-onboard/` only (links, devices, absolute paths, `..`, more than 2,000 entries or 16 MiB are refused, and the destination is deleted again on a refusal), the unpacked `SKILL.md` must be the hydo-onboard skill of the version asked for, and `hydo_agents::replace_dir` swaps each target folder in one step through two short-lived siblings that are deleted again. Without `--agent`/`--to` it updates every copy in this repository's and the home directory's `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills` that is a folder (not a symbolic link, as in hydo's own repository); a copy at the release's version is left alone, a newer one is kept unless `--version` asks; `--check` changes nothing (exit 0 up to date, 3 newer available); offline (`--offline`, `HYDO_OFFLINE`) it refuses before any request. `hydo skill install` now names the version it installed, and `hydo skill version` prints the carried skill's version. Tests (`src/skillupdate/tests.rs`, a local HTTP server, no real network): the newest tag chosen; an older copy updated with the release's files only (a file of the old version gone), the parent's other files and folders untouched and no temporary folder left; an up-to-date copy fetches only the list; a wrong sha256 refused with nothing changed; offline refused with no request; a newer copy kept, `--version` installs the older release, an unreleased version refused; a release whose SKILL.md has another version refused; a foreign folder, a symbolic link and plain HTTP to another host refused before any request; each `--agent` value's folder. `hydo_agents::release` tests: the archive keeps its bytes when the files' modes change, it unpacks, and seven bad archives are refused leaving nothing.

**The skill's release** (docs/RELEASING.md "Releasing the onboarding skill", new docs/PUBLISHING.md): `hydo/dist/skill/build-skill-release.sh` (refuses uncommitted skill changes; builds `hydo-skill-pack`, a new hydo-tools program over `hydo_agents::release::pack`: sorted entries, every time 0, owner 0:0, modes 0644 or 0755, gzip level 9 without a name or time) writes `hydo/dist/out/skill/hydo-skill-<version>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS`, packs twice and compares, checks the plugin entry's version and prints the tag `skill-v<version>`. Run on the merged branch: `hydo-skill-1.0.0.tar.gz` (6.3 kB, sha256 `d48ca650cd4fe2d2ecbbd372e48f80ae9f1cc53caf75513f518dc2149e75e0e1`), packed twice with the same bytes; served with its `SHA256SUMS` and a release list from a local web server (`HYDO_RELEASE_API`, `HYDO_RELEASE_URL`), `hydo skill update --check --to <empty dir>` said "not installed (release 1.0.0)" (exit 3), `hydo skill update --to <dir>` installed it (the folder equal to `skills/hydo-onboard/`, nothing else in the directory), and a second run said "already at hydo-onboard 1.0.0". Nothing was tagged, released or pushed.

**Checks.** `skill_check` (10 tests) also checks `metadata.version` and `metadata.hydo-min`, that the marketplace lists `./skills/hydo-onboard` with the same version, that the folder holds nothing Claude Code would load as another plugin component, and that every `hydo guide <topic>` written in the skill (19) or the guide (64) names a topic the guide has. skills-ref was not available on this Mac (installing it was not allowed here), so only the test's own implementation of its rules ran. `public_content` accepts the owner also in `api.github.com/repos/<owner>/hydo` and in the marketplace shorthand `<owner>/hydo` (new positive and negative cases). The CLI goldens were re-recorded with `HYDO_BLESS=1` and reviewed: only the help text (`--version`, `skill update`), `hydo guide` and `--list`, the edited `composer` topic's and MANIFEST.md's hashes, the skill usage and install lines (now with the version) and the installed files changed; `agents.jsonl` gained `guide skill|overview|references/composer.md|references/install.md|examples/...|init/...`, `skill version` and two `skill update` refusals. The input sets of hydo-build's and hydo-manifest's equivalence goldens and hydo-composer's plan list name the three moved example manifests by path: only those rows were re-recorded (the paths, and the `--check` answers and check digests that print a path, 7 characters shorter; a full `HYDO_BLESS=1` would also have taken in `hydo/dist/*/third-party.json`, which is tracked but was never recorded, and shifted thousands of mutant rows, so it was not used), and in `composer.sha256` only chunk 0 of the two renamed plans, the one that holds the folder's path, changed. No engine, image, fingerprint or the project format changed (format 1).

**End to end on this Mac.** A scratch release root: the published Mac 0.1.0 tarball's files with this tree's `bin/hydo` and skill folder (its `SHA256SUMS` rewritten for them; `hydo doctor`: all checks passed). A scratch git repository `kvstore` with only a README (Redis 7.2.4 with `appendfsync always`, and the promise that an acknowledged SET is never lost) and the aarch64 Redis files; `hydo skill install --agent claude` (1.0.0). Then `claude -p` (Claude Code 2.1.319, 46 turns, 230 s), asked to onboard it with the skill: it invoked the skill, ran `hydo --version`, `hydo guide workflow`, `--list`, `services`, `composer`, `schema`, `checks`, `capabilities`, `error-logs`, `faults`, `invariant-patterns` and `examples/...`, ran `hydo init`, wrote `hydo/hydo.yaml` (one service, the knob `R` for `appendfsync`, the fault kinds without `disk`, with its reason), a SET driver, an anytime GET, a final check and an `eventually` check, ran `hydo build --check` until OK, built the image and ran `hydo run "disk=none | run"`: `HYDO-ORACLE: OK`, 43 commands, `fp=c81fc161c8288de3`; run again by hand: the same fingerprint. Its report listed each check for review, its assumptions and what it could not decide. Friction seen: the session's tool permissions did not include `rm`, so the skeleton's two placeholder files stayed (it turned them into aliases and said so); `hydo init` does not add the run directory `hydo-out/` to `.gitignore`.

**Left** (AGENTS.md open item 52): publishing (tag `skill-v1.0.0` and its assets, pushing the marketplace to `main`) is the user's; `hydo skill update` was never run against the real GitHub API; skills-ref; the marketplace install from GitHub (`kakoc/hydo`) can only be tried once this commit is on `main`; `hydo init` and `hydo-out/` in `.gitignore`; a released hydo with the new topics (until then a released hydo is 0.1.0, which the skill handles through its fallback).

### Milestone 167 — DONE (continuous integration on GitHub Actions: fmt, clippy and the release-mode workspace tests on Linux and macOS runners, the guest agent and the store reader on Linux, the five SDKs; the tests that depended on the machine running them made independent of it; 2026-11-07)

Branch `worktree-agent-a8ce690560951e88f` from `main` = `afa1186`, `main` = `9149861` (M170) merged in, tried on the public repository as the branch `ci` (nothing else pushed). (`main` at M169 failed `cargo fmt --check` on one call in `hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/runs.rs`; M170's `main` has it formatted.) Nothing in it boots a guest: a GitHub runner has neither the hvx module nor access to Hypervisor.framework. `docs/CI.md` is the reference (what runs, what is skipped where and why, durations).

- **The workflow** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`; on every push and pull request; `permissions: contents: read`, the checkout keeps no credentials, every action pinned by commit, no secret, `bash -eo pipefail` for every step): `rust (ubuntu-24.04)` and `rust (macos-15)` run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked --release --workspace --no-fail-fast` (382 tests pass on Linux, 381 on macOS, 2 ignored) and a step that prints the run-time reasons of the tests that skip; skills-ref 0.1.1 from PyPI is installed for the skill check. `guest programs (ubuntu-24.04)` tests `hydo/crates/hydo-agent` (including the agent as PID 1 of its own namespaces, which needs `sudo -n`: the runner has it) and `hydo/crates/hydo-read`. `sdks` runs the Rust SDK, the Rust test SDK, the Go SDK (`sdk/go` and the order service's frozen copy in `hydo/stack`) with Go 1.26.5 (every case but the one `emit_line` case runs; Go 1.27 would skip five invalid-UTF-8 cases), the Python SDK with 3.9 and 3.13, the JavaScript SDK with Node 22. Caching: `Swatinem/rust-cache` (registry and compiled dependencies), `setup-go`'s module cache.
- **Durations:** the `rust` jobs take 15 to 25 minutes, almost all compiling the workspace with the release profile (11 minutes on Linux, 18 on macOS with the dependencies cached; the workspace's own crates are always compiled again, since a fresh checkout's files are newer than any cached build); the tests take 3 and 5 minutes. The other two jobs take about a minute each.
- **Made independent of the machine** (each failed or could fail for the machine's reasons, never for hydo's): the `hydo` command's `cli_matches_golden` (package `hydo` since M169, directory `hydo/crates/hydo-cli`) (a runner has `kvm` loaded, so `module load --dry-run` planned `sudo rmmod kvm`; Ubuntu's `debugfs` on PATH changed how a Mac case reads an image; the bare-metal machine has hvx loaded): `hydo` reads the host's module state (`/proc/modules`, `/proc/locks`, `/sys/module`, `/dev`, `/etc/udev/rules.d`) under the new developer switch `HYDO_CLI_HOST_ROOT` (`/` when unset; printed paths and writes unchanged; in `hydo/crates/hydo-config/INVENTORY.md`), and the test sets an empty directory there and a PATH whose directories with a `debugfs` are replaced by symlink copies without it. its `agents_equivalence`, `hydo-compose`'s `equivalence` and `hydo-build`'s `oci` set the umask to 022 (the first two also copy their inputs with git's checkout modes): with umask 002 `agents_as_recorded` and `oci_staging_matches_hydo_oci` failed on the Mac, as the M158 addendum saw on the bare-metal machine. The JavaScript and Python shared-case children read a monotonic clock that advances 1 ns per reading: every case expects `elapsed_ms` 0, and on a busy runner the JavaScript child once measured 1 ms between `begin` and `done`; the Go and Rust SDKs keep the system clock (their bytes are inside recorded images). No recorded answer changed.
- **Skipped on a runner, with the reason printed:** `hydo-errors`' `recorded_files` (M94's run results are not in the repository), `public_content`'s list of concrete values (git-ignored; the generic patterns run), `hydo-read`'s five live-store tests. Ignored on purpose: `hydo-history`'s `dump_cases` and `hydo-compose`'s registry recorder.

### Milestone 172 — DONE (the two missing pieces of the 0.2.0 release prepared, nothing published: the Mac programs signed with the project's Developer ID and notarized, with the signatures published apart from the programs so that the signed tarball is reproducible from the source by anyone; the KVM engine in the Linux release with its guest kernel and its license entry; both releases built twice to the same bytes and verified from clean prefixes, the Linux one with hvx and with KVM; the version stays 0.1.0 until the release; 2026-11-07)

User decision 2026-11-07: everything ships together as 0.2.0. This milestone is the preparation; the version bump, the tag, the publication and the Homebrew tap change are left for release day (below). Branch `worktree-agent-a9342004e336c8394` from `main` = `33355f5`. The candidates were built from its commit `089c187`; a first set built from `a5f7780` gave the same values everywhere but showed one defect (the built-in modes, below), so everything was built and checked again.

**Part 1: signed, notarized and reproducible Mac programs** (docs/design/signing.md).
- *Design.* `build-release.sh` builds the tarball unsigned and reproducibly as before; its packing step is now `hydo/dist/mac/pack-release.sh` (`SHA256SUMS`, no extended attributes, times 0, sorted GNU tar without owners, `gzip -n`). `hydo/dist/mac/sign-release.sh <unsigned tarball> <out>` (the key's owner, once per release) signs `bin/hydo`, `bin/hydo-build`, `bin/hydo-fetch-image` and `bin/hydo-hvm` with `codesign --force --options runtime --timestamp -s "Developer ID Application: Konstantin Matsiushonak (5C3JA2N5X6)"` (`bin/hydo-hvm` with `--entitlements hv/hvm/hv.entitlements`, the only entitlement), submits the four in one zip with `xcrun notarytool submit --keychain-profile hydo-notary --wait --timeout 3h` (it must be Accepted; the answer and the log are kept), and writes the signatures asset `hydo-mac-<version>-signatures.tar.gz` with `hydo-release signatures extract`; then it makes the signed tarball from the unsigned one with `hydo/dist/mac/attach-signatures.sh`, exactly as anyone can. A ticket cannot be stapled to a plain command-line program (stapler takes apps, disk images and installer packages); Gatekeeper finds it online by the code-directory hash, which is inside the signature and therefore the same in every attached copy.
- *What a signature file is.* Comparing a linker-signed Mach-O with the same program after codesign (first on a small test program, then on the four programs): the signature blob at the end of the file is replaced at the same offset, and three header numbers change (the blob size in `LC_CODE_SIGNATURE`, `__LINKEDIT`'s file size and its memory size rounded up to 16 KiB); nothing else. `hydo/crates/hydo-release/src/signatures.rs`: `extract` takes the blob as codesign wrote it and checks that `attach` of it to the unsigned program gives the signed program byte for byte (it refuses a moved signature or bytes after it); `attach` cuts the unsigned program at the blob's offset, appends the blob and sets the three numbers; the asset holds `SIGNATURES` (unsigned sha256, signed sha256, path), `bin/<program>.sig` and a README, with fixed times, owners and order; `attach_tree` checks both sha256 values of every program (another build is refused by sha256). Three unit tests; `hydo-release signatures extract|attach` is the command line.
- *`hydo setup` and `hydo doctor`.* With `bin/hydo-hvm` as `SHA256SUMS` lists it and already validly signed with the hypervisor entitlement, setup takes no step for it (its record has no `signed` line); an engine without the entitlement (an unsigned build, a cargo build) is signed ad hoc as before. A new test, `a_signed_mac_release_is_not_signed_again`. `hydo doctor` on the Mac prints who signed the engine ("signature: Developer ID Application: …", or "ad hoc").
- *The proof* (from `089c187`). Two unsigned builds on this Mac from a `git archive` at one tree path (`/private/tmp/hydo-m172-tree`), from clean target directories (460 s and 487 s): the same tarball, 30,526,272 bytes, sha256 `d835fd9e5856e6cdd85c5191fb5361ec2d7b1d88a039f88caacfbdea6ba9ee0a`, and the same sources archive, 690,040,177 bytes, `8a50ff50f6cff21bd847fbba40743b75d29593c95235e3c92368d77ebcbcc951`; unpacking the unsigned tarball and packing it again with `pack-release.sh` gives its bytes again. `sign-release.sh` on the first build: notarization submission `0acf0466-2915-4eeb-b3f1-85e0b81aba53` Accepted within about a minute ("Ready for distribution", no issues; the `a5f7780` set's submission `30707b5b-…` was Accepted as fast); the programs' sha256 unsigned → signed: hydo `db8108b2…` → `fecc5f72…`, hydo-build `7ad55e58…` → `1559ccda…`, hydo-fetch-image `e6a50be0…` → `46ba927c…`, hydo-hvm `0a9f8c35…` → `906f2b9d…`; the signatures asset is 79,729 bytes, `54d10172ab5e579c5065c90cc0d74d666596e4f6061b7ee775896141f7e3c9c3` (blobs of 40,784, 25,408, 25,376 and 20,464 bytes); the signed tarball is 30,458,556 bytes, `f4cd4eb795255c9eda6cf5477f6eb4ad2fc372d63f23d6eed8833195b7c468f7`. Then `attach-signatures.sh` with the saved asset on the **second** unsigned build gave `f4cd4eb7…` byte for byte, and its four programs pass `codesign --verify --strict`. Between the unsigned and the signed tree only the four programs and `SHA256SUMS` differ. (The same proof on the `a5f7780` set: unsigned `5a8dea46…` twice, signed `f6659f38…` reproduced from its asset `fd702211…`.) Codesign asked once for the key; the first prompt was denied by mistake and allowed on the retry.
- *Verified from a clean prefix* (the signed tarball, a fake HOME, the quarantine attribute put on `bin/*` as a browser would, stubs for Python, pip, Go, cargo, rustc, rustup, Nix, cc, gcc, g++, clang, make, xcrun and Docker first on PATH; no stub called): `install.sh --add-to-path`; setup's record has no `signed` line, and `hydo setup --check` and a second `hydo setup` say nothing to do (402 files and store entries, 53 pinned); `hydo doctor` all checks passed with the Developer ID line; each program `codesign --verify --strict` valid, `codesign -dvv` the Developer ID, team `5C3JA2N5X6`, `flags=0x10000(runtime)` and a timestamp; `spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature -v` "accepted, source=Notarized Developer ID" for all four (`--type execute` answers "rejected (the code is valid but does not seem to be an app)", as for any plain program); the Redis image `a3447614…`, data disk `9ddfc929…`; docs/REBASELINE.md 13.4's Mac values, each twice: `67e5d6469f1a90a5`, `a6870a92a1bbf0ae`, `ed3651af0bf0fb7e`, `aad758f1a6d55892`, `0441476f5fd74d0b`, `d6120f56fdef3f28`; `hydo repro` of the cut run reproduced; `hydo explore --seeds 1-20 --strategy swarm --workers 2` 11 failures, all reproduced, `hydo repro hydo-out/explore` 13 of 13; ledger-spin `aa732142c0f5567f` and `3b4dd4910d2a6123`, each twice. ### Milestone 171 — a fast development loop: test tiers, the `ci` profile, cargo-nextest, a local and a CI compile cache, golden pins that do not fail on their own (2026-11-07)

**Why (user decision, 2026-11-07: "the goal is also to move fast").** Several agents work in parallel, each in its own git worktree, and each built the whole workspace from scratch (minutes and 1.5 to 5 GB per worktree); CI compiled the workspace's own crates from scratch on every push (the cache kept only the dependencies) and ran every test in release mode, 22 to 24 minutes per push; and golden tests that pin the sha256 of the repository files they read failed on edits that changed none of their answers. No check may be dropped. Branch `worktree-agent-a59a5638e4f1b8f2d` from `main` = `33355f5` (M167 merged), tried on the public repository as the branch `ci-speed` (nothing else pushed).

**Measured first** (docs/CI.md "Where the time went"; this Mac shared with other agents' builds at load averages of 10 to 100). CI before (run 42379987465): `rust` jobs 22.8 min (Linux) and 24.0 min (macOS), of which compiling 17 min 16 s and 17 min 51 s, the tests about 4.5 and 5 min, the documentation examples 2 and 3 s. Locally, `cargo test --release --workspace --no-run` from scratch: 534 s, the workspace's crates 6,039 CPU-seconds against 305 for all dependencies: the release profile's thin LTO with one codegen unit makes every one of the 110 test programs and 20 programs a whole-program optimisation (about 100 s each under load; `hydo` 208 s). The tests: 317 s sequentially with `cargo test` (270 s on the Linux runner); the slowest are single tests over recorded corpora: `hydo-control::corpus` 100 to 135 s, `hydo-world::xcheck` 57 to 63 s, `hydo::equivalence` 27 s, `hydo-grpc::streams` 19 to 23 s, `hydo-control::features` 20 to 26 s, `hydo-build::equivalence` 18 to 20 s, `hydo-kvm::engine` 16 s, `hydo::agents_equivalence` 15 s, `hydo-manifest`, `hydo-composer`, `hydo-control::m123` and `::corpus_net` and `hydo-explore::corpus` 8 to 15 s each.

**The `ci` profile** (`Cargo.toml`): `inherits = "release"`, `lto = false`, `codegen-units = 16`, `incremental = false`, `strip = false`: the release profile's optimisation and semantics (no debug assertions, no overflow checks), so a test behaves as under `--release`. A cold build of every test program: 132 s (against 534 s), the workspace's crates 760 CPU-seconds (eight times less). Its tests run as fast as release's (every test with nextest: 121 s against 141 s). Nothing that ships uses it.

**cargo-nextest 0.9.148** (pinned by sha256 in the workflow; `.config/nextest.toml`, profile `ci`): one process per test, the test programs side by side, JUnit times in `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`, and the output of the tests that print why they skip something shown at the end. Every test passes under it (470 run, 2 ignored as before). One change was needed: `hydo-explore`'s `fake_engine` has its own harness (`harness = false`) and now answers libtest's `--list --format terse` (its 17 scenarios, no ignored ones) and runs one scenario for `--exact <name>`; without arguments it behaves as before.

**Test tiers** (`ci/test-tiers.txt`, `ci/tier-filter.sh`, `ci/affected-packages.sh`; docs/CI.md "Test tiers"). Every test binary has one line: `fast` (101 binaries: every push, and the full tier) or `full` (11: `hydo-control::corpus`, `::corpus_net`, `::features`, `::m123`, `hydo-world::xcheck`, `hydo-grpc::streams`, `hydo-build::equivalence`, `hydo-manifest::equivalence`, `hydo-composer::equivalence`, `hydo-explore::corpus` and `hydo-history::doctest`: the full tier, and a push that changes a file of their own package). The per-push tier runs the `fast` tests of the packages the change can affect: the workspace member owning each changed file and every member that depends on it (normal, dev and build dependencies from `cargo metadata`; a changed `tests/` file also selects the packages whose sources or tests name that crate's directory); any file outside the members, an unknown base or no changed file selects every package; `hydo-release` and `hydo-agents` always run. Checked on a temporary commit touching `hydo-image/src/lib.rs` and `hydo-schema-compat/tests/rules.rs`: 16 packages selected, the two as directly changed. The full tier (`.github/workflows/ci-full.yml`) runs `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` on both runners every night, on demand, and on a pull request labelled `full-ci`. **Nothing is dropped:** `hydo-release`'s new test `test_tiers` compares the file with `cargo metadata` (every test, bin, lib, example and bench target with `test = true`, every lib with `doctest = true`) and fails on a missing, unknown, doubled or mis-tiered line, and on a documentation example rustdoc would test in a library with `doctest = false`.

**Documentation examples.** 25 libraries had none and one (`hydo-history`) had one `no_run` example; they cost 2 s (Linux) and 3 s (macOS) per CI run. The 24 libraries without examples (all but `hydo-history`) have `doctest = false`; `hydo-history::doctest` is in the full tier. The time saved per full run is those 2 to 3 seconds; the per-push tier runs no documentation example (nextest cannot).

**The compile cache** (docs/CI.md "The compile cache"; user decisions 2026-11-07: no cache shared between machines, no remote cache server or bucket; locally a cache for hydo only, inside the repository). `.cargo/config.toml` sets `build.rustc-wrapper = ".cargo/rustc-wrapper.sh"` (a bash script: dash, Ubuntu's `/bin/sh`, drops environment variables whose names contain a hyphen, such as `CARGO_BIN_EXE_hydo-agent`, which broke the guest agent's test on the first try). With sccache on PATH it runs the compile through sccache with `SCCACHE_DIR=<main checkout>/.sccache` (git-ignored; a worktree finds the main checkout through its `.git` file), a server port derived from that path, `SCCACHE_CONF=/dev/null` and every remote backend variable unset, 8 GB at most; without sccache, with `HYDO_SCCACHE=0`, and for every compile whose output directory is a release profile's, it runs rustc itself. `.cargo/rustc-wrapper.sh --show-stats` reports. sccache 0.18.0 is installed on this Mac as `~/.cargo/bin/sccache` from its GitHub release (sha256 in docs/CI.md). `dev.sh` excludes `.sccache`. Measured: a second build of every test program after removing the target directory took 46 s (100 % of the 145 cacheable compiles from the cache); a copy of the tree at another path took 87 s (102 hits: every third-party library; 43 misses: the workspace's own libraries, whose keys contain the absolute `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; `SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` does not normalise it for Rust, tried); programs, test programs and procedural macros are never cached (sccache does not cache linked crate types: 162 of 318 calls). A new commit's `BUILT_FROM_COMMIT` (hydo-image's build script) was a cache miss, so a build script's value is part of the key. CI's `rust` jobs use sccache 0.18.0 with the GitHub Actions cache (`mozilla-actions/sccache-action` pinned by commit), readable and writable by this repository's workflows only.

**Release bytes unchanged.** `hydo`, `hydo-world` and `hydo-grpc` built with `--release` from `git archive` trees of `main` and of this branch at one path with one `hydo/COMMIT`: the same sha256 (`7aaf482d…`, `83327eed…`, `43765d2f…`; the release profile bypasses the cache, and `doctest = false` is not part of Cargo's metadata hash). The pinned recipes give the pinned bytes: `hydo/grpcgen/build-client.sh amd64 arm64` `3926d137…` and `fd762fa0…`, `hydo/crates/hydo-world/build.sh` `082592ae…`. No engine, fingerprint or image changed.

**Golden pins** (docs/CI.md "Golden tests and their pinned inputs"). `hydo-build`'s and `hydo-manifest`'s equivalence tests (`I` and `G` lines), `hydo-explore`'s goldens (`input` lines, `tests/support/mod.rs` `check_inputs`), `hydo-control`'s goldens (`check_golden`), `hydo-composer`'s plan folders and `hydo-errors`' known-errors pins: a digest that differs is printed and named in the failure when an answer differs, but no longer fails the test by itself; the input set stays pinned (a new, missing or reordered input of an explorer golden fails; a vanished file changes its answers). No golden was re-recorded. Checked: a description edited in `hydo/dist/linux/third-party.json` passes both equivalence tests (each prints the file); a comment added to `hydo/onboard/examples/redis/hydo.yaml` passes `hydo-explore::corpus`, `::identity` and `hydo-control::corpus_net`; a changed readiness command in the same file fails `hydo-build::equivalence` (7 of 7,430 answers) and `hydo-manifest::equivalence`, naming the file.

The full tier (`cargo test --locked --release --workspace` through sccache): 23.4 min (Linux) and 31.0 min (macOS) with a cold cache (run 42386413032), and 18.1 min (Linux) and 28.7 min (macOS) with a warm cache (run 42390523813): the release profile's link-time optimisation of every test program, which no cache holds, is most of it. ### Milestone 173 — DONE (libSQL's server onboarded as an outside user would, on the KVM engine: two durability findings in sqld, two silent passes in hydo fixed)

Part of an exploration round (user, 2026-11-07): onboard real projects with only the skill and the `hydo` command, keep each as an example, and write down what hydo lacked. Example `hydo/onboard/examples/libsql-replica/` (sqld 0.24.33, a primary and a read replica, on the build machine with `--backend kvm`); its `RESULTS.md` has the schedules, fingerprints (each verdict twice), the friction log, what a ready-made SQL workload generator should offer, and "What hydo lacked". Workload: `sqlgen` (Rust, seeded bank transfers and list-append transactions, batch and interactive, routed to either node); checks: the bank total, list-append histories (`serializable` for all, `strict-serializable` for the primary's view) and the replica converging to the primary. Findings: (1) sqld's default `durability_mode` (relaxed, `synchronous=NORMAL`) loses acknowledged transactions at a power cut (knob `D`; `strong` passes `407e8763e1a87215`, `D=relaxed` fails `34da9bd30009d4fe`); (2) sqld forgets its durability setting on any restart (found blind by `--strategy process`, 4 of 100, `c0b2e4ada71292ca`; confirmed in Docker after `kill -9` and a clean stop); no isolation anomaly; the replica took 47 s to catch up after a lossy link. Fixed in hydo: a check's verdict line must start with `HYDO-ORACLE:` (hydo-check's usage text, which contains the marker mid-line, had become a verdict); the explorer reads the fault space from any image with `/etc/hydo/hydo.yaml`, not only `explore-ob-*` names (a renamed image silently got the stack's services and 50 schedules passed). Seen and handed to an investigation: on one image KVM runs from the explorer's S1 snapshot and from a fresh boot gave different fingerprints with the same verdict. First green run after 16 minutes, everything in about 1 h 40 min.

### Milestone 174 — DONE (Medusa onboarded as an outside user would, on the KVM engine: a commerce backend with PostgreSQL, Redis and a faked Stripe behind TLS)

The same exploration round. Example `hydo/onboard/examples/medusa/` (Medusa 2.18.0, PostgreSQL 15, Redis 7, Stripe payments faked with `fakes:` behind a TLS front made of a test CA, an `alpine/socat` service and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, on the build machine with `--backend kvm`, about 45 s per run); its `RESULTS.md` has the schedules, fingerprints (each verdict twice), the friction log and "What hydo lacked". Findings: two refunds of one order at the same moment each create an order change with the same version, and the order's items are written twice (found blind twice; minimal schedule a kill of Medusa plus a pause of Redis, `be3b9a6efa1c155a`; Medusa's issue tracker not checked); a capture Stripe performed but answered with 500 stays out of Medusa's books (partly the fake's: real Stripe's signed webhook would correct it; `01ff126583889ab6`). Held: no acknowledged order lost, no order paid twice, no oversell across checkouts, no money held for a failed checkout. Fixed in hydo: fakes accept bracketed form and query names (`form:metadata[session_id]`, as Stripe's SDK sends); `hydo compose` gives a volume on `/data` its own directory when another service keeps a volume on the data disk; the public-content test reads `name:1.8.0.3` as an image tag, not an address. The manifest needs a hydo with the bracketed-name fix (`RESULTS.md` names the 0.1.0 workaround). What hydo lacked most: the reason a service failed to start (four of the first five runs said only `ERROR service start (medusa)`), TLS for fakes, a way to look at a run's final state without changing the image, a writable layer for image services (15 tmpfs mounts found by trial). First green run after 23 minutes, first blind finding after about 45.

### Milestone 175 — DONE (the KVM engine: a run from S1 equals a fresh boot wherever S1 lands)

Found in M173: on one libSQL image every KVM run the explorer started from S1 gave another fingerprint than `hydo repro` of the same schedule from a fresh boot, with the same verdict. Cause: the host's SNAP is served at the top of the run loop, before the engine decides to inject an interrupt; a fresh boot's vCPU still reports `ready_for_interrupt_injection = 1` from its last exit and injects at once, while a vCPU restored from S1 is new, reports 0 until its first `KVM_RUN` (the `kvm_run` output fields are not part of the state `KVM_SET_*` loads), asks for an interrupt window first and counts one more exit, so it runs one exit (2.5 µs of guest time) behind. Only an S1 that lands on a pending interrupt is affected (8 of 21 boot step sizes on the Redis image; not the default step, which is why `kvm-check.sh`'s S1 check never saw it). Fix (`hydo-kvm/src/vmm.rs`): `XSnap` keeps the vCPU's run flags and a restore gives them back, as the rewind mode's checkpoints (M161) already did; the scripted vCPU now behaves like KVM's, and `tests/engine.rs` takes S1 at each of the first 40 boot stops (fails at stop 20 without the fix). After it, 0 of 21 step sizes differ; `kvm-check.sh` 16 of 16 with every recorded value, the stack's reproducers from S1 and from a fresh boot unchanged; no KVM fingerprint was published, so the epoch stays. M173's other KVM note (two simultaneous fresh runs that differed once) did not reproduce (three pairs, one fingerprint) and stays unexplained. docs/design/kvm-engine.md "A run from S1 against a fresh boot".

### Milestone 176 — DONE (TigerBeetle onboarded as an outside user would, on hvx: one replica runs unmodified, a cluster does not fit; no real finding)

The same exploration round as M173 and M174. Example `hydo/onboard/examples/tigerbeetle/` (`hydo/hydo.yaml` three replicas, `hydo/hydo-single.yaml` one; the release binary fetched by `fetch-tigerbeetle.sh`; on the bare-metal machine with hvx); its `RESULTS.md` has the schedules, fingerprints (each verdict twice), 17 friction items and "What hydo lacked". One replica runs unmodified (its I/O stack, AES-NI and AVX2 under `guest.cpu: v3`) on 0.17.9, 0.16.45 and 0.16.29, each schedule twice with one fingerprint. Three replicas do not fit: each allocates and touches about 2.1 GiB at start (1.35 GiB in development mode), the x86_64 guest has at most 3072 MiB, and the OOM killer ends two replicas during provisioning (`ERROR provision failed`, `da2a2b47273222ec` twice). No real finding: with an honest disk 50 explored schedules lost no acknowledged transfer; the swarm exploration's 10 failures of 20 all need a disk fault and are TigerBeetle's documented behaviour for a replica with no peer to repair from (stopping on I/O errors, refusing to start on a lying disk plus a cut). The findings of its published analyses that hydo's faults could reach need three replicas; the rest need faults hydo lacks (corruption or loss of one replica's file, upgrades). A false finding cost 57 minutes: the check looked up acknowledged ids in `$HYDO_OUTCOMES`, which is empty in the recovery boot after a power cut; the disk image at the cut held every transfer. Fixed in hydo: the guide says so (composer and check-pattern topics); `hydo compose` warns about `network_mode: host` (peers named `0.0.0.0:<port>` must become their `addr:`, or import with `--network loopback`). What hydo lacked most: more guest memory or one guest per service, the unknown outcomes carried into the recovery boot, why provisioning failed and a look at the final state, faults on one service's storage, an upgrade fault, a usable `hydo` straight from a checkout (version 0.0.0, doctor 10 failures). First green run 85 minutes after the start (25 of them work; 59 minutes waiting for another session's quiet window).
