##### Continuous integration (M167, M171)

- Until M171, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ran on every push and pull request of the public repository: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` on GitHub's Linux x86_64 and macOS Apple Silicon runners (15 to 25 minutes, almost all of it compiling the workspace with the release profile); the guest agent's and the store reader's own workspaces on Linux (the agent as PID 1 in a namespace too, with the runner's sudo); the Rust, Rust test, Go 1.26.5 (`sdk/go` and the frozen copy in `hydo/stack`), Python 3.9 and 3.13 and Node 22 SDK tests. Actions pinned by commit, `contents: read`, no secrets. Nothing boots a guest there. `docs/CI.md` lists what runs, every test skipped or partly run on a runner with its reason, and the tests made host-independent in M167 (the CLI test's host root `HYDO_CLI_HOST_ROOT` and PATH without `debugfs`, umask 022 and checkout modes in three tests, a 1-ns clock in the JavaScript and Python shared-case children). A change that makes a test depend on the machine (a loaded module, a tool on PATH, the umask, the clock's speed) fails there.
- **Two test tiers and a compile cache (M171, user decision 2026-11-07: "move fast" without dropping a check; docs/CI.md):** `ci.yml` is the per-push tier: fmt, clippy, then `cargo nextest run --cargo-profile ci` (cargo-nextest 0.9.148, pinned by sha256) with the `fast` tests (`ci/tier-filter.sh`) of the packages the change can affect (`ci/affected-packages.sh`: the owning workspace member and every package that depends on it; any file outside the members selects all), plus the `full` binaries of the packages it touches directly. `ci-full.yml` is the full tier: `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` on Linux and macOS, nightly, on demand and before a release (docs/RELEASING.md step 1). `ci/test-tiers.txt` names every test binary with its tier (`fast`, or `full` for the ten large recorded corpora and `hydo-history`'s documentation example); `hydo-release`'s `test_tiers` fails when a binary has no line, a line names none, or a library with `doctest = false` (24 of them now) has an example. The `ci` profile (`Cargo.toml`) is the release profile without link-time optimisation and with 16 codegen units, for tests only. Compile cache: `.cargo/config.toml` runs every compile through `.cargo/rustc-wrapper.sh`, which uses sccache 0.18.0 when it is on PATH with this repository's own local cache (`<main checkout>/.sccache/`, git-ignored, shared by all worktrees, its own server port, no remote) and runs rustc itself otherwise, with `HYDO_SCCACHE=0`, and for every release-profile compile (release tarballs and pinned guest programs never touch the cache; checked: same bytes). CI's sccache uses the GitHub Actions cache only. Golden tests' pinned input digests (hydo-build, hydo-manifest, hydo-explore, hydo-control, hydo-composer, hydo-errors) no longer fail on their own: the answers decide, and a failure names the changed inputs. Numbers: per push, the Linux `rust` job takes about 3 minutes with warm caches (6.5 with none) and macOS about 4.5 (8 with none), against 22.8 and 24.0 minutes before; the full tier takes 18 (Linux) and 29 (macOS) minutes with a warm cache, 23 and 31 with none; locally a new worktree builds every test program in 87 s with the shared cache (132 s with none; 534 s with the release profile before) and runs the fast tier in 25 s. sccache 0.18.0 and cargo-nextest 0.9.148 are installed on this Mac in `~/.cargo/bin` (versions and sha256 in docs/CI.md); an agent in a worktree uses the cache without doing anything, and should run `cargo nextest run --cargo-profile ci --workspace -E "$(sh ci/tier-filter.sh fast)"` while working and the full `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` before a merge.
- **Releases publish themselves to the registries (M186, user decision 2026-11-08; docs/PUBLISHING.md "Publishing from GitHub Actions"):** `.github/workflows/release.yml` starts when a tag `v<version>` appears (creating the GitHub release with `gh release create` creates it; docs/RELEASING.md steps 7 and 10) or by hand with `dry_run` (default on; on a branch the version is `hydo/VERSION`'s). Jobs: `check` (every package has the tag's version; the GitHub release of the tag is published with its four tarballs and `SHA256SUMS`, waited for up to 45 minutes), `packages` (calls `packages.yml`), then `crates` (the 20 crates of docs/PUBLISHING.md's order and `hydo-assert`, `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`, a second token after 20 minutes), `pypi` (`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`, attestations), `npm` (npm 11.21.0, `--provenance`) and `go` (the annotated tag `sdk/go/v<version>` through the API, then a proxy fetch), each in the GitHub environment `release` with `id-token: write` (go: `contents: write` only), each skipping what its registry has, so a re-run is safe. `.github/workflows/packages.yml` is the packages' dry run on every pull request and push to main that changes one (`rehearse.sh` on Linux and macOS, sdist and wheel with `twine check --strict`, `npm pack --dry-run`). `hydo/dist/registries.sh` holds the jobs' logic (order, versions, release check, published lookups, the publishing loop). No token is stored anywhere; the one-time setup (a trusted publisher per crate, on PyPI and on npm: the repository `kakoc/hydo`, workflow `release.yml`, environment `release`) is the user's (open item 63). Validated with actionlint 1.7.12 and local runs of every read-only command; no run on GitHub yet.
- **One test program per crate (M185; docs/CI.md "One test program per crate"):** in every workspace crate with more than one integration-test file the files are modules of one program `it` (`tests/main.rs`, written by `ci/consolidate-tests.sh`; `autotests = false` and `[[test]] it`), so a test is `cargo test -p <package> --test it <file>::`; kept apart: hydo-explore's `fake_engine` (its own main) and hydo-grpc-gen's `client` (it sets process environment variables). Targets without a unit test have `test = false`. `ci/test-tiers.txt` keeps `<package>::<file>` lines and `ci/tier-filter.sh` turns a folded file's line into a test-name filter. After adding a `tests/<name>.rs` (or merging a branch that adds one) run `sh ci/consolidate-tests.sh` and `cargo fmt`; CI runs it with `--check`, and hydo-release's `test_tiers` fails when a test file is in no program.

##### The results format (M115)

- One versioned model for what runs and explorations report (crate `hydo/crates/hydo-results`; `hydo/PRODUCT.md` "Where the results are"; experimental until hydo 1.0, additions only from version 1 on). A run directory holds `result.json` (one `run` document: schedule, image path and SHA-256, engine, verdict, fingerprints, findings, the run's property table, error-log analysis, consoles); an exploration directory holds `events.jsonl` (written while it runs: `start`, a `run` record for every run with its `role` — `first`, `rerun`, `shrink`, `minimal`, `error-shrink`, `error-minimal`, `trace`, `probe`, `manual`, `branch` —, `shrink`, `end`) and `exploration.json` (configuration, summary, failures with reproductions, shrinks, error kinds, property table, liveness, freeze-sweep stages). Findings have one shape: `kind` (`invariant`, `assertion`, `history-check`, `error-log`), `id`, `status`, `message`, `details`. Every record has `"v": 1` and a `"type"`.
- Kept as views: `report.md` (made from `exploration.json` by `hydo_explore::md`; `hydo report` prints the same text from the document) and the printed summary line. Kept as inputs or working files, not results: the consoles, `engine.log`, `worker-*.err`, `points.txt` (`--sweep-dry`), the `$HYDO_EXPLORE_CACHE` file. Gone: `run.json`, `runs.jsonl`, `shrink.jsonl`, `report.json`, `errors.json`, `properties.txt`, `sweep-points.jsonl`, `fc-traces.jsonl` (`--fc-traces` reads an `events.jsonl`, or an old file), `fc-adaptive.json`, `consoles/<tag>.errors.json`, `<tag>.checks.log`/`.checks.txt`, `consoles-merged/` and the compiled `hydo_assert_report` (the property table is Rust now, byte-identical).
- Readers ignore unknown fields and record types and skip records of other versions (`hydo_results::reader`, tests `hydo-results/tests/reader.rs`); `hydo report`, `hydo repro`, `hydo save`, `hydo errors list|accept` and `hydo-bench depth1map` read through it. Schema `hydo/schema/results-v1.json` (generated; `tests/schema.rs` fails when it differs, and when it is not an additive change of `hydo/schema/released/results-v1.json`, the last released one, so far M115's); examples recorded from real runs in `hydo/schema/examples/results/v1/` (`tests/examples.rs`: they parse, validate and cover every record type, finding kind and main run role). `hydo-explore/examples/legacy_check.rs` maps every value of the old files to the new documents (M115's proof; `--convert` moved the CLI test fixtures).
- **One additions-only check for every format (M148):** `hydo/crates/hydo-schema-compat` (`check(released, now, &Rules)`, a dev-dependency of the three format crates, so no format crate depends on another) compares a released schema with the generated one; the project, results and agent-protocol schema tests all use it, and M114's and M115's two checkers are deleted. One rule set (the crate documentation says why each rule is what it is; `tests/rules.rs` is the table of schema changes with their verdicts) and one per-format option, who reads: `Readers::Current` (the project format: only hydo reads a project, an older hydo refuses what it does not know on purpose, so a widening passes) or `Readers::Released` (results and the agent protocol: readers built for the released schema read what is written now, ignoring unknown fields and root alternatives and nothing else, so a known place may not widen); `Rules::open_enum` names places whose enum may still gain values (the agent's refusal code, kept as text by the host, and command fields, gated by hello features). Always refused: a removed or renamed key, a new or newly required key, a lost type kind or enum value, a changed default, const, format or pattern, a tighter bound, a closed object, an inserted, removed or reordered variant inside a value, a removed root alternative, a reference turned inline or back. Always allowed: notes, new optional keys (also in closed objects), opening a closed object, new root alternatives anywhere, renamed and unreferenced definitions.

##### Storage faults of one service (M183; user decision 2026-11-07; docs/design/storage-faults.md)

- **What:** two guest tokens for one service's storage, driven by the host controller through the agent's existing commands (no engine, module, kernel or agent change; the same on hvx, hvm and KVM): `G=<svc>@<at>[+<down>]:flip|zero|trunc[,n=][,len=][,range=<from>-<to>][,file=<text>][,seed=<hex>]` changes one file under the service's `storage:` directory (bit flips, a zeroed range, a truncation; with `+down` while the service is killed, else under the running service; the file and places a pure function of the token and the directory's listing, `hydo_schedule::Corruption::plan`), and `L=<svc>@<at>+<down>` is a power loss of that service alone: its process tree stopped, its own file system shut down through ext4's `trigger_fs_error` (mounted with `errors=remount-ro`), killed, unmounted and mounted again (journal replayed); what the kernel had not written back is lost, the others run on. Not taken away: writes handed to the disk and not flushed (the engines' per-range drop is the later refinement).
- **Manifest (format 1 additions):** `services[].storage: <dir under /data>` or `{dir:, size_mib: 16..3072}` (`hydo_manifest::storage`); with `size_mib` hydo-build makes the directory a journaled ext4 logical partition of the data disk (an extended p3 holding /dev/vda5, vda6, ... in the manifest's order of the services, inside p2's MBR entry, which runs to the end of the disk so that the hvx engine snapshots, fingerprints and carries the own file systems with the data partition; the disk stays within 4 GiB), and the controller mounts it after the data disk (also in the recovery boot); `faults:` gained `corrupt` and `powerloss`. Images of manifests without `storage:` are built as before. The letters G and L are reserved (no manifest knob used them; `Z` was not taken because the control corpus has an unknown knob `Z=1`).
- **Explorer:** `--storage-faults` draws them from their own stream (G= in half of the schedules, 70% while down; L= in 40% on services with their own file system) when `faults:` lists the kind or has no list; shrinking drops each, shortens the down time and a flip to one bit; class `corrupted-files` for a failure with G=.
- **Proven** (bare-metal machine, hvx, each schedule twice with one fingerprint; docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 183"): TigerBeetle 0.17.9's single replica (`examples/tigerbeetle/hydo/hydo-single-storage.yaml`) refuses to start after its superblock area is zeroed (`panic: superblock not found`) or its data file is truncated (`data file inode size was truncated or corrupted`), found by its own checks and reported as error-log findings; it survives its own power loss and scattered bit flips; Redis (`examples/redis/storage-faults.yaml`) keeps every acknowledged SET at its own power loss with `appendfsync always` and loses them with `R=no`.

##### No silent passes (M184)

- **What a schedule names is checked against the image** (`hydo/crates/hydo-control/src/names.rs`): a guest token for a service, link, port, fake, proxy, route, knob, freeze, composition or BUGGIFY the image does not have is refused before any VM, naming what the image has (`hydo run`, `repro`, `explain`, `explore --schedule`, the explorer's runs); the identity corpora keep the old ignored paths through `run_unchecked`. `hydo-control/tests/silent.rs` checks every schedule of `recorded.json` and the bench plans, `hydo-explore/tests/names.rs` every generated one. An image without a readable manifest is not explored with the stack's built-in space any more; `--concurrency` needs a knob `Q`, `--buggify` needs `buggify: true`.
- **`guest.outcomes_after_cut: true`** (opt-in, a format-1 addition): the recovery boot's `$HYDO_OUTCOMES` holds the first boot's last outcome per id (`Ending::PowerCut.outcomes`, in the transcript only when non-empty). Not the default because it would move the recorded values of every power-cut run whose workload writes outcomes.
- **Vacuous passes and the final verdict**: `Run.warnings` and `Summary.vacuous_passes` (results additions) flag a pass whose workload acknowledged nothing, a history check over 0 operations and a reaction whose event no record names; `hydo run` prints them and prints `hydo: VERDICT ...` when the host's checks changed the `RESULT` line's verdict. `hydo-build` warns about a `ready:` command that runs, through `hydo-oci`, a program the image lacks; `hydo guide capabilities` has the KVM engine.
- **`hydo doctor` never fetches** (at the merge, 2026-11-08): it looks only in this machine's directories (`hydo_image::kernels::locate_here`) and names `hydo setup --get <version>` for a missing release file; before, its KVM check downloaded the whole Linux release archive when the KVM kernel was missing (test `doctor_never_fetches`). The names check also covers M183's `G=` and `L=`.

##### Explaining a failure: where two runs first differ (M165)

- **`hydo diff <run dir A> <run dir B> [--out DIR]`** (`hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/diff.rs`; design `docs/design/explain.md`): reads each run as events per conversation (boot, run, recovery, result): the control transcripts' commands, engine actions and ends, the controller's notes and reports, and the guest's own console lines from `<tag>.log` (at the stop of the report they precede), each with its stop number and guest time; aligns them per conversation with Myers' diff on keys without ids, nonces, stops, times and the controller's echo of the schedule. It reports the first difference (shared context, the events only one run has under the controller note they came after, what differs inside events of one family), the guest-time divergence, the first difference in what the checks judge (acknowledged and failed lists, verdicts, ends, history, fake-world and error-log records, failing assertions, assertions both runs write there with other content; not an extra passing evaluation), the records of a kind only one run writes, and counts per conversation and level. Writes `diff.json` (results format v1, `"type": "diff"`, `hydo_results::Diff`, an addition; example `hydo/schema/examples/results/v1/metal-stack-diff/`) and `diff.txt` (its view).
- **`hydo explain <image> "<schedule>"`** or **`hydo explain <run dir>`** (`src/explain.rs`): runs the schedule's neighbours one VM at a time (every guest token removed once, every fault with a step moved one step earlier and later, `disk=none` instead of the disk faults; `--with "<schedule>"`, `--with-image IMG2`, `--max N`; runs already in the output directory are reused), writes a run directory with `diff.json` per neighbour, prints a table (verdict, where it first differs, the first judged difference in one line) and the report of the passing neighbour whose first difference comes latest (`explain.txt`). The main help text does not list the two commands (it is a recorded answer of the CLI golden); each has `--help`.
- Proven (docs/HISTORY.md Milestone 165): on the old against the fixed order service the first judged difference is `hydo-explore-acked: only in B: 11`, and the fixed code's only-there records show its skipped cache write for order 11 right after the kill; the pinned schedule's neighbours show the unacknowledged order following the kill step; the Redis minimal schedule's report is only the knob and the verdict (the cause is in the disk's content, below these levels; `disk=cut` against `disk=none` differs in the fingerprint only).

##### Why a run failed, and looking inside a run (M178)

- **Made for AI agents** (user decision 2026-11-07; design docs/design/inspect.md; guide `hydo guide inspect`). A failed `hydo run` writes `diagnosis` into `result.json` and prints `hydo: diagnosis:` / `hydo: likely:`: the failing service, process (status, signal, whether hydo sent it), readiness check (`deadline` or `died`, tries, last status), conclusions with their reason, the kernel's memory and crash lines, and for an ERROR the evidence of one replay of the run to the verdict's stop (every service's log tail, setup and provisioning logs, the readiness check run once, `dmesg`, `free`, `ps`; `--no-diagnose` skips it). The diagnosis runs after the run's result is written and replays on a separate engine, so no recorded value can move. On hvx the agent's lines go over the host-call port, not the console, so `hydo run` keeps the replay's agent events in `agent-events.jsonl`.
- **`hydo inspect`** (`hydo-cli/src/inspect.rs`, `src/inspect/`; nothing in hydo-control, the engines or the agent changed): `events` (the run's events with points such as `run:812`, filters and pages, no VM), `diagnose [--evidence]`, `start <run dir> --at end|<conv>:<stop>` (a background session in `$HYDO_HOME/inspect/<id>/` that replays the recorded transcripts to the stop and holds it: a snapshot in the boot and the workload, each call resuming from it; a live branch after the workload's end, in a recovery boot and under timing tokens), `exec`, `read`, `ls`, `logs`, `ps`, `sockets`, `advance`, `status`, `list`, `stop`, and one-shot calls on a run directory. One JSON document per call (results format v1 additions: `Run.diagnosis`, `diagnosis`, `timeline`, `inspect`, `inspect-error` with `try`); the recorded run's directory is only read. Proven on hvx (three broken Redis images, the Redis power cut, the stack's pinned reproducer: order 11 published in MySQL, absent from Redis, never acknowledged) and on the Mac; every recorded fingerprint unchanged after inspecting (docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 178").

##### Small fixes found by the onboardings (M181)

- `hydo` built in a checkout (`cargo build -p hydo`) knows its version and, with no release around it, uses `$HYDO_HOME/versions/<version>` as a cargo-installed hydo does (`hydo setup` fetches it; `hydo doctor` names `hydo setup --get <version>`). `hydo compose` imports services with `build:` as local builds (never pulled by tag; `fetch-images.sh` prints the `docker build`/`docker save` lines). Results format additions for eventually checks: `Property.within_s`, `Liveness.within_s`, `slowest_late_s`, `slowest_late_run` (report.md's liveness table shows the deadline and the slowest episode that held late). hvx keeps 64 KiB of a VM's console (the module's buffer), KVM and the Mac 4 MiB; `hydo run` warns when hvx's is full. `root.share_images: true` (format-1 addition, opt-in): services of one image share one unpacked tree (not for `writable: true` services). Fakes: `save:`/`load:` objects that keep what was answered (carried across a power cut) and `webhook.sign:` (HMAC-SHA256). The `hydo-world` program's bytes changed (open item 59). docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 181".

##### The image records (M155, user decision 2026-11-05)

- **Why:** an image built today must still run, and reproduce, after hydo is upgraded, so every image records what shapes its runs but is not inside it. Crate `hydo/crates/hydo-image` (format and lookup), `hydo/PRODUCT.md` "An image keeps working after hydo is upgraded".
- **Inside the image:** `/etc/hydo/image.json` (next to `/etc/hydo/control`), canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, one newline), `"v": 1`, `"type": "image"`: `arch`, `epoch` (the fingerprint epoch), `kernel` (`file`, `sha256`, `version`, `cmdline`: the kernel by sha256, the rest for people) and, on x86_64, `initrd` (`file`, `sha256`). Nothing that changes with every release is in it (a version there would move every fingerprint at every release). Written by `hydo-build` (`src/record.rs`) for both architectures; the arm64 netns image also keeps M99's `/etc/hydo/kernel`.
- **Next to the image:** `<image file>.json` (`"type": "build"`, written by `hydo build`): the image's and (arm64) the data disk's sha256, a copy of the image record, `hydo.version` and `hydo.commit` (the commit comes from `git rev-parse HEAD` at compile time, or from the git-ignored `hydo/COMMIT` in a tree copied without `.git`), the manifest's path and sha256, and the services' Docker/OCI image digests. Schema `hydo/schema/image-v1.json` (both records), released copy `hydo/schema/released/image-v1.json` (M155's), checked by `hydo-image/tests/schema.rs` with `hydo-schema-compat` (`Readers::Released`).
- **The fingerprint epoch** (`hydo_image::EPOCH`, 1 since M155): increase it by one in the same commit as any change of an engine, the host controller, the agent pin or the guest kernels that moves a recorded fingerprint, that is, at every re-baseline (docs/REBASELINE.md gets a section naming the new epoch; the crate documentation says the same). Runs of one epoch compare fingerprints exactly; across epochs only verdicts. A run, exploration or explorer-cache entry without an epoch (before M155) counts as epoch 1.
- **The kernel at run time** (`hydo_engine::image::boot_files`, used by `hydo run`/`repro`, the explorer and hydo-bench on both platforms): with a record, the kernel (and the x86_64 initramfs) is looked up by sha256 among the files with a known kernel name in the default kernel's directory and the release's `guest/` or the tree's `build/` (`hydo_image::kernels::KNOWN`, the four pinned files, checked against both `assets.sha256` by `tests/kernels.rs`); then (in the `hydo` command, since M162) the install cache: `kernels::obtain` asks the source `hydo` registers, which takes the file from the content store or from the archive of the release that shipped it ("The install cache" below). Missing (the message then ends with why the cache could not provide it): "<image> was built for the guest kernel <file> (Linux <version>, sha256 <hex>), which this hydo (<version>) does not have (looked in <dirs>). The image was built by hydo <version>, commit <hex>. Install hydo <version>'s guest kernel (the file <file> with that sha256) into one of those directories, or rebuild the image with this hydo (hydo build)." An image without the record boots today's choice (the default, or M99's `/etc/hydo/kernel`) with "warning: <image> has no /etc/hydo/image.json (built before Milestone 155): it boots this hydo's default guest kernel; rebuild it with hydo build to record the kernel it needs".
- **Epochs compared:** `hydo repro <run dir|exploration>` and `hydo repro --transcript` say REPRODUCED/DIFFERENT by fingerprint within the epoch; for another epoch they print "the recorded fingerprints are from fingerprint epoch N and this hydo (<version>) is at epoch M: fingerprints from another epoch are not comparable, so the verdicts are compared instead" and SAME VERDICT/DIFFERENT by verdict class. `hydo run` notes when the image was built at another epoch. The explorer's `$HYDO_EXPLORE_CACHE` answers only from entries of its own epoch (each entry carries `epoch`).
- **Results format additions (format 1):** `Run.epoch`, `Start.epoch`, `Exploration.epoch` (the running hydo's epoch); `Image.epoch`, `Image.kernel`, `Image.built_by` (`version`, `commit`), `Image.manifest_sha256`, `Image.services` (`service`, `image`, `digest`, `config_digest`), filled from the two records (`hydo_explore::results::image_of`). The running hydo's version was already `hydo_version`.
- **The one re-baseline:** every image's bytes changed once (the new file), so every example fingerprint and the pinned reproducers moved; docs/REBASELINE.md section 13 has the values.

##### The recorded example values and how to re-record them (M164)

- **`hydo/onboard/recorded.json`** is the source of every recorded example value (since M164; generated once from docs/REBASELINE.md's latest tables, which keep the history): per image its platform (`hvx`, `hvm`, `kvm`), how it is built from the tree (a stage of `hydo/onboard/rebaseline/stage.sh`, the folder, the manifest, `hydo build` arguments, owners), its sha256, and per schedule the verdict line, `fp` and, where recorded, `ctl` and `wfp`. Format: `hydo/crates/hydo-bench/src/recorded.rs`; `cargo test -p hydo-bench --test it recorded::` checks it. When another branch moves values, it re-runs the tool with `--write` instead of editing tables by hand.
- **`hydo-bench rebaseline`** (a development tool, in neither release) does one platform on the machine it runs on. **Default mode (fast, these are tests):** an image whose inputs (the tree's paths its stage reads, `stage.sh sources`, with the recipe, the staging script, the image builder and the release) are those of the build kept in the work folder is neither staged nor built; otherwise staged and built once; a schedule whose result for the image's bytes and the engine (platform, fingerprint epoch, engine program, loaded module) is cached is not run; the others run once, one fresh boot per image and the rest in a worker pool from the provisioned snapshot (`--jobs`: 2 on Linux, 4 on a Mac; a `big` image alone), and a second time from a fresh boot only when the first did not give the recorded values. **`--thorough`** (releases, nightly): every image built twice and compared, every schedule twice from fresh boots, nothing reused. Reports verdict changes, nondeterministic runs and unreproducible builds (exit 1), moved values (exit 3 with `--check`; written with `--write`); also `--only`, `--changed-only`, `--build-only`, `--reuse-builds`; it waits while `HYDO_QUIET_FILE` exists and, on Linux, for free memory; every VM goes through the prefix's `libexec/hvx-run` (`~/bin/hvx-run`). The run cache trusts the fingerprint epoch rule. How to use it: docs/REBASELINE.md "How to re-baseline"; before a release: docs/RELEASING.md step 1.4 (with `--thorough`).

##### The install cache (M162; for after the first release, not merged)

- **What:** `hydo` fetches what a version needs from its GitHub release, verified by sha256, into one per-user cache (`$HYDO_HOME`, default `~/.hydo`): `store/<sha256>/<name>` (release archives and the guest kernels taken out of them, read-only, checked again on use), `releases/<v>/SHA256SUMS`, `downloads/<sha256>.part`, `versions/<v>/` (installed releases), `bin/hydo` (a link to the current one), `.lock` (flock). Design and reasons: `docs/design/install-cache.md`. Code: `hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/cache.rs` (archives, kernels, restore, install, import) and `src/fetch.rs` (ureq with rustls, the crates hydo-compose already ships, so no crate was added), `hydo/crates/hydo-image/src/store.rs` and `src/releases.rs`, `kernels::set_source`/`obtain`; variables `HYDO_HOME`, `HYDO_RELEASE_URL` (default `https://github.com/kakoc/hydo/releases/download`, `<url>/v<version>/<file>`; https only, plain http only to a loopback host), `HYDO_OFFLINE`.
- **Verification:** an archive's sha256 comes from the **release index compiled into hydo**, `hydo/dist/releases.txt` (`archive` and `file` lines per published release; additions only; 0.1.0's two archives `58aab3b1…` and `5c02e7f3…` and four guest files are in it), else, for the running hydo's own version only (its archive cannot be in its own program), from the release's `SHA256SUMS` asset over TLS; a file taken out of an archive must have the sha256 it is wanted for (the image's record, the tree's `SHA256SUMS`, this hydo's pins). Nothing downloaded is executed: archives are read in Rust (tar, flate2). Downloads resume with Range, retry four times (connection errors, short bodies, 408/429/5xx), refuse a wrong sha256 (fetched once more from the start only when it was a resumed one), stop at 4 GiB; proxies from `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY`.
- **Commands:** `hydo setup` restores a damaged release's files from its archive (store or fetched) and names them; `--check` says "hydo setup would: restore <n> files from <archive> (in the install cache | fetched from <url>)" with exit 3, and exit 1 when nothing can restore them (offline without the archive, a `bin/hydo` of another release); `--verify` as in M154. `hydo setup --get [VERSION]` installs this hydo's own version or one the index knows into `versions/<VERSION>` (unpacked into a temporary directory, set up with M154's steps, checked, renamed), enters its guest files into the store and points `bin/hydo` at it; a `bin/hydo` that is a program (a release `install.sh` put into the same `~/.hydo`, its default prefix) is left alone. `hydo setup --archive FILE` puts a downloaded archive into the store (index pin, or the release's `SHA256SUMS` next to it). `--offline`/`HYDO_OFFLINE=1` never connects; what is missing is refused with its URL. A run (`hydo run`/`repro`/`explore`) whose image names a kernel the release lacks takes it from the store or the release that shipped it.
- **Proven:** 13 tests against a fake release on a local HTTP server (`hydo-cli` `src/cache/tests.rs`: own-version archive by `SHA256SUMS` fetched once, pinned archive with other bytes refused, an interrupted download resumed by Range, a server that ignores Range, always-cut downloads failing after the attempts, 503 retried and 404 not, a bad kept part fetched again, a kernel taken out of the release that shipped it, two versions sharing one store entry, offline installs and refusals, the flat-install `bin/hydo` left alone, `--check`/setup restoring a damaged release, `--archive`), `setup.rs`'s store-tree restore and foreign-pin refusal, `hydo-image` `tests/obtain.rs` and the index and store tests. By hand on this Mac against the real v0.1.0 release: `hydo setup --get 0.1.0` fetched `hydo-mac-0.1.0.tar.gz` (30.3 MB, pinned), set it up (signed `bin/hydo-hvm`), and the installed 0.1.0's own `hydo setup --check` said nothing to do (428 files, 53 pinned); a second `--get --offline` made no connection; the release's Redis quickstart image (`a3447614…`), run by this tree's `hydo` with an empty cache, fetched the archive for its kernel `Image-explore` and gave `67e5d6469f1a90a5`, the value of docs/REBASELINE.md 13.4 and of the release's own run; offline from the store the same; offline with an empty cache the refusal named the URL.

##### Linux determinism, clocks and the module

- hvx boots real Linux 6.6.35 deterministically: two boots from scratch and every branch-from-snapshot reach a bit-identical full state (console, snapshot, guest RAM, disk). Current boot baselines: no-disk `7a5559028ffbf52c`, with-disk `36583d533d7c989b` (M34). Guest RAM can be up to 3 GiB, below the MMIO hole, and 3 GiB boots are identical; `hvx_bigram_test` checks every page of a 3 GiB guest (M28, M36). **Up to 8 GiB on the side module `hvxbig` (M179, not in the main module):** the first 3 GiB at guest-physical 0, the rest from 4 GiB (`hvx_abi.h` "Guest RAM layout", `HVX_RAM_LOW_MAX`/`HVX_RAM_HIGH_BASE`/`HVX_RAM_MAX`; the RAM mmap stays one linear buffer; the e820 map of `hvx_boot.h` and `hydo-hvx/src/boot.rs` gets a third entry only above 3 GiB); `hvx_hugeram_test` checks every page of both blocks and the hole of an 8 GiB guest.
- The default clock counts VM exits: the virtual TSC advances by a fixed step per exit. The **PMU branch clock** (`HVX_VM_PMU_CLOCK`) counts the guest's retired conditional branches in hardware and gives a tick every period (default 2^20 branches, 2 ms of guest time) at an exact instruction (M33). Since M65 the branch counter is frozen while the firmware handles a System Management Interrupt; before that fix, SMIs (which fwupd causes) shifted ticks and caused rare fingerprint differences. Without `tsc=reliable` on the guest command line or the PMU clock, a heavy guest can livelock.
- VM flags (`struct hvx_config.flags`), all off by default: bit 0 `IDLE_HEARTBEAT` (a synthetic tick when the guest idles with nothing armed, M27), bit 1 `X86_64_V2` (M31), bit 2 `PMU_CLOCK` (M33), bit 3 `PAUSE_EXIT` (every `PAUSE` exits and moves the clock, M34), bit 4 `PT_TRACE` (M40), bit 5 `SMP_SCHED` (M66), bit 6 `SMP_BOOT` (M69), bit 7 `X86_64_V3` (AVX/AVX2/FMA/BMI and XSAVE for x87, SSE and AVX only, M68). Since M138 (in the main module since 2026-11-02): bit 8 `HOSTCALL` (the host-call port) and bit 9 `DIRTY_LOG` (the dirty-page log), with the ioctls `HVX_RESET_VM`, `HVX_GET_DIRTY` and `HVX_HC_GET`/`PUT`/`GET_STATE`/`SET_STATE` (numbers 64–69) and the exit reason `HVX_EXIT_HOSTCALL`; an older module ignores the two flags and refuses the ioctls, which the engine detects.
- Timing controls for exploring thread interleavings: seeded tick jitter `HVX_SET_TJITTER` (M43), a shorter tick period and inserted extra ticks `HVX_SET_XTICK` (M49), a power cut at the k-th disk FLUSH `HVX_SET_FLUSHCUT` (M56), and the disk's volatile write cache saved and restored through `HVX_GET/SET_UNSYNC` (M43 addendum).
- Code coverage: Intel Processor Trace of the guest (`HVX_SET_PT`, tools in `hv/hvx/pt/`, libipt) gives exact per-instruction coverage; tracing on or off gives identical fingerprints (M40).
- The module's safety net (M97, `hv/hvx/SAFETY.md`): the debug kernel (Linux 6.8.12 with KASAN, kmemleak, UBSAN, lockdep, KCOV) boots in a nested VM on the build machine and runs the deploy-metal suite, three Linux boots and the reproducers (33 pass, 6 PMU tests skip, 0 splats, 0 leaks). syzkaller (`b498adee`) fuzzes `/dev/hvx` with guest programs (`syz_ext_hvx_guest`). Nine module bugs were found and fixed on `main` (a NULL dereference, two heap overflows from snapshot or unsync state, two interrupts-off CPU hangs a guest can cause, a UBSAN shift, an mmap use-after-free, an OOM deadlock, unchecked PT filter MSRs); guest RAM and disk pages are now charged to the caller's memory cgroup and fail with ENOMEM instead of OOM-killing. The fixed module, built as a side module, gives all 33 recorded fingerprints on the bare-metal machine. The main module on the bare-metal machine has had these fixes since 2026-10-30. M140 ran main's module with M138's code under a debug kernel on the bare-metal machine itself (`hv/hvx/safety/onbox/`, booted once with kexec): the whole suite, the explorer, the host-call port and in-place reuse gave their normal-kernel values and no KASAN, UBSAN, lockdep or kmemleak report.
- **The branch counter counts only in the guest (M156, in the main module since 2026-11-06):** a host NMI between a VM exit and the next entry (the perf-based watchdog's) makes perf's handler re-enable every counter in IA32_PERF_GLOBAL_CTRL, and PMC0 then counted the host's own branches as the guest's, so a tick or a turn end landed early: `hvx_sched_sweep_test 2000` failed in about one run of 40, and single-vCPU PMU-clock runs can be hit the same way. The fix (`hv/hvx/hvx.c`, module parameter `pmu_guard`, default 1) keeps PERFEVTSEL0 at 0 in root mode and switches it with one-entry VM-entry and VM-exit MSR-load areas; `chaos_nmi=N` (default 0) sends the CPU an NMI every N-th PMU-clock exit to reproduce the miscount on demand. Proven on the side module `hvxfix` (`hv/hvx/m156/side.sh hvxfix <rev or file> load`): with `chaos_nmi=20000` the guarded module gives 0 mismatches in 28,400 runs and the recorded sweep hash, the unguarded one fails every case; the side-module suite keeps every recorded value. Cost: +32 % wall time on the sweep test (dense turn ends), +4.5 % on a stack run; `pmu_guard=0` turns it off. In the main module since 2026-11-06 (srcversion `14D39A96F319623EC2AD8D1`).
- The Rust KVM monitor (`src/`, which could not get past Linux's `RDTSC` calibration under stock KVM and is why hvx exists) was removed in M100; its baselines and results are in `docs/HISTORY.md`.

##### The kernel-module package (M138, on the side module `hvxgc` only; not merged)

- **Where:** this tree's `hv/hvx/hvx.c` built as `hvxgc.ko` (`/dev/hvxgc`) by `hv/hvx/gc/build-hvxgc.sh [build|load|unload]` (it writes `~/m138-side-loading` on the bare-metal machine while it loads); the main module and its userspace are untouched, and the engine detects a module without the features and runs as before. Every feature is opt-in and inert when off. With all of them off the side module passes the whole suite with the recorded values (`hv/hvx/gc/side-suite.sh off`, run on the bare-metal machine: the 31 deploy-metal checks, both pinned reproducers three times in one serve, M118's lock-step check, M121's agent boot check on M121's and M131's images: ALL PASS, 36 checks); with them on, the engine's checks pass too (`side-suite.sh on`, 5 checks). The side module was unloaded at the end of M138; load it again with `build-hvxgc.sh load`.
- **The host-call port** (VM flag bit 8; on by default in the hvx engine since M140, `HYDO_HVX_HOSTCALL=0` turns it off; hydo-agent 0.3.0 pinned in `hydo-build` since M140; docs/design/guest-control.md "Phase 2", as built): the agent's lines go to the host as records on I/O ports 0x5f0/0x5f4 and the run call returns at the committing OUT (`why=hostcall` stops); the host's lines are staged on the port and announced by one doorbell byte on the serial line; the port's buffers travel with the engine's snapshots. Negotiated: the engine offers `hydo.hc=1`, hydo-agent 0.3.0 (hello feature `hostcall`) takes the port when it answers its magic, and the engine moves the host's lines to the port when the agent's first record arrives there; an older agent, an older engine or the main module stays on the serial line. Proven on the Redis example (seven schedules) and the stack (four, old order service): the serial line's verdicts and M136's, each run twice identical, every transcript replay reproduced. The gRPC stack's lock-step hang (open item 30 d) does not happen over the port.
- **In-place reset with a dirty-page log** (VM flag bit 9 and `HVX_RESET_VM`; `HYDO_HVX_REUSE=1` in the engine; `HYDO_HVX_CHECK_RESET=1` compares every page with a fresh VM's): a worker keeps up to two VMs and brings one back to the next run's snapshot by rewriting only the pages that changed (a clean Redis run: 1,247 RAM pages of 262,144 and 66 disk pages). Identical results to fresh VMs (both pinned reproducers; a Redis exploration, 69 runs and 107 consoles; a stack exploration, 21 runs and 30 consoles). Explorations 38.1 s → 33.1 s (Redis) and 146.6 s → 133.8 s (stack); per run the RAM restore drops from 12–17 ms to 1 ms (Redis) and from about 95 ms to 5 ms (stack).
- **Not built:** copy-on-write VMs from a snapshot and a read-only root shared between VMs (open item 36).

##### Devices and fault injection

- Devices: a 16550 serial port with input (`HVX_PUT_INPUT`), an emulated x2APIC and IOAPIC, a virtio-blk PCI disk (device 3, MSI-X, a page-array image of up to 4 GiB mapped zero-copy into userspace) and a virtio-net PCI device (device 4, scripted receive with `HVX_PUT_RX`, captured transmit with `HVX_GET_TX`). Every device is inert unless attached (M18–M24, M28).
- Disk faults (`HVX_SET_FAULT`) are a pure function of a seed and the request index: delay, I/O error, lying-disk drop, reorder, torn write, and `DROP_UNFLUSHED`, a faithful power loss in which writes held in a volatile cache are lost unless flushed (M22, M26). Network faults (`HVX_SET_NET_FAULT`) are drop, delay, corrupt, duplicate and reorder (M24).
- Current hand-written test fingerprints (all in `deploy-metal.sh`): iso `7e586473f6e494d7`, pci `3f95ef833747f3ec`, fault `91170d4dbf101c5b` / `88f680fc22cc9bb0` / `9090286f3fc59682`, net `0e2b7acf2f4f94ee`, net-fault `883a00eb6a14a6f0` / `37490fb78da33064` / `40659aabb208aaa0`, bug_f0 `1083e400458728ff`, avx `3bb428a134ce542a`.

##### Real-service flagships

Each flagship boots an unmodified service, runs a workload and an oracle, and passes four checks: without faults the result is correct; with the durable setting the data survives a power cut; with the relaxed setting a power cut loses an acknowledged write, and replay and branch reproduce the loss exactly; and different fault seeds give different, reproducible results. The values below are for the original images. The images rebuilt with the pinned toolchain (`*-pin-disk.img`) have their values in `docs/REBASELINE.md` (M61), and new comparisons should use those.

##### The four-service stack

- One guest runs unmodified MySQL 8.4.10, Kafka 3.5.0 and Redis 7.2.4 plus our gRPC order service (`hydo/stack/main.go`; older notes call it the "front door"). Each `Place(id)` writes MySQL, publishes to Kafka with an idempotent franz-go producer, writes Redis as a best-effort cache, and only then acknowledges. Only one `Place` per order id runs at a time, and the "send started" state lives in MySQL (`published` 0 / 2 / 1) (M35, M37, M39, M50). Built by `build-stack.sh`; verified by `hv/hvx/hvx_stack_verify.c` (`mode=all`, `mode=fault`).
- MySQL runs with the binary log on and `sync_binlog=1`, and Kafka with `log.retention.ms=-1` (M63). These two settings fix the bugs found in M58 and M63.
- Current baselines (M77, image `stack-nq-disk.img` `161996bb…` = the M63 recipe plus the M71 netem drain, one vCPU): SANITY `2235f9d76a592a07`, F1 `815cc64346e728fc`, F2 `32024d0b245aff3c` (the expected VIOLATION from MySQL's relaxed window, order 8; durable `7323951e90d21b4f`), F3 `96e2e7ddb963ee66` / `e8c16382540eba2e`.
