##### The explorer

- **The hvx engine is Rust and runs in-process (M132; the default since M137, which deleted `hv/hvx/hvx_explore.c`):** `hydo/crates/hydo-hvx` is hvx_explore.c ported function by function (hand-written `hvx_abi.h` types checked against the header by a C probe, hvx_boot.h's recipe byte for byte, `parse_sched` against the C one's recorded answers on 23,351 inputs, `tests/golden/parse_sched_c.txt`). Every `hydo_engine::hvx::Hvx` method runs it on a thread of the calling process (`hydo-engine/src/inproc.rs`) when that process can open `/dev/hvx` (root, or a user in the udev rule's group); the engine thread then holds the module lock shared itself (`$HYDO_LOCK`, default `~/.hvx-module.lock`, the sudo user's home under sudo). Otherwise it starts the program `hydo-hvx` (the C engine's command line; `hydo_engine::hvx::program`: `$HYDO_HVX_EXPLORE`, `<root>/target/release/hydo-hvx` or a release's `bin/hydo-hvx`) under `hvx-run sudo`. `HYDO_ENGINE=inproc|process` forces one. On the bare-metal machine run a tree's explorer as `~/bin/hvx-run sudo env HOME=$HOME hydo-explore …` to get the in-process engine. Coverage tracing (`HVX_EXPLORE_PT_ELF`/`_RANGES`, `hydo-hvx/src/pt.rs`; the libipt decoder `pt/ptedges.c` only with the cargo feature `pt`: `cargo build --release -p hydo-explore -p hydo-hvx --features hydo-hvx/pt`) and the diagnostics RETLOG, ZSKIP, DIRTY, SIM_DRAIN_DROP and the PHASES counters are ported (M137). It keeps S0/S1 in memory as non-zero pages, fills fresh VMs with non-zero pages only, hashes with the exact zero-page shortcut, prepares the next VM and tears old ones down on helper threads (`HYDO_HVX_PREPARE=0`, `HYDO_HVX_REAPER=0`). Identical to hvx_explore on the pinned reproducers, M118's lockstep check, M121's agent boot check, M126's runs and ten explorations (M132: 388 runs, 554 consoles) and M137's further explorations (the M137 results are in docs/HISTORY.md Milestone 137; `hydo-explore/examples/engine_equiv.rs`); Redis runs 3.2 s → 0.6–0.8 s, stack runs 7.8 s → 3.2–4.5 s (with a power cut 15.4 s → 8.5–12.3 s), worker boots 5 → 2 s and 64 → 17 s.
- The run engine (`hydo-hvx`; `hv/hvx/hvx_explore.c` until M137) boots a guest once, snapshots it at "root mounted" (S0) and "provisioned" (S1), and starts each schedule in a fresh VM restored from S1; after a power cut, only the flushed data disk goes into a recovery VM restored from S0. The explorer (`hydo/crates/hydo-explore`, M102; `hydo explore` in a release, or the `hydo-explore` binary with explore.py's old command line in a tree) generates schedules from seeds, runs them on a worker pool, re-runs every failure (the fingerprints must match), shrinks one failure per signature, and writes its results in the results format (M115: `events.jsonl` while it runs, `exploration.json` at the end, `report.md` made from it; before M115 `runs.jsonl`, `shrink.jsonl`, `report.json` and side files, M38). Run it on the bare-metal machine from a tree as `cargo build --release -p hydo-explore -p hydo-hvx && ~/bin/hvx-run sudo env HOME=$HOME target/release/hydo-explore --image <agent image> --seeds 1-200 --out /var/tmp/explore/run1` (`--image` is required since M146) (`. ~/hydo-rust/env.sh` first; without `hvx-run sudo` each worker is a `hydo-hvx` program under `hvx-run sudo`, same results). Reproduce one schedule as `hydo run <image> "<schedule>"` (a fresh boot under the host controller; the engine program's plain `one`/`serve` modes and the requests RUN and BRANCH, which ran shell-init images, were deleted in M145: every image is an agent image, and a shell-init image is refused with "built before Milestone 136; rebuild it with hydo build").
- **Explorer images:** every image is an agent image built by `hydo build` (M136, M145). The M71 shell image `explore-binlog-ret-xr-nq-disk.img` and its predecessors were deleted from the bare-metal machine on 2026-11-03 (their results stay in docs/HISTORY.md M67, M71); the stack's agent images are `~/hydo/build/m145/explore-ob-stack-{old,fix}-disk.img` (the pinned reproducers) and the M140 real builds in `~/hydo-nixb-work/img/<case>/b1` on the bare-metal machine.
- **Pinned reproducers** (check them after every module change; M145, re-recorded in M155 with the image record): `disk=none dseed=4d5cb825dfaab05b | run K=redis@11+1 C=24` with `hydo run` from a fresh boot gives `1dc3677fb94053cf` (VIOLATION: order 11 is in Kafka but the client was never ACKed; ctl `e873020651036931`) on `explore-ob-stack-old-disk.img` (`dc8f8a89…`, the stack example with M38's order service) and `ba0aa0612502a1df` (OK; ctl `07c598044a68e5be`) on `explore-ob-stack-fix-disk.img` (`1de40b6a…`, M39's fixed one), each twice. Both images (with their build records) are in `~/hydo/build/m155` on the bare-metal machine (M145's `8fc461db23ef6642` and `aad6a563e2046361` on `e053a633…`/`0afcbed9…` in `~/hydo/build/m145`, images without the record); `hydo/onboard/examples/stack/build-reproducers.sh` rebuilds them byte for byte (the order services from git commits `d26ed1d` and `0112b48` with the pinned Go). Until M145 the reproducers were the hand-made shell images `explore-disk.img` (`2403499c9a3f8419`) and `explore-fix-disk.img` (`f87130453609a5d6`), M38, M39; docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 145".
- Strategies: `random` (the default), `swarm` (M42), `swarm-pos` and `process` (a Jepsen-style fault process, the best so far, M56), the research strategies `portfolio.py` (M44), `guided.py` and `richguided.py` (coverage-guided, negative results, M41, M44) and `abranch.py` (negative, M45), deleted in M108, and `--sweep kill|cut|net|killcut|pause|clock|oneway|frontkill|tail|depth1|freeze|protocol` (`protocol`: every `H=` rule kind on every fake/proxy target, one step at a time, M89; `freeze`: every packet point of a traced run as one `F=` schedule, options `--fc-*`, `--sweep-every`, `--sweep-with`, M76). Options: `--timing` (tick jitter, M43), `--new-faults` (pause, clock jump and one-way loss, M46), `--durable-only`, `--concurrency` (concurrent and duplicate clients, M50), `--more-faults` (timed kills `X=` and k-th-flush cuts `cf=`, M67), `--preempt` (M49; on the Mac it gives PCT points, M57), `--buggify` (M56), `--vcpus N --turns` (M69), `--cpu v3` (M68), `--ram-mib` (M59), `--manifest` (M52), `--backend hvm` (the Mac, M51), `--knob-rule` (M56), `--protocol-faults` (`H=` on fakes and proxies, M89) and `--reactive fault|heal|both` (reactions `A=` on top of any strategy, from their own stream, M139; `--react-events`, `--heal-events` on a manifest). `--branch` (mid-run timing variants, M43, which found nothing tick jitter does not) was deleted in M145 with the engine's BRANCH request; `--timing` is its replacement.
- Schedule tokens. Guest side (after `|`): `K=` kill, `P=` pause, `N=` netem, `O=` one-way loss, `C=` power cut, `T=` clock jump, `Q=` concurrency, `X=` timed kill, `B=` BUGGIFY, `H=` protocol fault on a fake or proxy (M89), `A=` a reaction to the first SDK assertion record of an event (`A=<event>[@<step>][+<ms>]:cut|kill-<svc>|stop-<svc>-<ms>|cont-<svc>`, decided by the host controller during the run, M139), and `M=` / `R=` durability knobs. Host side (before `|`): `disk=` and `dseed=`, `tj*` tick jitter, `pp=` / `xt*` preemption, `cf=` flush cut, `rb=` run budget, `q=` / `qs=` turn lengths, and `pct*` (Mac only).
- **Adaptive freeze sweep (M92):** `--sweep freeze --fc-adaptive` sweeps the manifest's `freeze_match:` streams (or, without them, every `--fc-stride`-th packet, default 8), then every packet in a ±`--fc-window` window (default 16) around each failure on the frozen service's links, widened until the failing band is mapped. On the sweep it was measured on, it found all 17 of M76's every-packet failing points with 305 runs instead of 1,145. Without `freeze_match:`, a stride of 8 can step over a narrow failing band; a stride of 4 found all 17. Pool options for a shared box: `HYDO_QUIET_FILE` (start no new VM while that file exists), `HYDO_EXPLORE_CACHE` (resume an interrupted deterministic sweep from earlier results), and a worker restarts its engine if it dies.
- The main lesson of M41–M57: where and in what combination faults land matters more than how the next schedule is chosen. The fault process, BUGGIFY, and timed kills with flush cuts find what the guided strategies did not.
- **Reactive exploration (M139, design step D2):** the guest token `A=<event>[@<step>][+<ms>]:cut|kill-<svc>|stop-<svc>-<ms>|cont-<svc>` is a fault or a heal the host controller applies at the first SDK assertion record of an event (`hydo-control/src/features/react.rs`; MANIFEST.md "Reactions"); `--reactive fault|heal|both` draws it on top of any strategy. A reactive run is reproduced by its schedule string and by `hydo repro --transcript` (proven on the scripted engine and on the bare-metal machine); a schedule without `A=` runs the same commands as before. On the bug benchmark (agent images, `hydo/bench/c2-plans/m139*.txt`, hydo/bench/README.md "Reactive exploration") it is **negative**: against `--strategy process --more-faults` no defect is found more often (d0–d7, d10: 3/3 each for every mode; d11 2/10 for both px and pxr) and every reactive mode needs more runs to the first detection (sum 154 for px, 181–187 with reactions), because an early reaction pre-empts the base schedule's later fault and a heal shortens or lengthens the outage the defect needed. The token stays useful by hand to aim at a known moment (d4 and d10 each fail on one hand-written reactive schedule and pass on their controls).
- Assertions with `always`, `sometimes`, `reachable` and `unreachable` properties (`hydo/ASSERTIONS.md`, the Go SDK in `hydo/stack/hydoassert`, `hydo_assert.sh` for shell, and the report tool `hydo_assert_report`) include `eventually` liveness properties (M38, M59).
- The bug benchmark `hydo/bench/` (M54, M56, M62, M67) has defects d0–d12, each patched into a copy of the order service and each with a confirmed trigger. Its runner is `hydo-bench` (M108: `run` for cells of strategy × defect × repetitions, `table`, `confirm`, `list`). The process strategy with `--more-faults` finds every defect except d11 in most repetitions; d11 (the M58 window) is found rarely. Since M135 the benchmark's images are its manifest form (`hydo/bench/manifest/hydo.yaml`, built on the bare-metal machine by `hydo/bench/build-bench-manifest.sh` into one directory as `explore-ob-bench-<defect or control>-agent-disk.img`; agent images only since M136, and the order service's M67 path is its `restart_may_fail: true`): hydo-bench runs only them (`--kind agent` is accepted; `--kind stack`, the hand-written stack images of `build-stack.sh` with `stack-explore.sh`, was deleted in M145 with `HYDO_BENCH_KIND` and `HYDO_M59_SUFFIX`; `--kind shell` in M136). A pool boots an image with its manifest's `guest.ram_mib` and `guest.cpu` (M136). Since M146 the images are built from sources and pinned Nix store paths only (the manifest's `root.nix` MySQL and OpenJDK, Kafka's libs from its store path, the pinned Redis; the order services always by `hydo/bench/build-order-services.sh` with franz-go v1.22.2, `hydo/stack/go.mod`), on the bare-metal machine with its Nix; the hand-written stack images, their builders (`build-bench{,-m59,-bg}.sh`), `hydo/explore/stack-explore.sh`, `hydo/explore/stack-src*/` and `build-stack.sh`'s explorer hooks are deleted (`git show ed706db:<path>`). `build-stack.sh` stays for the flagship stack images (`hvx_stack_verify`), which keep franz-go v1.17.1 (`hydo/stack/go.mod.baseline`). The current images and triggers are in `hydo/bench/README.md` "The manifest images from sources (Milestone 146)".

##### Onboarding projects

Every example's fingerprints changed at the switch to agent images (M136) and once more in M140 (hydo-agent 0.3.0 in every image; on hvx the host-call port on by default); the current values are in `docs/REBASELINE.md` section 13 (M155, fingerprint epoch 1; node-kv's, python-kv's, python-kv-hist's and rust-kv's (both architectures) in section 16, M163; M140's in section 9, M136's in section 8) and in the examples' `RESULTS.md` sections "Milestone 155", "Milestone 157" and "Milestone 163"; the shell-image values this section listed until M136 are in docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 136" (verbatim).

- **The project format (M114, experimental until hydo 1.0):** `hydo.yaml`, a JSON plan, the plan's `test:` and the `hydo/` folder are one model (`hydo/crates/hydo-manifest/src/model.rs`), version `format: 1` (a file without it is read as format 1; a newer format is refused first, naming the format it needs). The authority is the generated, committed schema `hydo/schema/project-v1.json` (`hydo guide schema`) and the 57 permanent example documents in `hydo/schema/examples/project/v1/` with their `model.json`; tests fail when the schema is not the model's, when it changed by more than additions since `hydo/schema/released/project-v1.json` (the check of `hydo-schema-compat`, M148, for readers of the current format: a key or value may widen), or when an example reads into another model. Within format 1 keys are only added; unknown keys are errors. The folder's mapping onto the model is MANIFEST.md "The project format". Retired spelling: a history check in `test.checks` (its home is the top-level `checks:`); `hydo migrate [FILE] [--check]` rewrites it and adds `format: 1`, after checking that the file means the same. `hydo init` and `hydo compose` write `format: 1`.
- **Restart policies (M134):** `services[].restart` takes Docker Compose's words (`no`, the default: a service whose process ends by itself stays down until the heal's restart passes; `always`; `unless-stopped`; `on-failure[:max]`). The host controller follows it (`hydo-control/src/schedule/restart.rs`: a supervisor per service from the workload's start and in the recovery boot, Docker's delays of 100 ms doubled up to 60 s in guest time, a restart at a defined stop; hydo's own K=/X= kills keep their restart points). `hydo compose` writes it from `restart:` or `deploy.restart_policy`. MANIFEST.md "Restart policies"; proof `hydo-control/tests/restart.rs`.
- **A restart after the faults that may fail (M136):** `services[].restart_may_fail: true` (default false): when the service does not come back at the heal's restart pass, the run goes on without `workload.retry`, a `cf=` power cut still reaches its recovery boot (which gives the verdict), and without a cut the verdict is `ERROR restart after the faults (<svc>)`. MANIFEST.md "A restart after the faults that may fail"; proof `hydo-control/tests/restart_may_fail.rs` and the benchmark's order service (it replaced M135's wrapper script).
- A project is described by one `hydo.yaml` (`hydo/onboard/MANIFEST.md`). `hydo build` (or the `hydo-build` program, same command line; `hydo/crates/hydo-build`) compiles it into an agent image (above, "Guest control"); the host controller starts the services, applies fault tokens by service name and runs the invariants (M47's generic init until M136). The `hydo-onboard` skill (`skills/hydo-onboard/`, M93) writes a project's `hydo/` folder.
- Features: services with readiness checks and crash recovery; faults that reach a service's whole process tree (M52); `params:` (M52); `eventually` liveness invariants (M59); Docker/OCI images by digest with `image:` (M59), with `writable: true` a container's writable root (M180: the image's tree as a layer on the data disk, bound over the service's root, kept at a kill and as flushed at a power cut; MANIFEST.md "A writable root for image services"); `guest.ram_mib`, 256–8192 MiB on every engine since M179 (before it 256–3072 on Linux and 256–4096 on the Mac; M59); per-service `addr:` with link faults between services (M60; on the Mac with the second guest kernel, M99); `guest.cpu: v3` (M68, x86_64 only); and `hydo-build --arch arm64` for the Mac (M51).
- **gRPC faults (M90):** a proxy with `protocol: grpc` is a streaming HTTP/2 proxy (`hydo/crates/hydo-world/src/grpc.rs` since M111); `H=` rules `drop`, `status=<NAME>[,effect=yes]`, `delay=`, `reset[=conn]`, `cut=`/`hold=` with `dir=`, selected by route, `rpc=`, `call=` or `p=`/`seed=`; `kind=call` records say what the client got and whether the server acted (`hydo-world check calls`); `hydo explore --grpc-faults`. Example `examples/stack-grpc` (cur, old, planted): `H=orders.place@10-13:drop` passes on cur and old and duplicates order 10 on planted.
- **Generated gRPC drivers (M91, Rust since M113; `hydo/onboard/MANIFEST.md` "gRPC services"):** `hydo/onboard/hydo-grpc-gen <proto dir> [--hints hints.yaml] --out <dir>` (or `--descriptor-set`, `--reflect host:port`) writes the schema and plan, one static client `hydo-grpc` (`hydo/crates/hydo-grpc-gen`, `hydo/crates/hydo-grpc`; the clients come from `--client DIR`, which the wrapper fills with `hydo/grpcgen/build-client.sh`, the same bytes on a Mac and on Linux: amd64 `3926d137…`, arm64 `fd762fa0…`), one test-composer `parallel_driver` per RPC (`drive`, requests from the entry's `HYDO_SEED`) and a starter `test:` section; `steps`/`retry`/`call` for numbered steps, end-of-run retries and invariants. Valid random requests from a seeded stream (hints: ranges, choices, lengths, unique ids, `from: <Rpc>.<field>`), per-attempt deadlines, retries of unknown outcomes with the same request, outcomes ok/failed/unknown from the gRPC status, `HYDO-HIST grpc` records. Demo `hydo/grpcgen/demo` (orders on Redis, planted idempotency race): the minimal schedule `disk=none dseed=d7071eb1f9d436b9 | run P=redis@16+11 W=5764a73c,p1,q2,r200,n3,x0.2.6.13.26-27.34.46-47,o0.2-3` violates on the buggy build (`r1 created 5 orders`) and passes on the fixed one. `examples/stack/hydo-grpcgen.yaml` replaces `hydostack place/retry` with the generated driver.
- **Ready-made SQL workloads and checks (M182; docs/design/workloads.md, MANIFEST.md "SQL systems: ready-made workloads and checks", `hydo guide workloads`):** `hydo sql-gen --dialect postgres|mysql|libsql --endpoint NAME=ADDRESS[,replica] ... [--workloads bank,list-append,register,set,counter|none] [--shapes batch,interactive]` (in `hydo`, `hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/sqlgen.rs`) writes a project's composer commands and checks (`workload/helper_sql.conf`, `first_sql_init`, `parallel_driver_sql_*`, the bank checks, list-append and register history checks with the claims the endpoints' roles allow: `la` without real time and `lap` with it when replicas are on the route, set and counter read-backs, replica convergence, a `.sql` check). They call the guest program `hydo-sql` (`hydo/crates/hydo-sql`: its own workspace, built like hydo-read, x86_64 `0bb5bc8f…`, arm64 `5e5544d6…`, docs/BUILD-PINS.md), which `hydo build` stages as `/bin/hydo-sql` only when a command or folder file names it (`HYDO_SQL_BIN`, `HYDO_SQL_BIN_ARM64`); it compiles hydo-read's `pg.rs`, `mysql.rs` and `check.rs` into itself through its build script, so hydo-read's sources and pinned bytes are unchanged (making their internals public moved hydo-read's bytes, measured). Outcomes written once (`src/db.rs`; retryable SQLSTATE 40001/40P01, MySQL 1213/1205, `SQLITE_BUSY` retried as new transactions); `hydo-sql read`/`check` are hydo-read/hydo-check plus the sources `sql`, `libsql`, `dump` and `world` (the fake world's record). A non-executable `checks/<final|always|eventually>_<name>.sql` is a query that must return no rows (`-- hydo: store=<endpoint>`), read by hydo-manifest's folder reader (an addition: such a file was refused before; no schema change; example case `sql-checks-folder`). Proofs on the build machine with KVM: `examples/libsql-replica` now uses only generated files (its 868-line client deleted) and reproduces both durability findings of M173, twice each, and the process exploration finds the restart finding blind (4 of 100, as in M173); `examples/postgres-sql` (the voting app's PostgreSQL, all five workloads) runs clean, cut and kill schedules twice identically and its swarm exploration finds lost acknowledged set elements and counter increments on a lying disk. `hydo-bench rebaseline --check --build-only` on the bare-metal machine: 33 of 39 hvx images have their recorded bytes, the other 6 are open item 53's, as in M164 (docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 182").
- **Docker Compose import (M84, Rust since M106):** `hydo compose <docker-compose.yaml>` (or the `hydo-compose` program) writes a starting `hydo.yaml`. Images are pinned by digest from the registry (no skopeo), recorded in `hydo-compose.lock.json` and fetched by `fetch-images.sh`, which calls `hydo-fetch-image` (M107). Each service gets its own `addr:` (with `network: bridge`), and the Compose names resolve through `/etc/hosts`. The importer maps healthchecks to readiness, volumes to the data disk and `restart:` to restart policies, and it writes a TODO workload and TODO invariants for the `hydo-onboard` skill to fill in. Image services gained `mounts:` (bind, volume with copy-up, tmpfs). Example `examples/compose-voting` (Docker's voting app, 5 services, 2048 MiB): clean and `K=worker@5+5` OK, `C=12` VIOLATION (the app acknowledges votes held in a Redis list that has no persistence); since M134 its check says what it saw (database not answering, the `votes` table not there yet, too few votes counted).
- **Store readers (M88, Rust since M112):** `hydo-read <store> <args>` prints MySQL/PostgreSQL rows, a Kafka topic, Redis keys or etcd keys as sorted JSON Lines (exit 2 = could not read), and `hydo-check <check>` compares two readings (subset, equal, exactly-once, disjoint, no-duplicates, count, never-wrong-value) with one explanation line and the invariant exit codes. One static Rust binary (`hydo/crates/hydo-read`, its own Cargo workspace, `build.sh` for x86_64 and arm64; bytes per build host in `docs/BUILD-PINS.md`), staged by `hydo-build` only when a command (also `test:` entries and `hydo/` folder files) calls it. Examples `stack/hydo-read.yaml`, `miniflux/hydo-read.yaml`, `redis-composed-read/`, `examples-mac/redis/hydo-read.yaml`; the stack's pinned-reproducer schedule violates on the old order service (order 11) and passes on the fixed one. Native tests: `hydo/crates/hydo-read/native-test.sh` (build machine) and `bare-metal.sh` (the bare-metal machine, in a chroot with the stores of the recorded images).
- **The onboarding skill: process apart from facts (M170, user decisions 2026-11-07):** `skills/hydo-onboard/` holds only the process (SKILL.md and `references/install.md`, `inventory.md`, `choosing-checks.md`, `pitfalls.md`), with its own version (`metadata.version` 1.0.0, `metadata.hydo-min` 0.1.0) and its own releases (tag `skill-v<version>`, assets `hydo-skill-<version>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS`, built reproducibly by `hydo/dist/skill/build-skill-release.sh` with `hydo-skill-pack`; docs/RELEASING.md "Releasing the onboarding skill", docs/PUBLISHING.md). Every hydo fact (keys, commands, options, fault kinds, limits, examples, `hydo init`'s template) is in the guide `hydo/guide/`, built into `hydo` and printed by `hydo guide <topic>` (new topics `workflow` and `services`; the old topic names and the old `references/…`/`assets/…` paths still answer; `hydo guide` alone prints the version, how to get the skill and the topics; `hydo guide skill` prints SKILL.md). The skill checks hydo first (`hydo --version`, M169's; 0.1.0 prints usage), asks before installing it, and with 0.1.0 reads 0.1.0's own `hydo guide`. Claude Code: the marketplace `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` lists the folder itself as the plugin `hydo-onboard` (no `plugin.json`, no copy or link; `/plugin marketplace add kakoc/hydo`, `/plugin install hydo-onboard@hydo`). Other tools: `hydo skill install --agent <tool>` and the new `hydo skill update [--check] [--version V]` (`hydo-cli` `src/skillupdate.rs`: the newest `skill-v*` from `HYDO_RELEASE_API`, the archive accepted only with the sha256 its `SHA256SUMS` names, swapped in one step, nothing else written). `skill_check` also checks the skill's version against the plugin entry and that every `hydo guide <topic>` the skill or the guide names exists.
- **The onboarding skill for any AI tool (M93):** the skill is an Agent Skills folder (https://agentskills.io/specification) at `skills/hydo-onboard/` (SKILL.md, `references/`; its `assets/` moved to `hydo/guide/` in M170), valid by skills-ref; it writes the code-first `hydo/` folder by default. Both release CLIs have `hydo guide [topic|manifest]` (until M170 it printed the skill, so any tool could be told "run `hydo guide` and follow it"; since M170 that is `hydo guide skill`), `hydo skill install --agent claude|codex|cursor|copilot|gemini|all [--user] | --to DIR` (`.claude/skills/` for Claude Code, `.agents/skills/` for Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Gemini CLI) and `hydo init` (the `hydo/` skeleton, `.gitignore` lines and a marked section in AGENTS.md, idempotent), in `hydo/crates/hydo-agents` (M106); the Rust test `hydo-agents/tests/skill_check.rs` (M108) validates the skill and its synced copies.
- **A GUI application through a real browser (M166, an experiment):** `hydo/onboard/examples/compose-voting-browser/` (design and costs in `docs/design/gui-testing.md`) is the voting app with headless Chromium 156 (`chromedp/headless-shell:156.0.8078.48` by digest) as the voters. The static Rust driver `hydo-gui` speaks the DevTools protocol over `--remote-debugging-pipe`, and an acknowledgement is what the page shows after the click. Chromium is deterministic under hvx with no special measures: fresh-boot runs are twice identical, and the screenshots are pixel-identical. Results on x86_64, each twice: clean OK `f4c8cd57de61b337`; `K=worker@5+10 C=12` VIOLATION `screen.confirmed_counted_soon` `0d240a50bec1aa87` (12 votes shown as cast, 5 counted); `K=db@5+5` VIOLATION `results.page_live` `b22f460ebda8308c` (the results page stays down after PostgreSQL restarts). Image `f84c3412…` (+537 MB), 3072 MiB, 41–51 s per run. On the Mac, each twice: clean OK `0155008471df8611`; `disk=cut | run K=worker@5+10 C=12` VIOLATION `91c1e47f1e3e27d8` (12 shown as cast, 4 counted).
- **The first third-party project (M141):** `hydo/onboard/examples/nats-jetstream/`, a three-node NATS JetStream cluster onboarded from a Compose file with only the skill and the `hydo` command (Mac, agent images, `network: bridge`): one command (publish), one check (every acknowledged message readable after the faults), a Go test client, `params:` for the release (`nats=2.10.22|2.10.23|2.12.1`) and the configuration (`conf=nats-server-sync-always.conf`). Jepsen's 3.1 (2.10.22 deletes the whole stream) found blind at seed 1 of `hydo explore --strategy process --new-faults`, shrunk to `disk=cut dseed=4127cc1347fae6ba | run C=30 W=:p1,r1000,cparallel_driver_publish,0.0.0.1390654497` (b22 `8c81413d2915448a` twice), passing on 2.10.23 (every one of 30 cut points loses the stream on 2.10.22 with `sync_interval: always`, none on 2.10.23); without a power cut too: two blind schedules on the `always` image, shrunk by hand to one kill plus a pause (`K=n1@15+1 P=n1@1+1`, `04d81d362011c8c5`) or plus a clock step; all three nodes killed at once by reactions `A=nats.publish_acked:kill-n1 A=…:kill-n2 A=…:kill-n3` (b22 `2fb2fcece2249f37`); 3.4 (the default `sync_interval`) as a configuration finding with `C=12` (2.12.1 default: 20 of 20 acknowledged messages lost `bdc72936b4501190`; `always`: OK `f43c79941cec2bbd`). Tables and the friction log: its RESULTS.md.
- Examples in `hydo/onboard/examples/`: redis, redis-ram, redis-oci, stack, miniflux (M52), etcd (M60), avx2 and restate-oci (M68), node-kv (M80, Node.js with the JavaScript SDK, Mac), rust-kv (M82, Rust with the Rust SDK, static musl via rust-lld; Mac, and x86_64 image `explore-ob-rust-kv-v2`), python-kv (M83, Python with the Python SDK, Mac; also python-kv-hist) (the current values of these four: docs/REBASELINE.md section 16, M163); the Mac copies in `hydo/onboard/examples-mac/` (redis, redis-ram, redis-bridge, ledger, ledger-spin, redis-composed).
- **The SDKs as registry packages (M160, M163; nothing published yet):** the four assertion SDKs: crates.io `hydo-assert` (`sdk/rust`), PyPI `hydo-assert` (`sdk/python`), npm `hydo-assert` (`sdk/js`), and the Go module `github.com/kakoc/hydo/sdk/go` (`sdk/go`, packages `hydoassert` and `hydohist`, Go 1.22+, published by the tag `sdk/go/v<version>`), all at the release's version with Apache-2.0 and a `LICENSE` copy. The Rust test SDK (`hydo-test`, `hydo-test-macros`, `cargo-hydo`, `sdk/rust-test`; `cargo-hydo` its own crate since M160) is not published until the user decides about code-first tests (user, 2026-11-07): `publish = false`, which the `sdks` test requires. **The public API (M163)** is only what a user's program calls (declare, evaluate with `check`/`hit`/`cmp`/`fire`/eventually, `catalog`, `setup_complete`, the details type, the history recorder and its token functions); a comparison is `cmp` with an operator (the named greater/less helpers and `emit_line` are gone); the rest is Rust `#[doc(hidden)]`, Python `_`, JavaScript outside the `.d.ts`, Go unexported (docs/PUBLISHING.md "The API a first publication freezes"). `hydo/stack/hydoassert` and `hydohist` stay as a frozen copy inside the module `hydostack` (the order service's bytes are inside recorded images); `cargo test -p hydo-release --test it sdks::` fails when `sdk/go` and that copy differ beyond three documented lines of `cases_test.go` and the seven identifiers `sdk/go` made unexported in M163 (`Type` → `kind`, `TAlways` … `TEventually` → `tAlways` … `tEventually`, mapped back word by word before the byte comparison; `sdk/README.md` "The Go module and the frozen copy in `hydo/stack`"), and when any package's name, version, license, repository or `LICENSE` copy is off. How to publish, in order, and what is permanent: `docs/PUBLISHING.md`; a version change moves the bytes of rkv, redis-composed-rs, node-kv and python-kv (listed there).
- Assertion SDKs: Go (`sdk/go`; frozen copy `hydo/stack/hydoassert`), shell (`hydo_assert.sh`), JavaScript/TypeScript for Node.js (`sdk/js`, M80), Rust (`sdk/rust`, crate `hydo-assert`, std only, M82; call-site macros with file:line and `declare!`, registered before `main`) and Python (`sdk/python`, distribution `hydo-assert`, import `hydo_assert`, standard library only, Python 3.8+, thread- and asyncio-safe; M83). A manifest with `buggify: true` turns the schedule token `B=` into the SDKs' BUGGIFY seed, and `hydo explore --buggify` keeps `B=` for it (M80). **Shared cases (M110):** the Rust SDK is the reference; its test `cargo test --test cases` (in `sdk/rust`; `HYDO_BLESS=1` rewrites them) writes `sdk/cases/` (67 cases, 114 runs since M163: each a call sequence, an output target and a BUGGIFY configuration, with the exact bytes and return values), and the Go (`go test ./...` in `sdk/go` and in `hydo/stack/hydoassert`), Python (`python3 -m unittest discover -s sdk/python/tests`) and JavaScript (`node --test` in `sdk/js`) SDKs each read every case and compare their own bytes, with no other language installed. The cases equal Go 1.26.5's output (the guest Go; with Go 1.27 the invalid-UTF-8 cases are skipped); format and how to add a case: `sdk/README.md`, "The shared cases".
- **The test composer** (M86, `hydo/onboard/MANIFEST.md` "The test composer"): a plan's `test:` (or the `hydo/` folder next to `hydo/hydo.yaml`) lists commands by kind prefixes (`first`, `parallel_driver`, `serial_driver`, `singleton_driver`, `anytime`, `eventually`, `finally`) and checks (`final`, `always`, `eventually`) as argv lists; the hydo-composer crate expands them into the manifest's workload, provisioning and invariants, the host controller runs rounds of commands from `W=<seed>,p<at once>,q<per round>,r<ms>[,n,t,x,o]` (the guest composer `hydo-composer.sh` did until M136), and the explorer draws and shrinks `W=` for such plans only. Driver exit status 100 = violation. `hydo repro --regressions` / `hydo save` on both CLIs; `hydo_version:` and `format: 1` in the plan; `hydo/VERSION` is the engine version. Rust test SDK `sdk/rust-test` (crate `hydo-test`: `system()` builder, `#[driver(..)]`, `#[check(..)]`, `<bin> plan` on the host, `cargo hydo`). Example `examples/redis-composed/` (and `-rs`, and the Mac copy under `hydo/onboard/examples-mac/`, atomic and racy builds: `W=0000002a,p4,q2,r100` passes on the atomic build and violates on the racy one). **Stable compositions (M98):** commands have ids `<kind>_<name>`; the shrinker's output and `hydo save` use the resolved form `W=:p,r,c<id>+<id>,<entry>.<round>.<k>.<seed>,...` (or `W=@<key>` staged from a `# compose:` line when long), so a saved regression replays the same commands when commands are added or reordered, fails with a clear message when a used command is gone, and warns when its content changed (`# command-sha:`); old seed-form regressions with `# commands:` replay against that list.
- **History checks (M87, Rust checkers since M105):** a manifest's `checks:` (`type: linearizable` with `model: register|cas`, or `type: list-append` with a `consistency:` level), or a composer plan's `test.checks` of kind `linearizable` / `list_append` (`hydo/checks/linearizable_<name>` = its read-back), make the workload record operations with `hydo_hist` (Go `hydo/stack/hydohist`, Rust `hydo_assert::history`, JavaScript and Python recorders since M96) and the host check them after the run (`hydo-history`; `hydo run`, `hydo explore`, `hydo check-history`); the verdict names a sound witness. Examples `examples/redis/hydo-hist.yaml`, `examples/etcd/hydo-hist.yaml`, `examples/redis-composed-hist/`, `examples-mac/redis/hydo-hist.yaml`, `examples/python-kv/hydo-mac-hist.yaml` (results `hydo/history/RESULTS.md`).
- **Fake outside services and protocol faults** (M89, Rust `hydo-world` since M111, `hydo/onboard/MANIFEST.md` "Fake outside services and protocol faults"): `fakes:` declares fake HTTP (and cleartext-HTTP/2 gRPC) services with routes, templated answers, idempotency keys and webhooks back to the system; `proxies:` puts a fault proxy (`tcp`, `http`, `grpc`) in front of a real service. One static in-guest program, `hydo-world` (`hydo/crates/hydo-world`, `build.sh`, the cross-check `tests/xcheck.rs`; x86_64 `082592ae…`, arm64 `fefcca66…`), serves them and records every request (`/tmp/hydo/world.log`; a summary goes to the console before the verdict). Schedule token `H=<target>@<from>-<to>:<rule>,...` (`status=`, `retry-after=`, `delay=`, `drop`, `reset`; webhooks `dup`, `reorder`, `late=`, `lost`; `p=`, `effect=yes|no`), decided by a hash of the token and the request's index. `hydo-world check at-most-once|exactly-once|effect-for-acked|none-after` reads the record as an invariant; `hydo-world event <name> <ref>` adds the system's own events. At a power cut the world is frozen and carried into the recovery boot by the host controller (`Ending::PowerCut::world`; hydo-world's limit is 3,000 bytes). Example `examples/shop` (planted bug: a new idempotency key per charge retry): `H=payments.charge@0-1:drop` violates on the buggy build and passes on the fixed one, also on the Mac; the buggy build fails exactly the 48 "effect without answer" points of the 228 of `--sweep protocol` (M89, M127). **HTTPS (M180):** `tls: {hosts: [...], port: 443}` on a fake or proxy: hydo-build makes the image's own test CA and a certificate per endpoint (P-256 keys derived from the manifest, RFC 6979 signatures, validity 2000 to 2099: reproducible), maps the names in `/etc/hosts`, adds the CA to the guest's and every image's system bundles and sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE`; `hydo-world-tls` (hydo-world with the cargo feature `tls`, pure-Rust TLS 1.3; 0.2.0 x86_64 `69b2828f…`, arm64 `e288d4e9…`) is staged instead of hydo-world only for such manifests, so the plain program and every recorded image keep their bytes (MANIFEST.md "HTTPS for fakes and proxies"; example `examples/medusa`).
- **Error logs as findings (M94, Rust host side since M104; `hydo/onboard/MANIFEST.md` "Error logs as findings"):** with `errors:` in a manifest (per service `format: auto|redis|none`, `files:`, `match:`/`ignore:`, `normalize:`, `level: warning`), the host controller reads each service's log at the end of every boot and prints one `HYDO-ERRLOG` record per error kind (a template with times, numbers, ids and client ports blanked); `hydo-errors` gives each kind a signature and compares it with `hydo/known-errors.yaml` (`sig:` or `match:`, a reason, optional `with:`/`during:` faults; not in the image, so accepting changes no fingerprint). New kinds are findings: the explorer lists them in `report.md` and `exploration.json`, shrinks each (`--errors-shrink`) and runs the minimal schedule twice; `unknown: fail` or `--errors fail` also fails the run; `hydo errors list|accept|check` on both CLIs. Examples `examples/redis-errors/` and `examples/stack/hydo-errors.yaml` + `known-errors.yaml`.
- **Service networks (M95):** `network: bridge` gives every service its own network namespace (private `localhost`, `eth0` = its `addr:` in 10.89.0.0/16) on one bridge at 10.89.0.1 (the workload, the checks and `hydo-world`). `setup:`/`cmd:`/`ready:` and `hydo-oci` run in the namespace. `N=`/`O=`/link faults are netem on the veths and act on real traffic, and a heal prints the packets they saw; `F=` freezes in the frozen service's namespace (the agent's `freeze` with `netns`, M131). On the Mac with the second guest kernel (M99). `hydo compose` writes it (`--network loopback` = M84). The explorer draws links only between services joined by `depends_on`. Examples `examples/redis-bridge` (and `examples-mac/redis-bridge`) and the voting app. Guest kernel modules the release lacked (`llc`, `stp`, `bridge`, `veth`) come from the guest kernel's own Nix store path (`hydo-nar-extract`, M108).
- **arm64 parity (M96):** `hydo-build --arch arm64` builds `fakes:`/`proxies:`, `hydo-read`/`hydo-check`, `params:`, and (with the second guest kernel, M99) `addr:`, `network: bridge` and the freeze; the Mac `hydo run` and `hydo explore` run the history checkers; the gRPC demo runs with the arm64 generated client (`hydo/grpcgen/demo/hydo-mac.yaml`).
- Images of the examples with network or link faults made before M71 dropped netem's queue at a heal (M77 rebuilt them as `-nq`). On etcd 3.5.5 the 14685 bug is found (M60, M78, M127: 7–8 of 30 process seeds; `disk=none dseed=1 | run K=etcd1@10+1 P=etcd3@26+1` shows the second symptom, a client's revision going back) and absent on 3.5.6.

##### hydo 0.2.0 (M177; built and verified, nothing published)

- **The release commit** is `9d08b660` (the version 0.2.0 everywhere it lives, the marketplace file live at `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, every example re-recorded); docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 177". Its five files and `SHA256SUMS` are in `hydo/dist/out/0.2.0/` of the main checkout (git-ignored), each platform built twice to the same bytes: `hydo-linux-0.2.0.tar.gz` `7c396fbd61c33627db6daf40ca45eb7ea63db9c5a5369d2238c679754bee898a`, `hydo-linux-0.2.0-sources.tar.gz` `08ffe7ea747248236852f7a5513ac99692b572577b7eb28a36f69b78b46d4366`, `hydo-mac-0.2.0.tar.gz` (signed and notarized, submission `3ded9dc3-e953-4bd8-9ff5-29e2433a2ecc`) `2cfacb95235b2486020725476944af0757d51ab8cbac05cad7170bdcdd52d4f0`, `hydo-mac-0.2.0-sources.tar.gz` `e3238bdb465dda48cb29a00737b717dc6cc2e6277d994d7fe2faa8786109a3e4`, `hydo-mac-0.2.0-signatures.tar.gz` `e34560d004ff11d581e5505198c943a9e50bce9f250cf9bd22b2f47436722591` (attached to the unsigned build `8029a162…` it gives the signed tarball byte for byte). The run engine needs no compiling. `hydo doctor|module|build|run|repro|explore|report|init|guide|skill` drive everything, and runs/reloads share the bare-metal machine's `~/.hvx-module.lock` (M75). As a user who cannot open `/dev/hvx` the engine runs as `bin/hydo-hvx` under `libexec/hvx-run sudo`; as root (or with the udev rule) it runs inside `hydo` (M137).
- `hydo build` needs no Nix: bundled busybox, static helpers, guest tc/iptables closures and modules, and e2fsprogs + libfaketime run with their own glibc loader. Images are the same bytes on any machine: frozen build clock read in UTC+4 (`TZ=UTC-4` on every faketime call; since M81 hydo-build and the hand-written build scripts set it themselves, so a plain build in any zone matches the build machine), no host `/etc/mke2fs.conf`, umask 022, root inodes owned by 0:0.
- Runs need no sudo when the user can open the device: `hydo module udev install` (or `install.sh --udev`) installs an optional udev rule giving `/dev/hvx` to group `hydo`, mode 0660; `libexec/hvx-run` then drops sudo. Anyone in that group can run guests through the kernel module, so it is for people one would give sudo. Not installed on the bare-metal machine (M81).

##### Several virtual CPUs

- With `HVX_VM_SMP_SCHED` and the PMU clock, one `HVX_RUN` runs every vCPU in turns of exactly Q guest branches (or seeded lengths), on one shared clock, and stops only at clean points. `HVX_GET/SET_SCHED` carry the scheduler state (M66).
- With `HVX_VM_SMP_BOOT`, real Linux starts the other CPUs with INIT and STARTUP IPIs and boots on 2, 3 and 4 vCPUs, identically across boots and branches: 2 vCPUs `6584c954c2839491`, 3 `e1a2bb0dd744a9ab`, 4 `1dfafae6887e3a01` (`hv/hvx/hvx_smp_boot_verify.c`, M69). Device interrupts are routed by destination.
- Tests in `deploy-metal.sh`: `hvx_sched_pmu_test` (snapshot `73a465516c4e0094`), `hvx_sched_race_test` (grid `8cb7c61a2393f44e`), `hvx_sipi_test` (`eef5c1ebd4df2e7d` / `c8d015ab3b57252d`), `hvx_sched_sweep_test 2000` (`39971eed9c2f35fe`) and the 2-vCPU boot.
- The explorer takes `--vcpus N` and `--turns`, and `hvx_stack_verify` takes `HVX_VCPUS`; so does `hydo-bench run` (`hydo/knownbugs/sqlite/hunt.py` did; it was deleted in M108). Measured value so far (M74): on the benchmark's race defects and the SQLite WAL bug, several vCPUs found nothing that one vCPU with concurrent clients or tick jitter misses, at about 3× the cost per run; each turn end costs about 0.8 ms of host time, about 0.49 ms with the opt-in margin 160, and burst turns (M85, side module only so far) make dense switching affordable on average. Write-ups: `hv/hvx/SMP_PLAN.md`, `hv/hvx/SMP_STAGE1.md`, `hv/hvx/SMP_STAGE2.md`, `hydo/explore/TURNS.md`.

##### The Mac backend

- **Homebrew (M168):** `brew install kakoc/tap/hydo` installs the published Mac tarball of v0.1.0 (`5c02e7f3…`) on Apple Silicon with macOS 13 or later. The tap is the public repository https://github.com/kakoc/homebrew-tap (`Formula/hydo.rb`, a README, Apache-2.0). The formula puts the unpacked release unchanged into the keg's `libexec` (Homebrew neither cleans nor relocates `libexec`; it copies `LICENSE` into the keg's top directory so that Homebrew does not move the release's own out of `libexec`), links `hydo`, `hydo-build` and `hydo-fetch-image` into Homebrew's `bin` (hydo finds its release through the resolved symlink), and runs `hydo setup` as its `post_install_steps` (Homebrew 7's replacement of `post_install`), which checks every file and signs `bin/hydo-hvm` inside the keg; `brew uninstall` removes the keg with the setup record. Its `test do` runs `hydo setup --check`, `hydo doctor` and `hydo build --check` on the Redis example. `hydo/dist/mac/update-homebrew.sh <version> <tap clone>` rewrites the formula's `url` and `sha256` from a release's `SHA256SUMS` (docs/RELEASING.md step 8). Checked on this Mac: doctor all checks passed, the Redis image `a3447614…`/`9ddfc929…`, `disk=none | run` `67e5d6469f1a90a5` and `disk=cut | run C=12 R=everysec` `a6870a92a1bbf0ae` twice each, `brew test`, `brew audit --strict --new --online` clean; docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 168".
- **The Rust Mac engine (M143):** `hydo/crates/hydo-hvm` is `hv/hvm/hvm.c`, the virtio devices, `spin_observer.c` and `explore/serve.c` (hvmx) ported function by function on Hypervisor.framework (`unsafe` only in `hv.rs` and `mem.rs`), on M142's typed calls (`hydo_hvx::port::Port`, hydo-schedule's `Schedule`; hvmx's text only in the program, through `hydo_hvx::text::TextPort`) and M144's configuration (`hydo_config::hvm`). It is the only Mac engine (`hydo_engine::hvm::program`: `HYDO_HVM_ENGINE`, else the tree's `target/release/hydo-hvm`, else the release's `bin/hydo-hvm`); `HYDO_HVM=inproc` runs it in the calling process (one VM per process; the process must carry the hypervisor entitlement). Identical to hvmx on every comparison: M119's lock-step check, M121's agent boot check, the netns boot `33ab6e219a6afd5c`, all 67 schedules of docs/REBASELINE.md 9.1 plus four host-token schedules (each the same RESULT, the Rust runs twice identical; 9.1's values on the four images with M140's bytes), and six explorations by `engine_equiv`; equally fast. `hv/hvm/explore/lockstep-check.sh` has an agent-image variant of its `run`/`rewind` groups (`hydo-control/examples/hvm_agent_check.rs`).
- **The C Mac engine deleted (M147):** `hv/hvm/hvm.c`, `virtio.c`, `virtio.h`, `virtio_blk.c`, `virtio_int.h`, `virtio_net.c`, `spin_observer.c`, `explore/serve.c`, `explore/build.sh`, `cut-test.sh`, `explore/netfault/check.py` and `hv/guest-control-exp/` (15 files, 3,566 lines), with every user: `HYDO_HVM=c` and `hvm::program`'s fallback, `hydo doctor`'s check of `hv/hvm/hvm`, `lockstep-check.sh`'s `ENGINE=c`, the release scripts' copies of `hvm`/`hvmx` (the release ships `bin/hydo-hvm` only), and `hydo build`'s Mac helper VM, which formats the data disk with `hydo-hvm hvm run` now (`Release::Mac { engine }`; the same disk bytes). `hydo-hvm/tests/c_layout.rs` compares with the C's recorded answers (`tests/golden/c_layout.txt`; `HYDO_HVM_C_SRC` checks against the C from git again). The C files' notes (the interrupt delivery rule, the spin rules, the fault model, the engine's particulars) are in the crate's module documentation. The M48 boot (`81711ada76a4a236`) was not taken with the Rust engine: its `Image` and initramfs are on neither machine any more.
- Real arm64 Linux 6.6.35 boots bit-identically on the M2 (boot `81711ada76a4a236`), also under full host load and from branches (M48). The guest kernel needs `CONFIG_ARM_ARCH_TIMER_FORCE_CNTPCT` (`hv/hvm/linux/force-cntpct.patch`), LSE atomics and `CONFIG_ARM64_HVM_IDLE_HVC` (M48, M51).
- It has virtio-mmio disk and network devices with the same fault model as hvx (with delays counted in exits), runs Redis and miniflux with PostgreSQL, and serves the explorer (`hydo-hvm`, until M143 the C `hvmx`; `hydo explore` on the Mac). The Redis `disk=none | run` baseline is `ca13bcd1d77e2b4b` (M51, M53).

##### Guest control: every image is an agent image (M116–M136)

- **The switch (M136, step C3):** every image `hydo build` makes has the guest agent `hydo-agent` (Rust, PID 1, primitives only; pinned since M140 at 0.3.0, x86_64 `398f297e…`, aarch64 `099e5444…`; M136's 0.2.0 was `b72c5caa…`/`340a1eec…`; docs/BUILD-PINS.md) as its first process and `/etc/hydo/control` = `agent 1`; the host controller `hydo-control` (inside `hydo`, `hydo-explore`, `hydo-bench`) drives services, workload, faults and checks through it, under lock-step control of both engines. The shell init (`hydo-init.sh`), its spliced extensions (`hydo-init-*.sh`, `hydo-liveness.sh`), the guest composer (`hydo-composer.sh`) and `hydo-build`'s `init.rs` are deleted (`git show d9202e7:hydo/onboard/<file>` restores them); `--control shell` and `--print-init` are refused with a message, `--control agent` is accepted and changes nothing; the default image name is `explore-ob-<name>` again. Since M145 the engines run agent images only: the plain boot to the shell init's markers, RUN, BRANCH and `--control one` are deleted from both Rust engines and the protocol crate, and a shell-init image is refused ("built before Milestone 136; rebuild it with hydo build"); the pinned reproducers are agent images of the stack example. Current example fingerprints: docs/REBASELINE.md section 13 (M155, fingerprint epoch 1; before it sections 8 and 9; x86_64 and Mac, every recorded schedule twice identical).
- **The design and its steps:** `docs/design/guest-control.md` (steps A1–C3 done; D1, the host-call port, and D2, reactive exploration, later). The protocol: `hydo/crates/hydo-agent-proto` (version 1, additions only, checked by `hydo-schema-compat` for readers of the released protocol: new names only in a refusal's `err` and in command fields; schema `hydo/schema/agent-v1.json`; features `freeze`, `freeze-netns`). The engines' lock-step protocol: `hydo/crates/hydo-hvx` (`src/engine.rs`, `src/ctl.rs`; until M137 the C engine's header) and `hydo/crates/hydo-hvm` (`src/serve.rs`; until M147 the C `hv/hvm/explore/serve.c`) (CTL, RESUME, `--control one|boot`, EVENT/SENT/DROP/STOP, SEND/ACK/SNAP/CONT/END, DISKOFF, CUT). Every run leaves a control transcript (`<tag>.control.jsonl`, `ctl=` in the RESULT, `Run.control` in the results); `hydo repro --transcript` types one again.
- **The controller** (`hydo/crates/hydo-control`; its `HANDOFF.md` has every decision where the shell was ambiguous, M120–M136): one Rust function per former shell function (`src/schedule.rs`), the feature modules (`src/schedule/{fakes,freeze,netfault,netns,history,errlog,composer,restart}.rs`, `src/features/{liveness,clock,buggify,recovery}.rs`), restart policies (M134), `restart_may_fail` (M136). Proofs without a VM: the identity corpora (`tests/corpus.rs`, `corpus_net.rs`, `features.rs`, `fakes.rs`, `m123.rs`, `restart.rs`, `restart_may_fail.rs`) on a scripted agent and engine, compared with the controller's recorded transcripts (`tests/golden/`) and replayed; until M145 also against shell models of the deleted shell files (`tests/support/model*.rs`, deleted in M145; commit fb54e8d has them).
- **Equivalence before the switch (C2):** `docs/C2-MAC.md` (M128, M130, M131, M134), `docs/C2-LINUX.md` (M127), `docs/C2-BENCH.md` (M129, M133, M135): the agent images gave the shell images' verdicts at the level of meaning; every difference was classified (timing, disk-request order) or fixed.
- **Not under control yet:** several vCPUs and a schedule's own `rb=` are refused for agent images (BRANCH was deleted in M145); the Mac engine's lock-step mode refuses SNAP for `tj=`/`pct=` schedules. Lock-step control costs wall time: a boot under control at `rb=16` takes about 1–2 minutes for Redis on hvx, and long idle phases cost many stops (open item 30).

##### Bugs found so far

- In our own order service: a failed cache write failed an order that was already published (M38, fixed in M39); and a duplicate under overlapping retries, a panic on the shared Redis connection, and a crash that forgot which sends had an unknown outcome (M50, all fixed).
- In the stack configuration: with the MySQL binary log off, a commit was visible before its redo fsync finished, found only by the k-th-flush cut (M58, fixed by the binary log in M63); and Kafka's default 7-day retention deleted acknowledged orders after a large forward clock jump (M63, fixed with `log.retention.ms=-1`).
- Upstream: etcd 3.5.5 issue 14685 (member revisions diverge after an online defrag and a crash), found without being told and absent in 3.5.6 (M60); both symptoms reproduce on the `-nq` image (M77, M78).
- Upstream, a known bug found blind (M141): NATS 2.10.22 deletes a whole JetStream stream when every node stops at once shortly after the stream was created (Jepsen's NATS analysis 3.1, nats-server issue 6888, fixed in 2.10.23 by PR 5700): 14 of 50 process-strategy schedules, the first at seed 1, shrunk to one publish and a power cut; also by process crashes alone (reactions); 2.10.23 and 2.12.1 pass. The default `sync_interval` (two minutes) loses acknowledged messages at a power cut on every release (Jepsen 3.4, documented by NATS), `sync_interval: always` does not.
- Upstream, aimed: the SQLite 3.51.2 WAL-reset corruption, reproduced under hydo once a workload restarted the WAL often and its seed was fixed (only timing varied); it passes on 3.51.3 (M85). A blind hunt has not found it: under hydo the workload restarts the WAL 10–70 times less often than natively (M52, M49, M74, M85).
- In the kernel module (M156): the PMU branch clock counted the host's own conditional branches after a host NMI in root mode (perf's NMI handler re-enables every counter), so a tick or a turn end could land a few branches early: rare, host-timing-dependent fingerprint differences (`hvx_sched_sweep_test` failed in about one run of 40). Fixed by keeping the counter's event off in root mode (`pmu_guard`), in the main module since 2026-11-06.
- Upstream, in the order service's Kafka client: franz-go v1.17.1 (issue 1484) lets the idempotent producer acknowledge a record it never wrote, so after a long Kafka pause an acknowledged order is missing from Kafka (M129's agent-only difference, explained in M133). Fixed for the manifest-built images by franz-go v1.22.2 (M135): `disk=none dseed=0 | run P=kafka@14+16`, which lost order 15 on M129's agent control, passes on the new agent control twice (`a41a29598b2738ea`). The stack images keep v1.17.1 as the engine's baselines.

##### `cargo install hydo` (M169; prepared, nothing published)

- The `hydo` command is ready to be published to crates.io (docs/PUBLISHING.md "Publishing the hydo command"): the package in `hydo/crates/hydo-cli` is named `hydo` (so `-p hydo`, not `-p hydo-cli`; the directory keeps its name), and it and the 19 workspace crates it depends on are published under their own names in one documented order (all 20 names free on 2026-11-07); every other workspace crate has `publish = false`. The guest programs are never built by cargo: they, the guest kernels and tools and the engine programs (`bin/hydo-hvm`, signed at setup; `bin/hydo-hvx`, `bin/hydo-kvm`) come from the version's release archive through `hydo setup --get` (M162). A `hydo` in a cargo install prefix (cargo's `.crates2.json` names `hydo`, no `SHA256SUMS` there) uses `$HYDO_HOME/versions/<its version>` as its release root (`hydo-cli/src/ctx.rs` `installed_root`); plain `hydo setup` then installs that version, and `hydo doctor` names `hydo setup --get` for what is missing. The Mac quickstart from a cargo-installed `hydo`, its release fetched from a loopback mirror of the v0.1.0 assets: Redis image `a3447614…`, `disk=none | run` `67e5d6469f1a90a5` and `disk=cut | run C=12 R=everysec` VIOLATION `a6870a92a1bbf0ae`, each twice (docs/REBASELINE.md 13.4's).
- What made the crates build from crates.io alone: files compiled in from outside a crate are read through links inside it (`hydo-cli/pins/<platform>/*.sha256` -> `hydo/dist/<platform>/`, `hydo-agents/embed/` -> the skill and MANIFEST.md, `LICENSE` in every published crate); `hydo-image`'s build script takes a packaged crate's commit from `.cargo_vcs_info.json` and never runs git there; `[workspace.dependencies]` carry versions; dev-dependencies on workspace crates are path only (no published cycle); `include` publishes the sources only. `hydo-agent-proto` keeps its own version (the agent compiles it). `hydo --version` (new) prints the version and commit.
- Checks: `cargo test -p hydo-release --test it crates::` fails when a crate of the closure is not publishable (metadata, versions, included files outside the crate, tests in the package, size, order in docs/PUBLISHING.md, guest programs in the closure, `publish = false` on the others). `hydo/dist/crates/rehearse.sh` is the dry run: one `cargo package` of all 20 (each built from its `.crate`), a stand-in registry (the packed crates plus `cargo vendor`), `cargo install hydo --locked --offline` in a fresh Cargo home outside the repository, and the installed `hydo` run (`HYDO_REHEARSAL_LINUX=1` also checks the Linux code for the musl target).

##### The KVM engine (M159, M161; merged after v0.1.0; in the Linux release since M172's 0.2.0 candidates)

- `hydo/crates/hydo-kvm` runs hydo's x86_64 agent images on stock Linux KVM (`/dev/kvm`, no module, no root; KVM from Linux 5.10, nested virtualization in a VM) with the Mac engine's trade-offs: one vCPU at the v2 level (several vCPUs and `guest.cpu: v3` are refused), guest time counted in the VM exits that reach the engine (exit-free code takes no guest time and gets no timer), interrupts only at exits from the engine's own 8259 PIC, a spin observer that turns exact exit-free cycles into idle (stepping to hardware breakpoints since M159) and, since M161, proves counter loops (`while (flag) n++`) infinite and resolves them in a port of the Mac's rewind mode (`spin=rewind`: checkpoints at stops with KVM's dirty-page log, a replay, the interrupt at the first arrival at the loop's canonical instruction); without the mode such a run ends at once as a SPIN and the host runs it again in the mode, as for hvm (`HVM_SPIN_REWIND=0` turns that off). Since M161 snapshots share memory: the disk is copy-on-write over the mapped image file (hydo-hvm's `disk`, also the Mac engine's), RAM is a sealed `memfd` base (S0, S1) mapped privately plus the pages that differ (from `/proc/self/pagemap`): a stack worker 10 GB to 3.2 GB (2.3 GB of it the image file's shared page cache), Redis 3.6 GB to 0.24 GB. A patched guest kernel (`hv/kvm/linux/`, `bzImage-kvm` `d50fbc67…`, pinned Nix recipe, docs/BUILD-PINS.md) takes all its time from the exit clock and never reads the TSC; the same images as hvx, with the KVM build of their recorded kernel (`hydo_kvm::kernel::TWINS`). `hydo run|repro|explore|doctor --backend kvm` or `HYDO_BACKEND=kvm`. Its fingerprints are its own (one kind of host CPU; `hydo repro` across engines compares verdicts). It has run on Intel (the build machine, a hybrid CPU: performance and efficiency cores give the same fingerprints) and, with the published 0.2.0, on AMD EPYC 9V45 and 9V74 (GitHub's runners, 2026-11-08: the same verdicts, other fingerprints, one per CPU vendor; open item 45 (a)). Current values (M159, unchanged in M161): Redis `disk=none | run` `bfa03053d51bec8a`, `disk=cut | run C=12 R=everysec` VIOLATION `8ed16d6da60c34c6` (191 runs), the stack's pinned-reproducer schedule old `c3419179cf1a55ba` VIOLATION order 11, fixed `c0746a7568ccf3b8` OK; `hv/kvm/kvm-check.sh` 15 of 15 (16 with `SPIN_BIN=`: the counter-loop example `hv/kvm/spin/ledger-spin`, x86_64, `disk=none | run` `f796ae624a9473d1` OK through the rewind mode). Design, every nondeterminism source, the review, the rewind mode and the memory measurements: docs/design/kvm-engine.md; docs/HISTORY.md "Milestone 159" and "Milestone 161". Since M179 guest RAM goes up to 8 GiB: up to 3 GiB in memory slot 0 from address 0, the rest in slot 1 from 4 GiB (`layout::ram_blocks`, `ram_offset`; the dirty-page log per slot, the devices' and the page-table walker's view of RAM through the same rule).

#### Open items

Items marked **[user decision]** need the user before anyone acts on them.

2. **[user decision]** The single-Kafka image (`build-linux.sh` §2l) and `hydo/onboard/examples/stack/hydo.yaml` still use Kafka's default retention, and `build-mysql.sh` and the onboarding stack example still use `skip-log-bin`. Fixing them moves unrelated baselines, so they were left unchanged (M63).
3. **[user decision]** The build machine disk keeps filling up; cleaning other sessions' build outputs needs the user's approval.
4. Several vCPUs (M69): Linux marks the TSC unstable with 2 vCPUs (`tsc=reliable` removes the message). Each PAUSE exit moves the virtual clock, so guest time depends on the PAUSE setting. NMIs between CPUs, logical-destination interrupt routing, virtio-net routing beyond the first deliverable queue, paravirtual lock help and more than 4 vCPUs are not done. `hydo/explore/TURNS.md` lists module wishes: a per-turn length list, a short/long mix and a starve mode.
5. Guest AVX (M68): there is no AVX-512, XSAVEOPT, XSAVEC, XSAVES or PKRU; the pending #GP of an invalid XSETBV is not in the snapshot; and with the flag off, a guest that sets CR4.OSXSAVE anyway reads the host's XCR0.
6. The d11 defect (an ACK on an unflushed flag) has a window of about 3 of ~310 flush-cut points and is rarely found by strategies (M67, M72: 3/6 then 0/6 over 3-repetition cells); measuring its detection rate needs many more repetitions or a cell that always draws `cf=`. The m59 bench set now defaults to `-pin-kr` (Kafka retention fixed, M72). On the M136 agent images (M139, ten repetitions of 60 runs each): process with `--more-faults` 2 of 10, the same with reactions 2 of 10 (one hit each that the other missed, both timing moved by the reactions' extra commands).
7. fwupd still runs on the bare-metal machine; it is harmless to the fixed module. Older single outliers (M34 MySQL, M39 I/O error) were not checked against fwupd times (M65).
8. etcd 3.5.5: 14685's second symptom (a client's revision going back) is reproduced again on the `-nq` image by `K=etcd1@10+1 P=etcd3@26+1` (M78), found by a hand sweep, not by the explorer. Why etcd1's one-revision lead appears only together with the later pause of another member was not investigated.
9. Explorer and tools: the oracle reads Kafka before it restarts when Kafka is killed at the last order (M55); `pp=`/`xt=` are refused in branch mode, and the `xt` shrinker does not turn a seeded policy into a list (M49); the guest RAM size is not part of the schedule string, so a hand-run `hvx_explore one` on a non-default image needs `--ram-mib` (M59); the OK verdict shows only the first invariant's details (M47).
10. etcd 3.6.8 against 3.6.9 (stale reads with a paused leader) showed no difference; it needs timed pauses aimed at the leader.
11. Images built before M71 drop the packets queued in netem when a delay fault is lifted. The onboarding examples and the default stack were rebuilt as `-nq` images in M77; any other image with network faults that predates M71 keeps the old behaviour.
12. Processor Trace limits: guest kernel modules are not traced, very early boot needs tracing started after the kernel's self-patching, JIT-compiled Java is out of scope, buffers of about 1 GiB can fail to allocate, and host PT use is suspended during traced runs (M40). Whole-system coverage runs often filled the 256 MiB buffer (M44).

33. hydo-world in Rust (M111). Known limitation, kept for now and to be improved later: when the real service answers a gRPC call trailers-only (an error status and no message), the gRPC proxy forwards that status in the first HEADERS frame and ends the stream with an empty DATA frame instead of sending trailers, exactly as the Go version did (`grpc.rs`, the module comment). A gRPC client then probably reports INTERNAL ("server closed the stream without sending trailers") instead of the service's own status, and the call record's `status=` still shows the service's code. The fix is to send a trailers-only answer (or the status as trailers) when the upstream answered trailers-only; it changes what clients see and the fingerprints of images with a gRPC proxy, and the cross-check's golden (`tests/xcheck.rs`, the "Fail" and "unknown method" steps) must then be re-recorded on purpose. Also open: only single schedules ran on Rust-world images (no explorer campaign, no `--sweep protocol`); and `hydo-world/build.sh` reaches host-independent bytes with its own recipe (`rustc-host.sh` plus dropping `.comment`), while `hydo-agent` and `hydo-grpc` use M113's (`hydo/grpcgen/rustc-stable` plus `hydo-elf-comment`); moving hydo-world to M113's recipe changes its bytes and so every Rust-world fingerprint.

40. Decided: the release after 0.1.0 is 0.2.0 (user, 2026-11-07), raised in M177 as this item describes; kept as the list of what a version change moves. The first release's version number (M149). `hydo/VERSION` and `build-release.sh`'s default (`HYDO_VERSION`, `0.1.0`) were left at `0.1.0`. What a bump changes: (a) the tarball's and top directory's name (`hydo-linux-<v>`) and the release's `VERSION` and `hydo/VERSION` files, against which a plan's `hydo_version:` is checked (open item 19 says a plan with the M98 `content:` key is refused by an older hydo, which is a reason to bump); `hydo/VERSION` in the repository is the tree's engine version for the same check; (b) the QUICKSTART's `tar xzf hydo-linux-0.1.0.tar.gz` lines; (c) bumping the Cargo workspace version (`Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package] version`, which every workspace crate uses) also changes the bytes of the two guest programs that are workspace members, because Cargo puts the package version into every crate's `-C metadata`: measured in M149 on the bare-metal machine with `0.2.0`, `guest/hydo-grpc` `3926d137…` becomes `f2ad5e72…` and `guest/hydo-world` `082592ae…` becomes `bdafadb3…`, so every image with `fakes:`, `proxies:` or a generated gRPC driver gets new fingerprints and the pins in docs/BUILD-PINS.md must move; `hydo-agent` (0.3.0, its own workspace) and `hydo-read` (0.1.0, its own workspace) do not change, and `exploration.json` records the new version in `hydo_version`. (c) A release installed flat into `~/.hydo` by `install.sh` (the default prefix) is not moved into `versions/`; `--get` leaves its `bin/hydo` alone, and the Linux `install.sh` replaces its whole prefix, the cache inside it included. (e) The Linux side (static musl `hydo`, `--get` of the Linux archive, a kernel fetched for an x86_64 image) ran only in the tests against the local server, not against the real release on a Linux machine. Left: (a) **[user decision]** neither release ships `guest/hydo-world-tls` (0.2.0's scripts were not to change): a release's `hydo build` of a manifest with `tls:` stops naming the missing file until `hydo/dist/{linux,mac}/build-release.sh` build it (`HYDO_WORLD_TLS=1 hydo/crates/hydo-world/build.sh`), `guest-programs.sha256` pins it and the third-party lists name its new crates (rustls, tokio-rustls, p256, aes-gcm, hmac and their RustCrypto dependencies); (b) the arm64 side of both was built into the code but never run (no Mac VM in M180): `tls:` with `hydo-world-tls-arm64`, and `writable: true`, whose arm64 launcher copies the root to the data disk at the first start; (c) CI builds hydo-world without the feature only (no `--features tls` compile for the musl target in `ci.yml`); (d) TLS 1.3 only, no client certificates, Java's own `cacerts` untouched (MANIFEST.md says how to import the CA; Temurin's `USE_SYSTEM_CA_CERTS=1` untried), a gRPC client over TLS was not run (HTTP/2 over TLS was, with curl) and the generated gRPC client `hydo-grpc` has no TLS; a request's `from` in the record is hydo-world's own address; (e) the writable layer is a full copy (the data disk grows by the image's size; disk faults reach the program's own files), not an overlay (no guest kernel of every engine has overlayfs); (f) hvx was not run with a `tls:` or `writable:` image (the Medusa example ran on the KVM engine); (g) the rebaseline check of existing images (`--build-only`, all 39 hvx images as recorded except open item 53's six, the shop's two traced to the checkout's file mode of `hydo.yaml`) ran on the branch at `424a443a`, before 0.2.0 was merged in; (h) hydo-build copies the manifest into the image with the checkout's file mode, so an image's bytes depend on the umask the tree was checked out under (found in M180's comparison; not changed).
59. **[user decision]** The guest programs of the next release (M180, M181, M182). `hydo-world`'s bytes changed with M180 (the TLS code behind a feature, shared sources) and M181 (fake objects, signed webhooks); its pin in `hydo/dist/{linux,mac}/guest-programs.sha256` was NOT moved, so the tree's releases still ship 0.2.0's `guest/hydo-world` and every recorded value stays. Neither release ships `guest/hydo-world-tls` (M180) or `guest/hydo-sql` (M182) yet. At the next release, in one step: build the three with the release scripts, pin them in `guest-programs.sha256`, name their new crates in `hydo/dist/<platform>/third-party.json`, and re-baseline every image with `fakes:` or `proxies:` (`hydo-bench rebaseline --write`; their fingerprints move with the new `hydo-world`; the fingerprint epoch does not change, since no engine, controller, agent or kernel moved). If it is not done, a release's `hydo build` of a manifest with `tls:` or an SQL workload stops naming the missing file, and the release's fakes lack M181's keys.
60. Ready-made SQL workloads (M182; docs/design/workloads.md "Left for later"). Left: (a) neither release ships `guest/hydo-sql` (adding it to `hydo/dist/*/build-release.sh`, the pins and the component lists is a release-script change, held for after 0.2.0); until then a release's `hydo build` of a folder that calls `hydo-sql` stops with "HYDO_SQL_BIN not found at <release>/guest/hydo-sql" and `HYDO_SQL_BIN` must name a build of `hydo/crates/hydo-sql/build.sh`; (b) the MySQL dialect and the arm64 build ran only in unit tests and scripted servers, not in a guest; nothing ran on the Mac; (c) `hydo-world`'s record keeps no request fields beyond `ref` and `idem`, so a refund's amount cannot be compared with the books; recording chosen fields changes `hydo-world`'s pinned bytes and every fakes image's fingerprints (the shop's recorded ones), a user decision for a release that re-pins it; (d) no plain SQLite file source (an embedded database without a server), no business operations from SQL templates, no generated durability knob, no console room for long histories; (e) a counter check has only the lower bound (an attempt that was killed mid-flight leaves no outcome line, so "at most the attempts" is not checked); (f) the PostgreSQL knob `synchronous_commit=off` lost nothing at `C=12` and was not hunted further.
61. Storage faults of one service (docs/design/storage-faults.md "Left for later"). (a) `L=` keeps the writes the kernel had handed to the disk but the disk had not flushed; taking those away too needs the engines to drop the unflushed writes of the partition's block range at the same stop (hvm and KVM first; hvx only on a side module, the user approves a reload); until then `L=` is a power loss of a disk whose volatile cache survived. (b) `G=` changes what the page cache shows, through busybox `dd`; there is no block-level corruption below the file system (misdirected or lost writes of one service). (c) NATS JetStream (Jepsen 3.2, 3.3, 3.5 on 2.12.1) was not hunted with the new tokens: its example needs `storage:` per node and a run on the Mac or KVM (its images and client are not on the machines). (d) The release tarballs were not rebuilt (0.2.0 is published from main without these tokens).
62. No silent passes (M184; `hydo-bench rebaseline --check` from this branch: hvx 131 schedules and kvm 11, nothing moved). Left: (a) an `A=` event is checked only after the run (a warning when no record names it); (b) the `ready:` check of `hydo-build` looks only at `hydo-oci <svc> <program>` commands; (c) **[user decision]** `outcomes_after_cut` stays opt-in until an epoch change makes it the default (or `hydo init`/`hydo compose` write it for new projects); if neither, a check that reads `$HYDO_OUTCOMES` still sees an empty file after a power cut unless its author adds the key (the guide and MANIFEST.md say so).
63. **[user decision]** Trusted publishing (M186). Left: (a) the one-time setup on each registry (docs/PUBLISHING.md "The one-time setup on each registry": the environment `release` on GitHub; a trusted publisher on each of the 21 crates on crates.io, on the PyPI project and on the npm package `hydo-assert`, whose entry expires if unused for two days, so it is added just before a release); without it the publishing jobs fail with an authorization error and the release is published by hand as before (npm then asks for the second factor at every publish); (b) no run of `release.yml` or `packages.yml` has happened (they need the merge to `main`; a `workflow_dispatch` dry run on `main` is the first check, `gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f dry_run=true`); (c) the `go` job creates the tag `sdk/go/v<version>` with the workflow's token: a ruleset that restricts tag creation would refuse it (then push it by hand; the job accepts a tag already on the same commit); (d) a crate that is new to the closure of `cargo install hydo` must have its first version published by hand with a token (crates.io takes a trusted publisher only for an existing crate).
