#### Where to look

- `docs/CI.md`: the GitHub Actions workflow: what runs on which runner, what is skipped there and why, how long a run takes (M167).
- `docs/PUBLISHING.md`: publishing the SDKs to crates.io, PyPI, npm and the Go module proxy, in order, with each dry run, where the tokens live and what is permanent (M160).
- `docs/RELEASING.md`: the release checklist (build each tarball and its sources archive twice, compare, verify from clean prefixes, scan, collect, publish) and how to keep the component lists `hydo/dist/<platform>/third-party.json` complete (M158).
- `hydo/PRODUCT.md`: hydo from a user's point of view — what it offers, the known gaps, and the user's decision on each (2026-10-24): approved and in progress (history checkers, protocol faults and fake outside services, a Rust SDK, Docker Compose import), to document only (CI mode, running locally and in CI, scale, blind spots), not decided (test composer, fast-forwarded time).
- `hv/hvx/hvx.c` (the module), `hv/hvx/hvx_abi.h` (the ioctl ABI shared with userspace), `hv/hvx/hvx_boot.h` (the bzImage loader recipe), and the `hv/hvx/hvx_*_test.c` and `hv/hvx/hvx_*_verify.c` tests and harnesses.
- `hydo/crates/` (the Rust workspace; `hydo-explore` is the explorer, `hydo-bench` the benchmark runner), `hydo/explore/` (notes on vCPU turns and search research; the stack explorer's guest side was deleted in M146), `hydo/stack/` (the order service and the assertion SDK), `hydo/bench/` (the bug benchmark: patches, bases, build scripts, results), `hydo/onboard/` (manifests), `hv/hvx/pt/` (Processor Trace tools), `hv/hvx/race/` (race calibration and side-module scripts), `hydo/cutflush/` (flush-cut findings), `hv/hvx/tdet/` (the SMI test and its side module).
- `hv/hvx/images/` (`build-linux.sh`, `build-stack.sh`, `build-kafka.sh`, `build-mysql.sh`: the x86_64 guest kernel and the hand-written guest images, with the guest programs they compile), `docs/BUILD-PINS.md`, `docs/REBASELINE.md`.

#### Useful tools and references

- Check a change on the real system, not only by reading code: `hv/hvx/deploy-metal.sh` on the bare-metal machine, or the Mac backend's `hydo` (`hydo/dist/mac/`).
- Review changes to the determinism engine with special care, and keep the baseline fingerprints above passing.
- To onboard a project, follow the hydo onboarding skill (`skills/hydo-onboard/SKILL.md`, an Agent Skills folder that any agent can read; `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` hold symlinks to it). Check it with `cargo test -p hydo-agents --test it skill_check:: -- --nocapture` after a change (M108). Since M170 the skill is the process only: a fact about hydo goes into `hydo/guide/` (a `hydo guide` topic), never into the skill, and a skill change raises its `metadata.version` and the plugin entry's version together (docs/RELEASING.md).
- For kernel and VMX work there is no ready-made helper: use the Intel SDM Vol. 3C (VMX chapters), the KVM source, and "Hypervisor From Scratch".

### Milestone 188 — DONE (the package pages rewritten, every example a test)

User decision 2026-11-08: the pages registries show (crates.io and docs.rs, PyPI, npm, pkg.go.dev) were badly written. Rewritten after Diátaxis and the Rust API Guidelines' documentation chapter: the `hydo` crate (what hydo is, install with `cargo install hydo` and `hydo setup`, a first run with the Redis example, testing one's own system), the four assertion SDKs with one parallel structure (what it is, install, one complete program with the exact lines it writes, how-tos, reference), and the 19 internal crates as short pages ("This crate has no stable API", what it contains). Every library's README is its crate documentation (`#![doc = include_str!("../README.md")]`). Examples are tests: the `hydo` page's commands checked against both help texts and run where cheap (`hydo::readme`); the Rust SDK's blocks as doctests plus its complete program compared with `examples/kv_store.rs`; Python and JavaScript tests that run every README block; Go `Example` functions with `// Output:`. hydo-release's `crates` and `sdks` checks fail on a missing page, a relative link, a library whose documentation does not start with its README, an internal page without the stable-API sentence, or SDK pages that differ in structure. `#![warn(missing_docs)]` on `hydo-assert`, every public item documented, 73 rustdoc warnings fixed, `cargo doc` clean. SDK maintainer material moved to `sdk/README.md`. No file inside a recorded image changed (`rkv`, redis-composed-rs and `hydo-agent` byte-identical). The pages show on the registries from the next version.

### Milestone 189 — DONE (the KVM engine at x86-64-v3: `guest.cpu: v3` on KVM; a v3 vCPU on one kind of core of a hybrid CPU; TigerBeetle found not to run on KVM; 2026-11-08)

Branch `worktree-agent-aab5d4ece38bf00d9` from `main` (`f25c9e90`, rebased on `62e4db08`). Design,
every nondeterminism source and the measurements: docs/design/kvm-engine.md, "x86-64-v3".

**Why.** KVM is hydo's main Linux path (no kernel module), and programs built for newer CPUs need
AVX2 at start (TigerBeetle's release binary, the official Restate image). The KVM engine refused
`guest.cpu: v3`.

**What.** `hydo-kvm/src/cpuid.rs`: `Level` and `table_for(level)`; the v3 table is hvx's v3 set
(M68: FMA, MOVBE, XSAVE, AVX, F16C, BMI1, AVX2, BMI2, LZCNT; the XSAVE leaf for x87|SSE|AVX in the
standard format, sub-leaf 1 zero), basic leaves up to 0xD, the same on every host; `check(level)`
names what a host lacks and checks that the host's XSAVE layout puts AVX at 576; the v2 table and
its recorded hash are unchanged. `sys.rs`: `Kvm::with_level` (and `KVM_CAP_XCRS`), XCR0 through
`KVM_GET_XCRS`/`KVM_SET_XCRS` in a v3 vCPU's state (`CpuState.xcr0`, 0 at v2). `cpu.rs`: a v3 state's
hash adds XCR0, XSTATE_BV & 7 and the AVX state; a v2 state hashes as before (a recorded test).
`hybrid.rs`: on a hybrid Intel CPU a v3 vCPU thread is bound to the performance cores the process
may use, else its efficiency cores. `hydo-kvm --cpu v3`; `hydo-engine` passes the image's level to
the KVM engine (only several vCPUs are refused now); `hydo run`/`repro`, `hydo explore --backend
kvm`; `hydo doctor --backend kvm` prints whether v3 can run. `hv/kvm/v3-check.sh` and
`hv/kvm/v3/hydo.yaml`: the v3 check for any KVM host. The guide's capability table, the Linux
QUICKSTART and MANIFEST.md (the CLI golden of `hydo guide manifest` re-recorded, two lines).

**Found: the core decides what a v3 guest's XSAVE writes.** The first runs of the avx2 example on
the build machine gave `963aa26e9b7a5a08` and once another value; pinned to CPU 0 (a performance
core) always `963aa26e9b7a5a08`, pinned to CPU 16 (an efficiency core) always `2068294767586e14`,
unpinned sometimes a third value. RAM dumps of the two kinds differed in two bytes, the low byte of
XSTATE_BV in saved XSAVE areas (2 on the performance core, 3 on the efficiency core: the cores
differ in whether they track the x87 state as initial). Bound to one kind, 20 unpinned runs of the
clock schedule gave one value.

**Checked on the build machine** (Core i7-13700HX, Linux 6.6.35; this tree's static `hydo` built on
the bare-metal machine, in the M172 0.2.0 candidate's prefix): `hv/kvm/kvm-check.sh` 16 of 16 with
every recorded KVM value (Redis's eight schedules, netem, S1 `ac512c2616cef6a4`, the exploration's
46 runs and repro 14 of 14, ledger-spin `f796ae624a9473d1` through the rewind mode); the stack's
pinned reproducers' schedule `c3419179cf1a55ba` and `c0746a7568ccf3b8`, each twice. At v3: the avx2
example `2dcb4305…` OK, `963aa26e9b7a5a08` from fresh boots and from S1, `T=4:3600`
`9da9f9e442eb9aa4`, the v2 control VIOLATION; restate-oci `77978db5…` `disk=none | run` OK 6 of 6
`62acce98929d1369`, `K=restate@2+2` OK 4 of 6 `69c72be4dbd8e583`, `disk=cut | run C=4` OK 4 of 6
`04f9abeff6e9c10b`, each twice (hvx's verdicts); `hv/kvm/v3-check.sh` 5 of 5.

**TigerBeetle.** M179's three-replica image (`4dfaec44…`, 8 GiB, v3) ends `ERROR boot: SPIN` on
KVM: `tigerbeetle format` (the first replica's `setup:`) runs its AVX2 code, then polls io_uring's
completion queue from user space with no system call and no VM exit, so the disk completion (16
exits after the request) never reaches it; with `HYDO_KVM_SPIN_SECS=600` it spun until stopped. The
spin observer cannot prove such a loop (stores, calls, VEX instructions). This is open item 45 (c),
not a v3 problem; the three-replica cluster runs only on hvx (M179).

**Left** (AGENTS.md open items 5 and 45): a v3 guest on an AMD host (`hv/kvm/v3-check.sh` does the check;
docs/design/kvm-engine.md "x86-64-v3" lists the steps for GitHub's runners); TigerBeetle and other io_uring busy-pollers on
KVM; VT-x cannot make XSAVEOPT, XSAVEC or XGETBV1 fault.

### Milestone 191 — DONE (a plan of only checks or regressions keeps the manifest's own workload; 2026-11-08)

**Found** by the CI stage 1 agent (2026-11-08): a `regressions/` folder beside the shop example's manifest, which has its own `workload.run`, made every run pass. The saved double-charge regression passed even on the buggy build. A silent pass, the kind M184 refuses.

**Cause.** hydo-manifest's `scan_folder` and `expand` were right: with only `regressions/` (or only `checks/`) the plan has no commands to compose, `expand` keeps `workload.run` and writes the plan meta with `"composed": false`, and hydo-build stages that meta (`compose.json`) with the manifest's workload in the image. The host controller (M123) ignored the flag: `hydo-control`'s `ComposePlan::of` made a composer plan of any plan meta, and `step_range_run` then ran the composer's step (rounds with no command to launch, a guest `sleep` per round) instead of the workload. No request reached the shop, so every check passed. The shell init (until M136) always ran `$HYDO_WORKLOAD_RUN`, which `expand` made `compose.sh step` only for a composed plan, so the port lost this distinction.

**Fix** (`hydo/crates/hydo-control`): `ComposePlan.composed` (the meta's `composed`) and `Plan::composed()`. Only a composed plan replaces the workload (`step_range_run`), sets `W=` through the composer and answers "is a request in flight" from the composer's commands; a plan of only checks still has its checks evaluated through the composer (`composer::eval`). `names::check` refuses `W=` on such an image: "... this image's plan has no test composer commands (only checks or regressions; its workload is the manifest's workload.run)". With this, `hydo repro --regressions` replays a saved schedule against the real workload, which it already supported (it runs each regression's schedule on the image). Refusing the combination was the other choice; it was not taken because a saved regression of a `workload.run` project is useful and every other path already supported it.

**Test** `hydo-control/tests/silent.rs` `a_plan_without_commands_keeps_the_manifests_own_workload`: the shop's manifest copied beside a `regressions/` folder (and, second, a `checks/` folder), the plan from `hydo_manifest::for_explorer`, a run of the double-charge schedule on the scripted agent; it requires the workload's `shop place` to be spawned and no `HYDO-COMPOSE` report, and `W=` to be refused. Before the fix it failed: the run spawned only the service, timers and the world's summary.

**Nothing recorded moved.** No tracked manifest has a plan without commands next to its own `workload.run` (every tracked YAML and JSON manifest checked with `hydo-build --print-shell`: each that stages a plan has `compose.sh step` as its workload; the only folder without `workload/` is hydo-manifest's `regressions-only` fixture, which has no `workload.run` and is refused). hydo-manifest and hydo-build did not change, so no image byte changed; the controller's recorded transcripts (`hydo-control`'s corpora, features, fakes and `m123` tests) are unchanged.

### Milestone 192 — DONE (small fixes found by the onboardings and checks; 2026-11-08)

Six small fixes. Each has a test, and no recorded value moved.

**1. `hydo explore --schedule` with a schedule without `dseed=`.** `hydo explore --schedule "disk=none | run"` printed the run's result and then stopped with `cannot read the schedule "disk=none | run": no dseed=` and exit status 1. The run itself was fine: the engines read a missing `disk=` as `none` and a missing `dseed=` as 0 (`hydo-schedule`). After the run, the explorer read the schedule again with its own reader to give the run a finding class, and that reader needs both tokens. The fix (`hydo-explore/src/run.rs`, `Cx::manual_class`) reads a missing value as the engines' default for the class only, and a text that still cannot be read gets no class. The scripted-engine tests `stack_manual_no_dseed` and `stack_manual_no_disk` (`hydo-explore/tests/fake_engine.rs`, new goldens) run both forms. On the Mac, with the release's Redis example (image `a3447614…`, the recorded bytes), this tree's `hydo explore --schedule "disk=none | run" --workers 1` exits 0 with `67e5d6469f1a90a5` (the recorded value), and 0.2.0's `hydo` exits 1 with the old message after the same result.

**2. The diagnosis of a service that does not come back after a power cut.** A service that exits while it starts in the recovery boot ends the run with `HYDO-ORACLE: VIOLATION service cannot recover (committed data unrecoverable) (<service>)`. The diagnosis (M178) treated every violation as a failed check and said "No process failed" without looking, so a user read "committed data unrecoverable" as data loss. The fix (`hydo-cli/src/inspect/diagnose.rs`):

- `verdict_service` reads the service from `service cannot recover (committed data unrecoverable) (S)` and `service cannot recover after the faults (S)`. The summary names the exit and the readiness result, for example "redis exited while it started in the recovery boot after the power cut, before its readiness check passed (exit status 2)".
- For any other violation, the host layer looks in the verdict's conversation for a service whose last process ended by itself, without a signal from hydo and without a later start, or whose last readiness check did not pass. It names that service (`service-exited` or `service-not-ready`) and says that the check may have read a service that was down. When the consoles carry no agent lines (hvx sends them over the host-call port), the summary says so and names `hydo inspect diagnose <dir> --evidence`, instead of claiming that no process failed.
- `hydo run` replays a run for the evidence also for a violation that names a service, and for a recovery-boot violation whose consoles have no agent lines. The summary then ends with the service's own last log lines.
- Process ends during the workload also find the boot's command text: the services the boot started keep the boot's command numbers after snapshot S1.

Tests: `services_in_verdicts` and three fixture tests on copies of the power-cut fixture with replayed agent events: a start failure in the recovery boot with the real verdict text; an exit with status 2 after the readiness check passed; a readiness deadline; a clean recovery, which keeps the old words. On the Mac the release's Redis example, changed so that redis exits with status 2 when it starts in the recovery boot, gave with `disk=cut | run C=12`, twice: `VIOLATION service cannot recover (committed data unrecoverable) (redis)`, fp `644d9dd8e1564d6c` (also with 0.2.0's `hydo`), and "hydo: diagnosis: redis exited while it started in the recovery boot after the power cut, before its readiness check passed (exit status 2); its log ends: refusing to start on recovered data". The replay into the recovery boot was not run on hvx.

**3. A failing `.sql` check keeps its rows.** `hydo-sql none --file` (M182) prints up to five offending rows, one per line, and then a summary line. A check's finding and the verdict keep only the last line, so the rows were only in the agent's console frame. The host controller (`hydo-control/src/schedule/composer.rs`, `sql_rows_in_last_line`) now appends the first three rows to that line for checks run as `exec hydo-sql none --file ...`. Each row is cut at 160 bytes and the rows together at 400, and `| ...` marks more rows. So the rows reach `result.json`'s finding details, `report.md` and the printed verdict, for example `primary: 4 rows where none may be; first rows: primary: id=3 bal=-20 | primary: id=7 bal=-5 | primary: id=9 bal=-1 | ...`. `hydo-sql`'s bytes did not change. No recorded image has a `.sql` check (`hydo/onboard/recorded.json`), so no transcript or fingerprint moved. Test: `a_failing_sql_check_keeps_its_first_rows_in_the_verdict`.

**4. The guide on ordering by the system's own times.** `hydo guide checks` ("What not to check") and `hydo guide workloads` (SQL checks) now say: a clock fault (`T=`) steps the realtime clock, so a check that orders events by the system's own timestamps fails without a bug or misses one. Order the events as the client saw them: the client's outcome lines, or a sequence number the client writes. Neither topic is in the CLI's recorded answers.

**5. `hv/kvm/kvm-check.sh` started by a relative path.** The script changed into its output folder before it looked up its own folder, so the ledger-spin check did not find its example. It now finds its folder first. This is commit `3e5ec2b2` of another branch, cherry-picked unchanged.

**6. `hvx_hugeram_test 8192` in `hv/hvx/deploy-metal.sh`.** The main module has the split guest RAM since 2026-11-08 (Milestone 179). The script compiles the test with the others and runs it once after the several-vCPU tests, with a 900 s limit, after it waits for 9 GiB of free memory. It checks the RAM hash `b71aaf1096f96f02` (three rounds, one hash). The suite then reports 34 checks. The script was not run: a run of the whole suite on the bare-metal machine belongs to the module's owner, and another session's re-baseline was running there.

**Nothing recorded moved.** The workspace's fast test tier passed on this Mac (556 tests), and so did the full `cargo test --locked --release --workspace`. `hydo-bench rebaseline --check` on this Mac, from a new work folder with Go 1.26.5 from go.dev (sha256 `efb87ff2…`, checked against go.dev's list), built all 21 images once with their recorded bytes and ran all 75 schedules: every verdict, fingerprint and ctl value as recorded (560 s). The re-baseline was not run on hvx or KVM. The two changes that act during a run (the explorer's class of a hand-given schedule, and the `.sql` check's verdict line) touch no recorded schedule: none is a `--schedule` exploration and no recorded image has a `.sql` check.

**Vale.** `docs/STYLE.md` and `ci/vale.sh` were not on this milestone's base, so its text was first written to the standard by hand; at the integration `sh ci/vale.sh` ran on every listed document with no findings.

### Milestone 193 — DONE (YugabyteDB onboarded on hvx as an outside user would; three hydo fixes; 2026-11-08)

The first onboarding of the second round: YugabyteDB 2025.2.8.1 (the official image
`yugabytedb/yugabyte:2025.2.8.1-b8`) as three nodes with replication factor 3, each one
`yb-master` and one `yb-tserver`, YSQL on every tserver. It started from a Compose file in the
style of the documentation's manual deployment. After that it used only the onboarding skill,
`hydo guide`, `hydo compose`, `hydo sql-gen` (three primaries; the bank, list-append, register,
set and counter workloads) and a Linux release built from the tree. It ran on the bare-metal
machine with the hvx engine, in 8 GiB guests, with `storage:` per service for `G=` and `L=`. The
example is `hydo/onboard/examples/yugabyte/`; its `RESULTS.md` has every table, the friction log
and the comparison with the first round (Milestones 173, 174 and 176).

**Getting it to run** took eight runs and about two hours. The diagnosis of Milestone 178 named
the failing process and its status in four of the six failed runs, and `hydo inspect` explained
the other two without a change of the image. The causes: a hydo bug (below), hvx's empty CPUID
leaf 4 (no cache sizes, so glibc 2.28's `memcpy` faults; worked around with `GLIBC_TUNABLES`), a
readiness deadlock (hydo starts services one after the other, and a tserver's YSQL needs a second
live tserver), YugabyteDB's 3 GB free-disk floor, and a guest clock that started before the
release was built (`guest.clock_start` 2026-11-08, and `guest.clock_after_cut: 60`).

**Findings.** Every schedule ran twice with one fingerprint, on the default image (`1afe802f…`)
and on the image with `durable_wal_write=true` (`0f4d61e0…`).

1. The default `durable_wal_write=false` loses acknowledged writes at a power cut of the whole
   cluster: three of four cut points lost an increment, a set element or a register write, each
   found by a different generated check (`C=8` `086f686c474bb4f8`, `C=12` `6620196fd74d07c6`,
   `C=16` `b75a03c991330339`). With `durable_wal_write=true` the same schedules pass. YugabyteDB
   documents this default as meant for deployments without correlated power loss.
2. A backward step of the clock by 60 s (`T=10:-60`, `5287ef9b01dd36ac`) stops the tservers
   ("Too big clock skew is detected"), and they cannot start until the clock has caught up.
3. Not found: no isolation anomaly, no lost write without a power cut. TA-30772 (a transaction of
   more than 100,000 records partly undone after a restart) was not reproduced: a user-table
   version of its trigger passes on 2025.2.2.2 and on 2025.2.3.0 alike (`bigtxn/hydo/`).

An exploration of 20 process schedules with `--more-faults --storage-faults` (96 minutes) gave 17
failures, all reproduced: finding 1 in four (shrunk to one cut at the 4th flush), finding 2 in
eleven, and two false findings from the recovery boot's clock after a cut at the k-th flush
(`cf=`), whose clock the controller does not carry.

**Three hydo fixes**, each with a test, no recorded image changed:

- `hydo-build`: a PAX value that is not UTF-8 (Docker writes them for file capabilities) ended
  the reader of an image layer silently, so YugabyteDB's image lost 8,615 of the 9,188 entries of
  its base layer. The value is now decoded lossily.
- `hydo-engine`: a `debugfs` that is not on PATH is named, instead of
  `hydo: No such file or directory`. The CLI golden's one case with that message was re-recorded.
- `hydo-control`: the power loss of an image service (`L=`) unmounts every mount of the device,
  its binds too. Before, every `L=` of an image service ended in the false verdict "storage
  unmountable after its power loss".

The example's manifest joined the identity corpora (`hydo-control` `corpus-quick.txt`, and
`hydo-explore` `corpus-full.txt` and `identity-quick.txt`, re-recorded on the bare-metal machine).

**Gaps found** (open item 64): hvx's CPUID leaf 4 is empty; readiness gates deadlock a cluster
whose health check needs its peers; the diagnosis reads only a service's stdout, not the logs a
database writes into its data directory; the recovery boot's clock after a `cf=` cut starts at
`clock_start` again; the explorer never cuts links between peers of one cluster; one 4 GiB disk
is tight for six services.

### Milestone 194 — DONE (interrupts for guest code without VM exits on KVM: research, and the full-state cycle as an opt-in prototype; TigerBeetle's single replica runs on KVM; 2026-11-08)

Branch of the worktree, from `main` (`d6fce49e`). The research note is
`hydo/explore/RESEARCH-kvm-exit-free.md`; the design section is docs/design/kvm-engine.md "Loops that
store: full-state cycles".

**Why.** M189 found that TigerBeetle never finishes `format` on the KVM engine: it waits for its
disk by polling io_uring's completion queue, and the completion comes only at a VM exit, which the
loop never makes. The user asked for research into how the engine can deliver interrupts to such
code deterministically.

**What the loop is.** Sampled at the watchdog's kicks and disassembled: `while (!done) io.tick()`;
with nothing to submit, `tick` makes no system call; `flush_completions` fills a 4 KiB array with
`0xaa` (Zig's `undefined` in a ReleaseSafe build) with an AVX2 `memset`, reads the ring's head and
tail and returns. Every store rewrites the bytes already there.

**Researched** (details and sources in the note):
1. An interrupt from the host's performance counter (as hvx's PMU clock): measured with the new probe
   `hv/kvm/pmu/pmuprobe.c` on the build machine without root. The guest's user-mode conditional
   branches are counted exactly (events `0x11c4` on performance cores, `0x7ec4` on efficiency cores;
   10^9-branch runs, and under preemption); the guest kernel cannot be counted at
   `perf_event_paranoid` 2; the overflow signal stops the guest 26 branches late on a performance
   core and 8 to 18 on an efficiency core; single steps reach the exact count (1.4 and 2.5 µs per
   step); an exit costs the same with the counter on. Not built: a stop without the trap flag needs
   breakpoint stepping over a full x86-64 decoder (the trap flag leaks through PUSHF, SYSCALL and
   exception frames, and page faults inside the stepped stretch depend on host timing), AMD needs
   root for exact counts (rr's `SpecLockMap` workaround), and it is a new clock with new values.
2. The spin observer proving loops that store: built.
3. Help from the guest kernel: ruled out (the loop makes no system call; completing disk requests
   at once changes the device model; io_uring settings change the program; rings mapped as MMIO
   would need KVM to emulate VEX).

**Built** (`HYDO_KVM_SPIN_STATE=1`, off by default; hydo-config's registry and INVENTORY.md):
`Vmm::observe_state` (the whole vCPU state at a kick, a hardware breakpoint on its instruction,
KVM's dirty-page log and a page compare between two arrivals with that state), `Vmm::state_walk`
(one period by trap-flag single steps, the canonical state by the general-register hash, ties broken
by the whole vCPU state and the written pages; SYSCALL run over to a breakpoint; PUSHF, POPF, IRET,
INT, UD2, SYSRET and SYSENTER refused: `spin::saves_flags`, `spin::syscall_len`),
`Cpu::single_step` (`KVM_GUESTDBG_SINGLESTEP`), and `CpuState::without_stale_events` for the mode's
fingerprint. `HYDO_KVM_DIAG` also prints the vCPU state's parts (segment registers, XSAVE, MSRs,
events, debug registers).

**Found.** (a) TigerBeetle's `start` calls one `memset` twice from one frame, so the general registers
alone gave no single canonical state and every look gave up; the tie-break fixed it. (b) The first
TigerBeetle runs gave two fingerprints (`e7776fa561cf7371`, `bbecba0468407612`) whose only difference
was KVM's leftover of a finished page fault in `KVM_GET_VCPU_EVENTS` (error code 6 or 20, nothing
injected or pending): KVM re-injects an exception when a VM exit interrupts its delivery, and the
mode's dirty-page log, turned on at host-timed kicks, causes such exits. The mode's fingerprint
leaves those fields out; the default fingerprint still hashes them (AGENTS.md open item 45 (h)).

**Checked on the build machine** (TigerBeetle 0.17.9's single-replica image `9bb2da8a…`, built by
the 0.2.0 candidate release; this branch's static `hydo`): without the mode `ERROR boot: SPIN`; with
it `disk=none | run` OK (33 of 33 commands, both invariants) `3a4bc40c537fa2e5` six times from fresh
boots and once from the worker's S1, about 20 s per run, 205 cycles resolved per run;
