### Milestone 195 — DONE (faults aimed at several services or a role, and partitions; 2026-11-08)

**Why.** A schedule could fault one service per token, and a second `K=`, `P=` or `X=` was refused
(M141). Killing every node of a cluster needed one hand-written reaction per node, and a
partition into halves needed several `N=` tokens, of which the last replaced the others without a
word. docs/design/jepsen-gaps.md ranks node sets, roles and partition shapes as items 2 to 4.

**The syntax** (hydo-schedule's one parser; `src/target.rs`; MANIFEST.md "Groups of services and
partitions"). No new letter: the existing tokens take more targets.

- `K=`, `P=` and `X=` take a list (`K=n1,n2,n3@5+2`) or a selector over a group:
  `<group>.one[.<i>]`, `.minority[.<i>]`, `.majority[.<i>]`, `.all`, `.primary`. `one`,
  `minority` (floor(n/2) members) and `majority` (floor(n/2)+1) choose the `<i>`-th subset of
  their size, the subsets counted in the lexicographic order of the members' positions, `<i>`
  modulo their number and not written when 0.
- `N=` takes components (`n1/n2,n3`: every link between two components, both ways) or a shape
  over a group: `halves[.<i>]`, `isolate[.<i>]`, `primary`, `bridge[.<i>]` and `ring` (one way:
  each member hears itself and the next floor(n/2) members around the list). `O=` refuses them.
- The manifest key `groups:` (a format-1 addition: `name`, `services`, `primary:`, `description`;
  `hydo/schema/project-v1.json`, example case `groups-and-shapes`). `primary:` is a command that
  prints the current primary's service name.
- The schedule keeps the selector (the lead's decision): the intent stays in the schedule, and
  the control transcript records what it meant in the run.

**The controller** (`hydo-control/src/schedule/targets.rs`, `netfault.rs`). A list or a
selector is resolved before the token's step; `primary` runs the group's `primary:` command in
the guest, up to 10 times one second of guest time apart, and ends the run in ERROR when no
answer names a member (a fault aimed at nothing would be a silent pass). Each resolution is a
note in the control transcript (`K: nodes.primary = n2`, `N: nodes.ring = n3>n1 n1>n2 n2>n3`),
and the commands that follow name the services, so `hydo repro --transcript` replays them. A
kill of several services kills each in the list's order and restarts each at the restart step;
a storage fault's restart of one of them takes it out of the list. A partition is one fault
(`net_on_links`): the set of directed links, one netem queue per device, one u32 filter per
directed link (on `lo` with `addr:`, on the receiving service's veth with `network: bridge`),
lifted with the M71 drain. A plain service target takes the path it took before, with no
command and no log line more.

**Repeated tokens.** Checked first: no recorded schedule (recorded.json, the bench plans, the
goldens) repeats `N=`, `O=`, `T=` or `C=`; two identity-corpus cases of hydo-control do, and
they keep their meaning (reported to the lead; open item 65 (a)): `N=<svc>@1-<m>:delay,9ms
N=<svc>@2-<e>:delay,20ms` (`corpus_net.rs`, the later token on the same target wins) and
`T=1:3 T=2:-5` (`features.rs`, the later clock step wins). Decided per token:

- `C=`: a second one is refused ("a run has one power cut").
- `N=` and `O=`: several are one fault when they share the window, the direction and the netem
  arguments and each names a link, a partition or a shape (a link fault written link by link is
  the partition it means); a second token with another window or other arguments is refused, and
  so is a service's port fault beside another token (one netem queue per device). The same
  target twice: the later token, as before.
- `T=`: unchanged (the later token wins), because the corpus case records it.

**The names check** (M184, `names.rs`) refuses a group, a member or a primary probe the image
lacks, and a group too small for its selector or shape (a ring and a bridge need 3 members,
halves and an isolation 2), before any VM.

**The explorer.** `hydo explore --cluster-faults` (refused without `groups:`) draws from its own
stream (`CLUSTER_SALT`): a kill with a selector in 50% of the schedules, a pause in 30%, a
partition shape replacing the network fault (and the one-way fault) in 50%. Without the option a
manifest with `groups:` draws what it drew before (`hydo-explore/tests/cluster_faults.rs`: 2,000
schedules of four strategies, only K/P/N/O differ, every schedule and shrink candidate canonical
and accepted by the names check). The shrinker moves a selector towards one member
(`nodes.majority` to `nodes.one` to `n1`), a list towards fewer services and a shape towards
`isolate`.

**Tests.** hydo-schedule: round trips and refusals of every new form, the subsets and shapes.
hydo-control: every identity corpus byte-identical (corpus, corpus_net, features, m123 and the
rest); new `tests/groups.rs` on the scripted agent and engine (lists, selectors, the probe and
its failure, timed pauses and kills, partitions on `lo` and on veths, merged link tokens, every
refusal), each run twice and replayed from its transcript, the transcripts recorded in
`tests/golden/groups.txt`. Goldens re-recorded: hydo-hvx `parse_differences.txt` (two fuzz inputs
the C engine typed, a `K=` and a `P=` whose target holds `.` or `,`, now parse; their host part
arms the same values), hydo-manifest and hydo-build answers (the top level's known keys gain
`groups`, and the pinned list is the tracked files of today), the CLI's guide topics, and the
explorer's identity and corpus input pins (the new `hydo-groups.yaml`).

**Proof on the Mac** (hydo-hvm; NATS JetStream's three nodes, `hydo/onboard/examples/nats-jetstream/hydo/hydo-groups.yaml`:
the M141 project with `groups: [{name: nodes, services: [n1, n2, n3], primary: <the JetStream
meta leader from /jsz>}]`; images built from this tree with the client of M141 (`bccebbe8…`):
2.10.22 `46d0108f…`, 2.10.23 `53b8fc64…`). Every schedule twice from a fresh boot (`hydo run`),
one fingerprint each:

| schedule | 2.10.22 | 2.10.23 |
|---|---|---|
| `disk=none \| run K=nodes.all@1+2` (Jepsen's 3.1: every node at once) | VIOLATION stream lost (acked=2) `10afd1c5d6170bd2` | OK `25a3d38b0c8dc3d2` |
| `disk=none \| run K=n1,n2,n3@1+2` | VIOLATION stream lost `10afd1c5d6170bd2` | OK `25a3d38b0c8dc3d2` |
| `disk=none \| run K=nodes.primary@5+1` | VIOLATION stream lost (acked=19; the primary was n1) `e97d8040917cb5db` | OK (n3) `4b9dc76af77a1164` |
| `disk=none \| run P=nodes.majority@4+3` | OK `6548f86e06c233de` | OK `5db57fb4f1e6e6ac` |
| `disk=none \| run N=nodes.halves@3-9:loss,100%` | VIOLATION lost 9 of 38 acknowledged messages `956df32ad9956f56` | OK `05c5a0496fb0aea0` |
| `disk=none \| run N=nodes.primary@3-9:loss,100%` | VIOLATION lost 10 of 38 `8e916a9d1bbb78f7` | OK `da818e743a72a051` |
| `disk=none \| run N=nodes.ring@3-9:loss,100%` | OK `d9a6f7a30e7eb49a` | OK `f20f9d1d0b87dd8d` |

`K=nodes.all` and `K=n1,n2,n3` give one fingerprint (the guest does the same) and different ctl
values (the transcript's note). M141 needed three reactions for the first row.

**The explorer finds them** (`hydo explore --seeds 1-30 --strategy process --workers 4` on the
2.10.22 image): without `--cluster-faults` 9 failures (seeds 1 5 6 8 12 17 20 21 26; 143 s), all
with a power cut, as in M141; with it 11 (352 s), those 9 and two without a power cut: seed 18
(`K=nodes.all@19+3 N=nodes.halves.7@9-15:delay,500ms P=n3@15+5 T=2:-2592000 W=06dd08ca,p2,q1,r500`,
stream lost) and seed 22 (`K=n3@17+2 N=nodes.primary@2-10:loss,100% P=nodes.majority.3@9+3
T=11:-300 ...`, lost acknowledged messages, a new signature). Every failure reproduced. The
shrinker shrank seed 22 to `disk=none dseed=d9f3d4e02b8520f9 | run N=nodes.isolate@2-10:loss,100%
T=11:-18 W=e195e771,p4,q2,r500` (82 runs; lost 5 of 34, `e6b474bf9a8a5c14` twice; the same from
fresh boots, twice; 2.10.23 passes it, `299bd7e6e1714f99`; without the clock step it passes on
both, so the isolation of n1 and a clock step back 18 s are both needed); it shrinks one
failure per signature, so the stream-lost signature's minimal schedule is seed 1's power cut
again. Seed 18 shrunk by hand: its kill alone, `disk=none dseed=f92a9eae7103378b | run
K=nodes.all@19+3 W=06dd08ca,p2,q1,r500`, loses the stream on 2.10.22 (`40eea7912a3bab48`) and
passes on 2.10.23 (`351a0fcb8bb88bbd`), twice each; the whole seed-18 schedule from a fresh boot
gives the explorer's `2de3e4b8d5c83f79`.

**Left** (AGENTS.md open item 65):

- [user decision] The two identity-corpus cases above keep "the later token wins". Refusing a
  second `N=` on one target, or applying several clock steps in order, re-records one case
  each. Until then a hand-written second `T=`, or a second `N=` on the same target, replaces the
  first without a message.
- `G=` and `L=` take one service, and `O=` takes no partition.
- Several `N=` tokens with different windows are refused. Two faults in force on one device
  need a netem queue each (a prio band per fault).
- Repeated windows in one token (`K=n1@3+2/7+2`, docs/design/jepsen-gaps.md item 6) are not
  built.
- The primary probe runs once, before the fault's step, in the guest's own network namespace. A
  leader elected during the fault is not followed.
- No schedule with a group ran on hvx or on the KVM engine. They run the same controller;
  `hydo-bench rebaseline --check` ran on the Mac only.
- The loss of acknowledged messages on NATS 2.10.22 under a partition was not matched to an
  upstream issue. 2.10.23 passes the same schedules.

### Milestone 196 — DONE (messaging checks, steps 1 to 3 of docs/design/messaging.md: the checker, the declaration and its plumbing, the Rust recorder; 2026-11-08)

**What.** A `type: messages` history check for message-passing systems (queues, logs, publish-subscribe). The project declares what its system promises (`claims:`, `acknowledgement:`, `retention_ms:`, `clock_steps:`, `measures:`, `include:` bundles); hydo checks exactly those claims and measures the history. hydo knows no messaging system, protocol or API (the user's rule, 2026-11-08). The design is `docs/design/messaging.md`; this milestone builds its proof-plan steps 1 to 3.

**The checker** is the module `messages` of `hydo/crates/hydo-history` (`decl.rs` the declaration, `hist.rs` the records, `index.rs` the lookups, `claims.rs`, `queue.rs`, `measures.rs`). It is a module, not a crate, because the console parsing, the HYDO-CHECK declarations, the combined verdict, `hydo check-history` and the explorer's and `hydo run`'s host checks already go through hydo-history; a new crate would also have joined the 20 published crates and their order. `run_checks` turns a messages check into one property per claim, `<id>.<claim>`, so each claim is a `history-check` finding, the verdict names the first violated claim (`HYDO-ORACLE: VIOLATION [jobs.no-loss] ...`), and the explorer's failure signature is the claim. `Checks.messages` carries each check's report (the declaration with every default, the claims' statuses with judged and undecided counts, the measures). Every claim of the design is implemented with a witness: `no-phantom` (always), `no-loss`, `at-most-once`, `duplicates` (forbidden, or a window by message or deduplication id), `after-ack`, `processing`, `lease` (fixed or per delivery, extensions, nacks, overlapping receives), `order` (`fifo`, `fifo-blocking`, `log`, `causal`; scope key or channel; ordered batches), `dead-letter`, `delay`, `fan-out`, `members`, `linearizable` (FIFO or unordered). Undecided: no `drained` record for a claim that reads the end, no system ids for `duplicates`, no offsets for `order: log`, no `v=` for per-delivery leases; pairs across a power cut or a `T=` step (unless `clock_steps: strict`) are counted, never judged. Fifo, blocking and the reorder measure run in O(n log n) (a prefix maximum and a Fenwick tree); causal order is a sweep over positions that follows the transitive past.

**The queue claim.** `linearizable` uses four patterns of queue histories with unique values: a value received and never sent (or sent only after the receive returned), received twice, received against FIFO order (including a value surely in the queue that never came out while a later one did), and an empty receive while, at every point of its interval, some value was surely in the queue (one value or several in turn). Each witness is confirmed by an exhaustive search over its operations before it is reported. The test `messages::queue_patterns_match_search` generated 20,000 small histories (up to four values, overlapping operations, unknown sends) and found the patterns and the search agree on every one, for both kinds of queue.

**Tests** (`hydo-history` `tests/messages.rs`, 22 tests): every claim on hand-written violating, passing and unknown-outcome histories, the design's record example and its lease sentence (`m41 was delivered to process 7 at 12.410 s while process 3's lease from 12.002 s held until at least 42.002 s ...`), the declaration's refusals and defaults; a seeded simulation of a queue server that keeps every claim (two groups subscribed from the start, 50 ms leases, stale acknowledgements refused, first deliveries in send order per key, a dead-letter channel after three deliveries, delays on keys of their own, system ids, lost answers of sends, receives and acknowledgements, drains at the end): 300 seeds, every claim held with all eleven declared; nine mutations of those histories, each required to break exactly its claims (a phantom delivery: `no-phantom`; a group's deliveries removed: `fan-out`; another system id: `duplicates`; a refused stale acknowledgement accepted: `processing` and `after-ack`; a redelivery after an acknowledgement: `after-ack`; a redelivery inside a lease: `lease`, and `members` when the holders differ; a batch reversed: `order`; an attempt count of 0: `dead-letter`; a delay that had not ended: `delay`), each applied at least five times over the 300 seeds.

**The declaration** (`hydo/crates/hydo-manifest` `src/messages.rs`, `model.rs`, `validate.rs`): `checks[].type: messages` and its keys are additions to format 1 (the schema regenerated; the test against `hydo/schema/released/project-v1.json` passes). `include:` bundles are resolved when the manifest is loaded (paths relative to the manifest; later sources replace earlier keys, per key inside `claims:` and `measures:`; a bundle has only a declaration's keys). The combinations of the design's table are refused, naming both keys. `hydo build --check` prints each check's resolved declaration. The HYDO-CHECK line carries the declaration's keys as given (hydo-build's `check_spec` and hydo-control's `spec`); an image's compiled manifest has them with the bundles resolved, and `agent::plan_of_image` takes them from there, because the manifest an image carries keeps `include:` and not the bundles. Five permanent examples: `messages-work-queue`, `messages-keyed-log`, `messages-ordered-groups`, `messages-measure-only`, `messages-include` (with its bundle). Tests: `hydo-manifest` `tests/messages.rs`.

**Results** (`hydo/crates/hydo-results`): `Run.messages` (`MessagesCheck`: id, history, declaration, claims, typed measures, ops, warnings, error), additions to results format version 1 (the schema test against the released schema passes). The permanent example `hydo/schema/examples/results/v1/scripted-messages-run/result.json` is what the host-side path of `hydo run` makes from a scripted console (`hydo-explore` `tests/messages_results.rs` writes and checks it; no VM ran). `hydo report <run dir>` lists each messages check's claims and measures. A messages claim with nothing to judge is a run warning ("holds vacuously"). `hydo check-history <console>` checks a recorded history file with its HYDO-CHECK line, or with `--check '<json>'`.

**The Rust recorder** (`sdk/rust`, `hydo_assert::history::messages`: `Item`, `Messages`, `MsgOp`): items with the attributes in one fixed order, values encoded with `enc` plus `;` and `=`, `send` refusing an id already sent for another intent (`resend` for a retry). The module is behind the opt-in cargo feature `messages`, declared on the last lines of `history.rs`; the SDK's own tests turn it on through a dev-dependency on the crate itself (`Cargo.lock` unchanged). Without the gate, rust-kv's program `rkv` (built with build-rkv.sh's flags at one path, old and new SDK) changed bytes on both targets (aarch64 `c9dc0941…` to `a1010798…`, x86_64 `bf50b443…` to `bf6ef88b…`), which would have moved the recorded rust-kv images at their next build; with the gate both are the old bytes again, and the old build reproduced. The shared case `sdk/cases/history/messages` is written with generic records whose tokens the Rust `Item` makes, so Go, Python and JavaScript replay it unchanged (their case tests pass, as does the frozen Go copy in `hydo/stack`); `sdk/rust/tests/messages.rs` checks that `Messages` writes the same lines.

**Decisions where the design left a choice:**

- `final:` stays a shell command string, as for the other history checks (the design's sketch wrote an argv list).
- `no-loss` holds when an acknowledged message reached at least one drained group that had to receive it; `fan-out` requires every such group. Otherwise the two claims would be one.
- The group `-` exists from the start; a named group must receive what was sent after its first completed `sub` or `recv`, or everything after `sub ... from=start`.
- A nack with `r=0` (a reject) excuses a missing message as `rejected`, beside the design's three excuses.
- The dead-letter channel does not say which group moved a message, so a dead-lettered message is excused in every group, and "delivered again after the move" is judged only in a group that had delivered it `after` times before.
- Completion times get 10 ms added (the coarsest recorder's resolution) for every recorder.
- A clock step's position is that of the controller's `fault.clock_back|fwd` record.
- The error for an unknown check type keeps its recorded words ("one of linearizable, list-append"), and a linearizable or list-append check keeps its known-key list, so no golden of hydo-manifest or hydo-build moved; a messages check has its own key list.
- hydo's YAML reads `0.5` as text: a quantile may be a number's text, and the HYDO-CHECK line carries numbers.

**Recorded values.** No image, fingerprint, transcript or recorded answer moved, except the CLI goldens' listings of `hydo guide` topics, which gain the new topic `messages` (`hydo-cli` `tests/golden/cli.jsonl`, `agents.jsonl`: `guide`, `guide --list`, and the command ids after the new topic), and the hash of `hydo guide manifest`'s output, because MANIFEST.md's history-checks section gained a bullet on `type: messages`. `hydo guide messages` is new; HISTORIES.md has a section on the checker.

**Left** (open item 66): the per-window measures (the declaration's `windows:`) and `Exploration.messages` (the per-fault-class tables) are not computed; `unseen` is the count at the end, not a backlog curve per step; the witness does not name the faults active around it; the Go, Python, JavaScript and shell recorders have no messaging helpers (they write the records with their generic calls); the planted-bug example server, the NATS JetStream and Redis Streams onboardings, `hydo compare` and the history channel through the agent are the design's later steps; no VM ran a messages check.

### Milestone 197 — DONE (hydo in a team's continuous integration, stage 1: `hydo ci run`, the GitHub Action, the GitLab template)

User decision 2026-11-08: "go" on docs/design/ci.md stage 1, with the design's defaults for its open questions (a pull request does not fail on findings already on the base; history in a branch is stage 2; CI settings in a new `hydo/ci.yaml`; the action under `action/` in hydo's repository). Built in the design's order:

1. **What results record.** Every run and exploration records the host's CPU (`engine.host_cpu`: `vendor`, `model`, from `/proc/cpuinfo` or `machdep.cpu.brand_string`; `hydo_engine::host_cpu`), a results-format addition: KVM fingerprints depend on the vendor. The explorer's result cache (`$HYDO_EXPLORE_CACHE`) was keyed by the image's *path* and the engine's options, so two images at one path shared entries; it is now keyed by the image's sha256, the backend, the sha256 of this program and of the engine program, the loaded module's srcversion (hvx) or the host CPU vendor, and the engine options (entries of the old key never match; the epoch was already checked). The scripted-engine scenario `cache_key_is_the_image_bytes` (hydo-explore `fake_engine`) runs an exploration twice (the second answered from the cache), changes the image's bytes at the same path (nothing answered from the cache), and runs again (answered). The explorer goldens mask `host_cpu` like `module_srcversion`; no recorded fingerprint or golden value moved.
2. **`hydo ci run`** (`hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/ci/`, `hydo ci --help`): flags, then `hydo/ci.yaml` (format 1, `hydo_manifest::ci`, schema `hydo/schema/ci-v1.json`, its released copy the first schema, checked with `hydo-schema-compat` for readers of the current format, examples in `hydo/schema/examples/ci/v1/`), then the CI system's variables (`src/ci/env.rs`: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, Buildkite, Azure Pipelines; one function per system; flags win), then git. The image comes from the image cache (`$HYDO_HOME/ci/images/<input key>/`) when its input key (`ik1-…`, `src/ci/inputkey.rs`: hydo's version and commit, the architecture, the `--set`s, the manifest and its `hydo/` folder but `ci.yaml`, every `src:` path's content, the `inputs:` of `ci.yaml`) is there; a hit skips the `build:` command and `hydo build`. It explores the image with the mode's fixed seed range, takes the base's findings from `--base-run` or explores the base commit's image (built in a detached `git worktree` inside the output directory, removed afterwards) with the same budget, and decides every finding by replay: the finding key (`src/ci/key.rs`, `f1:<kind>:<10 hex>` of the verdict's bracketed property id, else its signature) groups routes (minimal schedules); each route this commit found that the base did not is replayed on the base's image (passes: `new`, proof `base-replay-ok`; fails with the key: `pre-existing` or `present`; fails with another key: `changed`; refused because the base lacks what it names: `new`, `base-refused`), and each base finding this commit did not find is replayed here (passes: `fixed`; same key: `present`; another: `changed`; refused or no result: `unverified`). A new finding's two replays are compared with `hydo diff`, whose first judged difference goes into the report. It replays the saved regressions and writes `ci-run.json` (`hydo_results::CiRun`, `"type": "ci-run"`, a results-format addition), `report.md` (the pull-request comment of design section 5.1) and `junit.xml` (every finding and regression a test case: failed when its state is in `fail_on`, skipped when it is already on the base), and exits 0 (passed), 1 (failed by `fail_on`, default `[new, reappeared, regression]`) or 2 (not completed: `hydo`'s and the explorer's stops exit 2 inside it). `hydo ci compare <base> <head>` compares two recorded runs by key, offline, and never calls a finding fixed.
3. **The adapters.** `action/action.yml`, a composite GitHub Action: makes `/dev/kvm` usable, restores `~/.hydo` with `actions/cache` (by version and project), installs the release verified by its `SHA256SUMS` (`hydo setup --archive`, then `--get --offline`), fetches the pull request's base commit and runs `hydo ci run --base <base sha>`, uploads the output directory, writes `report.md` into the job summary, posts or edits one comment (found by a marker line) with `gh` and the job's token (a fork's read-only token gives a warning), and fails by the exit status; actions pinned by commit (`actions/cache` v6.1.0, `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.2). actionlint 1.7.12 reports nothing for a workflow that uses it (and does read its inputs), and shellcheck nothing for its scripts. `action/gitlab/hydo.gitlab-ci.yml`, a hidden job `.hydo` to copy and extend: the same install, `HYDO_HOME` inside the project for GitLab's cache, `junit.xml` as the merge request's test report, one note through the API with a project token. `hydo guide ci` is the generic recipe for every other system, with the variable table, the runner requirements and the states. The public-content test accepts the action's public name `<owner>/hydo/action@<ref>`.
4. **Proof, on this Mac (hvm, one VM at a time, Apple M2 Pro), with throwaway git repositories in the scratch directory:**
   - The shop example (`hydo/onboard/examples/shop`, its `params:` removed, its Go service built by a `build:` script with `inputs: {shop: [src/, build.sh]}`, `pr: {seeds: 1-60, strategy: process, options: [--protocol-faults], workers: 1}`). The pull request "a request id per charge attempt" (the planted bug) against the base "charge keyed by the order": exit 1, `hydo: 1 new finding (failed)`, the finding `VIOLATION [payments.charged_at_most_once] …` (`f1:invariant:d4f25624c2`) found at seed 46 and shrunk to `disk=none dseed=fbb60485ae17b0ba | run H=payments.charge@6-9:reset,p=50` (the minimal schedule of the shop's RESULTS.md), proof `base-replay-ok`, the first judged difference the fake provider's record `idem=charge-o0` only on the base; 74 runs and 2 replays, 4 min 55 s with both images built. The reverse change against the buggy base: exit 0, `hydo: no new findings, 1 fixed (passed)`, both images from the image cache (the same input keys from another clone of the repository), 1 replay. `junit.xml` holds the finding as a failed test case of type `new` with the schedule and the reproduce command.
   - The Redis quickstart (the 0.2.0 release's example, `pr: {seeds: 1-20, strategy: swarm, workers: 1}`), the change `appendfsync always` → `everysec`: exit 1, `1 new finding, 1 changed`: the new route `disk=cut dseed=70c9101f818fe74 | run C=14` (class `durable-defaults`, a plain power cut) to the key `VIOLATION [redis.acked_writes_survive]`, which the base also has through a lying disk and an unsafe knob: the base passes that route. The lying-disk route this commit shrank differently fails on the base too and is not reported as new. An io-error run error the base also has is `present`, and the base's other io-error message on its schedule now gives the first one (`changed`, not failing). The second run took both images from the image cache: 3 min 15 s.
   - Saved regressions: `hydo save` of the pull request's exploration, changed to `# expect: ok` and committed as `hydo/regressions/double-charge.schedule`, was replayed by `hydo ci run` and reported (`1 of 1 regressions as expected`, a junit test case) on the fixed and **also on the buggy** commit. The cause is outside `hydo ci`: a `hydo/regressions/` folder makes `hydo build` read the `hydo/` folder as a test-composer plan, and for this numbered-steps manifest (`workload.run`, no `hydo/workload/`) the composer's rounds run `sleep 0.20` instead of the workload, so nothing is ordered or charged and every check holds vacuously (`payments.charge: 0 effects`); the explorer warned (`5 passing first runs may have checked nothing`). `hydo ci run` now carries that count (`summary.vacuous_passes`) and `report.md` prints a warning with it. Saved regressions therefore work only for test-composer plans today; this silent pass should be fixed in `hydo build` (refuse, or keep `workload.run`, when a `hydo/` folder has regressions but no commands). Milestone 191, merged before this milestone, fixed it: such a plan keeps the manifest's own `workload.run`.

Left for stage 2 and later (docs/design/ci.md section 9): the history branch, the ledger with `reappeared` and `accepted` (`known-findings.yaml`), budgets from history and `--time-limit`, sharding and `hydo ci merge`, `hydo bisect`, `hydo ci reproduce`. Not run: `hydo ci run` on Linux (the KVM engine on the build machine or a GitHub runner), the action and the template on GitHub and GitLab (a trial needs a throwaway public repository: the coordinator asks the user), an `error-log` finding through `hydo ci run`. The main help text does not list `hydo ci` (its recorded answer; `hydo ci --help` does). The CLI and agents goldens were re-recorded for the new guide topic only.

### Milestone 198 — DONE (cost tracking: performance as deterministic work counts, an experiment; 2026-11-08)

User decision 2026-11-08: an experiment with a written result, not a feature. The question: time
inside a guest is virtual, so hydo cannot measure latency, but counts of work are exact; are they
stable across runs, and do real changes move them? The result is `docs/design/cost-tracking.md`.

**Built** (opt-in, off by default): `HYDO_COST` (`hydo-config`, developer; `0`, `1` or `full`)
and `hydo/crates/hydo-control/src/schedule/cost.rs`. With `1` the host controller runs one busybox
probe after the verdict that reads the guest's `/proc` counters (disk I/O per partition, packets
per interface, forks, context switches, page faults, memory per process) and reports them as
`HYDO-COST` lines in the control transcript. With `full` it also probes before and after the
workload and in the recovery boot; those probes move the run's timing. With the option off, every
recorded value comes back.

**Found** on hvx, KVM and the Mac engine:

- Stable: every one of about 160 to 300 counters per run was identical in five fresh boots and
  five runs from S1, on all three engines.
- Sensitive to the right things: Redis's `appendfsync` moves flushes from 40 to 0; the same 2.0
  flushes and 16.4 KiB per acknowledged write on all three engines; a Redis restart costs 28 to
  77 % more work; the stack's recovery boot after a power cut costs 9 to 31 times the workload. An
  extra unsynced write per request shows on every engine. Extra CPU work shows only on hvx (its
  branch counter), and only above a noise floor of about 0.8 % that comes from the timing shift
  of any program change.
- Across engines, device counts that do not depend on time are equal; engine clocks and anything
  driven by timers agree in direction, not in size.

**Recommendation:** worth building as a small, opt-in part of CI stage 2: device counts and
engine clocks per schedule against the base commit, only changes above a threshold, never shown
as latency (the design note's section 6). Nothing of it is built beyond the probe.

### Milestone 199 — DONE (deterministic, branchable environments for AI agents: a spike; 2026-11-08)

The user asked (2026-11-08) whether hydo can serve as an environment for AI agents that is
exactly reproducible and can be branched, so that several actions can be tried from one state.
The answer, with every number, is `docs/design/agent-environments.md`. It was measured on the
build machine with the KVM engine.

**Built** (opt-in; no recorded value moves):

- `hydo inspect exec <session> --branch NAME [--from OTHER] -- <command>`: runs the command from
  the branch's state and keeps the state after it as the branch (the engine's snapshot
  `b:NAME`). A branch call writes the command's output to one fixed file name, so the same
  command from the same state leaves the same state on any branch.
- `state_fp` in every `exec` answer: the engine's fingerprint of the whole guest state after the
  call. Results format additions: `Inspect.branch`, `Inspect.state_fp`, `InspectBranch`.
- The KVM and Mac engines keep 64 named snapshots instead of 8, so a session holds 61 branches.
- `HYDO_KVM_NO_FP` (developer): the KVM engine computes no fingerprint, to measure its cost.
- The example `hydo/onboard/examples/agent-workspace/`: a Git repository of a small Python
  project with 20 tests and a planted bug, an agent's session as six numbered steps, and
  `branch-demo.sh`.

**Found.** From one stop of the workspace, 16 calls on 13 branches: the same action on two
branches gave the same output and the same `state_fp`; different actions differed only by their
effect; the same sequence reached the same state on two branches, in two sessions and in three
fresh boots. `random.random()`, a UUID, `os.urandom` and the time were the same on every branch,
and a wheel built on two branches had the same bytes (natively, two builds differ). A call costs
about 30 to 50 ms plus about twice the command's native time without the fingerprint; with it,
every call costs about 0.8 s more, almost all of it hashing the 739 MB disk image. A branch keeps
about 1 MB after a trivial command and about 46 MB after a test run.

**Missing for real agent use:** the network (a local mirror in the image, or record and replay
at the edge), an incremental state hash, an API made for agents with fewer stops per call, more
than one vCPU, and dropping a snapshot (open item 68).

### Milestone 200 — DONE (Ghost onboarded on the KVM engine as an outside user would; 2026-11-08)

The second onboarding of the second round: **Ghost 6.75.0** (publishing and newsletters, Node.js,
MySQL 8) from its official Docker image, with both outside providers faked over HTTPS (`tls:`):
Mailgun for newsletters and Stripe for readers' donations, Stripe's checkout webhook signed
(`sign:`) and the webhook endpoint kept as a fake object (`save:`/`load:`). The business rules are
`.sql` checks and `hydo-sql check` comparisons between MySQL and the fakes' record. Everything ran
on the build machine with the KVM engine; the images were built on the bare-metal machine. The
example is `hydo/onboard/examples/ghost/`; its `RESULTS.md` has every table, the friction log and
the comparison with Medusa's onboarding (Milestone 174).

**Did the first round's fixes remove its friction?** Mostly. HTTPS to both providers was two
`tls:` lines and worked at the first run; no image needed a writable root or a tmpfs; the first
run of the first image passed. Where a run failed for a reason its verdict did not give,
`hydo inspect` found the cause in one or two calls without a rebuild.

**Found:**

1. **A donation is recorded once per webhook delivery** (known upstream: Ghost pull request
   30118, open, not in 6.75.0). With Ghost's Docker defaults (no mail server), the staff e-mail
   fails after the row is saved, the handler answers 500, and each of Stripe's retries saves the
   donation again: six times, with no fault (`9ed2444c91345b13`, twice). The same with the mail
   provider failing (`H=mailgun.transactional@0-12:status=500`, `6774796b63f455e5`) or a
   duplicated webhook (`H=stripe.checkout_session@0-12:dup`, `e5fec8e77b90eadb`). The exploration
   found it blind at seed 20 and shrank it to one protocol fault.
2. **A newsletter batch whose acceptance answer is lost goes out again** (by design): Mailgun has
   no idempotency key and Ghost retries a failed send up to six times
   (`H=mailgun.messages@0-12:reset`, `4fdb7b1ae7053e88`, 8 extra messages for 36 batches).

Not found: no check of Ghost's crash-resumable sending failed under kills, pauses, power cuts,
clock steps and protocol faults, though few faults landed inside a send. Two false findings on the
way were the onboarding's own mistakes (a plain-http site URL that Ghost refuses at its next start
once Stripe is connected; a check that ordered events by Ghost's timestamps under a clock step).

**What hydo lacked**, ranked: the diagnosis of a service that dies in the recovery boot (fixed
since by Milestone 192); request fields and multipart bodies in the fake's record (open item 60
(c)); a KVM fingerprint difference on one schedule with identical transcripts, consoles and
verdicts (`e922311754d0d30c` three times and `c7393aac8517f6ee` twice in five fresh boots;
open item 69); a release buildable from the tree with `hydo-world-tls` and `hydo-sql` (done in
0.3.0, Milestone 190); a failing check's rows in the results (Milestone 192).

The example's manifest joined the identity corpora (`hydo-control` `corpus-quick.txt`,
`hydo-explore` `corpus-full.txt` and `identity-quick.txt`).

### Milestone 201 — DONE (flaky test verdicts of coding tasks, natively and under hydo: a measurement; 2026-11-08)

A question from the agent-environments study (Milestone 199): when a coding task's tests give
other verdicts on identical runs, an AI agent's score or a CI result moves for no reason in the
code. How often does that happen natively, and does hydo remove it? The answer and every table:
`docs/design/flaky-verdicts.md`; the scripts to run it again: `hydo/explore/flaky-verdicts/`. No
product change.

**Setup.** 31 tasks of SWE-bench Lite (pytest, pylint, sphinx, flask, django, requests, sympy,
seaborn, xarray, scikit-learn, astropy) with 928 listed tests, each task's evaluation image
prepared once with its patches applied and flattened. Natively: 10 `docker run` runs per task,
and 10 with a quarter of one CPU for 19 tasks. Under hydo, on the KVM engine of the build machine
with the environment as a `writable: true` image service: 10 fresh boots per task, 3 on a loaded
CPU for 19 tasks, and 10 calls from a held snapshot (`hydo inspect exec`).

**Result.** No test verdict changed between identical runs, natively or under hydo (310 native
runs, 190 on a quarter CPU, 310 hydo fresh boots, 57 on a loaded CPU, 310 calls from a snapshot).
The noise stayed below the verdict: in 27 of 31 tasks the native test logs differed between
identical runs, and under hydo every log of a task was the same byte for byte, with one
fingerprint per task in every fresh boot, also on a loaded host CPU. Median seconds per run:
native 0.9, hydo fresh boot 8.9, hydo from the snapshot 4.3.

**The `.pyc` finding.** hydo changed a verdict once, for a reason outside the tests:
`hydo-build` gives every file of an image one fixed time, so Python's timestamp byte-code caches
are stale under hydo and Python compiles the installed packages again at every start, with the
compile-time warnings a cached run does not get. In flask-4045 a `DeprecationWarning` from
`blinker`, turned into an error by `filterwarnings = error`, failed all 52 tests under hydo while
they passed natively. Rewriting the caches as checked-hash caches (`python -m compileall
--invalidation-mode checked-hash`) in the preparation removed every difference. This affects
every Python image service; Milestone 202 adds the opt-in `root.fix_pyc` for it.

### Milestone 202 — DONE (seven fixes from the YugabyteDB onboarding; 2026-11-08)

The YugabyteDB onboarding (`hydo/onboard/examples/yugabyte/RESULTS.md`, merged here with
Milestone 192's fixes) named seven problems. Each fix has a test. The changes that could move a
recorded value are opt-in, and the default paths send the same commands as before.

**1. Starting services together (`services[].start_after`).** hydo started the services in order
and started the next one only when the one before it passed its readiness check. A tablet server
whose check needs a second tablet server therefore never became ready, and the run ended with
`ERROR service start` after `ready_timeout`; two YugabyteDB runs went to it. The new key
`start_after: started` (a format-1 addition, default `ready`) starts a service once every service
before it was started. The controller (`hydo-control/src/schedule.rs`, `start_all`) splits a
service's start into `launch_svc` (setup and process) and `await_ready` (the readiness probe).
A run of services joined by the key is launched first; their probes then run in the start order,
before the next service without the key and before `start_all` returns, so every service is
ready before provisioning and the workload. The recovery boot starts the services the same way.
The heal's restart pass still restarts dead services one at a time. Without the key `start_all`
calls `start_svc` as before, command for command: the identity corpora (`corpus`,
`corpus_net`, `m123`, the explorer's) and every example golden are unchanged. `hydo compose`
writes the key for a service whose `depends_on` uses Compose's long form with `condition:
service_started` for every dependency (Compose's own meaning). The short form keeps the readiness
wait, so the imports of existing Compose files do not change. Tests: `hydo-control` `start_after`
(the scripted guest's readiness check `HYDO_FAKE_PEERS=` passes only while its peers run: the
default boot ends `ERROR service start (n1)`; with the key the boot sends `spawn n1, n2, n3`, then
`probe n1, n2, n3`, then the next service; `ready` written out is the default command for
command; the recovery boot starts them the same way) and `hydo-compose` `start_and_clock`.

**2. The recovery boot's clock after a cut at the k-th flush.** With `guest.clock_after_cut`, the
recovery boot continues the first boot's clock, which the controller reads on its power-cut path
(`C=`). A cut at the k-th disk flush (`cf=`) is made by the engine at the workload's end
(`EngineAction::DiskFaultsOff`), so the controller never took that path, and the recovery boot
started at `guest.clock_start` plus the seconds of the key. YugabyteDB then refused to start
("Too big clock skew"), a false finding in two of nine exploration schedules. Now, when the
schedule has `cf=` and the plan has the key, the controller reads the clock before it reads the
acknowledged ids and writes `clock=<epoch>` into the `hydo-explore-acked:` line, as on the `C=`
path; `RecoveryInputs::from_transcript` already read it from there, and the runner leaves the
token out of the ids (`runner.rs`). Without `cf=`, or without the key, the run sends the same
commands. The only recorded values that moved are in `hydo-control`'s
`tests/golden/features-quick.txt`, re-recorded on purpose: 94 of its 9,474 conversations
differ, every one a run conversation of a `cf=` schedule on a plan with `clock_after_cut`. Each
gets one `clock_get` before the acknowledged ids are read and the `clock=` token. No image in
`hydo/onboard/recorded.json` has the key, so no recorded fingerprint can move. The default (no
key: the recovery boot's clock restarts at `clock_start`) is unchanged, and `hydo guide faults`,
`hydo guide hazards` and MANIFEST.md now say plainly that clock-sensitive systems (hybrid clocks,
leases, certificates) need the key. Test: `hydo-control` `clock_cut` (a scripted engine that cuts
at the workload's end: the clock is carried and the recovery boot's clock is set to it plus 60;
without `cf=` or without the key nothing changes). Not run on hvx, the only engine that applies
`cf=`.

**3. A service's own log files (`services[].logs`).** The diagnosis read only a service's output
(`/tmp/hydo/<svc>.log`); YugabyteDB writes its real log under its data directory, so two
provisioning failures needed an `hydo inspect` session each. The new key `logs:` (a format-1
addition) lists absolute paths or shell patterns; the plan also takes `errors.files`. The
diagnosis evidence adds "the log files of <svc>" (the last 30 lines of every matching file, after
a `==> <file> <==` line), and `hydo inspect logs` prints them after the service's output. Tests:
`hydo` `inspect::calls_tests::logs_shows_the_files_a_service_names`.

**4. An explicit `clock_start` in new projects.** The format's default, 2026-01-01, is before
software released since; YugabyteDB's catalog snapshot (built 2026-11-02) was in the guest's
future. The default stays (it would move every recorded image). `hydo init` and `hydo compose`
now write `guest.clock_start` with today's date at 00:00 UTC, and a comment with the date.
`HYDO_INIT_CLOCK_START` (hydo-config, user kind) names another value; the CLI, agents and Compose
goldens set it to 1794096000 (2026-11-08) and were re-recorded on purpose. Tests:
`init_skeleton_builds` (today's date) and `hydo-compose` `start_and_clock`.

**5. Python bytecode (`root.fix_pyc`).** hydo-build gives every file one fixed time, so a
timestamp-checked `.pyc` (PEP 552 flags 0) looks stale and Python compiles the module again in
every run. The flaky-verdict experiment (`docs/design/flaky-verdicts.md` on its branch) saw flask's
tests fail on the compile warning. `hydo-build/src/pyc.rs` rewrites each such cache whose source
is in the image: the recorded time becomes the file time the guest sees (the fixed time on the
root and in an arm64 initramfs, 0 in a writable layer on the data disk, whose times hydo-build
zeroes) and the recorded size the source's size. Hash-based caches, caches without their source
and other layouts are left alone. It is opt-in (`root.fix_pyc: true`, a format-1 addition),
because it changes the bytes of every image that holds such caches. Measured on this Mac by
scanning the 21 recorded Mac images built from this tree: only `hvm/voting` holds such caches
(803, all of the voting service's Python image); the Python examples `hvm/python-kv` and
`hvm/python-kv-hist` hold none. The x86_64 voting images (`hvx/voting`, `hvx/voting-generated`,
`hvx/voting-loopback`) carry the same Python image and are expected to hold them too; they were
not scanned. Turning the key on by default would move those images' bytes and fingerprints, a
decision for the user. Test: `hydo-build` `pyc::tests`.

**6. `hydo inspect` calls do the same guest work.** Each call wrote its output to
`/tmp/hydo-inspect/<call number>.out`, so from the 10th call on the guest did one more character
of work. Every call now writes `/tmp/hydo-inspect/out` and `err` (calls run one after another and
read their files before the next call). Tests: `inspect::calls_tests::repeated_calls_do_the_same_guest_work`
and the updated `work::tests`.

**7. The Compose importer.** The generated header named the deleted Python tools
(`hvx/onboard/hydo-compose`, `HYDO_SEEDRNG=... hvx/onboard/hydo-build`; open item 38 d); it now
names `hydo compose`, `hydo guide skill`, `hydo guide services` and `hydo build`. The lock file's
`generated_by` was left as it is, because the Voting app's committed lock file is compared byte
for byte. `fetch-images.sh` fetched both architectures; it now fetches the one this machine builds
(x86_64 on Linux, arm64 on a Mac) and takes `x86_64`, `arm64` or `all` as its argument. Every
Compose golden was re-recorded on purpose. Test: `hydo-compose` `fetch_arch` (the YugabyteDB
example's import with its lock file and a recording fetcher).

**Run on the Mac engine.** A three-node manifest whose readiness check needs all three nodes
(each node's command touches a file; the check tests all three files; `ready_timeout: 5`), built
with this tree's `hydo` over the 0.3.0 Mac release, each schedule twice from a fresh boot:
without the key, `disk=none | run` ends `ERROR service start (n1)` (`507ce9f19efd4a2f` twice; the
diagnosis names n1's readiness check that did not pass in 5 s); with `start_after: started` on the
second and third nodes it is OK (`62d9937e3831ca00` twice). The first node's `logs:
[/data/n1/*.log]` appears in the diagnosis evidence as "the log files of n1" (`==>
/data/n1/node.log <==` and its lines), and `hydo inspect logs <run dir> n1 --at end` prints the
file after the service's output.

**Nothing recorded moved.** `hydo-bench rebaseline --check` on this Mac, with this tree's
programs over the 0.3.0 Mac release and Go 1.26.5 from go.dev (sha256 `efb87ff2…`, checked against
go.dev's list): all 21 images built once with their recorded bytes, all 76 schedules ran with
every verdict, fingerprint and ctl value as recorded (a first pass was stopped when the Mac's free
disk fell below 20 GB, and the second pass ran every schedule again; 673 s). On the build machine
with KVM (`--platform kvm --thorough --jobs 1`, the 0.3.0 Linux release): the two release Redis
images built twice with their recorded bytes and their 11 schedules ran twice each from fresh
boots, every value as recorded. The two stack images were not built there: their build keeps the
build machine's owners with `sudo setpriv`, and this session has no sudo there. hvx was not run.
The workspace's fast tier, clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `sh ci/vale.sh` and the
full `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` pass.

**Decisions left for the user.** Whether `root.fix_pyc` becomes the default: it would move the
recorded voting images (open item 70). Whether `hydo compose` should also map Compose's short
form of `depends_on` (whose Compose meaning is `service_started`) to `start_after: started`: it
would change the import of every Compose file with dependencies, and services that crash when a
dependency is not ready yet would then fail to start.

### Milestone 203 — DONE (the CPU's caches in CPUID: `guest.cpu_cache` on hvx and KVM, opt-in; AlmaLinux 8's glibc copies work at v3; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-08)

**Found** by the YugabyteDB onboarding on hvx (its `RESULTS.md`, friction 5): `yb-master` and `curl` of the AlmaLinux 8 image ended with SIGSEGV in `libc-2.28.so` at once. The onboarding worked around it with `GLIBC_TUNABLES` in every service.

**What CPUID answered before** (the module's `hvx_cpuid`, since M12, fixed in the kernel; userspace cannot set a table on hvx):

| leaf | hvx | KVM engine (`cpuid::table_for`) |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | zero (no descriptor, not even the round count) | EAX 1: one round, no descriptors |
| 4, every sub-leaf | zero | zero (one entry, sub-leaf 0) |
| 0x80000000 | EAX 0x80000001: leaves 0x80000002 and above are out of range | EAX 0x80000008 |
| 0x80000005, 0x80000006 | zero | zero |
| 0xB | zero with one vCPU; the x2APIC topology with `HVX_VM_SMP_BOOT` | absent (at v2 above the maximum basic leaf 7, so KVM answers with leaf 7's sub-leaf; at v3 zero) |
| 0x1F | zero (above the maximum basic leaf 0x16) | above the maximum basic leaf: KVM answers with that leaf's sub-leaf (at v3, leaf 0xD's) |

The Mac engine runs arm64 guests, which have no CPUID; it is not concerned.

**Why glibc fails.** The glibc 2.28 of Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 (and AlmaLinux 8, Rocky Linux 8, UBI 8) computes its non-temporal copy threshold from the cache sizes it reads from leaves 2 and 4. With no sizes the threshold is 0, so every copy above eight vectors takes the large-copy path of its AVX `memcpy`, which then faults (the YugabyteDB onboarding saw the faulting AVX instructions in the kernel's segfault lines). Reproduced on hvx with `hydo compose` of an `almalinux:8.10` service (digest `sha256:1965cb10…` for linux/amd64) and AlmaLinux's own Python 3.6 (`platform-python`) copying 13 sizes from 1 byte to 9 MiB: at `guest.cpu: v3` the test crashes, at v2 it passes (the SSE copy does not take that path). `getconf` in the guest prints empty cache sizes on hvx and 0 on KVM.

**The fix: one fixed cache hierarchy, opt-in.**

- Module (`hv/hvx/hvx.c`, `hvx_abi.h`): the VM flag `HVX_VM_CPU_CACHE` (bit 10). With it, leaf 2 is `0x0000ff01` (one round, descriptor 0xff: "read leaf 4"); leaf 4's sub-leaves 0 to 3 are `HVX_CPUID4_SUB` (32 KiB L1 data and instruction caches, 8-way; 256 KiB L2, 4-way; 8 MiB inclusive L3, 16-way; 64-byte lines), the sub-leaves after them zero; the maximum extended leaf is 0x80000006, whose ECX is `0x01004040` (the L2 again). With `HVX_VM_SMP_BOOT` every sub-leaf counts the vCPUs as cores of one package (EAX[31:26]) and the L3 is shared by all (EAX[25:14]); one vCPU gives the table as written. Without the flag every leaf answers as before. The new ioctl `HVX_GET_CAPS` (number 70) returns the flags the module knows (`HVX_VM_KNOWN_FLAGS`, bits 0 to 10); an older module refuses it with ENOTTY and ignores the flag.
- The hvx engine (`hydo-hvx`): `--cpu-cache on` (and `HVX_CPU_CACHE`) sets the flag after asking `HVX_GET_CAPS`. A module without it is refused before the boot: "HVX_CREATE_VM: the image asks for the CPU cache leaves (guest.cpu_cache), which this hvx.ko (/dev/hvx) does not give (it is older than Milestone 195); load a module built from this hydo (hydo module install), or remove guest.cpu_cache from the manifest and rebuild the image" (in `engine.log`; the run's verdict is `ERROR harness boot vm`).
- The KVM engine (`hydo-kvm`): `cpuid::table_with(level, cache)` adds the same values for one logical processor, taken from `hydo_hvx::abi::HVX_CPUID4_SUB` (which `hydo-hvx`'s ABI test checks against `hvx_abi.h` entry by entry), so both engines describe the same caches. `table_for(level)` is unchanged byte for byte (`table_is_fixed`; the tables with the cache leaves are recorded too). `--cpu-cache on`.
- The project format: `guest.cpu_cache: true|false` (a format-1 addition; the schema, the example case `cpu-cache`). `hydo run`, `repro` and `explore` and hydo-bench's pools read it from the image's manifest and pass `--cpu-cache on` (`BootSpec.cpu_cache`). The Mac engine ignores it.
- `hydo-build` warns when an image service has the Red Hat family's glibc 2.28 (`/usr/lib64/libc-2.28.so` and `/etc/redhat-release`) in a manifest with `guest.cpu: v3` and without the key.
- The example `hydo/onboard/examples/glibc-cache/` (`hydo.yaml` with the key, `hydo-nocache.yaml` without it, the Compose file and the image lock from `hydo compose`), MANIFEST.md "The CPU's caches", the guide (`hazards`, `services`, `capabilities`), docs/design/kvm-engine.md "The CPU's caches".
- The test `hv/hvx/hvx_cpucache_test.c` (in `deploy-metal.sh` and `side-suite.sh`): a guest runs CPUID for 19 (leaf, sub-leaf) pairs in a VM without and with the flag. Without it the cache leaves must be zero (fp `64329d56a2c9b638` on the main module and on the side module), with it the table above and every other leaf as without it (fp `1bd88c47553e9b3c`); on a module without `HVX_GET_CAPS` it checks only the first part and passes, so it can join the suite before the main module is reloaded. It compiles against an older `hvx_abi.h` too.

**Why opt-in, and not the default.** A guest that reads other CPUID answers boots differently: Linux fills `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache`, and every program that reads the leaves takes other paths, so every recorded x86_64 fingerprint would move. Making it the default needs a fingerprint epoch bump and a re-baseline; that is the user's decision (open item 65).

### Milestone 204 — DONE but for one decision (the fingerprint epoch 2: five fixes made the default in one change, every example re-recorded; three hvx verdicts changed and wait for the user; 2026-11-08)

The user decided (2026-11-08) to make several fixes the default in one change, with one raise of
the fingerprint epoch (1 to 2) and one re-recording of every example. Branch of the worktree, from
`main` at `8bcf6dc6` (Milestones 192 to 203 merged).

**What became the default.**

1. `guest.cpu_cache` (M203) for x86_64 images: the CPUID leaves 2, 4 and `0x80000006` describe the
   fixed cache hierarchy. `cpu_cache: false` keeps the old behaviour. The main `hvx.ko` has had
   the flag since the user's reload of 2026-11-08 (srcversion `91D86B693F4D4035C368F9B`, from
   `main` at `8bcf6dc6`, `deploy-metal.sh` ALL PASS with 35 checks).
2. The KVM engine's full-state cycles (`HYDO_KVM_SPIN_STATE`, M194). The variable still turns
   them off (`0`) or on (any other value); unset, the image's epoch decides.
3. The KVM fingerprint leaves out what KVM keeps of a finished event (the vector and error code of
   the last re-injected exception and the last interrupt's vector, reported with nothing injected
   or pending; `CpuState::without_stale_events`), with the full-state cycles on or off. This closes
   AGENTS.md open item 45 (h).
4. `root.fix_pyc` (M202): Python's timestamp-checked bytecode caches get the image's fixed file
   time. `fix_pyc: false` keeps the old bytes. It is decided when an image is built.
5. `hydo compose` imports Compose's short form of `depends_on` (and the long form with condition
   `service_started`, as since M202) as `start_after: started`, Compose's own meaning; `condition:
   service_healthy` stays `ready`. It prints one line per service that says how the service starts
   and why, and the written `hydo.yaml` has a comment for the short form. A service's `restart:`
   policy (M134) is in force from its start: while `start_all` starts the services (the boot and
   the recovery boot), a process that ends during its readiness check is started again as the
   policy says (Docker's decision and delays, the same as the workload's supervisor), within the
   check's `ready_timeout`. Only future imports change; existing `hydo.yaml` files keep their text.

**The schema, and why it stays additions-only.** The project format is additions-only within
format 1, and `hydo-schema-compat` refuses a changed default. The check compares the generated
schema with the last released one, `hydo/schema/released/project-v1.json` (the 0.1.0 release's,
M149). `guest.cpu_cache` (M203) and `root.fix_pyc` (M202) are not in it: they came after the
0.3.0 release commit (`76a51408`), so no published hydo knows them and their defaults are not yet
part of a released format. Their `default` in the schema is now `true`, with a description that
says the default holds for images built at the fingerprint epoch 2 and later; the schema test
(`format::schema_changed_only_by_additions_since_the_release`) passes unchanged. The meaning of an
image does not change: what an absent key means is taken from the epoch in the image's record
(`/etc/hydo/image.json`), which every image carries since M155. `hydo_image::defaults(epoch, arch)`
is the one table (`cpu_cache`: x86_64 and epoch 2 or later; `kvm_full_state`: epoch 2 or later;
`kvm_stale_events`: before epoch 2), and `hydo_engine::image::cpu_cache_of` and `image_epoch` read
the record. An image built at epoch 1 therefore keeps every default it was built with.
`root.fix_pyc` needs no such table: hydo-build applies it when it builds, at this hydo's epoch, so
an image built before keeps its bytes. The compose change is an importer change, and the restart
change acts only when a service with a policy ends during its readiness check, where the run used
to end in `ERROR service start`. No format change was needed for either.

**How an old image keeps its values.**

- `hydo run`, `repro`, `explore`, `inspect` and hydo-bench's pools resolve `guest.cpu_cache` per
  image: the manifest's value, else the image epoch's default (`runs.rs`, `hydo-explore`'s
  `run.rs`, `hydo-bench`'s `pools.rs` and `rebaseline.rs`).
- `BootSpec` has the image's `epoch`. For an image of epoch 1 the KVM engine gets
  `--image-epoch 1` (the program's option; `Start::image_epoch` in process): the full-state cycles
  stay off unless `HYDO_KVM_SPIN_STATE` turns them on, and the fingerprint keeps the leftover event
  fields unless the cycles run, as at epoch 1. `hydo repro` takes the epoch from the image, not
  from the recorded engine arguments.
- The host controller sends the same commands as before unless a service with a policy ends during
  its readiness check (the identity corpora of `hydo-control` and the explorer gave every recorded
  transcript; none of the recorded runs ends that way).
- Checked by running images built at epoch 1 with this branch's `hydo`: on KVM (the build
  machine) the 0.3.0 release's Redis image (`d255fb2b…`, built by the 0.3.0 release) gave
  `bfa03053d51bec8a`, `8ed16d6da60c34c6` and `c5b4f7cbd0ec3ac7`, each twice, the recorded epoch-1
  values; on the Mac the integration tree's `hvm/redis` (`da37b9ad…`) gave `25b1201e4067fa47` and
  `793ebdf0717899ec`, and `hvm/voting` `43733e843f702aac` and `0933dc3789d8653a`, each twice;
  on hvx the pinned reproducers' epoch-1 images in `~/hydo/build/m155` gave
  `1dc3677fb94053cf` (ctl `e873020651036931`) and `ba0aa0612502a1df` (ctl `07c598044a68e5be`), each
  twice. `hydo run` notes that the image was built at epoch 1 and `hydo repro` compares
  verdicts across epochs, as the epoch rule says.

**Release notes for the next release** (what users see):

> **New fingerprints (fingerprint epoch 2).** This release changes four defaults: the guest's CPUID
> describes a fixed cache hierarchy on x86_64 (`guest.cpu_cache`), Python's bytecode caches are
> made valid in the image (`root.fix_pyc`), and the KVM engine proves busy loops that store to
> memory and leaves host-dependent leftovers out of its fingerprints. An image you build with this
> release has new fingerprints. On the Mac and KVM every verdict of hydo's recorded examples is
> unchanged; on hvx the cache leaves change the guest's timing, and three timing-sensitive
> recorded schedules of hydo's own examples end differently. A schedule of yours whose fault is
> aimed at one exact moment may need to be found again with `hydo explore`. An image
> built by an earlier release keeps running as it did: hydo reads the epoch from the image's
> record and keeps that epoch's defaults, so its fingerprints stay the same on hvx, the Mac and
> KVM, and `hydo repro` of a run recorded by an earlier release compares verdicts. To keep the old
> behaviour in a rebuilt image, set `guest.cpu_cache: false` or `root.fix_pyc: false`; on KVM,
> `HYDO_KVM_SPIN_STATE=0` turns the busy-loop proof off.
>
> **Docker Compose imports.** `hydo compose` now reads `depends_on` as Compose does: the short
> form (a list of names) and `condition: service_started` start the service once its
> dependencies have started (`start_after: started`), and `condition: service_healthy` waits
> until they are ready. It prints how each service starts and why. A service's `restart:` policy
> now applies from its start, so a service that crashes because a dependency is not ready yet is
> started again, as under Docker. Existing `hydo.yaml` files are not changed.

### Milestone 205 — DONE (several vCPUs with the host-call port, `--vcpus` on `hydo run`, the turn sweep, and test programs as workloads; from the nats-server flaky-test example; no recorded value moved; 2026-11-08)

**Where it came from.** The example `hydo/onboard/examples/nats-flaky-8363` (nats-server's flaky `TestRegisterAndUnregister`, issue 8363) showed that on hvx with two vCPUs the verdict depends only on the vCPU turn length, and its RESULTS.md listed what hydo lacked. This milestone fixes items 1, 2, 3 and 5 of that list.

**1. Several vCPUs hung with the host-call port.** Cause: with several vCPUs (`HVX_VM_SMP_SCHED`) the module's run loop handles a committed host-call record without ending the run call (`hvx_hc_pio` sets `hc_exit` only when `!vm->sched_on`, so that the in-kernel turns stay exact), and the engine read the port's records (`HVX_HC_GET`) only when a call returned with `HVX_EXIT_HOSTCALL`, which never happens with several vCPUs. The agent's first line (its hello) therefore never reached the host, and the run waited until its wall limit at 100 % of a CPU (12 minutes once; another try gave nothing in 290 s). With `HYDO_HVX_HOSTCALL=0` the lines went over the serial line, which the engine reads at every return. The fix is in the engine only (`hydo/crates/hydo-hvx/src/engine.rs`; no module change): with several vCPUs and the port, (a) `run_until_any` reads the port at every return of a run call that ended at a turn or budget boundary (a point that is a pure function of the guest's execution), and a return that brought records is a stop with `why=hostcall`, as a record is with one vCPU; (b) `run_call` ends such a call every `HC_SMP_CAP` = 8,192 retired exits, so that at most 32 KiB of records (one 4-byte OUT per exit) wait in the port's 64 KiB buffer; such a return is a stop only when it brought records, a send is due, or it is the 8th quiet one in a row (`HC_SMP_QUIET`), which is the module's own cadence without the cap (`HVX_MAX_INKERNEL_EXITS` = 2^16). One vCPU, a VM without the port and the serial line are unchanged (the unit test `several_vcpus_with_the_port_end_their_calls_often_enough` pins the rule). No run with several vCPUs and the port had given a result before, so no recorded value can move.

Proof on the bare-metal machine (hydo built from this branch in `~/hydo-m205`, the loaded main module `869F246124D8A3F84879E74`, one VM at a time beside another session's long rebaseline), each schedule twice from a fresh boot, the port on by default, the images of the example's RESULTS.md (buggy `d1ce39a4…`, fixed `db212e31…`, rebuilt to the same bytes from the pinned test programs):

| image | schedule | vCPUs | verdict | fp (both runs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
