### Milestone 207 (tentative) — DONE (the worker pool and a fresh boot differed on four hvx schedules: hydo-bench's pools booted without the CPUID cache leaves; fixed, and the fast check compares the two; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-08)

**Where it came from.** AGENTS.md open item 76 (Milestone 206). At the fingerprint epoch 2, four hvx schedules gave another fingerprint and ctl value in the fast `hydo-bench rebaseline --check` (a worker pool that starts every run from the provisioned snapshot S1) than from a fresh boot with `hydo run`, with the same verdict: `hvx/redis-composed`, `hvx/redis-composed-hist` and `hvx/redis-composed-read` with `disk=cut dseed=1 | run C=12 R=everysec W=...`, and `hvx/redis-errors` with `disk=ioerr:1 dseed=281cc34161f446f4 | run K=redis@1+1 W=...`. hydo promises one fingerprint for a schedule from S1 and from a fresh boot, so this was a determinism gap until it was explained.

**Reproduced.** On the bare-metal machine, with this branch's tree before the fix in `~/hydo-m207`, a new work folder, the 0.3.0 Linux release's guest files and the loaded main module `91D86B693F4D4035C368F9B`: `hydo-bench rebaseline --check --only hvx/redis-composed,hvx/redis-errors` gave M206's result. The pool gave `c0daeb01f242ebb7` (ctl `a7e6fb8d48e24b8e`) for redis-composed's cut schedule and `7fc3174b9b541522` (ctl `83de6290c54abb1b`) for redis-errors' schedule. The second runs from a fresh boot gave the recorded `4211f14f9326cb96` and `3c4321d67e4fe7b9`.

**The cause: hydo-bench booted another guest, not the engine.** The recorded fresh-boot runs have `--cpu-cache on` in their `engine.args` (`result.json`). hydo-bench's pools took the guest's settings (`guest.ram_mib`, `guest.cpu`, `guest.cpu_cache`) from the image's manifest with `hydo_manifest::from_embedded(text, None)`, without the test composer's plan meta (`/etc/hydo/compose.json`). `hydo run` (`hydo-cli` `runs::image_guest`), the explorer (`Space::from_text`) and the host controller (`plan_of_image`) read the manifest with the meta. For a composed plan, a manifest with a `test:` section whose commands are in the `hydo/` folder, the reading without the meta fails. All four images are composed plans. On that failure the two `guest_of` functions of hydo-bench (`pools.rs` and `rebaseline.rs`) returned the values for an image without a manifest: 1024 MiB, v2, and the cache leaves off. At epoch 2 an absent `guest.cpu_cache` means on (Milestone 204), so the pool's guests booted without the CPUID cache leaves and the fresh boots booted with them. That is why:

- the pool's value at epoch 2 equals a fresh boot of an epoch-1 image (M206: `c0daeb01f242ebb7`), because an epoch-1 image boots without the leaves too, and its other differences (the image record says epoch 1) are not in what the guest reads;
- the gap appeared at epoch 2 and not before: until then both paths booted without the leaves, and RAM and CPU level were the defaults for these four images;
- only these four schedules showed it: the fast mode runs each image's first schedule from a fresh boot and only the others in the pool, and the four are the second schedules of the only composed hvx images in `recorded.json`. M206's note that the same schedules "without the knob or the disk errors agree" compared fresh boots (the images' first schedules), not pool runs. With the old reading, the pool also gives another value for the first schedules (below).

The engine, the module, the snapshots and the controller were not involved: the explorer's own pool, which reads the manifest with the meta, gives the fresh-boot values (below). The Mac and KVM cannot show the gap. The cache leaves are an x86_64 setting, so an arm64 guest has none on either path, and the Mac's composed plans have the default RAM. hydo-bench has no KVM pool (its KVM entries run with `--thorough`), and the explorer's KVM pool reads the meta.

**The fix.** One reading of the guest's settings for every boot path: `hydo_control::agent::image_guest(image)` reads `/etc/hydo/hydo.yaml` with `/etc/hydo/compose.json` and `/etc/hydo/params`, as the host controller does, and `guest_of_embedded(text, compose, params)` does the same from the files' text. An image without a manifest gives the defaults; a manifest that cannot be read is an error, not the defaults. `hydo run`'s `image_guest` (it keeps its fallback to the defaults), hydo-bench's two `guest_of` (an error ends `hydo-bench`, or fails the image's pool in `rebaseline`) and, through `cpu_cache_of`, an image without a manifest (the epoch's default instead of off) use it. The explorer reads the whole fault space from the same manifest and meta, and keeps its reading.

**The new check.** In the fast mode, the image's first schedule, which runs from a fresh boot, also runs in the worker pool (tag `x<run>`), and the two results must have one fingerprint, one ctl value and one verdict. Otherwise the report has the section "Schedules whose worker-pool run differs from their fresh boot" and the check exits 1. The summary line "The worker pool against a fresh boot" counts the schedules run both ways. The check runs whenever the image's first schedule runs (a cache miss), and costs one run from S1 per image (and one pool boot for an image whose other schedules are all cached or which has one schedule). It compares the two paths in general, not only the guest's settings: any state that S1 does not carry would show up the same way. The test `hydo-control` `image_guest::` pins the reading: the four composed examples' manifests do not read without their meta, `guest_of_embedded` refuses that reading and gives the explorer's `guest:` with the meta, and a `guest:` key of a composed plan is seen.

**Proofs.**

- The negative control (the bare-metal machine, the fixed tree with only `rebaseline.rs`'s reading put back to the old one): the check named 4 of 4 schedules run both ways, the first schedule of each of the four images, for example redis-composed's `disk=none dseed=1 | run W=0000002a,p4,q2,r100` fresh boot `a8b8fe1a2b91b0aa` against worker pool `96023abe8675ca7b`, and exited 1. The four schedules of item 76 differed between their two runs as in M206.
- The fix, the same four images: every schedule as recorded from the pool, the four first schedules run both ways with one result each, exit 0.
- The explorer's own pool on hvx (`hydo explore --workers 1 --schedule`, each twice): redis-composed `4211f14f9326cb96` (ctl `bffacce822ee19a7`), redis-composed-hist `ebeb6a48b3c02cf1` (ctl `9ca8c7ee42eaca4c`), redis-composed-read `03f52a430ec924f6` (ctl `bc64ac72b494cd4b`), redis-errors `3c4321d67e4fe7b9` (ctl `6edc5a17e6209a7d`): the recorded fresh-boot values, before and after the fix.
- KVM (the build machine, one VM at a time): the epoch-2 redis-composed image from the bare-metal machine with its cut schedule gave `7426c56b8223c21e` (ctl `e30c50d77d26c8fb`, VIOLATION `k:21`) twice with `hydo run --backend kvm` and twice with `hydo explore --backend kvm --schedule`.
- hvx (the bare-metal machine, the fast mode with this tree over the 0.3.0 Linux release, a new work folder, the loaded main module `91D86B693F4D4035C368F9B`, two VMs at a time): all 41 images built once with their recorded bytes (the shop's two included), 137 schedules, every verdict, fingerprint and ctl value as recorded, the 40 first schedules that run on one vCPU run both ways with one result each (the 41st image, `hvx/nats-flaky-fixed`, has only a run on 2 vCPUs, which runs from a fresh boot), exit 0 (builds 1,365 s, runs 1,581 s). The fast check on hvx passes again, which it did not since M204.
- The Mac (hvm, this Mac, the fast mode with this tree over the 0.3.0 Mac release, a new work folder): 21 images built with their recorded bytes, 76 schedules, every verdict, fingerprint and ctl value as recorded, the 21 first schedules run both ways with one result each, exit 0 (577 s).
- KVM (the build machine, `--thorough`): the two release images built twice with their recorded bytes and the two epoch-2 stack images of the bare-metal machine (`--no-build`), 13 schedules twice each, every value as recorded, exit 0.

**Nothing recorded moved.** The recorded values are the fresh boots' (M204 recorded with `--thorough`), and the pool now gives them. The fingerprint epoch stays 2: no engine, controller, agent or kernel changed.

**Left.** The cross-check runs one schedule per image and only when that schedule is not in the cache. A difference that shows only on another schedule, or only after an engine change that the cache key does not see (the run identity has the engine programs, the module and the epoch, but not hydo-bench's own controller), is found by the next run that misses the cache, or by `--thorough`, which runs only fresh boots and so cannot see it.

### Milestone 208 (tentative) — DONE (refused schedules are no findings, and the explorer draws none on hvx; a record of where each forced preemption point fired on KVM and the Mac; 2026-11-09)

**Where it came from.** The Qdrant flaky-test example (`hydo/onboard/examples/qdrant-flaky-10200`,
RESULTS.md, "What hydo lacked") found two gaps. First, `hydo explore --timing --preempt` on hvx
gave 15 failures of the class `test-failed` in 100 schedules, all "reproduced", and every one of
them was `ERROR harness tick jitter (needs the PMU clock)` although the PMU clock was on. Second,
the verdict flips between `pctn=39` and `pctn=40` on KVM, and nothing said where the forced
preemption points fired.

**The cause of the false failures.** `--timing` draws seeded tick jitter with `tjmax=500000`
(the explorer's `TJ_MAX`) for half of the schedules, and on hvx `--preempt` draws `pp=65536` or
`pp=16384` (a shorter PMU tick period) for a quarter of them. The engine arms `pp=` first
(`HVX_SET_PMU`), then the jitter (`HVX_SET_TJITTER`). The module refuses a seeded jitter whose
largest delay is a tick period or more (`hvx.c`: `!t.n_explicit && t.max_delay >= vm->pmu_period`
gives `EINVAL`), and the engine reported that as the message it has for a VM without the PMU
clock. The explorer counts every verdict that is not OK as a failure, re-ran it (the same
ERROR, so "reproduced") and put it in the class of the image's workload (`test-failed` for a
test program). About one schedule in eight drew the pair; on Qdrant it was 15 of 100.

**The fix.**

- The rule is written down once: `hydo_hvx::sched::Sched::refusal` (with `PMU_PERIOD`,
  `PMU_PERIOD_MIN`, `HVX_XT_MAX_RATE`) says what the module refuses when a schedule is armed: a
  `pp=` period of 512 branches or less, a seeded `tjmax` or an explicit `tjx` delay of a tick
  period or more (the period of `pp=`, else 2^20), more than 64 extra ticks per period. The Mac
  and KVM engines' rule, the hvx-only host tokens, moved to
  `hydo_hvm::machine::host_token_problem` (both engines call it). `hydo_engine::refusal(kind,
  schedule)` gives the rule of each engine, and `hydo_engine::is_refused(verdict)` recognises a
  refused run's verdict (`ERROR refused: ...`, `UNSUPPORTED on <engine>: ...`).
- Refused before any VM: `hydo run` (and `repro`, `explain`, `ci`, through `run_engine_try`) stops
  with "the engine refuses the schedule: ..." before the engine boots. The explorer's worker
  answers `ERROR refused: ...` without running. The hvx engine refuses such a request itself
  before it restores S1 (`ERROR refused: ...`), and the program's one-shot mode before the boot.
- Never a finding: the explorer gives a refused first run the class `refused`, does not re-run
  or shrink it, and counts it in the results addition `Summary.refused` (with a warning line and
  a `refused` row in the printed summary and `report.md`).
- Never drawn: on hvx, when `--preempt` draws `pp=` and `--timing` drew a seeded jitter with
  `tjmax` of `pp=` or more, `tjmax` becomes `pp/2` (`TJ_MAX` is about half of the default
  period). The draws themselves are unchanged, so every other schedule is as before.

**What moved, and why.** Only schedules with both a seeded `tj=` and `pp=` changed: their
`tjmax=` (and the `tjx=` lists the shrinker derives from it). The explorer's identity golden
`tests/golden/identity-quick.txt` was re-recorded: 119 of 15,249 lines changed. A comparison of
the stream before and after the fix found only such lines, and 267 refused schedules in the old
stream against none in the new one. The full stream (`HYDO_IDENT_FULL=1`) changes in 2,572 lines
with the same property; its golden was already out of date on `main` (new examples are inputs
of it) and was not re-recorded. The scripted-engine scenario `stack_swarm_pos_preempt` was
re-recorded: the same 19 failures, all reproduced; its `mean_run_s` went from 5.6 to 5.3,
because the scripted engine's seconds are a function of the schedule text. The explorer's schedule
corpus (`corpus-full.txt`, 519,343 strings, full tier) changed in 121 of its 127 chunks. hydo-control's
identity corpora (`corpus-quick.txt`, `features-quick.txt`, full tier) take their schedules from
the same generator and were re-recorded: 52 of their 62 per-manifest count lines changed with the
scripted runs of those schedules. With the old draw (the halving switched off by hand for the
test), the three corpora and the explorer's identity stream pass against their old goldens, so
nothing else moved. No recorded fingerprint moved (below).

**The preemption record.** With `HYDO_PREEMPT_RECORD=1` (a registry entry; the KVM and Mac
engines' options), a run with `pct=` writes `<tag>.preempt.jsonl` into the engine's output
directory: `one.preempt.jsonl` in a `hydo run` directory. Each line is one point
(`hydo_hvm::machine::PctRec`): `i`, `exit`, `result` (`moved`, `due`, `missed`, `passed`),
`vtime_ns`, `to_ns`, and the guest's `pc`, `mode`, `page_table` (CR3, TTBR0_EL1),
`thread_pointer` (the FS base, TPIDR_EL0) and `sp` (RSP; SP_EL0, which Linux keeps as the
current task at EL1). The point logic moved into `Pct::at_exit`, shared by both engines, with the
same results and counts as before. The engines read the registers only at a point, and only
when the record is on (`KVM_GET_REGS` and `KVM_GET_SREGS`, `hv_vcpu_get_reg` and
`hv_vcpu_get_sys_reg`); the KVM rewind mode drops the records after its checkpoint before it
replays. Readers: `hydo inspect events` lists each point as an event of the kind `preempt` at
the stop that follows it (`at` is its exit count), and `Timeline.preempt` (`PreemptSummary`)
counts what the points did. `hydo diff` compares the two runs' records point by point in exit
order and writes the first difference to `Diff.first_preempt` (level `preempt`, the stop after
the point in each run, the record only one run has or both differing records, how many points
both share, and the other run's next point), with a section in `diff.txt`. All three are
results-format additions. The scripted KVM vCPU of the tests keeps a `Print`'s place across an
interrupt (`r13`), because a forced point can make the timer due between two of its bytes.

**Tests.** `hydo-hvx` `refusals_follow_the_module`; `hydo-explore` `refusals::` (every schedule
the explorer generates with `--timing --preempt --new-faults`, and `--more-faults` on hvx, for
the built-in space, Redis and the stack, 400 seeds of three strategies on each engine: 10,800
schedules, every one accepted by its engine, with more than 100 that draw `tj=` with `pp=` and
more than 100 `tj=` with `pct=`; the halved `tjmax`; the refusal of the Qdrant pair);
`hydo-hvm` `the_record_does_not_change_what_a_point_does`; `hydo-kvm`
`preemption_records_name_every_point_and_move_nothing` (with and without the record, and with
the rewind mode: the same fingerprints, verdict and extras, one record per point reached,
`pctf=` equal to the moved and due records); `hydo` `preempt::` and
`the_first_preemption_point_where_the_records_differ`.

### Milestone 209 — DONE (an experimental steered search: exploration by a number the system reports, how close a run came to failing; on Qdrant's flaky test it did not help, on KVM or on hvx; 2026-11-09)

**In short.** The steered search is experimental. On the one system it was measured on, Qdrant's
flaky test, it did not help. On KVM the plain exploration found the first failure after a median
of 72 schedules, and the steered search after a median of 118. On hvx neither found it. It is
opt-in, and without its options nothing changes. It was built on a branch cut from `16d20437`,
before the 0.3.1 release, and merged after it.

**Where it came from.** The Qdrant flaky-test example (`hydo/onboard/examples/qdrant-flaky-10200`,
RESULTS.md gap 5) prints the update queue's length when its test checks it. The test fails at
length 0. The random KVM exploration read lengths from 2 to 36, mostly 18, and failed in 4 of 400
schedules. The user decided (2026-11-09) to build an exploration steered by such a number.
Design: `docs/design/steered-search.md`.

**Built.**

- `hydo explore --steer <id>` or `--steer-match REGEX` (hydo-explore `src/steer.rs`, `run.rs`
  `steer_search`). A run's value is the best number of the run: the SDK's `HYDO-STEER` records
  of the id, or the first capture group of a pattern over the consoles and the verdict line.
  `--steer-goal min|max`. The search runs rounds of `--steer-batch` schedules (default 4). Once
  its corpus has an entry, a schedule is a mutant with probability `--steer-mix`/1000 (default
  500), otherwise the strategy's schedule of the next seed. The corpus keeps the
  `--steer-corpus` best runs (default 16); a parent has the weight 1 / ((rank + 1)(picks + 1)).
  A mutant is one change: a step or count moved (40 %), a seed drawn again (20 %), a part removed
  (15 %), a part taken from another seed's schedule (25 %). `--steer-stop` ends the search after
  the round of the first failure. The first runs then go through the usual re-runs, shrinks and
  report. A mutant must read back and be one its engine accepts (`hydo_engine::refusal`). The
  search is a pure function of its options and the runs' results; with `--steer-mix 0` it runs
  the plain exploration's schedules in its order.
- Results format additions: `Run.steer` (`value`, `origin`, `drawn_seed`, `parent`, `change`,
  `best`) and `Exploration.steer` (`SteerSearch`: source, pattern, goal, options, stream seed,
  counts, best value and run, first failure, `stopped`, `progress`, `corpus`). report.md has a
  section "Steered search"; the summary line has `steer`, `steer_mutants`, `steer_best`,
  `steer_first_failure`. None of them appear without `--steer`.
- The manifest key `steer:` (format-1 addition, `hydo_manifest::model::SteerValue`): `id`,
  `match`, `goal`, `description`. hydo-build checks the id, the regular expression and the goal.
  New example document `steer-value`; MANIFEST.md "Values that steer the explorer".
- The Rust SDK: `hydo_assert::minimize`, `maximize`, `Steer::value`, behind the cargo feature
  `steer` (off by default). It writes `HYDO-STEER {"id":..,"goal":..,"v":..,"msg":..}` for the
  first value and each better one, at most 64 per id in a process. Shared cases
  `sdk/cases/steer/` (3 cases, 4 runs, need `steer`); the Go, Python and JavaScript readers skip
  them. hydo/ASSERTIONS.md "Steered values".

**The feature, and why.** Without the feature gate the new module moved rkv's bytes (the rust-kv
example's program, inside recorded images), although rkv calls none of it: at the rebaseline's
fixed path, aarch64, main's SDK gives `e36746cd3a9b55ce`, with the module `4c69fd83ffe5142f`.
README text alone changes nothing. With the module behind `#[cfg(feature = "steer")]` rkv is
`e36746cd3a9b55ce` again.

**Measurements on the Qdrant example.** The image is the recorded buggy image (`9aa2213a…`),
built with this tree's `hydo` over the 0.3.0 Linux release with its recorded bytes. The value is

of 4, a budget of 400; 2.3 to 2.4 s a run):

| seeds | plain: runs to the first failure | steered: runs to the first failure | the steered search's failing schedule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–400 | 37 (seed 37) | 78 | the random schedule of seed 37 |
| 1001–1400 | 145 (seed 1145) | 118 | a mutant of run 102 (`tj=` drawn again) |
| 2001–2400 | 22 (seed 2022) | 47 | the random schedule of seed 2022 |
| 3001–3400 | 152 (seed 3152) | 221 | a mutant of run 158 (`tjmax=1000 -> tjmax=900`) |
| 4001–4400 | 72 (seed 4072) | 133 | the random schedule of seed 4072 |

The median is 72 for the plain exploration (22 to 152) and 118 for the steered search (47 to
221). The steered search was earlier in 1 of 5 ranges. In 3 ranges its failure was the plain

|---|---|---|---|---|

| steered, random schedules | 320 | 18 | 3.1 % | 3 (0.9 %) |
| steered, mutants | 288 | 17 | 7.6 % | 2 (0.7 %) |

The mutants read small lengths twice as often and did not fail more often. The steered search of

### Milestone 210 — DONE (`hydo <command> --help` without an image; `cargo install hydo` and `hydo setup` run on Linux, so the README offers cargo there too; 2026-11-13)

**In short.** Every `hydo <command> --help` and `-h` now prints the command's options and ends
with status 0. It needs no image, no project, and no recorded run. `cargo install hydo --locked`
followed by `hydo setup` ran on Linux for the first time, on a GitHub runner with KVM. The Redis
example built to its recorded image and gave the verdicts of the Linux quickstart. The README
and `docs/INSTALL.md` now offer cargo on Linux, and open item 50 is closed. Nothing recorded
moved.

**The help.** The 0.3.1 release notes listed `hydo explore --help` as a known defect: it looked
for an image and stopped without one. A check of every command's `--help` and `-h` in an empty
directory found more:

- `hydo doctor --help` checked the machine.
- `hydo report --help` read `--help` as a directory.
- `hydo repro --help` printed `hydo run`'s usage.
- `hydo build --help`, in a folder with `hydo/hydo.yaml`, started a build.
- `hydo save`, `hydo compose` and `hydo module` printed their usage as an error, with status 1.
- After a sub-command, `hydo errors list --help`, `hydo inspect logs --help`, `hydo ci compare
  --help`, `hydo skill install --help` and `hydo check-history DIR --help` read `--help` as an
  argument.

The new file `hydo/crates/hydo-cli/src/help.rs` answers these commands before they do anything
else. `hydo explore --help` prints its own usage, hydo's defaults (the image, `--out
hydo-out/explore`, the seeds 1-20), and the explorer's full option list. A command with
sub-commands prints its own help after a sub-command too. The words after `--` belong to the
program that `hydo inspect exec` starts, so `hydo inspect exec DIR -- ls --help` still runs
`ls --help`. The explorer's usage text says `--seeds A-B` instead of its internal default
`1-200`, and no longer names `explore.py`. The commands that had a working help keep it.

The new test is `equivalence::every_command_prints_its_help_without_an_image`. It covers 30
commands, and two more on Linux. It runs each with `--help` and with `-h` in an empty directory
both as the Linux and as the Mac command. It requires status 0, an empty stderr, the command's name in
the output, and nothing written. Two unit tests are in `help.rs`. The golden file
`tests/golden/cli.jsonl` changed in two answers only: `compose --help` on both platforms now ends
0 and prints on stdout.

**`cargo install hydo` on Linux.** Before, it was checked only with `cargo check` (Milestone
169), so the README offered cargo only on the Mac. A one-off workflow on a temporary branch
`tmp-cargo-linux`, deleted afterwards, ran the published 0.3.1 from crates.io on GitHub's
ubuntu-24.04 runner: https://github.com/kakoc/hydo/actions/runs/43375819063. The runner had an
AMD EPYC 7763 with 4 vCPUs and Linux 7.0.0-1017-azure, with nested virtualization. A udev rule
gave its user `/dev/kvm`, as in Milestone 190's AMD check. The steps and their results:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo install hydo --locked --version 0.3.1` (rustc 1.100.0, stable) | built in 2 min 10 s; `hydo --version` printed `hydo 0.3.1 (b3f730878702…)` |
| `hydo setup` | fetched `hydo-linux-0.3.1.tar.gz` (67.8 MB) from the GitHub release, checked and unpacked it into `~/.hydo/versions/0.3.1` in 4.6 s |
| `hydo doctor --backend kvm` | `doctor: all checks passed` |
| `hydo build hydo.yaml` in a copy of `~/.hydo/versions/0.3.1/examples/redis` | `explore-ob-redis-disk.img` with sha256 `668bf8ad…`, the image recorded on Intel (`recorded.json`, `kvm/release-redis`) |
| `hydo run --backend kvm "disk=none \| run"` | `OK invariants=1 held (redis.acked_writes_survive: acked=20 all present)`, `fp=2846084b7f0ab1e2`, `ctl=ff77abf64599af16` |
| `hydo run --backend kvm "disk=cut \| run C=12 R=everysec"` | `VIOLATION [redis.acked_writes_survive] key k:1 lost`, `fp=bca22e72dbf0da18`, `ctl=f4b7017fdcd089fd` |
| `hydo repro` of the second run | `REPRODUCED`, `hydo: 1 of 1 reproduced with the recorded fingerprint` |

The verdicts and the control fingerprints (`ctl=`) are the Intel recordings'. The fingerprints
differ from Intel's (`b04d1932dfb20e09`, `1b61c2c7501a6f25`), as KVM fingerprints do between
CPU vendors. These are the first epoch-2 values on AMD; the Linux quickstart, section 6, says so
now. The install cache's Linux side fetched from the real GitHub release for the first time
(open item 47 said it had run only against a local server).

**Documents.** README.md "Install" offers cargo for both platforms first, then Homebrew on the
Mac, and the tarball for Linux without cargo. It says that on Linux the user must be able to
open `/dev/kvm`. docs/INSTALL.md "With cargo" covers both platforms. It gives the run's numbers and
says that the kernel module `hvx.ko` was not tried with a cargo install.

**Left.** The kernel module after a cargo install was not tried. The rest of the epoch-2 KVM
values (open item 45) have not run on AMD.

### Milestone 211 — DONE (an etcd flaky test, issue 22796, made to fail on every run of one hvx schedule under a CPU limit in the guest; hydo's timing tokens alone never reach it; a fjall race tried and not reproduced; 2026-11-13)

**In short.** The next flaky test after Qdrant's is etcd's `TestCacheCompactionResync`
(issue 22796, opened 2026-11-11, no fix). It fails when the whole test process gets no CPU for
about 40 ms at one moment. Without a CPU limit it never failed: 0 of 8,000 native runs, and 0 of
about 1,000 hydo schedules on hvx and on the Mac. With a CPU limit in the guest that two busy
loops use up, `disk=none pp=65536 | run` fails on every run on hvx (`a69b353e5e4c2528`, three
runs) and `disk=none | run` passes (`c5ff83b44504bb74`). A test-only change passes the failing
schedule. The same CPU limit fails the test natively too, in 190 of 200 runs, so hydo adds little
here. The example is `hydo/onboard/examples/etcd-flaky-22796` (RESULTS.md). Nothing recorded
moved; no hydo code changed.

**How the candidate was picked.** The shortlist, from open GitHub issues of 2026:

- etcd-io/etcd#22796, `TestCacheCompactionResync`: Go, a small module, two days old, a
  quarantine pull request closed unmerged. Risk: a race against a 50 ms timer.
- fjall-rs/fjall#345: the last blocking `send(WorkerMessage::Flush)` into the bounded worker queue
  can deadlock both workers. Its reporter found it by reading the code and did not reproduce it.
  Risk: no test exists; a stress program must be written.
- tursodatabase/turso#11399, `test_sync_pull_waits_for_open_write_transaction`: Rust, `Busy`
  errors under nextest. Risk: the test starts a local Turso server.
- quickwit-oss/quickwit#6565, `test_drain_is_called`: Rust, already explained by a commenter,
  who made it fail in 41% to 47% of runs under CPU contention. Risk: little left to show.
- hashicorp/raft#711, `TestRaft_HasExistingState`: Go, fails in about 1 of 15 runs of the whole
  package with `-count=3`. Risk: the whole package runs for minutes, and the cause is unknown.

databendlabs/databend#20728 and temporalio/temporal#12694 were left out: both test programs are
large, and temporal's needs `-race` and a host saturated by other processes.

**The cause.** After the test sends a compaction error, the cache's `getWatchLoop` waits 50 ms and
restores the store from the stub's second snapshot (revision 20). The test polls `Ready()` every
10 ms and then calls `Get`, which must return revision 5. A `time.Sleep(60ms)` before the test's
`Get` made it fail on 3 of 3 runs with the report's line. The CI job runs four test programs and
the compiler in a pod with a limit of 4 CPUs, so the pod can stop for part of a 100 ms period.
`getWatchLoop` reads `defaultConfig()`, so the option `WithInitialBackoff` has no effect there.

**Under hydo.** Every value is in the example's RESULTS.md. On images without a CPU limit:

- hvx, 1 vCPU, `--timing --preempt`: 0 of 200 failed.
- hvx, 2 vCPUs: the turn sweep (12 lengths) and 100 schedules with `--turns --timing` passed.
- Mac, `--timing --preempt`: 0 of 300 failed, and dense `pct=` points did not change that.

The manifest's parameters `limit` and `busy` put the workload in a cgroup v2 with that `cpu.max`
and run busy loops beside the test. With `limit="10000 100000" busy=2`, 38 of 100 hvx schedules
of `--timing --preempt` failed, all reproduced. Every failure had `pp=` (26 of 32) or `xt=` (12
of 17), and none of the 51 schedules without them failed. The tick period has a boundary between
`pp=129024` (fails, `0fe47c2cf2ee41f7`) and `pp=130048` (passes, `0c928e2eca742e38`), each twice.
The fixed program passed the failing schedule (`0f32443537bd2c09`) and all 100 schedules.

**The fjall race, tried and not reproduced.** A stress program (not committed) opens a fjall
3.1.13 database with two worker threads and 1 KiB memtables, runs 8 writers on 4 keyspaces and
drops the database, 20 rounds per run. A watchdog reports a hang after 10 s without an insert. A
probe build of fjall counted 26 sends of `Flush` on a full queue in 5 rounds on the Mac, so the
queue does fill. No hang occurred: 230 rounds on the Mac, 200 on Linux, 100 hvx schedules with
`--timing --preempt` (2,000 rounds), and 46 hvx schedules on 2 vCPUs with `--turns --timing`
(920 rounds) before that exploration's 15-minute limit ended it.

**What hydo lacked.** hydo has no token that stops a process or a thread for some guest time.
On the Mac and KVM a busy loop makes no VM exits, so a CPU limit in the guest works only on hvx.
Both are open item 80.

### Milestone 213 (tentative number) — DONE, STAGE 1 (several vCPUs on the KVM engine: the design, and a probe that showed KVM can run them one at a time from one thread with the local APIC in user space, deterministically, on AMD and Intel; the parts of stage 2 that leave the engine alone; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-13)

**In short.** Open item 45 says the KVM engine has one vCPU. `docs/design/kvm-vcpus.md` designs
several: N KVM vCPUs in one VM, run one at a time from one host thread in turns of `q` counted
exits, with one VM clock, an x2APIC per vCPU emulated in the engine (no in-kernel interrupt
controller), INIT and STARTUP handled by the engine, and a second guest kernel
`bzImage-kvm-smp` whose `cpu_relax()` exits. Its largest risk is that a turn can switch only at
an exit, so a race window without an exit stays out of reach. Stage 1 of its plan, a C probe
against `/dev/kvm`, passed on GitHub's runners. The engine is unchanged: one vCPU is still the only
machine, and every recorded value stays.

**The probe** (`hv/kvm/smp/smpprobe.c`, in the manner of `hv/kvm/pmu/pmuprobe.c`): hand-written
32-bit guests on two vCPUs, no in-kernel irqchip, every vCPU run from one thread. A one-off
workflow on a temporary branch `tmp-kvm-vcpus`, deleted afterwards, ran it in four jobs:
https://github.com/kakoc/hydo/actions/runs/43407838670. The lead added `udevadm settle` and a
wait for `/dev/kvm` to the workflow (the same race was fixed in `action/action.yml`, 500a0b7a).
The hosts were an AMD EPYC 7763, two EPYC 9V74 and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C, each with 4 vCPUs and
nested KVM on Linux 7.0.0. Each job ran the probe twice and its race test under four busy loops:
17 of 17 checks twice and 4 of 4 under load, on every job.

| check | result on every job |
|---|---|
| x2APIC | reads and writes of the x2APIC MSRs exit to user space with their index; CPUID leaf 1 has the APIC and x2APIC bits; an access to the xAPIC page is an MMIO exit |
| INIT and STARTUP | vCPU 1 starts in real mode at the vector's page and reaches protected mode; the second STARTUP is ignored |
| an IPI | injected into vCPU 1 with `KVM_INTERRUPT` at its next turn; the handler ran once; `d5862710e31e565b` |
| a two-vCPU counter race in turns of `q` exits, `q` = 1..200 | every exit equals a model of the guest; one hash per `q` in both runs; grid hash `9ec051b85c9f3a4b` on AMD and Intel alike; the 100 odd turn lengths lose updates; 206 runs from snapshots restored into fresh VMs equal their straight runs |
| a switch at every exit, one thread | 21 to 124 ns over an exit on AMD, 2,467 ns on Intel; an exit costs 8.2 to 13.6 µs there |

A handover between two threads cost about one exit more (16.4 to 24.2 µs per exit), so the
design's choice of one thread holds.

**The parts of stage 2 and 3 that leave the engine alone** (the state search, Milestone 212,
changes `hydo-kvm` and is not merged yet):

- `engine::one_vcpu_fingerprints_are_pinned` (`hydo/crates/hydo-kvm/tests/engine.rs`) pins
  six scripted one-vCPU runs: idle, tick jitter, preemption points, another cadence, an exact
  spin, and a counter loop in the rewind mode. Their values are this tree's.
- `hydo_kvm::apic` (`hydo/crates/hydo-kvm/src/apic.rs`), the x2APIC model with six unit tests:
  priorities, EOI, the TPR, the APIC turned off in software, ExtINT on LINT0, ICR decoding, and
  the timer in the exit clock. Nothing calls it yet.
- The SMP kernel's recipe: `hv/kvm/linux/kernel-smp.nix` (an override of `kernel.nix`, which
  does not change), `hydo-kvm-smp.config`, `hydo-kvm-smp.patch`, and `SMP=1` for
  `build-kernel.sh`. A trial build on the bare-metal machine's single-user Nix (a compile check,
  not a pin; no KVM there) found that `outb %al, $0x5f0` assembles to port `0xf0`: an immediate
  port has 8 bits, and the build gave 207 assembler warnings. The relax port's OUT now takes the
  port in DX. The second build had no warning and 198 sites that load `0x5f0` into DX. The
  configuration checks passed, and `audit-rdtsc.sh` listed the UP kernel's 10 sites and no RDTSC.
  The trial `bzImage-kvm-smp` was `a43b7bc3…`, not a pin.
- Reading Linux 6.6.35 for the recipe found that the PIC reaches the boot CPU's LINT0 only when
  the I/O APIC is turned off, so the SMP kernel's command line needs `noapic`.

**Left.** Stage 2's engine code waits for the state search's merge. The SMP kernel was not booted
and is not pinned. Intel KVM ran only the probe, on one runner model.

### Milestone 214 (tentative number): DONE (Compose services with `build:` in one import: `hydo compose` builds their images with Docker and pins each file's digest; fetch-images.sh builds a missing file again and stops at other bytes; 2026-11-13)

**In short.** Before, a service with `build:` was imported unpinned. fetch-images.sh printed the
`docker build` and `docker save` commands to run by hand, and a second `hydo compose` read the
file and pinned it. Now one `hydo compose` does all of it when a Docker command answers. The
manifest then has the image's own settings (its `HEALTHCHECK`, `EXPOSE` and `VOLUME`) from the
first import, and the lock file pins the file's digest. A later build that gives other bytes
stops fetch-images.sh until the user accepts it.

**The choice.** The task allowed either fetch-images.sh or `hydo compose` to run the build.
`hydo compose` builds, because only the importer can read the built file's settings into
`hydo.yaml`. A build in the script alone would still need a second import, which also rewrites a
`hydo.yaml` that the user has edited by then. `hydo compose` builds without asking, because an AI
agent or a CI job cannot answer a prompt; `--no-build` turns it off. fetch-images.sh keeps a
build of its own for the files that are missing later: a fresh checkout (`hydo/images/` is
git-ignored) or the other architecture.

**What changed** (`hydo/crates/hydo-compose`):

- `src/localbuild.rs`: the Docker command is `--docker <cli>`, else `docker`, else `podman`; it
  counts when `<cli> version` exits 0. Without one, the message names what to install: Docker
  Engine on Linux, Docker Desktop or Colima on a Mac, or Podman. When the command is there and
  its engine does not run, it names how to start it.
- `hydo compose`: for a local build whose file and pin for this machine's guest are missing, it
  runs `<cli> build --platform linux/<arch> -t <tag>` with Compose's `context`, `dockerfile`,
  `args`, `target`, `labels`, `network`, `extra_hosts`, `shm_size`, `no_cache` and `pull`. Before,
  only the context, `dockerfile:` and `target:` were passed. `ssh`, `secrets`, `dockerfile_inline`
  and `additional_contexts` get a warning. `<cli> save` writes the file that `hydo.yaml` names.
  The lock entry has `local_build: true` and the platforms' digests and settings, as a registry
  image's entry has them. A file whose digest differs from its pin is pinned again, with a
  warning. On a Mac, where only the arm64 file exists, the settings come from it.
- fetch-images.sh calls `hydo-fetch-image build <arch> <file> <tag> <lock> <ref> -- <args>` for
  each missing file. The same digest as the pin puts the file in place. No pin yet records one
  and says to run `hydo compose` again for the settings. Another digest keeps the build as
  `<file>.rebuilt` and exits 1, and says whether the settings changed too.
  `HYDO_ACCEPT_REBUILD=1` takes it and re-pins it. `HYDO_DOCKER` names another command. These
  are the script's variables, so hydo-config's inventory leaves them out, as it does every shell
  script's.
- `src/ocilocal.rs`: the importer's reader of `docker save` archives read only the files of the
  top directory and the `.json` files. Docker 25 and later keep the config at
  `blobs/sha256/<hex>`, so the first real run failed: the digest of the config it read (an empty
  file, `e3b0c442…`) did not match. Files under `blobs/` below 4 MiB are read now. hydo-build's
  own reader was right.
- The two compose help texts of the `hydo` command, the importer's usage text, `hydo guide workflow`,
  MANIFEST.md "From Docker Compose" (a table row for `build:`), the crate's README and
  `docs/YOUR-PROJECT.md` describe it.

**Tests.** `cargo test -p hydo-compose` passed: 13 tests of the integration program, 10 unit
tests. `tests/local_build.rs` has six tests with a fake Docker command that saves prepared
archives. They cover the build arguments, the settings read from the file, the pin, a second
import that builds nothing, and a rebuild with the same bytes. They also cover other bytes with
the same settings (stopped, then accepted) and other settings, a file replaced by hand (pinned
again), and no Docker. The golden `compose_equals_python` passes `--no-build`, so its answers do
not depend on whether the machine has Docker. It was re-recorded for the 34 cases with a local
build and the 3 usage cases; no other case and no rc changed. Two new cases import
`tests/fixtures/local-build`. The golden of the `hydo` command changed in the 4 compose usage answers and
the 2 `hydo guide manifest` hashes. `cargo test -p hydo`, `-p hydo-agents` (with
`public_content::`), `-p hydo-config`, clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt` passed.

**The real run** on this Mac with Docker 28.4 (Colima, the containerd image store), from
`tests/fixtures/local-build` (busybox 1.36.1, about 2 MB):

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `hydo compose docker-compose.yml --out hydo/hydo.yaml` | built linux/arm64, `port: 8080` and `ready:` from the image's `HEALTHCHECK`, pinned `sha256:87dde3d5…` |
| the file deleted, `sh hydo/fetch-images.sh` | built `sha256:e214799c…`, stopped with status 1, kept `…-arm64-oci.rebuilt`, the settings the same |
| `HYDO_ACCEPT_REBUILD=1 sh hydo/fetch-images.sh` | built `sha256:31d5fa05…`, accepted and re-pinned, status 0, the `.rebuilt` file removed |
| `sh hydo/fetch-images.sh` again | nothing built, status 0 |
| `hydo-build hydo/hydo.yaml --arch arm64 --check` | `OK (1 services, 1 invariants, 20 workload steps)` |

Every build of that Dockerfile gave other bytes, also with every step cached. The two configs
differ in one history line: Docker 28.4's BuildKit writes a Go pointer into the history of an
`EXPOSE` step (`EXPOSE &{[{{7 0} {7 0}}] 0x400108b340}` and `… 0x4003889dc0}`). The pin makes
that visible, as intended, but such an image stops fetch-images.sh on every rebuild. The image
`shop-app:latest` was removed afterwards; BuildKit's cache keeps the busybox layer.

**Left** (open item 81). The real run was on a Mac only, with Docker; Linux and Podman ran only
with the fake command. `hydo compose` builds for this machine's guest only, and fetch-images.sh
builds the other one on request (`sh fetch-images.sh all`). `ssh`, `secrets`,
`dockerfile_inline` and `additional_contexts` are not passed. No VM ran the built image.

### Milestone 215 (tentative number) — DONE (Formance Ledger onboarded on the Mac engine as an experiment in business bugs; a race of two first uses of one account fails a payment with `500`, found by the error logs and by no business rule; 2026-11-13)

**In short.** Formance Ledger v2.4.18, a double-entry ledger in Go on PostgreSQL 16, runs
unmodified from its tag in `hydo/onboard/examples/formance-ledger` (RESULTS.md). The experiment
gave it two kinds of rules. Eight domain rules read the ledger's own state: balanced
transactions, balances equal to the sum of the postings, effective volumes, no overdraft, one
transaction per operation, reverts, atomic bulks, and the audit log. One rule compares the
ledger with what the client saw acknowledged. Every run used the Mac engine with the published
0.3.1. The bare-metal machine ran another agent's timing measurement, and the build machine was
off. Nothing recorded moved, and no hydo code changed.

**What was found.**

- A ledger bug, found by the error logs and by no rule. Two transactions that first use one
  account at the same moment, in two different assets, race in `UpsertAccounts`. Both insert
  the account, and the second fails on the unique index `accounts_ledger` with `500 INTERNAL`.
  The check-then-insert came with the ledger's pull request 1064 (v2.4). Natively, 192 of 200
  such pairs fail one request on v2.4.18, and none on v2.3.24, which used `ON CONFLICT`. Under
  hydo it shows in the run without faults (fp `8fd7ae2f4353b6de`, twice). The client retries a
  `500` with the same idempotency key, so no business rule fails. An upstream issue is drafted,
  not posted.
- A client mistake, found by rule 1.5 and the client-record rule, and by no rule over the
  ledger's state. Without idempotency keys, an answer lost after the commit makes the retry
  record the operation again. The explorer found it in 1 of 20 schedules and shrank it to
  `O=ledger@20-25:resp:loss,81%` (`3b4c45cc98cd20b9`, twice). The saved regression passes on the
  default image, where every unanswered operation took effect at most once.
- Expected losses: a lying disk, or `synchronous_commit=off`, lost 3 to 34 acknowledged
  operations at a power cut in 5 of 36 swarm schedules. Again only the client-record rules saw
  it, since each loss is a whole transaction gone.
- A documented behaviour: a backdated transfer can leave a past balance below zero, since the
  ledger checks only the final balance.

**Runs.** 156 explored schedules and 21 directed runs, on hydo 0.3.1's Mac release:

| exploration | strategy | schedules | failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| e1, e2 | `process --new-faults` | 70 | 0 |
| e5, the client without keys | `process --new-faults` | 20 | 1 (the client mistake) |
| e3 | `swarm --new-faults` | 36 | 16, all lying disk, I/O errors or `S=off` with a cut |
| e4 | `process --new-faults --timing --preempt` | 30 | 0 |

The directed runs aimed at answers lost after the commit (slow and lossy windows on the ledger's
port, pauses). Every SQL rule returned the broken rows on a deliberate break of a native
database. The image without faults, `1fce9750…`, gives `8fd7ae2f4353b6de` twice.

**What hydo lacked.** Open items 82 to 84: a recovery boot that hangs when its carried records
pass the 4 KiB receive queue of the Mac and KVM engines, a limit of 1,024 control messages per
run, and error kinds split by a ten-character request id, with `hydo errors accept` writing the
login name into `known-errors.yaml`.

### Milestone 216 (tentative number) - DONE (pauses of the workload: the timed pause stops the workload's own process tree for some guest time, as a CPU limit does, and `hydo explore --pause-workload` draws it; etcd's flaky test fails on every run of one such pause without a CPU-limit model, on the Mac and on hvx; nothing recorded moved; 2026-11-13)

**In short.** Open item 80 asked for a fault that stops a process for some guest time, as a
container's CPU limit does when its quota runs out. The pause fault already had a guest-time form,
`P=<svc>@<at>~<off>:<dur>` (Milestone 46), on agent images and on all three engines, also for
groups (Milestone 195). It could not name the test program. Now it can: `P=workload@0~4:45`
stops every process of the workload 4 ms of guest time after step 0 starts, for 45 ms. No new
token and no agent change. `hydo explore --pause-workload` draws such pauses from a stream of
its own. On etcd's `TestCacheCompactionResync` (Milestone 211) the pause fails the test on every run
without the cgroup `cpu.max` and the busy loops, on the Mac engine and on hvx, and its neighbours
pass. The test-only fix passes the failing pause.

**Why the existing pause and not a new token.** The first question was whether `P=...~` covers
the item. It does with small extensions:

- `P=<target>@<at>~<off>:<dur>` is a thread of the host controller (`pause_timer` in
  `hydo-control/src/schedule.rs`). It runs `busybox sleep <off>` in the guest, sends the agent's
  `signal STOP` with `tree` to each target's handle, sleeps `<dur>`, and sends `signal CONT`. The
  agent signals every process of the tree, so every thread stops, as under a CPU limit.
- The guest kernel's clock measures both times. The engines' stop clocks count other units: hvx
  counts retired branches or exits, and the Mac and KVM count VM exits. How many of them make a
  millisecond depends on the engine and on what the guest does. A CPU limit's period is guest
  time, so the guest's clock is the clock to use. An engine stop at an engine clock value, as the
  state search's `br=` does (its branch, not merged), would need each engine to report guest
  nanoseconds at its stops.
- Every decision is taken at the stop where the controller sees the agent's answer. That stop is a
  pure function of the run, so a schedule with a pause of the workload replays bit for bit.
- The pause ends on its own. While the target is stopped, the guest has only the sleep left to
  run, and its timer ends after `<dur>` ms of guest time.

The other mechanisms were left out. A cgroup v2 freezer needs the target in a cgroup of its own,
so the agent would have to change, and the agent's bytes are inside every image. A `cpu.max`
quota needs the guest to use CPU time, which a busy loop on the Mac or KVM does not.

**What changed.**

- `hydo-control`: `P=...~` may name `workload`, the handle of the workload's own run. That is
  the test program of `workload.kind: test`. It may stand alone or in a list with services
  (`targets::read_timed_pause`). Such a pause skips the request-in-flight check, a `pgrep` in the
  guest that would only delay the stop. A pause of services takes its old path exactly. The names
  check refuses `P=workload@<at>+<n>`: the workload does not run between steps. The tests are
  `hydo-control`'s `workload_pause::`.
- `hydo-explore`: `--pause-workload` draws `P=workload@<at>~<off>:<dur>` in half of the
  schedules. The draws come from the stream `WP_SALT`, so every other field of a seed's schedule
  stays. The step is one where the workload runs. The start is at most `--pause-max` ms (default
  1000). It is drawn evenly for half of the pauses and on a log scale for the others. So about a
  quarter of the starts fall in the first 10 ms. The length is 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, or 500 ms.
  The fault space keeps such a pause when `faults:` has no `pause`. The shrinker tries half the
  length (down to 10 ms) and the start 0. The tests are `hydo-explore`'s `workload_pauses::`.
- `hydo-schedule`: nothing; the language test `workload_pauses` holds the examples.
- `hydo guide faults` has the section `Pause the workload`. `hydo guide flaky-tests` shows the
  pause instead of the CPU-limit model.

**The proof on the Mac engine.** This tree's `hydo`, the arm64 images of Milestone 211 rebuilt to
the same bytes (initramfs `b0664c70c7e99735…`, fixed `c7053aab15b1f584…`). Runs with a length
of 60 ms failed for starts of 0 to 7 ms and passed from 8 ms on. At a start of 4 ms, lengths of 35
ms or less passed and 40 ms or more failed.

| image | schedule | verdict | fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| buggy | `disk=none \| run P=workload@0~4:45` | VIOLATION, `expected cached revision 5 after compaction, got 20` | `24dedf9da7af0a08` (3 runs) |
| buggy | `disk=none \| run P=workload@0~4:35` | OK | `b8b9b46b4027b5af` (2 runs) |
| buggy | `disk=none \| run P=workload@0~8:45` | OK | `9402add9274c87ce` (2 runs) |
| fixed | `disk=none \| run P=workload@0~4:45` | OK | `8171ca80d265840d` (2 runs) |
| buggy | `disk=none \| run` | OK | `985f97632370e53b`, Milestone 211's value |
| fixed | `disk=none \| run` | OK | `0e32a33ecd1d0a7b`, Milestone 211's value |

`hydo explore --pause-workload --seeds 1-100 --workers 1` on the buggy image found 13 failures,
all with the report's line and all reproduced. The shrinker took seed 3's failure to
`disk=none dseed=1d0b14e4db018fed | run P=workload@0~0:50` (`a980b7222dcce5ee`, two runs).
Milestone 211 ran 300 schedules of `--timing --preempt` on the same image, and none failed.

**The proof on hvx.** The runs were on the bare-metal machine, after the state search's campaign
ended. They used this tree's `hydo` and `hydo-hvx` over the 0.3.1 Linux release and the module
loaded since 2026-11-08. Milestone 211's plain images were rebuilt to the same bytes

passed for starts of 0 to 149 ms, failed for 151 to 163 ms except at 159 ms, and passed from 165

| image | schedule | verdict | fingerprint |

| plain | `disk=none \| run P=workload@0~155:45` | VIOLATION, the same line | `2ae2f4390bb012b8` (3 runs) |
| plain | `disk=none \| run P=workload@0~155:30` | OK | `3244703db66dae96` (2 runs) |

| fixed | `disk=none \| run` | OK | `4c4eac3a06a2181a`, Milestone 211's value |

`hydo explore --pause-workload --pause-max 200 --seeds 1-200 --workers 2` found 3 failures, all

**Nothing recorded moved.** A plain schedule, and a timed pause of services, take the
controller's old path; the explorer draws nothing new without `--pause-workload`.

- `hydo-bench rebaseline --check` on this Mac, in the fast mode, with this tree's programs and a
  work folder without a run cache, one VM at a time: all 76 hvm schedules of 21 images gave their
  recorded values, the verdicts unchanged.
- On hvx, the pinned reproducers with this tree's `hydo` gave `a76d7fe857fdb37c` (VIOLATION,
  order 11) and `efbde7b57264be0f` (OK). Neither the hvx engine nor the module changed, so

- The explorer's `identity::` test passed without a re-record, and so did the fast tier of
  `hydo-schedule`, `hydo-control`, `hydo-explore`, `hydo-agents` and `hydo` (300 tests).

**Qdrant (Milestone 208).** Its race needs the test's thread held off while a worker thread of
the same process takes 35 operations. A pause of the workload stops the whole process, the worker
too, so it does not help there. Item 4 of that example's "What hydo lacked" stays open: a pause
of one thread. On hvx, `hydo explore --pause-workload --pause-max 3000 --seeds 1-60 --workers 2`
on its buggy image (`9aa2213aea1a5295…`, the recorded bytes) gave 60 passes. Every run read a
queue length of 34 to 36, as without such pauses.

**Also in this change.** Milestone 211 re-recorded only the explorer's quick identity golden for
its new example, and the Formance Ledger example added a known-errors file since. Then the full
tier's explorer corpus and the controller's identity corpus failed: the inputs of their goldens
had changed. Both are re-recorded in a commit of their own; the controller's golden only gains
the etcd example's lines. `hydo guide manifest` prints MANIFEST.md, so the CLI's golden answer
for it is re-recorded too.

**Left.** The KVM engine did not run a pause of the workload: the build machine was out of reach.
A one-off workflow on the branch `tmp-workload-pause-kvm` is ready to run it on a GitHub runner.
A pause of one thread, and pauses that repeat in every period of a CPU limit, are not built.

### Milestone 212 — DONE (an experimental state search: exploration from mid-run snapshots, with new faults and timing for the rest of a run; on the bug benchmark and on etcd 3.5.5 it did not help; 2026-11-13)

**In short.** `hydo explore --search state` keeps snapshots that runs took at rare moments and
runs the rest of a run again from them, with new faults. It is experimental and opt-in, and
without the option nothing changes. On hvx it did not help. It ran on the slow benchmark defects d7 and
d10 at about the same worker seconds as the plain exploration. It found each defect in 2 of 5
seed ranges, and the plain exploration in 3 of 5. On etcd 3.5.5 neither found the second symptom of issue 14685 in
5 ranges each. Its branches cost about two thirds of a fresh run and did not fail more often.
The Qdrant flaky test on KVM was not measured.

**Why, and what was different from the earlier attempts.** The explorer draws every schedule
from its seed and runs it from S1. The user approved (2026-11-13) closing that gap by exploring
from mid-run states near rare events. The design, written before the prototype, is
`docs/design/state-search.md`. It names why Milestones 41, 43, 44, 45, 139, and 209 found
nothing. Milestone 45, the closest, branched one schedule at its rarest assertion with 6 tick
jitter variants. The variants repeated each other, and its budget counted a variant as a run.
The state search changes three things:

- A branch draws new faults for the rest of the run, moved into the remaining steps. On KVM and
  on the Mac it also draws new timing.
- The cost is the worker's wall time. It includes the snapshots and the restores.
- Half of the schedules stay the plain exploration's.

**Built** (opt-in; without `--search state` nothing changes):

- `hydo explore --search state` and its options:
  - `--state-mix`: branches per 1,000 once the corpus has an entry, default 500. With 0 the
    search runs the plain exploration's schedules with the same bookkeeping and no snapshots.
  - `--state-corpus` (default 4 on hvx, 32 otherwise), `--state-rare` (default 2),
    `--state-snaps` (snapshots per run, default 2), and `--state-stop`.

  The search runs on one worker, which holds the snapshots (hydo-explore `src/state.rs`,
  `run.rs` `state_search`). Each run is a line of `state-search.jsonl` in the exploration's
  folder. The results formats are unchanged.
- The host controller (hydo-control `src/search.rs`). `RecLink` records every stop of a run (the
  engine's report and the commands sent). It takes `SNAP` at stops whose guest console shows a
  rare feature: an SDK assertion record, or a console-line class with numbers made `#`. For a
  target whose console shows no feature, it takes `SNAP` at stops spread over the median guest
  clock. `BranchLink` replays a parent's stops to a branch's controller, requires the parent's
  commands, and goes live at the snapshot after `RESUME`, with no resynchronisation.
  `agent::check_branch` runs that replay without a VM first and refuses a branch whose prefix
  differs. The runner gained `Link::before_step` and `Link::timing`, both inert for every
  existing link.
- A branch's schedule is one schedule string. A fault branch is an ordinary schedule. A timing
  branch has the new host token `br=<clock>` followed by timing tokens. The parser has
  `branch_points`, `without_branch_points`, and `BRANCH_KEYS` (hydo-schedule). The host
  controller takes the token out of the engine's schedule. At the first stop whose clock
  reaches it, the controller sends the new engine command `TIME <tokens>` (`SwitchLink`). A
  branch and a run from S1 do this alike.
- The KVM and Mac engines keep tick jitter and forced preemption points in a snapshot (before,
  such a `SNAP` was refused) and take `TIME`. hvx refuses `TIME`, and `hydo_engine::refusal`
  refuses `br=` for hvx before any VM.
- A branch keeps the step range in progress. The controller runs the workload in step ranges
  split at fault steps (`HYDO_FROM`, `HYDO_TO`), so a new fault inside the running range would
  change the run from that range's start. A branch keeps every fault of its parent that starts at
  or before the end of the range in progress, and moves the fresh seed's faults after it.
- After the measurements: a branch never has both an `N=` and an `O=` window. The strategies
  never draw both, and 17 measured branches with both ended in `ERROR tc setup failed` where the
  windows met. The branch keeps its parent's window and drops the fresh seed's
  (`state::tests::a_branch_never_has_both_network_windows`).

**Checks.** Branches replay bit for bit from a fresh boot. On hvx, 6 of 6 branches of the d7
image gave their fingerprints again under `hydo run`. On the Mac, 9 of 9 fault branches of the Redis
example did, and 9 of 9 timing branches. The Mac fast `hydo-bench rebaseline --check` gave all
76 schedules their recorded values. On hvx, the recorded schedules of etcd-3.5.5, redis,
redis-netem, redis-freeze and redis-hist gave every recorded value, and the pinned reproducers
gave `a76d7fe857fdb37c` and `efbde7b57264be0f`. The tests are these:

- hydo-control's `search::a_branch_equals_its_schedule_run_from_s1`;
- the unit tests of `state.rs`: the branch rule, branch points, the range in progress, and the
  search's determinism;
- hydo-schedule's `branch_points`.

 The explorer's identity goldens did not change.

**Measurements** (hvx, the bare-metal machine; the tables are in `docs/design/state-search.md`,
section "Measurements"). Each target ran 5 seed ranges. The plain exploration ran with
`--state-mix 0`. The budgets were 60 plain runs against 80 state-search runs on the benchmark,
and 80 against 100 on etcd, which cost about the same worker seconds. A benchmark detection is a
failure with the defect's signature whose schedule passes on the control image from a fresh
boot (hydo-bench's rule). The control runs are why the raw counts mislead: in the d7 search of
seeds 4001–4080, all 14 runs with d7's signature failed on the control image too.

| target | ranges with a detection, plain | state search | median worker seconds, plain | state search |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| d7 | 3 of 5 | 2 of 5 | 418 s | 503 s (no detection) |
| d10 | 3 of 5 | 2 of 5 | 474 s | 570 s (no detection) |
| d4 | 5 of 5 | 4 of 5 | 98 s | 115 s |
| d6 | 5 of 5 | 5 of 5 | 28 s | 28 s |
| etcd 14685, `client.revisions_monotonic` | 0 of 5 | 0 of 5 | none in 816–879 s | none in 810–866 s |

The state search was earlier in 3 of 20 benchmark ranges, each time by a branch (d10 once, d6
twice), and later or without a detection in 6. At equal worker seconds the plain explorations
showed 21 distinct failure classes over the 20 benchmark ranges and the state searches 16. The
state search found no class that the plain exploration missed in the same range. On etcd the
classes were the same in every range. A branch's median wall time was 4.0 to 5.4 s, against 6.0
to 9.9 s for a fresh run. Branches failed in 0.5 to 7.7 % of the runs, fresh runs in 1.5 to
30.6 %.

**Left** (open item 85):

- the Qdrant flaky test on KVM;
- the KVM engine's change on a real KVM host;
- the shrinker and `br=`;
- timing branches on hvx;
- one worker per search.
